Arah terkait tambahan mencakup metode *contextual biasing* berbasis konteks yang memerlukan daftar frasa yang telah ditentukan dan keterbatasan domain terbuka, *speech distillation* berbasis teks yang menggunakan sinyal *teacher* hanya selama pelatihan, serta model berbantuan teks sumber untuk interpretasi simultan yang mengasumsikan teks sumber tersedia secara langsung. Para penulis membangun dan membandingkan SAMA-ASR dengan keterbatasan ini dengan memperkenalkan *adapter* sisi *decoder* yang beroperasi tanpa domain yang telah ditentukan dan menggunakan terjemahan otomatis pada saat *inference*.

results.en:
Experiments on 30-hour datasets of Taiwanese Hokkien and Hakka show that SAMA-ASR consistently improves character error rates over audio-only adaptation, prompt-based baselines, and semantic-only translation-guided models like TG-ASR. Specifically, SAMA-ASR achieves character error rates of 23.48 percent on Taiwanese Hokkien and 22.48 percent on Hakka under practical automatic evaluation settings.

Furthermore, combining SAMA-ASR with a strong parameter-efficient fine-tuning baseline like LoRA yields further reductions in character error rates. Qualitative error analysis and ablation studies confirm that the explicit acoustic anchor successfully prevents text-side hallucinations and incorrect substitutions caused by noisy semantic anchors.
results.id:
Eksperimen pada dataset 30 jam bahasa Hokkien Taiwan dan Hakka menunjukkan bahwa SAMA-ASR secara konsisten meningkatkan *character error rate* dibandingkan adaptasi khusus suara, *baseline* berbasis *prompt*, dan model panduan terjemahan semantik saja seperti TG-ASR. Secara khusus, SAMA-ASR mencapai *character error rate* sebesar 23,48 persen pada bahasa Hokkien Taiwan dan 22,48 persen pada Hakka di bawah pengaturan evaluasi otomatis praktis.

Lebih lanjut, menggabungkan SAMA-ASR dengan *baseline* *fine-tuning* yang efisien parameter seperti LoRA menghasilkan pengurangan lebih lanjut pada *character error rate*. Analisis kesalahan kualitatif dan studi ablasi mengonfirmasi bahwa jangkar akustik eksplisit berhasil mencegah halusinasi sisi teks dan substitusi yang salah yang disebabkan oleh jangkar semantik yang berderau.

tldr.en: This paper proposes SAMA-ASR, a lightweight adapter mechanism that augments speech recognition decoders with semantic anchors from auxiliary translations and an acoustic anchor from speech. Experiments on Taiwanese Hokkien and Hakka demonstrate that SAMA-ASR improves recognition performance over baseline models in both oracle and practical automatic settings.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan SAMA-ASR, sebuah mekanisme *adapter* ringan yang memperkaya *decoder* pengenalan suara dengan jangkar semantik dari terjemahan bantu dan jangkar akustik dari suara. Eksperimen pada bahasa Hokkien Taiwan dan Hakka menunjukkan bahwa SAMA-ASR meningkatkan performa pengenalan dibandingkan model *baseline* pada pengaturan *oracle* maupun otomatis praktis.

2608.29239.title: Anchoring Speech with Semantics: A Multimodal Adapter Mechanism for Automatic Speech Recognition in Low-Resource Languages

2608.29284.abstract: Deploying large language models for legal question answering raises challenges that general-purpose leaderboards do not capture, particularly for low-resource languages and under hard operational constraints. We report on building and operating a retrieval-augmented (RAG) legal assistant for Uzbek that must run in two regimes: a managed cloud service that maximizes answer quality within a per-token cost ceiling, and an on-premises deployment for clients whose legal data may not leave their infrastructure, restricting us to open-weight models on limited local hardware under latency constraints. Because no evaluation existed for this setting, we build two domain benchmarks: a retrieval benchmark of 178 expert-annotated legal queries with gold provision spans, and an end-to-end benchmark of 504 expert-curated question--answer pairs scored by an LLM judge whose ratings we validate against human judgments and against an independent-family judge. Applying these benchmarks under each regime, we find the open-versus-proprietary gap is small and cheaply closed by fine-tuning. Therefore, we train UTE-1, which is a state-of-the-art text embedder among open models for Uzbek. We also demonstrate that closing the performance gap via fine-tuning is both impractical due to the intensive hardware demands of long-context legal Q\&A and unnecessary, given that legal acts change frequently. We support this by reporting a negative result from a QLoRA experiment. We distill practical guidance for similar deployments, drawn from a system serving real users in production. We release our benchmarks, evaluation code and the fine-tuned embedder (UTE-1) \href{https://metric-ai-lab.github.io/Uzbek-Legal-RAG/}{at this https URL} to support future work on low-resource legal NLP.
2608.29284.comment: Accepted to EMNLP 2026 (Industry Track). Project home: [https://metric-ai-lab.github.io/Uzbek-Legal-RAG/](https://metric-ai-lab.github.io/Uzbek-Legal-RAG/)
2608.29284.title: Cloud and On-Premises Deployment of Uzbek Legal RAG via Targeted Retriever Fine-Tuning

2608.29959.abstract: Language is humanity's most consequential technology, yet for over a billion speakers across India's twenty-two constitutionally recognised languages, its digital layer remains structurally incomplete. Named Entity Recognition (NER), the foundational step in transforming raw text into machine-interpretable knowledge, has been studied exhaustively for English but remains largely unsolved across most Indic languages. This paper presents a rigorous comparative study of generative and encoder-based neural architectures for NER on all eleven languages of the Naamapadam benchmark. We evaluate five classic model families spanning sequence-to-sequence transformers and multilingual encoders; four decoder-only large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned with LoRA and 4-bit NF4 quantisation; and nine generative models in zero-to-5-shot inference. Under strict CoNLL span-level evaluation, encoder-based models (mBERT and XLM-R, both F1=0.675 on Hindi) substantially outperform every generative architecture in ten of eleven languages, with gaps of 7.5-40 percentage points against the strongest competitor (Gemma-2-2B: avg F1=0.427). The best few-shot result reaches only 28% of the encoder baseline. We identify three language clusters--encoder-dominant, partial-coverage, and failure-zone; and provide actionable deployment guidelines grounded in transfer learning and low-resource NLP principles.
2608.29959.title: Generative vs. Encoder Models for Multilingual NER: A Comprehensive Empirical Study on Naamapadam

2608.30052.abstract: When a generative search interface answers a commercial question, which market's products it names is decided before the model reasons about the products. We report a controlled probe of 234 runs against the logged-out ChatGPT web interface and the OpenAI API, collected on 29 and 30 August 2026 across four exit countries and six query languages, with six identical runs per cell. Three results. First, the top recommendation is unstable: it changed across six identical runs on four of six prompts, and that rate was identical in the browser interface and in the API with web search both enabled and disabled, so instability is a property of the system and not of the surface. Second, query language, and not location, decides whether local suppliers appear at all. Where the query language matched the country, a global brand won 1 of 24 runs; asked in English on the same connections, local brands took 0 of 6 runs in Estonia and Turkiye. Third, language and location are separable and act on different things: holding the query language fixed and moving only the exit IP moves the market whose brands are named while the answer stays in the query language. We show this on two unrelated pairs, Turkish asked from Berlin and Russian asked from Tallinn, and in both the answer names the resident country's suppliers. A minority language occupies a middle tier: Russian asked from Estonia names an Estonian supplier in 4 of 6 runs and a global one in all six, where Estonian names a local supplier in every run and English names none. A negative control in a second category, coded with the same instrument, shows no language effect at all, and disconfirms our own expectation: that category does have domestic suppliers and none was named in any language, which points the explanation at whether a category is nationally regulated rather than at whether it is nationally supplied.
2608.30052.comment: 13 figures-free pages, 6 tables. Data, collectors and 246 run records: Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22181306
2608.30052.title: The Language of the Question Selects the Market: Query Language and Exit IP as Separable Factors in Commercial Recommendations from a Generative Search Interface

2608.30065.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong Helpfulness, Harmlessness, and Honesty (3H) alignment in English-centric settings, but these gains transfer poorly to low-resource languages due to cultural mismatches. Existing multilingual 3H benchmarks rely predominantly on automated translation or LLM based synthesis, propagating source-language biases while sacrificing local relevance. To address this gap, we introduce Pak3H1, the first human-validated, culturally contextualized Urdu benchmark suite for 3H alignment, comprising PakAlpaca (helpfulness), PakBeaverTails (harmlessness), and PakTruthfulQA (honesty). Our multi-stage pipeline integrates manual cultural adaptation and dictionary-guided post editing to prioritize native speaker judgment, ensuring both semantic fidelity and contextual authenticity. Zero-shot evaluations across multiple open and proprietary LLM architectures reveal systematic cross-lingual alignment gaps: helpfulness win rates decline under localized contexts, harmlessness guardrails break down against regional safety risks, and composite honesty metrics degrade substantially due to localized factual constraints. These findings expose structural limitations in current alignment approaches, underscoring the necessity of human-guided localization for equitable multilingual evaluation.
2608.30065.comment: We introduce Pak3H, a human-validated Urdu benchmark for helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty. Zero-shot evaluations show LLM performance degrades across all three dimensions in low-resourced contextualized settings
2608.30065.title: Pak3H: Evaluating the Cost of Cultural Mismatch in LLM Alignment with a Human-Contextualized Urdu Benchmark

2608.30092.abstract: We present Arkios, a 1.04B-parameter dense transformer pretrained from scratch on 150B tokens of bilingual English-Nepali text, using a custom single-file C/CUDA training stack and a Devanagari-aware byte-level BPE tokenizer built for this project. On ARC-Easy and ARC-Challenge, Arkios exceeds three comparably sized open models (Pythia-1.4B, TinyLlama-1.1B, OLMo-1B) despite an order of magnitude fewer training tokens, likely aided by a match between our educational-web-text pretraining data and ARC's grade-school-science format rather than a general capability advantage. We report full evaluation results under standard protocols, including a correction to an earlier partial-sample estimate, and findings specific to evaluating small models in a low-resource language: the standard multiple-choice-letter prompt format used by common evaluation harnesses places this model at chance on Nepali reading comprehension, and simultaneously at chance on English in the same format, which would lead a naive benchmark run to conclude the model has no Nepali ability when in fact it does. Concretely, both languages score at chance in the letter-choice format (0.240 Nepali, 0.236 English, against a chance baseline of 0.250), while scoring the answer text directly reveals genuine, English-favoring comprehension (0.306 Nepali, 0.387 English). We describe a manifest-conditioned tool-use contract introduced during instruction tuning, where tool calls are permitted only when a tool manifest is declared in context and suppressed otherwise, and report where that contract holds and where it does not. We release both the base and instruction-tuned model weights under Apache-2.0. The training code and a small privately-sourced portion of the Nepali pretraining corpus are not released; everything needed to reproduce the reported numbers from the released weights is included here.
2608.30092.title: Arkios: An Open Bilingual English-Nepali Language Model Trained From Scratch, with a Devanagari-Aware Tokenizer

2608.30541.abstract: Pixel-based language models (LMs) replace traditional tokenizers by processing rendered images of text, making cross-lingual transfer heavily dependent on the visual and structural properties of writing systems. However, the dynamics of adapting these models to low-resource languages with complex morphology and written in unique scripts are not yet explored. Using Tibetan as a case study, we analyze how continued pre-training of pixel-based LMs is influenced by data scale, initial script exposure, and cross-lingual transfer from languages written in other Brahmic scripts. We introduce four rendering-level metrics to quantify visual script similarity. We evaluate downstream performance across three tasks. Our results show that higher orthographic proximity enhances semantic transfer, even under severe data constraints. Additionally, we find a performance asymmetry based on the pre-training starting point: while multilingual pre-training PIXEL-M4 has stronger initial performance, its capacity for subsequent adaptation seems to be constrained, whereas adapting a monolingual model PIXEL with mixed scripts yields more gains on sentence-level tasks. Our metrics and case study offer empirical observations that could help inform data selection and script adaptation choices when working with pixel-based models in similar low-resource settings.
2608.30541.title: Seeing the Unseen: Visual Similarity for Pixel Language Model Adaptation

2608.30725.abstract: Recent multilingual vision--language encoders cover hundreds of languages in a single model, yet on two state-of-the-art instances retrieval on low-resource languages (LRL; e.g. Swahili) trails high-resource ones (HRL; e.g. English) by $30^+$\,pp. We ask where in the trained encoder this gap is located. Prior modality-gap and cross-lingual subspace work suggests a linear language direction at the output crowds out alignment-relevant geometry. We falsify this: LEACE drives the linear language classifier from $>99\%$ to near chance and iterated INLP to $37$--$50\%$ while LRL retrieval moves within $\pm 1.5$\,pp and all tier means within $2.2$\,pp, tracking random controls. The linear bias is a \emph{symptom}, not the cause. Instead, the alignment-causal factor lies along the encoder's forward path: the EOS (end-of-sequence) hidden state's per-language trajectory diverges with depth. Substituting the EOS with its parallel English value three blocks before the projector lifts Swahili from $22.1\%$ to $69.1\%$ on one encoder (and reproduces on the other); three controls rule out pooled-position tautology and English specificity. A front-layer trunk that pulls each language's projection toward the parallel-content centroid corroborates the diagnosis at training time, recovering $+9.6$ / $+17.1$\,pp on LRL XM3600 retrieval (1{,}000-image subset), with consistent gains across three further benchmarks while preserving HRL performance.

glossary.explanation_id: Arsitektur *model* yang menggunakan dua *encoder* terpisah untuk memetakan modalitas citra dan teks ke dalam ruang *embedding* bersama.
Teknik *interpretability* mekanistik yang melibatkan penggantian aktivasi internal pada *model* dengan aktivasi dari *input* lain untuk menguji peran kausal suatu representasi.
Fenomena di mana representasi *embedding* untuk modalitas citra dan teks terpisah secara geometris di dalam ruang *latent* dari *model* visi-bahasa.
Metode evaluasi di mana pengklasifikasi linier dilatih di atas representasi *model* yang dibekukan untuk menguji keberadaan informasi tertentu.
Prosedur matematis untuk menghapus informasi atau atribut tertentu dari *embedding* representasi *model* tanpa merusak fitur lainnya.
Alur internal dalam *transformer* di mana representasi dijumlahkan secara aditif di setiap *blok*.
Mekanisme *attention* di mana setiap *token* dapat memperhatikan semua *token* lain baik di sebelah kiri maupun kanannya dalam suatu *sekuens*.
Mekanisme *attention* yang dibatasi agar suatu *token* hanya dapat memperhatikan *token* sebelumnya dalam *sekuens*.

background.en: Recent multilingual vision-language encoders scale to hundreds of languages within a single model, yet they exhibit a substantial performance gap of 30 percentage points or more in image-text retrieval between high-resource languages like English and low-resource languages like Swahili and Bengali. While prior research points to potential modality gaps and cross-lingual subspace structures, it remains unclear where and why these representations diverge along the encoder's forward path, motivating the need to localize this cross-lingual failure.
background.id: *Encoder* visi-bahasa multibahasa baru-baru ini berskala hingga ratusan bahasa dalam satu *model*, namun *encoder* tersebut menunjukkan kesenjangan performa yang substansial sebesar 30 persentase poin atau lebih dalam temu kembali citra-teks antara bahasa *high-resource* seperti bahasa Inggris dan bahasa *low-resource* seperti bahasa Swahili dan bahasa Bengali. Meskipun penelitian sebelumnya mengarah pada potensi *modality gap* dan struktur *subspace* lintas bahasa, masih belum jelas di mana dan mengapa representasi ini menyimpang di sepanjang *forward-path* *encoder*, yang memotivasi perlunya melokalisasi kegagalan lintas bahasa ini.

contributions.en: The authors make three primary contributions: first, they falsify the hypothesis that the linear language-identifying direction causes the retrieval gap by showing that erasing it via LEACE or INLP does not significantly affect retrieval. Second, they mechanistically localize the alignment-causal factor to the end-of-sequence hidden state's forward-path trajectory using activation patching with rigorous controls. Third, they introduce a training-time front-layer trunk calibration method that successfully recovers low-resource language retrieval performance across multiple benchmarks while preserving high-resource performance.
contributions.id: Para penulis memberikan tiga kontribusi utama: pertama, mereka memfalsifikasi hipotesis bahwa arah pengenal bahasa linier menyebabkan kesenjangan temu kembali dengan menunjukkan bahwa menghapusnya melalui *LEACE* atau *INLP* tidak secara signifikan memengaruhi temu kembali. Kedua, mereka melokalisasi faktor kausal-penyelarasan secara mekanistik ke lintasan *forward-path* *hidden state* *end-of-sequence* menggunakan *activation patching* dengan kontrol yang ketat. Ketiga, mereka memperkenalkan metode *trunk calibration* *front-layer* pada waktu pelatihan yang berhasil memulihkan performa temu kembali bahasa *low-resource* di berbagai *benchmark* sambil mempertahankan performa *high-resource*.

future_work.en: The authors note several limitations, including model coverage restricted primarily to CLIP-style encoders, treating the vision tower as a fixed reference, and relying on parallel text supervision for trunk calibration. Future directions include generalizing these findings to generative vision-language model text encoders such as BLIP-2 and EVA-CLIP, and further investigating the exact pretraining optimization dynamics and data distribution factors responsible for the initial trajectory divergence.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat beberapa keterbatasan, termasuk cakupan *model* yang terutama terbatas pada *encoder* bergaya CLIP, memperlakukan *vision tower* sebagai referensi tetap, dan mengandalkan *supervisi* teks paralel untuk *trunk calibration*. Arah masa depan mencakup menggeneralisasi temuan ini ke *encoder* teks *generative vision-language model* seperti BLIP-2 dan EVA-CLIP, serta menyelidiki lebih lanjut dinamika *optimalisasi* *pre-training* yang tepat dan faktor distribusi *data* yang bertanggung jawab atas divergensi lintasan awal.

method.en: The study evaluates two primary dual-encoder models, MetaCLIP-2 and SigLIP-2, alongside additional cross-family encoders like AltCLIP, NLLB-CLIP-L, and mSigLIP, using datasets such as XM3600, Flickr30k-200, XTD-200, and Babel-ImageNet. The authors apply linear concept erasure tools, single-row activation patching at intermediate layers with parallel-content and random controls, and propose a novel front-layer trunk calibration method trained on parallel translation data from a subset of CC12M translated via GLM-5.1, utilizing an InfoNCE loss combined with a centroid-aligned cosine alignment term.
method.id: Studi ini mengevaluasi dua *model* *dual-encoder* utama, MetaCLIP-2 dan SigLIP-2, beserta *encoder* lintas keluarga tambahan seperti AltCLIP, NLLB-CLIP-L, dan mSigLIP, menggunakan *dataset* seperti XM3600, Flickr30k-200, XTD-200, dan Babel-ImageNet. Para penulis menerapkan alat *linear concept erasure*, *activation patching* *single-row* pada *layer* perantara dengan kontrol konten paralel dan acak, serta mengusulkan metode *trunk calibration* *front-layer* baru yang dilatih pada *data* *terjemahan mesin* paralel dari *subset* CC12M yang diterjemahkan melalui GLM-5.1, menggunakan *loss* *InfoNCE* yang dikombinasikan dengan suku *penyelarasan* kosinus yang berpusat pada *centroid*.

related_work.en: The paper builds upon prior studies analyzing the text-image modality gap, cross-lingual representation analysis via linear probing and Canonical Correlation Analysis, and closed-form linear concept erasure methods such as LEACE and Iterated Null-space Projection. Furthermore, it connects its intervention techniques to mechanistic interpretability research, specifically activation patching and language surgery in intermediate layers of multilingual large language models, alongside multilingual sentence-embedding distillation.
related_work.id: Makalah ini mendasarkan pada studi sebelumnya yang menganalisis *modality gap* teks-citra, analisis representasi lintas bahasa melalui *linear probing* dan *Canonical Correlation Analysis*, serta metode *linear concept erasure* bentuk tertutup seperti *LEACE* dan *Iterated Null-space Projection*. Selain itu, makalah ini menghubungkan teknik intervensi dengan penelitian *mechanistic interpretability*, khususnya *activation patching* dan *language surgery* pada *layer* perantara dari *large language model* multibahasa, beserta *distillation* *sentence-embedding* multibahasa.

results.en: Empirical results demonstrate that erasing the linear language direction has virtually no impact on retrieval accuracy, disproving the linear-bias hypothesis. Instead, substituting the end-of-sequence hidden state with a parallel English value three blocks before the projector dramatically rescues low-resource retrieval, improving Swahili on MetaCLIP-2 from 22.1% to 69.1%. Furthermore, the proposed front-layer trunk calibration yields substantial low-resource performance gains across four different evaluation benchmarks—averaging +7.8 pp on MetaCLIP-2 and +14.9 pp on SigLIP-2—while preserving high-resource performance.
results.id: Hasil empiris menunjukkan bahwa menghapus arah bahasa linier hampir tidak berdampak pada akurasi temu kembali, yang mematahkan hipotesis bias linier. Sebagai gantinya, mensubstitusi *hidden state* *end-of-sequence* dengan nilai bahasa Inggris paralel tiga *blok* sebelum *projector* secara dramatis menyelamatkan temu kembali *low-resource*, meningkatkan bahasa Swahili pada MetaCLIP-2 dari 22.1% menjadi 69.1%. Lebih lanjut, *trunk calibration* *front-layer* yang diusulkan menghasilkan peningkatan performa *low-resource* yang substansial di empat *benchmark* *evaluasi* yang berbeda—dengan rata-rata +7.8 pp pada MetaCLIP-2 dan +14.9 pp pada SigLIP-2—sambil mempertahankan performa *high-resource*.

tldr.en: This paper investigates why multilingual vision-language encoders underperform on low-resource languages during image-text retrieval. The authors discover that the linear language direction at the output is merely a symptom, and instead pinpoint the failure to the forward-path trajectory divergence of the end-of-sequence hidden state.
tldr.id: Studi ini menyelidiki mengapa *encoder* visi-bahasa multibahasa berkinerja buruk pada bahasa-*low-resource* selama temu kembali citra-teks. Para penulis menemukan bahwa arah bahasa linier pada *output* hanyalah sebuah gejala, dan sebaliknya mengidentifikasi kegagalan tersebut pada divergensi lintasan *forward-path* dari *hidden state* *end-of-sequence*.

2608.30725.title: Where Do Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders Fail on Low-Resource Languages?

2608.30754.abstract: Evaluating creativity in large language model (LLM) outputs remains challenging because creativity is multidimensional and human-centered. We examine how reliably LLMs evaluate short literary text in Persian, a low-resource language, across multiple evaluation strategies and prompt formulations. We find that LLM-human agreement varies substantially across dimensions: alignment is stronger for structured TTCT-derived properties such as Originality, Fluency, and Elaboration, but considerably weaker for more subjective dimensions, particularly Emotion and Attractiveness. Judgments are also sensitive to prompt formulation, while few-shot prompting, ensembling, and multi-agent debate provide no consistent improvement. Motivated by this dimension-dependent behavior, we investigate whether structured creativity dimensions can instead be approximated using simple, interpretable proxy metrics. We introduce CLIN, which evaluates three TTCT-derived dimensions separately using topic-aware novelty for Originality, contextual lexical clustering for Fluency, and lexical diversity for Elaboration. These proxies achieve human alignment comparable to or better than the strongest zero-shot LLM judge in our setting while requiring substantially lower evaluation cost.
2608.30754.title: CLIN: an Objective Framework for Evaluating Creativity in Short Persian Literary Text

2608.30866.abstract: Building language technologies and conducting NLP research for low-resource languages---particularly when led by native speakers or involving participatory research practices---are often framed as means of addressing inequality, serving local communities, and, at times, contributing to *decolonisation*. In this paper, we examine recently published NLP and ML papers, focusing on the narratives used to characterise multilinguality, low-resource languages, and underrepresented cultures. We propose a framework for analysing research framings and identify recurring rhetorical patterns that may hinder accountability and constrain equitable knowledge production for---and by---underserved communities. We further assess the evidential basis of assertions regarding community benefit and find that such statements are often weakly supported or left unsubstantiated. Although community ownership and participation are frequently presented as key objectives, our analysis, supported by statistics from the ACL Anthology, suggests that research outputs more often prioritise resource creation and benchmarking---important but distinct goals---over evidence of broader structural change. We conclude by offering practical recommendations to help authors, reviewers, and readers critically assess these assertions and avoid potentially misleading framings.

glossary.explanation_id: *Citation chaining* adalah metode perluasan pencarian literatur dengan menelusuri daftar pustaka dari makalah yang sudah ditemukan.
*Epistemic narratives* adalah bentuk narasi dalam penelitian yang berkaitan dengan bagaimana pengetahuan dan klaim ilmiah dibentuk serta dibenarkan.
Pendekatan *tech-solutionist* mengasumsikan bahwa masalah sosial yang kompleks dapat diselesaikan secara eksklusif melalui intervensi teknologi.
*Saviourism* dalam penelitian merujuk pada narasi yang memposisikan peneliti atau teknologi sebagai penyelamat bagi kelompok yang dianggap tertindas.
Bahasa *low-resource* adalah bahasa yang memiliki sedikit ketersediaan data digital, korpus teks, atau alat pemrosesan bahasa alami.
Penelitian *multilingual* melibatkan penggunaan atau pemrosesan berbagai bahasa secara bersamaan dalam suatu sistem.

background.en: Building language technologies and conducting NLP research for low-resource languages are frequently framed as addressing inequality, serving local communities, and contributing to decolonisation. However, such research narratives can sometimes create normative expectations and moral imperatives that exceed what the technical contributions and available empirical evidence can establish. This gap highlights the need for greater accountability and clearer alignment between technical contributions and claimed societal outcomes.
background.id: Pembangunan teknologi bahasa dan pelaksanaan penelitian NLP untuk bahasa *low-resource* sering kali dibingkai sebagai upaya mengatasi ketimpangan, melayani komunitas lokal, dan berkontribusi pada dekolonisasi. Namun, narasi penelitian semacam itu terkadang dapat menciptakan ekspektasi normatif dan imperatif moral yang melampaui apa yang dapat dibuktikan oleh kontribusi teknis dan bukti empiris yang tersedia. Kesenjangan ini menyoroti perlunya akuntabilitas yang lebih besar dan penyelarasasan yang lebih jelas antara kontribusi teknis dan klaim hasil sosial.

contributions.en: The paper contributes an analytical framework grounded in epistemic elements to examine the relationship between research goals, methods, stakeholders, and anticipated outcomes in multilingual and low-resource NLP. By analysing 100 selected papers and ACL Anthology statistics, the authors identify recurring rhetorical patterns, assess the evidential basis of community benefit assertions, and examine authorship trends such as the rise of multi-author papers. Finally, the authors provide a practical checklist for stakeholders to critically evaluate research framings, evidentiary support, and implicit premises.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyumbangkan kerangka kerja analitis yang didasarkan pada elemen-elemen epistemik untuk memeriksa hubungan antara tujuan penelitian, metode, pemangku kepentingan, dan hasil yang diantisipasi dalam NLP *multilingual* dan *low-resource*. Dengan menganalisis 100 makalah terpilih dan statistik *ACL Anthology*, para penulis mengidentifikasi pola retoris yang berulang, menilai dasar bukti dari pernyataan manfaat komunitas, serta memeriksa tren kepenulisan seperti peningkatan makalah dengan banyak penulis. Terakhir, para penulis menyediakan daftar periksa praktis bagi pemangku kepentingan untuk mengevaluasi secara kritis kerangka penelitian, dukungan bukti, dan premis implisit.

future_work.en: The paper does not explicitly detail a dedicated future work section, though the authors state limitations regarding their sample size of 100 papers, their primary focus on abstracts and introductions, and the exclusion of direct author engagement.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak merinci secara eksplisit bagian khusus untuk pekerjaan masa depan, meskipun para penulis menyatakan keterbatasan terkait ukuran sampel mereka yang hanya 100 makalah, fokus utama pada bagian *abstract* dan *introduction*, serta pengecualian keterlibatan penulis secara langsung.

method.en: The study selects 100 papers addressing multilinguality and low-resource languages through citation chaining, prominent research consortia publications, and keyword-based searches of the ACL Anthology. The authors analyse abstracts and introductions to extract relevant quotations, identifying the means, ends, and evidential support for each paper. The annotation process is conducted in two rounds by two expert annotators using an iterative, multi-label scheme with greater than ninety percent agreement.
method.id: Studi ini memilih 100 makalah yang membahas keanekaragaman bahasa dan bahasa *low-resource* melalui pelacakan sitasi, publikasi konsorsium penelitian terkemuka, dan pencarian berbasis kata kunci di *ACL Anthology*. Para penulis menganalisis bagian *abstract* dan *introduction* untuk mengekstrak kutipan yang relevan, mengidentifikasi sarana, tujuan, dan dukungan bukti untuk setiap makalah. Proses anotasi dilakukan dalam dua putaran oleh dua annotator ahli menggunakan skema *multi-label* yang bersifat iteratif dengan tingkat kesepakatan lebih dari sembilan puluh persen.

related_work.en: Previous studies have investigated corporate influence in NLP and AI systems, responsible AI considerations in text summarization, and epistemic narratives in automated fact-checking and hate speech research. Other work has examined how democratisation is conceptualised in NLP and ML research, revealing limited engagement with established theories of democratisation despite frequent rhetorical invocation. Building on these analyses, the authors focus on identifying problematic narratives and research framings specifically in multilingual and low-resource NLP.
related_work.id: Studi-studi sebelumnya telah menyelidiki pengaruh korporasi dalam sistem NLP dan AI, pertimbangan AI yang bertanggung jawab dalam penelitian *summarization*, serta narasi epistemik dalam penelitian *fact-checking* otomatis dan ujaran kebencian. Pekerjaan lain telah meneliti bagaimana demokratisasi dikonseptualisasikan dalam penelitian NLP dan ML, yang mengungkapkan keterlibatan yang terbatas dengan teori-teori demokratisasi yang mapan meskipun sering kali dipanggil secara retoris. Berdasarkan analisis-analisis tersebut, para penulis berfokus pada identifikasi narasi bermasalah dan kerangka penelitian secara khusus dalam NLP *multilingual* dan *low-resource*.

results.en: The analysis reveals that 42% of the examined papers rely on perceived threats, anecdotal justifications, self-citations, or weakly connected claims regarding inequality reduction and community benefit. Furthermore, 11% of the articles make unsupported claims about decolonisation or saviourism, and 14% exhibit techno-solutionist narratives. When paired with high-resource papers for the same tasks, multilingual and low-resource papers more frequently invoke broad societal outcomes and tech-solutionist narratives despite having comparable technical contributions.
results.id: Analisis ini mengungkapkan bahwa 42% dari makalah yang diteliti mengandalkan ancaman yang dirasakan, pembenaran anekdotal, sitasi mandiri, atau klaim yang terhubung secara lemah mengenai pengurangan ketimpangan dan manfaat komunitas. Selain itu, 11% artikel membuat klaim yang tidak didukung tentang dekolonisasi atau penyelamatan (*saviourism*), dan 14% menunjukkan narasi yang berorientasi pada solusi teknis (*techno-solutionist*). Ketika dipasangkan dengan makalah *high-resource* untuk tugas yang sama, makalah *multilingual* dan *low-resource* lebih sering memunculkan hasil sosial yang luas dan narasi solusionis teknologi meskipun memiliki kontribusi teknis yang sebanding.

tldr.en: This paper examines research framings in multilingual and low-resource NLP papers to assess whether claimed societal benefits are supported by evidence. The authors find that broad claims of community benefit and social impact are frequently weakly substantiated, often prioritizing resource creation over structural change.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti kerangka penelitian dalam makalah NLP *multilingual* dan *low-resource* untuk menilai apakah manfaat sosial yang diklaim didukung oleh bukti. Para penulis menemukan bahwa klaim luas mengenai manfaat komunitas dan dampak sosial sering kali didukung secara lemah, serta kerap memprioritaskan pembuatan sumber daya daripada perubahan struktural.

2608.30866.title: Beyond Good Intentions: When Does the Framing of Multilingual and Low-Resource NLP Research Become a Caricature?

2609.00763.abstract: Hierarchical Knowledge graph (KG)-based retrieval augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful approach for supporting large language models with structured knowledge. However, there are primary challenges: (i) the lack of methods for automatic KG construction using ontology expansion for low-resource languages such as Vietnamese, (ii) the absence of systematic evaluation for knowledge retrieval strategies leveraging the hierarchical structures. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end pipeline for KG construction and retrieval strategies evaluation. In the KG construction, we employ a three-phase hybrid relation extraction pipeline: intra-batch deduplication via Union-Find, approximate cross-batch search, and LLM extraction with a centroid filter that reduces prompts combined with a five-step dual-LLM validator to prevent bloated ontology. A two-tier architecture consists of unmergeable structural nodes to preserve the document structure and mergeable content nodes. The retrieval evaluation consists of three graph traversal strategies: Top-Down, Horizontal, and Bottom-Up, which are evaluated on a synthetically generated benchmark of 1,210 Vietnamese queries from 109 subgraphs, categorized by five query directions. In this paper, we construct the tree knowledge graph from Vietnamese high school History textbooks (nearly 400 pages) to produce 750 nodes and 4,341 semantic edges with controlled ontology growth from 40 to 41 types. Among experimental graph traversal strategies, the Top-Down strategy with structure surpasses the vector baseline by 4.7 percentage points in NDCG@10. As a result, tree-structural information provides valuable information beyond flat cosine similarity but degrades performance when the query does not require structural context.
2609.00763.title: Automated Tree Knowledge Graph Construction using Ontology Expansion and Retrieval from Vietnamese History Textbooks

2609.00998.abstract: Word Sense Disambiguation has advanced rapidly for English and a handful of well-resourced modern languages, but it continues to assume the existence of a sense inventory and a word-to-sense mapping in the source language (Navigli, 2026). These assumptions break down for most historical and low-resource languages, whose dedicated WordNets are either incomplete or still under construction. We present Inspicio, an open-vocabulary retrieval pipeline that links tokens in context to synsets of the Open English WordNet (McCrae et al., 2020) without requiring any source-language inventory or mapping. For each occurrence, an instruction-tuned LLM produces two English translations of the surrounding sentence, a small set of candidate dictionary-style definitions, and a few candidate English lemmas. These outputs drive a hybrid retrieval step that combines dense definition-synset similarity, sparse lemma matching, and Maximal Marginal Relevance re-ranking. We evaluate the pipeline across a 6x6 grid of LLMs and sentence-embedding models on a new bilingual set of manually annotated Latin and Ancient Greek perception verbs, on a subset of PREMOVE dataset (Farina, 2025), and on a diachronic sample of Italian. The best configuration reaches 96% Recall@50 on the perception-verb test set, with each component contributing measurable gains, and remains competitive in the out-of-domain and cross-lingual settings.
2609.00998.title: Inspicio: Open-Vocabulary, LLM-Based Sense Retrieval for Historical Languages

2609.03273.abstract: Tamil spell and grammar correction is challenging because Tamil is an agglutinative low-resource language with rich verbal morphology, complex sandhi (phonetic transformation) rules at word boundaries, and a script of 247 distinct letters. Prior work targets word-level surface errors with rule-based methods, statistical n-gram models, Minimum Edit Distance, or hybrid pipelines with a transformer re-ranker; such methods cannot reliably handle contextual errors - subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, or cross-word sandhi - which require sentence-level understanding. We propose an end-to-end sequence-to-sequence formulation and fine-tune mT5-small and mBART-50 on a synthetic corpus of up to 657,720 noisy-clean Tamil sentence pairs spanning ten error categories. Both backbones follow the same four-stage progressive schedule, each stage targeting one weakness: surface noise (v2), contextual grammar (v3), single-site sandhi (v4), and multi-site cross-word sandhi (v5). On a 1,000-sentence balanced diagnostic set verified disjoint from all training data, our best model, mBART-50 v5, reaches 69.3% top-1 exact-match accuracy, with 87.5% on sandhi and 43.5% on subject-verb agreement. The schedule is what produces these gains: subject-verb accuracy rises from 1.0% to 52.5% once contextual pairs are introduced, and sandhi from 0% to 87.5% once multi-site sandhi pairs are. We additionally quantify a precision-recall trade-off this literature has not reported: sandhi recall is paid for monotonically in identity accuracy. Finally, Tamil-LLaMA-7B-Instruct reaches 19.0% zero-shot and 24.7% with three demonstrations against a 20.0% copy baseline, showing that a Tamil-adapted instruction model does not transfer to specialised sentence-level correction without task-specific supervision.
2609.03273.title: Contextual Tamil Spelling and Grammar Correction Using Progressively Fine-Tuned Sequence-to-Sequence Transformers

2609.03350.abstract: Pretraining data for Armenian, a morphologically rich and low-resource language, is scarce, and no open Armenian LLM has been released with the data and recipe needed to reproduce it. To address this gap, we curate and release two datasets. ArmWeb is an extensively validated corpus of 4.37M Armenian news documents. ArmSTEM is a parallel English-Armenian collection of 373K math and science problems with step-by-step solutions, translated into Armenian and verified through both answer-preserving LLM judgment and human evaluation. Continued pretraining of Gemma-4-E4B on these datasets yields arm-gemma-e4b, which outperforms every existing open Armenian model as well as its unadapted base, and is the first open Armenian LLM with complete training data and recipe. Our ablations show that news-only continued pretraining improves fluency while eroding knowledge, a pattern we also observe in existing Armenian models, and that a small share of verified translated STEM data reverses the loss. We further find that the largest public Armenian corpora overlap web-derived evaluation panels heavily, including a train/test self-overlap inside FineWeb-2. We openly release all data, models, and code.
2609.03350.comment: 18 pages, 4 figures, 13 tables. Data and model: https://huggingface.co/collections/COPA-AI/armenian-llm-ecosystem. Code: https://github.com/COPATeam/armenian_llm_ecosystem
2609.03350.title: From Zero to Hero: An Open LLM Ecosystem for Armenian

2609.03410.abstract: Idiomatic expressions are an integral part of natural language, reflecting cultural nuances and posing unique challenges for computational models, particularly in low-resource languages. In this paper, we present the first large-scale benchmark dataset of Bangla idioms, complemented by a synthetic multiple-choice question (MCQ) dataset for idiom meaning identification. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of recent large language models (LLMs) across three idiom-related tasks: paraphrasing, idiom span detection, and meaning identification, leveraging zero-shot and few-shot prompting strategies. Our results reveal substantial variability in model performance, with no single LLM consistently outperforming others across all tasks. Notably, Phi-4-mini-instruct excels in paraphrasing, Kimi-K2-32b-instruct in span detection, and Gemini-2.5-flash in meaning identification. We believe that our datasets and analyses will provide valuable resources to guide future research in improving LLM comprehension of idiomatic expressions, particularly in Bangla and other low-resource languages.
2609.03410.title: To What Extent Do Large Language Models Understand Bangla Idioms?

2609.03775.abstract: Typological features are widely used in multilingual NLP, and the prediction of such features holds downstream utility. However, existing methods to predict missing values lack interpretable justifications for predictions, while their performance across resource levels and feature types remains underexplored. Given LLMs' abilities in meta-linguistic reasoning and in providing rationales, we investigate LLMs' performance in typological feature prediction via an in-context learning approach with linguistic data from URIEL+ and Glottolog. We find that zero-shot prompting is insufficient, but when given phylogenetic and geographic neighbour evidence, LLMs substantially outperform all baselines without disadvantaging low-resource languages. We further find that most LLM rationales are consistent with the provided evidence, offering a step toward explainable typological feature prediction.
2609.03775.title: Typological Feature Prediction with Large Language Models: An In-Context Learning Approach

2609.04653.abstract: Multilingual large language models often struggle to reason in low- to mid-resource languages. Prior work has shown that translation can improve multilingual reasoning by helping models access stronger English-centric representations. This raises a central question: How much translation is needed for multilingual large language models to reason reliably, and when does more translation instead trigger interference and overconfidence? Using LLaMA and Qwen models, we run extensive experiments varying text scope and language mode (target-only, English-only, bilingual) to evaluate both accuracy and reliability. Our results reveal a clear trade-off: English context often improve understanding and recover errors caused by non-English comprehension, yet adding redundant bilingual context intensifies interference. We address this trade-off with Reliability-Aware Adaptive Inference (RAAI), a training-free test-time framework that (i) performs Expected Calibration Error (ECE)-aware routing and prompt fusion, and (ii) uses a mid-layer Risk Index (RI) to gate sequential reasoning, allocating compute only when it is likely to help and suppressing harmful bilingual redundancy. Across two model families, RAAI enhances accuracy by 25-37.7% on low-resource languages and lowers calibration error by approximately 3-6%, with the most pronounced benefits in the lowest-resource language tiers.
2609.04653.title: Choosing the Right Language Mode at Inference Time for Multilingual Reliability

2609.04823.abstract: Although automatic text simplification (ATS) is critical for accessibility, its progress has not matched the rapid evolution of broader natural language processing techniques. This paper investigates the application of reinforcement learning (RL) to improve the quality of ATS for low-resource languages using Large Language Models (LLMs). The paper introduces a novel reward function, designed to guide LLMs toward a targeted simplification style with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), that combines the SARI metric with specific penalty components. The effectiveness of GRPO with this reward function is motivated and demonstrated by post-training IberianLLM-7B-Instruct on the ASSET dataset. After post-training on the English ASSET, the model's ATS performance improves on two curated Catalan benchmarks while also successfully suppressing previously observed negative behaviors. Cross-lingual transfer learning is explored by translating ASSET into Catalan and Spanish and post-training the model on each version, but these fail to show a significant improvement on the out-of-domain benchmark.
2609.04823.comment: Accepted at CLEAR-TEXT 2026: Readability and text simplification workshop at the International Conference Computational Linguistics in Bulgaria (CLIB 2026)
2609.04823.title: Reinforcement Learning for improving Large Language Models' Catalan text simplification capabilities

2609.06212.abstract: LLMs have achieved remarkable capabilities in generating language teaching slides. However, a critical mismatch persists between visual polish and actual instructional effectiveness. To address this gap, we introduce SLATE (Slide-based Learning Assessment for Teaching Effectiveness), the first benchmark that evaluates AI-generated language teaching slides through instructional effectiveness and learner knowledge acquisition. SLATE transforms linguistics olympiad puzzles from low-resource languages with negligible web presence into 90 standardized instructional units comprising 1,133 assessable items, paired with a structured course outline and matched near- and far-transfer test sets. This pretest-posttest design eliminates pretrained knowledge leakage, ensuring gains reflect learning rather than prior recall. Using VLMs as scalable learner proxies and directionally supported by a three-system human pilot, our results show that content validity exhibits a weak association with learning gain, while pedagogical design exhibits a robust positive association. Moreover, most systems show a significant gap between near- and far-transfer accuracy, and even frontier models can produce negative learning gains. SLATE reveals a dissociation between artifact quality and instructional effectiveness, calling for a paradigm shift in how generative teaching systems are built, evaluated, and deployed.
2609.06212.title: SLATE: Are AI-Generated Slides Educationally Effective? A Benchmark for Language Teaching Quality and Learner Knowledge Acquisition

2609.06963.abstract: Natural language processing systems underperform on code-mixed text, particularly for low-resource language pairs. Turkish-English poses a further challenge: it lets English stems combine with Turkish suffixes to form single mixed-language tokens. We introduce TurEngMix, a corpus of 5.5K noisy, naturally occurring social media posts (486,974 tokens) rich in Turkish-English code-mixing. From this corpus, we construct a new Turkish-English benchmark for code-mixed language identification (LID) and named entity recognition (NER), comprising 15K expert-annotated tokens. Evaluating both decoder LLM and fine-tuned encoder baselines, we find that monolingual Turkish and English tokens are labeled reliably, but all models have high error rates on mixed-language tokens for both LID and NER. For morphologically integrated tokens, NER error rates were 5.2x and 6.3x higher for GPT-4o and Qwen, respectively. This highlights how morphological integration remains a challenge. We release the corpus, annotations, and code to support future computational and sociolinguistic research on Turkish-English code-mixing.
2609.06963.comment: Accepted to W-NUT 2026 (11th Workshop on Natural User-generated Text), co-located with EMNLP 2026. 15 pages, 4 figures, 12 tables

glossary.explanation_id: Penggunaan dua bahasa atau lebih dalam satu kalimat atau frasa yang sama oleh penutur bilingual.
Tugas komputasi untuk menentukan label bahasa dari setiap *token* atau teks yang diberikan.
Tugas *sequence labeling* untuk mendeteksi dan mengklasifikasikan entitas bernama ke dalam kategori yang telah ditentukan seperti orang, organisasi, atau lokasi.
Sistem pembentukan kata di mana imbuhan atau sufiks ditambahkan secara berurutan pada akar kata untuk mengekspresikan fungsi gramatikal.
Proses pemberian label pada setiap *token* individual dalam sebuah urutan teks.
Evaluasi model tanpa memberikan contoh demonstrasi sebelumnya di dalam *prompt*.

background.en: Natural language processing systems underperform on code-mixed text, especially for lower-resourced language pairs. Turkish-English code-mixing presents a distinct linguistic challenge due to Turkish agglutinative morphology, which allows English lexical stems to combine with complex Turkish suffix chains into single mixed-language tokens. Processing such morphologically integrated tokens is a crucial prerequisite for downstream tasks like language identification and named entity recognition, yet existing systems struggle significantly with them.
background.id: Sistem *natural language processing* berkinerja rendah pada teks *code-mixed*, terutama untuk pasangan bahasa *low-resource*. Pencampuran kode bahasa Turki-Inggris menghadirkan tantangan linguistik yang unik karena morfologi aglutinatif bahasa Turki, yang memungkinkan akar kata leksikal bahasa Inggris bergabung dengan rantai sufiks bahasa Turki yang kompleks menjadi satu *token* campuran. Memproses *token* yang terintegrasi secara morfologis ini merupakan prasyarat krusial untuk tugas hilir seperti *language identification* dan *named entity recognition*, namun sistem yang ada saat ini masih sangat kesulitan.

contributions.en: The paper makes three primary contributions to code-mixed NLP research. First, it introduces TurEngMix, a large-scale corpus of 5,549 naturally occurring social media posts rich in Turkish-English code-mixing. Second, it constructs an expert-annotated benchmark comprising 15,012 tokens for language identification and named entity recognition. Third, it provides a systematic baseline evaluation of both decoder-based large language models and fine-tuned encoder models, highlighting the specific failure modes associated with morphological integration.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memberikan tiga kontribusi utama bagi penelitian *code-mixed* NLP. Pertama, makalah ini memperkenalkan TurEngMix, sebuah *korpus* berskala besar yang terdiri dari 5.549 unggahan media sosial alami yang kaya akan pencampuran kode bahasa Turki-Inggris. Kedua, makalah ini membangun *benchmark* beranotasi ahli yang mencakup 15.012 *token* untuk *language identification* dan *named entity recognition*. Ketiga, makalah ini menyediakan evaluasi *baseline* yang sistematis dari *large language model* berbasis *decoder* dan *model encoder* yang telah di-*fine-tune*, serta menyoroti mode kegagalan spesifik yang terkait dengan integrasi morfologis.

future_work.en: The authors note limitations regarding domain specificity, as the corpus is derived exclusively from Ekşi Sözlük, and potential selection biases introduced by using GPT-4o during data filtering. They suggest that future research should expand into other online communities and conversational settings, while addressing morphological integration through specialized approaches such as sub-token language attribution or morphological preprocessing rather than relying on model scale alone.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat keterbatasan terkait spesifisitas domain, karena *korpus* diturunkan secara eksklusif dari Ekşi Sözlük, serta potensi bias seleksi yang diperkenalkan oleh penggunaan GPT-4o selama penyaringan data. Mereka menyarankan agar penelitian masa depan harus berkembang ke komunitas daring dan pengaturan percakapan lainnya, sambil mengatasi integrasi morfologis melalui pendekatan khusus seperti *sub-token language attribution* atau *preprocessing* morfologis daripada hanya mengandalkan skala model semata.

method.en: The authors collected 30,000 public posts from Ekşi Sözlük using a curated list of topic tags designed to surface code-mixing. A rigorous three-stage filtering pipeline combining langdetect and GPT-4o filtering yielded a final corpus of 5,549 posts. From this, a benchmark of 250 posts (15,012 tokens) was expert-annotated for language identification and named entity recognition following established frameworks. The evaluation framework tested decoder models under zero-shot and three-shot prompting alongside fine-tuned transformer encoders trained across multiple random seeds.
method.id: Para penulis mengumpulkan 30.000 unggahan publik dari Ekşi Sözlük menggunakan daftar *tag* topik terpilih yang dirancang untuk memunculkan pencampuran kode. Alur penyaringan tiga tahap yang ketat menggabungkan pustaka *langdetect* dan penyaringan GPT-4o menghasilkan *korpus* akhir sebanyak 5.549 unggahan. Dari sini, sebuah *benchmark* yang terdiri dari 250 unggahan (15.012 *token*) dianotasi oleh ahli untuk *language identification* dan *named entity recognition* mengikuti kerangka kerja yang mapan. Kerangka evaluasi menguji *model decoder* di bawah pengaturan *zero-shot* dan *three-shot prompting* berdampingan dengan *encoder transformer* yang telah di-*fine-tune* yang dilatih menggunakan beberapa *random seed*.

related_work.en: Most existing code-mixed resources are heavily concentrated on a small set of popular language pairs such as Spanish-English and Hindi-English, while morphologically distinct pairs like Turkish-English remain largely unexplored. Although recent benchmarks and evaluation datasets have begun to expand corpus coverage to underrepresented languages, resources for evaluating named entity recognition and language identification with mixed-language tokens on Turkish-English are extremely scarce, with only one prior small-scale dataset available in the literature.
related_work.id: Sebagian besar sumber daya *code-mixed* yang ada sangat terkonsentrasi pada sedikit pasangan bahasa populer seperti Spanyol-Inggris dan Hindi-Inggris, sementara pasangan bahasa yang secara morfologis berbeda seperti Turki-Inggris sebagian besar masih belum terjelajahi. Meskipun *benchmark* dan *dataset* evaluasi baru mulai memperluas cakupan korpus ke bahasa-bahasa yang kurang terwakili, sumber daya untuk mengevaluasi *named entity recognition* dan *language identification* dengan *token* campuran pada bahasa Turki-Inggris sangatlah langka, dengan hanya satu *dataset* skala kecil sebelumnya yang tersedia dalam literatur.

results.en: While models reliably label monolingual Turkish and English tokens, all evaluated models exhibit high error rates on mixed-language tokens and named entities. GPT-4o achieved a macro-F1 of 0.5238 for language identification and 0.6140 for named entity recognition under three-shot prompting, outperforming fine-tuned encoders and Qwen3-8B. Crucially, error analysis revealed that named entity recognition error rates on morphologically integrated tokens were 5.2 times and 6.3 times higher for GPT-4o and Qwen, demonstrating that morphological integration is the primary bottleneck.
results.id: Meskipun model dapat memberi label *token* bahasa Turki dan Inggris monolingual dengan andal, semua model yang dievaluasi menunjukkan tingkat kesalahan yang tinggi pada *token* campuran dan entitas bernama. GPT-4o mencapai *macro-F1* sebesar 0,5238 untuk *language identification* dan 0,6140 untuk *named entity recognition* di bawah *three-shot prompting*, mengungguli *encoder* yang telah di-*fine-tune* dan Qwen3-8B. Yang terpenting, analisis kesalahan mengungkapkan bahwa tingkat kesalahan *named entity recognition* pada *token* yang terintegrasi secara morfologis adalah 5,2 kali dan 6,3 kali lebih tinggi untuk GPT-4o dan Qwen, yang menunjukkan bahwa integrasi morfologis adalah hambatan utamanya.

tldr.en: This paper introduces TurEngMix, a corpus and benchmark for Turkish-English code-mixing covering language identification and named entity recognition. The evaluation reveals that morphological integration remains a significant challenge for both large language models and fine-tuned encoders.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan TurEngMix, sebuah *korpus* dan *benchmark* untuk pencampuran kode bahasa Turki-Inggris yang mencakup *language identification* dan *named entity recognition*. Evaluasi mengungkapkan bahwa integrasi morfologis tetap menjadi tantangan besar bagi *large language model* maupun *encoder* yang telah di-*fine-tune*.

2609.06963.title: TurEngMix: A Text Corpus and Benchmark for Turkish-English Code-Mixed Language Identification and Named Entity Recognition

2609.07470.abstract: Robot foundation models are trained and evaluated predominantly in English, and robot demonstration corpora do not exist for most languages. We study the addition of Greek to an open vision-language-action stack using only machine-rephrased instructions and no architecture changes. The main challenge is measurement rather than translation. Several plausible instruments produce false conclusions: a color-histogram metric rewards noise, a single-goal benchmark scores 84.6% under correct Greek and 82.6% under deliberately wrong instructions, training loss fails to predict Greek success, and single-run comparisons are dominated by seed variation. On a discriminative ninety-task suite with three seeds per arm, a multilingual text tower without Greek demonstrations remains at its wrong-instruction floor, while Greek-only training exceeds its control by at most 2.7 points. Bilingual training yields a consistent 6.7-7.1 point margin over its control and reaches about two fifths of English performance. The policy also overfits the translator's phrasing; training on seven phrasings per task approximately halves this penalty. Warm-starting from a language-adapted world model and unfreezing the text tower both degrade performance. The results support two practical requirements for low-resource robot-policy localization: build a guaranteed null before trusting a metric, and replicate low-resource-language results across seeds.
2609.07470.comment: 22 pages, 16 figures, 6 tables. Model and reproduction information: https://huggingface.co/KIEFERSA/Sophea-Nano-Policy-LIBERO-Greek-v1

glossary.explanation_id: Arsitektur model yang menggabungkan pemahaman visi dan bahasa untuk menghasilkan aksi kontrol robot.
Proses pelatihan lanjutan pada model praterlatih menggunakan dataset spesifik untuk tugas tertentu.
Kemampuan model untuk melakukan tugas tanpa pelatihan atau contoh eksplisit sebelumnya pada tugas tersebut.
Kumpulan tugas standar yang digunakan untuk mengukur dan membandingkan performa model.
Kategori bahasa atau domain yang memiliki ketersediaan data pelatihan sangat terbatas.
Komponen yang memecah teks masukan menjadi unit-unit token yang lebih kecil untuk diproses oleh model.
Inisialisasi pelatihan model menggunakan bobot dari model lain yang telah dilatih sebelumnya daripada dari awal.
Model atau metode referensi dasar yang digunakan untuk perbandingan performa metode baru.

background.en: Robot foundation models and demonstration corpora are predominantly trained and evaluated in English, creating a barrier for speakers of other languages. Collecting target-language robot data by hand is expensive and time-consuming. This paper addresses the gap by testing whether machine-translated instructions can transfer language understanding to an open vision-language-action policy without modifying its architecture.
background.id: Model dasar robot dan korpus demonstrasi sebagian besar dilatih dan dievaluasi dalam bahasa Inggris, yang menciptakan hambatan bagi penutur bahasa lain. Mengumpulkan data robot target secara manual sangat mahal dan memakan waktu. Makalah ini mengatasi kesenjangan tersebut dengan menguji apakah instruksi hasil terjemahan mesin dapat mentransfer pemahaman bahasa ke kebijakan *vision-language-action* terbuka tanpa memodifikasi arsitekturnya.

contributions.en: The main contributions include a rigorous methodological study on adding a low-resource language to a robot foundation policy using purely machine-translated data. The authors identify and expose several failure modes of common evaluation instruments, introduce a cross-lingual attribution control with a guaranteed null, and demonstrate that bilingual training significantly outperforms target-only training when properly evaluated across multiple seeds.
contributions.id: Kontribusi utama mencakup studi metodologis yang ketat tentang penambahan bahasa *low-resource* ke *policy* dasar robot menggunakan data yang murni diterjemahkan oleh mesin. Para penulis mengidentifikasi dan mengungkap beberapa mode kegagalan dari instrumen evaluasi umum, memperkenalkan *cross-lingual attribution control* dengan *null* yang dijamin, dan menunjukkan bahwa *bilingual training* mengungguli pelatihan target saja secara signifikan ketika dievaluasi dengan benar di berbagai *seed*.

future_work.en: The authors discuss limitations such as focusing on a single language, a single model family, and simulation-only environments. Future research directions include resolving the remaining entanglement between representational depth and tokenizer fragmentation, extending phrasing diversity approaches, and evaluating real-robot deployment once suitable scoring proxies are established.
future_work.id: Para penulis mendiskusikan keterbatasan seperti fokus pada satu bahasa, satu keluarga model, dan lingkungan simulasi saja. Arah penelitian masa depan meliputi penyelesaian keterikatan yang tersisa antara kedalaman representasi dan fragmentasi *tokenizer*, memperluas pendekatan keragaman frasa, dan mengevaluasi penerapan robot nyata setelah proksi penilaian yang sesuai dibuat.

method.en: The study utilizes the Cosmos3 stack, employing an 8B multilingual text tower and action adapters. The training corpus incorporates machine-translated Greek instructions from DROID and LIBERO datasets using an LLM pipeline with a mandated glossary. Evaluation is conducted using closed-loop simulation in the LIBERO environment. To ensure robust evaluation, the authors implement rigorous controls, including wrong-instruction baselines, multi-goal discriminative suites, and multi-seed replication.
method.id: Studi ini menggunakan *stack* Cosmos3, dengan memanfaatkan *text tower* multilingual 8B dan *adapter* aksi. Korpus pelatihan menggabungkan instruksi bahasa Yunani terjemahan mesin dari dataset DROID dan LIBERO menggunakan *pipeline* LLM dengan glosarium mandatori. Evaluasi dilakukan menggunakan simulasi *closed-loop* di lingkungan LIBERO. Untuk memastikan evaluasi yang andal, para penulis menerapkan kontrol yang ketat, termasuk *baseline* instruksi salah, rangkaian diskriminatif multi-tujuan, dan replikasi multi-*seed*.

related_work.en: Prior research shows that multimodal agents often score well on benchmarks without actually utilizing their modalities, such as relying on image-blind question priors in VQA or ignoring language instructions entirely in vision-language-action suites. Other related areas include zero-shot cross-lingual transfer from multilingual encoders, the impact of fine-tuning on pretrained representations, and the use of video-generative pretrained world models as policy initializers. The authors build upon these findings while highlighting the limitations of standard evaluation benchmarks.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya menunjukkan bahwa agen multimodal sering kali mendapat skor bagus pada *benchmark* tanpa benar-benar memanfaatkan modalitas mereka, seperti mengandalkan *prior* pertanyaan yang buta gambar dalam VQA atau mengabaikan instruksi bahasa sepenuhnya pada rangkaian *vision-language-action*. Bidang terkait lainnya mencakup transfer lintas bahasa *zero-shot* dari *encoder* multilingual, dampak *fine-tuning* pada representasi terlatih, dan penggunaan *world model* praterlatih generatif video sebagai penginisialisasi *policy*. Para penulis membangun temuan-temuan ini sekaligus menyoroti keterbatasan *benchmark* evaluasi standar.

results.en: Standard metrics and single-goal suites often produce false positives, such as color-histogram metrics rewarding noise and single-goal benchmarks scoring high under wrong instructions. However, on a discriminative ninety-task suite across multiple seeds, bilingual training achieves a stable margin of 6.7 to 7.1 points over its wrong-instruction floor, whereas target-only training shows minimal progress. Furthermore, warm-starting from a language-adapted world model or unfreezing the text tower both degrade performance, and training loss fails to predict instruction-following success.
results.id: Metrik standar dan rangkaian satu tujuan sering kali menghasilkan positif palsu, seperti metrik *color-histogram* yang memberi penghargaan pada derau dan *benchmark* satu tujuan yang mendapat skor tinggi di bawah instruksi yang salah. Namun, pada rangkaian sembilan puluh tugas diskriminatif di beberapa *seed*, *bilingual training* mencapai margin stabil 6.7 hingga 7.1 poin di atas batas instruksi salahnya, sedangkan pelatihan target saja menunjukkan kemajuan minimal. Selain itu, *warm-starting* dari *world model* yang diadaptasi bahasa atau melepas pembekuan *text tower* sama-sama menurunkan performa, dan *training loss* gagal memprediksi kesuksesan pemahaman instruksi.

tldr.en: This paper investigates adding Greek instructions to a vision-language-action model for robot control using machine translation. The study finds that reliable measurement requires careful controls, and bilingual training combined with demonstration data is necessary for successful language transfer.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti penambahan instruksi bahasa Yunani ke model *vision-language-action* untuk kontrol robot menggunakan terjemahan mesin. Studi ini menemukan bahwa pengukuran yang andal memerlukan kontrol yang cermat, dan *bilingual training* yang dikombinasikan dengan data demonstrasi sangat diperlukan untuk transfer bahasa yang sukses.

2609.07470.title: Measuring Language Transfer in Robot Policies: Adding Greek to a Cosmos3 Vision-Language-Action Policy

2609.07699.abstract: Curating Web corpora for regional language variants like European Portuguese (PT-PT) is heavily bottlenecked by dialectal overlap (mainly with PT-BR) and data processing scale. This paper presents an efficient pipeline to curate a production-ready PT-PT corpus from the Portuguese Web, spanning 411 TB of raw data from Arquivo.pt. We introduce a novel post-scraping block that removes boilerplate and line duplicates prior to filtering. This early-stage intervention increases final document yield by 19.04% by rescuing valid text that standard heuristic filters prematurely discard. Integrated with rigorous language identification, weighted fuzzy deduplication, and neural quality classification, our pipeline offers a scalable framework and a clean, representative corpus optimized for LLM pre-training.
2609.07699.title: Fine PT-PT Web: A High-Quality 41 Billion Tokens Data Collection of the European Portuguese Web

2609.08029.abstract: Vision Language Models have achieved strong performance on multimodal benchmarks, yet their ability to reason about culturally grounded and metaphor-rich content remains insufficiently studied. Internet memes present a challenging setting where meaning emerges from implicit interactions between image, overlaid text, sarcasm, and shared socio-cultural knowledge rather than literal visual recognition. This challenge is amplified in low-resource languages such as Bangla, where code-mixing, stylized scripts, and culturally specific symbolism introduce substantial distribution shift. In this work, we introduce BanglaMemeX, a culturally grounded multimodal benchmark comprising 3,000 Bangla memes annotated with multi-dimensional labels (humor, sarcasm, offensiveness, motivational intent, and overall sentiment) and human-written explanations that explicitly describe textual and visual metaphors. We systematically evaluate modern VLMs on both classification and explanation generation, revealing that current models struggle to interpret implicit cultural cues despite reasonable surface-level accuracy. Our results highlight the need for culturally-aware multimodal systems capable of grounded reasoning under linguistic and cultural distribution shift.
2609.08029.comment: Accepted at EMNLP 2026 Findings - 37 pages, 17 figures, 19 tables, including appendices
2609.08029.title: BanglaMemeX: Advancing Cultural Metaphoric Image Interpretation in Bangla with a Multimodal Explainable Dataset

2609.08105.abstract: The Indonesian Digital Library of Culture (Perpustakaan Digital Budaya Indonesia, PDBI; budaya-indonesia.org) is a participatory platform that has collected tens of thousands of entries on Nusantara cultural heritage through public contribution since 2007. Manual contribution faces three structural barriers: coverage (knowledge is scattered across languages and sites), integrity (open sources mix authentic documentation with noise), and completeness (subjects are recorded but their data remain shallow). This paper presents a methodological framework for autonomous, AI-based harvesting of cultural knowledge from the open web, designed to expand corpus coverage while intensifying per-entry data depth. The methodology is organised as a five-stage economic funnel: focused crawling, multilingual extraction and canonicalisation, vector encoding with blocking, agentic decision-making, and idempotent publication, under the principle of deterministic orchestration, agentic decisions. Each stage is formalised: funnel economics and optimal filter ordering; crawl-frontier dynamics as a subcritical branching process that explains the necessity of recurrent re-seeding; fact-level novelty via a containment measure; Bayesian multi-source evidence fusion with elevated publication thresholds for sacred categories; exactly-once effects via idempotent upserts and the transactional outbox; sliding-window inference budgeting with a reservation protocol; statistical quality auditing; and seed selection as submodular coverage maximisation. The framework retains four high-value human roles: curator of direction, escalation approver, quality auditor, and guardian of meaning, while machine autonomy is raised in stages. Ethical, legal, and cultural-sensitivity implications are discussed, including the architectural guarantee that the machine never overwrites human contributions.

glossary.explanation_id: Teknik *crawling* web yang berfokus pada pengumpulan halaman web yang relevan dengan topik tertentu menggunakan *frontier* berprioritas.
Batasan skema data di mana setiap fakta yang diekstrak harus menyertakan referensi sumber yang valid agar dapat direpresentasikan dalam korpus.
Sifat operasi yang menghasilkan status akhir yang sama meskipun dieksekusi beberapa kali secara berulang.
Model probabilitas stokastik yang digunakan untuk merepresentasikan dinamika pertumbuhan dan kepunahan tautan pada *crawl frontier*.
Sifat fungsi himpunan yang menunjukkan pengembalian yang semakin berkurang (*diminishing returns*), diterapkan di sini untuk pemilihan *seed*.
Pola desain perangkat lunak yang mencegah kegagalan sistem berulang dengan mendeteksi kesalahan dan gagal cepat sebelum memanggil layanan eksternal.

background.en:
The documentation of intangible cultural heritage is a vital prerequisite for safeguarding traditions. In Indonesia, the Indonesian Digital Library of Culture serves as a participatory platform that has collected tens of thousands of entries since 2007. However, the manual collection model faces three structural barriers: coverage, as knowledge is scattered across various languages and websites; integrity, because open sources mix authentic documentation with noise; and completeness, as many recorded subjects remain shallow in data depth.

To address these limitations, the paper proposes an autonomous knowledge harvesting system that continuously discovers cultural knowledge artefacts from the open web in any language. The system distils these findings into source-bound canonical records in Indonesian, tests their data-level novelty, and publishes them while maintaining architectural guarantees of quality, traceability, and human contribution sovereignty.
background.id:
Dokumentasi warisan budaya takbenda adalah prasyarat penting untuk pelindungan tradisi. Di Indonesia, Perpustakaan Digital Budaya Indonesia berfungsi sebagai platform partisipatif yang telah mengumpulkan puluhan ribu entri sejak tahun 2007. Namun, model pengumpulan manual menghadapi tiga hambatan struktural: cakupan, karena pengetahuan tersebar di berbagai bahasa dan situs web; integritas, karena sumber terbuka mencampur dokumentasi otentik dengan kebisingan; dan kelengkapan, karena banyak subjek yang tercatat masih dangkal dalam kedalaman data.

Untuk mengatasi keterbatasan ini, makalah ini mengusulkan sistem panen pengetahuan otonom yang secara terus-menerus menemukan artefak pengetahuan budaya dari web terbuka dalam bahasa apa pun. Sistem ini menyuling temuan tersebut menjadi catatan kanonik terikat sumber dalam bahasa Indonesia, menguji kebaruan tingkat data mereka, dan mempublikasikannya sambil mempertahankan jaminan arsitektural atas kualitas, keterlacakan, dan kedaulatan kontribusi manusia.

contributions.en:
The primary contributions of this paper include a five-stage economic funnel architecture that renders national-scale harvesting affordable by placing expensive reasoning behind strong filters. Furthermore, it provides a complete mathematical formalization of every pipeline stage, covering frontier dynamics as a branching process, Bayesian evidence fusion with graded thresholds for sacred categories, and submodular seed selection.

Additional contributions encompass exactly-once reliability semantics combined with inference-budget control to guarantee operational sustainability, and a staged autonomy governance protocol supported by statistical quality auditing and defined human roles. The architecture guarantees that machine automation never overwrites human contributions.
contributions.id:
Kontribusi utama dari makalah ini mencakup arsitektur *funnel* ekonomi lima tahap yang membuat pemanenan berskala nasional terjangkau dengan menempatkan penalaran mahal di belakang filter yang kuat. Selain itu, makalah ini menyediakan formalisasi matematika yang lengkap dari setiap tahap *pipeline*, mencakup dinamika *frontier* sebagai proses percabangan, *Bayesian evidence fusion* dengan ambang batas bergradasi untuk kategori sakral, dan pemilihan *seed* submodul.

Kontribusi tambahan mencakup semantik keandalan *exactly-once* yang dikombinasikan dengan kontrol *inference budget* untuk menjamin keberlanjutan operasional, serta protokol tata kelola otonomi bertahap yang didukung oleh audit kualitas statistik dan peran manusia yang ditentukan. Arsitektur ini menjamin bahwa otomatisasi mesin tidak pernah menimpa kontribusi manusia.

future_work.en:
The authors identify several limitations and future directions, including the fact that frontier extinction demands continuous seed curation, and that certain sources protected by anti-bot mechanisms remain unreachable. They note that the conditional-independence assumption in evidence fusion is violated when sources copy one another, making source-kinship estimation a goal for future work.

Furthermore, cross-lingual canonicalisation quality depends heavily on the underlying language models and requires dedicated evaluation for regional languages with non-script Latin characters. Finally, closing the audit-label loop to train the learned similarity encoder is highlighted as a necessary step for future system deployment.
future_work.id:
Para penulis mengidentifikasi beberapa keterbatasan dan arah masa depan, termasuk fakta bahwa kepunahan *frontier* menuntut kurasi *seed* yang berkelanjutan, dan bahwa sumber tertentu yang dilindungi oleh mekanisme anti-bot tetap tidak dapat dijangkau. Mereka mencatat bahwa asumsi independensi bersyarat dalam *evidence fusion* dilanggar ketika sumber saling menyalin, menjadikan estimasi kekerabatan sumber sebagai tujuan untuk pekerjaan di masa depan.

Selain itu, kualitas kanonisasi lintas bahasa sangat bergantung pada *model bahasa* yang mendasarinya dan memerlukan evaluasi khusus untuk bahasa regional dengan karakter non-latin. Terakhir, menutup lingkaran *audit-label* untuk melatih *similarity encoder* yang dipelajari disorot sebagai langkah yang diperlukan untuk penerapan sistem di masa depan.

method.en:
