Retrieved contexts are then fed into generative models, specifically LLaMA3-ChatQA 8B for English and LLaMA 3.1 8B for Urdu, to synthesize the final answers. The evaluation setup uses SQuAD 2.0 and UQA, measuring performance via automatic lexical and semantic metrics as well as LLM-as-judge scoring.
method.id:
Kerangka kerja DR-RAG yang diusulkan mengindeks setiap dokumen dua kali: sebagai *chunk* teks yang tumpang tindih sebanyak 200 hingga 500 *token* menggunakan *recursive splitter*, dan sebagai pasangan pertanyaan-jawaban yang dihasilkan secara otomatis oleh *large language model* seperti LLaMA 2 7B untuk bahasa Inggris dan GPT-4o untuk bahasa Urdu. *Chunk* dan pasangan *QA* di-*embed* menggunakan *encoder* yang sesuai dengan bahasa seperti all-MiniLM-L6-v2 untuk bahasa Inggris dan multilingual-e5-large untuk bahasa Urdu, lalu disimpan dalam *database* vektor Qdrant.

Pada saat kueri, kueri yang masuk dicocokkan terlebih dahulu dengan indeks *QA* menggunakan *cosine similarity*. Jika kepercayaan kecocokan teratas jatuh di bawah ambang batas tau sama dengan 0,80, sistem beralih kembali ke *retrieval* berbasis *chunk*. Konteks yang diambil kemudian dimasukkan ke dalam model generatif, khususnya LLaMA3-ChatQA 8B untuk bahasa Inggris dan LLaMA 3.1 8B untuk bahasa Urdu, untuk menyintesis jawaban akhir. Pengaturan evaluasi menggunakan SQuAD 2.0 dan UQA, mengukur performa melalui metrik leksikal dan semantik otomatis serta penilaian *LLM-as-judge*.

related_work.en:
Prior work on Retrieval-Augmented Generation has explored hybrid retrieval combining sparse BM25 and dense vector search, modular architectures with query rewriting and reranking, and adaptive retrieval methods based on model uncertainty or reinforcement learning. Other studies have investigated multi-document reasoning, layered retrieval, and structured evaluation frameworks like RAGAS.

Despite this progress, virtually all RAG research has focused on English benchmarks. For Urdu, prior work includes the release of the UQA dataset and various multilingual models such as mBERT and XLM-R, as well as dedicated models like UrduLLaMA and Alif. However, these models still exhibit weaknesses in factual consistency, indicating that stronger generation capacity alone cannot compensate for retrieval-level failures.
related_work.id:
Penelitian terdahulu mengenai *retrieval-augmented generation* telah mengeksplorasi *hybrid retrieval* yang menggabungkan *sparse* BM25 dan *dense vector search*, arsitektur modular dengan *query rewriting* dan *reranking*, serta metode *retrieval* adaptif berdasarkan ketidakpastian model atau *reinforcement learning*. Studi lain telah menyelidiki penalaran multidokumen, *layered retrieval*, dan kerangka kerja *evaluasi* terstruktur seperti RAGAS.

Terlepas dari kemajuan ini, hampir seluruh penelitian *RAG* berfokus pada *benchmark* bahasa Inggris. Untuk bahasa Urdu, penelitian terdahulu mencakup rilis dataset UQA dan berbagai *model bahasa* multinasional seperti mBERT dan XLM-R, serta model khusus seperti UrduLLaMA dan Alif. Namun, model-model ini masih menunjukkan kelemahan dalam konsistensi faktual, yang mengindikasikan bahwa kapasitas *generation* yang lebih kuat saja tidak dapat mengkompensasi kegagalan pada tingkat *retrieval*.

results.en:
Evaluated on the Urdu UQA dataset, DR-RAG achieves substantial improvements over traditional RAG and LangChain MultiVector baselines, increasing METEOR by 38 times and ROUGE-1 by 140 percent, while reducing generation latency by 43 percent. LLM-as-judge scores confirm higher faithfulness, reaching 3.03 versus 1.93, and overall quality reaching 2.99 versus 2.21 compared to MultiVector.

In English SQuAD 2.0 evaluation, DR-RAG remains competitive across metrics, achieving the highest BERTScore while maintaining strong faithfulness. The authors interpret these findings as proof that representation-level alignment between queries and indexed content is the critical factor for reliable retrieval in underserved languages, rather than simply increasing model complexity.
results.id:
Dievaluasi pada dataset UQA bahasa Urdu, DR-RAG mencapai peningkatan substansial dibandingkan *baseline* *traditional RAG* dan *LangChain MultiVector*, meningkatkan METEOR sebesar 38 kali lipat dan ROUGE-1 sebesar 140 persen, sembari mengurangi latensi *generation* sebesar 43 persen. Skor *LLM-as-judge* mengonfirmasi *faithfulness* yang lebih tinggi, mencapai 3,03 berbanding 1,93, dan kualitas keseluruhan mencapai 2,99 berbanding 2,21 jika dibandingkan dengan *MultiVector*.

Dalam evaluasi SQuAD 2.0 bahasa Inggris, DR-RAG tetap kompetitif di berbagai metrik, mencapai *BERTScore* tertinggi sambil mempertahankan *faithfulness* yang kuat. Para penulis menginterpretasikan temuan ini sebagai bukti bahwa selarasnya tingkat representasi antara kueri dan konten terindeks adalah faktor krusial untuk *retrieval* yang andal pada bahasa yang kurang terlayani, alih-alih sekadar meningkatkan kompleksitas model.

tldr.en: This paper proposes DR-RAG, a dual-representation retrieval-augmented generation framework that uses both text chunks and generated question-answer pairs to address retrieval misalignment in morphologically complex low-resource languages. Evaluated on Urdu question answering, DR-RAG substantially improves lexical overlap metrics and generation latency while maintaining competitive English performance.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan DR-RAG, sebuah kerangka *retrieval-augmented generation* representasi ganda yang menggunakan *chunk* teks dan pasangan pertanyaan-jawaban yang dihasilkan untuk mengatasi ketidakselarasan temu kembali pada bahasa bersumber daya rendah yang kompleks secara morfologis. Dievaluasi pada *question answering* bahasa Urdu, DR-RAG secara substansial meningkatkan metrik irisan leksikal dan latensi *generation* sembari mempertahankan performa bahasa Inggris yang kompetitif.

acl:2026.chipsal-1.6.title: DR-RAG: Addressing Retrieval Misalignment in Low-Resource Urdu Question Answering
acl:2026.chipsal-1.6.venue: Proceedings of the Second workshop on Challenges in Processing South Asian Languages (CHiPSAL2026)

acl:2026.chipsal-1.7.abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is an important part of human–computer interaction, but most existing research focuses on high-resource languages, with very limited work on regional languages such as Punjabi. This paper focuses on detecting emotions from Punjabi speech using machine learning and deep learning techniques. We curated our own Punjabi speech emotion dataset using volunteer recordings and real-world sources, covering four emotion classes: angry, happy, sad, and neutral. The data was preprocessed for consistency and evaluated using a multi-strategy framework (E1–E4) to test domain generalization. Three models were evaluated: CNN, ResNet-34, and the transformer-based Wav2Vec 2.0. Among these, the ResNet-34 model performed the best in the combined-domain strategy (E4), achieving a test accuracy of 96%. While cross-corpus evaluations (E2, E3) highlighted challenges in generalizing to neutral emotions, the model achieved perfect scores for happy and sad classes in E4. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of residual networks and combined-domain training for emotion recognition in low-resource languages and highlight the potential for further work on Punjabi SER.
acl:2026.chipsal-1.7.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Second workshop on Challenges in Processing South Asian Languages (CHiPSAL2026)

glossary.explanation_id: Bidang komputasi yang bertujuan untuk mendeteksi status emosional manusia secara otomatis dari isyarat vokal.
Pengaturan evaluasi di mana model dilatih pada satu domain data dan diuji pada domain data yang berbeda untuk mengukur kemampuan generalisasi.
Kategori bahasa yang memiliki ketersediaan *dataset* dan sumber daya komputasi yang sangat terbatas.
Proses pelatihan lanjutan pada *pretrained model* menggunakan *dataset* target tertentu.
Model atau metode standar yang digunakan sebagai titik perbandingan untuk mengukur peningkatan performa model baru.
Kemampuan model untuk mengenali atau memproses data dari kelas atau domain tanpa pelatihan eksplisit sebelumnya.
Komponen yang memecah teks atau urutan data menjadi unit-unit yang lebih kecil seperti kata atau token.
Standar atau kumpulan data acuan yang digunakan untuk membandingkan performa berbagai model secara objektif.

background.en:
Speech Emotion Recognition is critical for human-computer interaction, mental health monitoring, and educational technologies, yet most research focuses on high-resource languages while regional languages like Punjabi remain underexplored. A major challenge in low-resource SER is the scarcity of diverse and naturalistic datasets, as existing corpora are often limited to studio-recorded speech that fails to reflect real-world acoustic variability.

To address this gap, the authors highlight the need for naturalistic datasets and systematic cross-domain evaluations to understand how acoustic domain mismatch and speaker variation impact model generalizability and robustness.
background.id:
*Speech Emotion Recognition* sangat krusial untuk interaksi manusia-komputer, pemantauan kesehatan mental, dan teknologi pendidikan, namun sebagian besar penelitian berfokus pada bahasa ber-*resource* tinggi sementara bahasa regional seperti Punjabi masih kurang dieksplorasi. Tantangan utama dalam *SER* *low-resource* adalah kelangkaan *dataset* yang beragam dan naturalistik, karena korpus yang ada sering kali terbatas pada rekaman studio yang gagal mencerminkan variabilitas akustik dunia nyata.

Untuk mengatasi kesenjangan ini, para penulis menyoroti pentingnya *dataset* naturalistik dan evaluasi *cross-domain* yang sistematis untuk memahami bagaimana ketidakcocokan domain akustik dan variasi penutur memengaruhi generalisasi serta ketahanan model.

contributions.en: The paper introduces a newly curated Punjabi speech emotion dataset comprising 893 labeled utterances from volunteer recordings and audiovisual media covering four emotion classes. Furthermore, it establishes the first systematic cross-domain evaluation framework for Punjabi SER through four experimental strategies, providing reproducible baselines and demonstrating the effectiveness of combined-domain training.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan *dataset* emosi ucapan bahasa Punjabi yang baru dikurasi yang terdiri dari 893 ujaran beranotasi dari rekaman sukarelawan dan media audiovisual yang mencakup empat kelas emosi. Selain itu, makalah ini membangun kerangka evaluasi *cross-domain* sistematis pertama untuk *SER* bahasa Punjabi melalui empat strategi eksperimental, menyediakan *baseline* yang dapat direproduksi dan menunjukkan keefektifan pelatihan *combined-domain*.

future_work.en: The authors outline several future directions, including dialectal dataset expansion to cover Pakistani Punjabi audiovisual content, domain adaptation techniques for studio-to-naturalistic transfer, multilingual transfer learning across South Asian languages such as Hindi and Urdu, and extension to dimensional emotion recognition.
future_work.id: Para penulis menguraikan beberapa arah masa depan, termasuk ekspansi *dataset* dialek untuk mencakup konten audiovisual Punjabi Pakistan, teknik adaptasi domain untuk transfer dari studio ke naturalistik, *transfer learning* multilingual di seluruh bahasa Asia Selatan seperti Hindi dan Urdu, serta perluasan ke pengenalan emosi dimensional.

method.en: The study evaluates three model architectures: CNN-BiLSTM, ResNet-34, and Wav2Vec 2.0, utilizing a multi-representation feature extraction strategy combining MFCCs, chroma features, mel spectrograms, spectral contrast, and tonnetz features. Four experimental strategies are implemented to test in-domain performance (E1), cross-domain transfer from RASA to curated speech (E2), reverse transfer (E3), and combined-domain training (E4).
method.id: Studi ini mengevaluasi tiga arsitektur model: *CNN-BiLSTM*, *ResNet-34*, dan *Wav2Vec 2.0*, dengan menggunakan strategi ekstraksi fitur multi-representasi yang menggabungkan *MFCC*, fitur *chroma*, *mel spectrogram*, kontras spektral, dan fitur *tonnetz*. Empat strategi eksperimental diimplementasikan untuk menguji performa *in-domain* (E1), transfer *cross-domain* dari RASA ke ucapan terkurasi (E2), transfer terbalik (E3), dan pelatihan *combined-domain* (E4).

related_work.en: Prior research in Punjabi SER includes early work using classical feature engineering with classifiers like Random Forest, and subsequent studies applying convolutional neural networks on larger film and web corpora, as well as released datasets like PEMO. However, these earlier studies are limited by lack of public accessibility for reproducibility, reliance on acted studio speech, and an exclusive focus on in-domain evaluation without testing model robustness under domain shift.
related_work.id: Penelitian terdahulu dalam *SER* bahasa Punjabi mencakup karya awal yang menggunakan *feature engineering* klasik dengan pengklasifikasi seperti *Random Forest*, serta studi lanjutan yang menerapkan *convolutional neural network* pada korpus film dan web yang lebih besar, di samping *dataset* yang dirilis seperti PEMO. Namun, studi-studi terdahulu ini dibatasi oleh kurangnya aksesibilitas publik untuk reproduktifitas, ketergantungan pada ucapan studio yang diperankan, dan fokus eksklusif pada evaluasi *in-domain* tanpa menguji ketahanan model di bawah pergeseran domain.

results.en: In the in-domain setting (E1), Wav2Vec 2.0 and ResNet-34 achieved high macro accuracies of 92.48% and 92.00%, respectively. However, cross-domain evaluations (E2, E3) revealed severe performance degradation due to acoustic mismatch and class imbalance priors. Combined-domain training (E4) successfully recovered performance, with ResNet-34 achieving a peak test accuracy of 96% and demonstrating that training on heterogeneous data mitigates domain shift.
results.id: Dalam pengaturan *in-domain* (E1), *Wav2Vec 2.0* dan *ResNet-34* masing-masing mencapai akurasi makro yang tinggi yaitu 92.48% dan 92.00%. Namun, evaluasi *cross-domain* (E2, E3) mengungkapkan penurunan performa yang parah karena ketidakcocokan akustik dan prior ketidakseimbangan kelas. Pelatihan *combined-domain* (E4) berhasil memulihkan performa, dengan *ResNet-34* mencapai akurasi pengujian puncak 96% dan menunjukkan bahwa pelatihan pada data heterogen memitigasi pergeseran domain.

tldr.en: This paper presents a cross-domain evaluation of machine learning models for Punjabi Speech Emotion Recognition using a newly curated dataset. The results demonstrate that combined-domain training significantly improves model robustness across diverse acoustic conditions.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan evaluasi *cross-domain* dari model *machine learning* untuk *Speech Emotion Recognition* bahasa Punjabi menggunakan *dataset* yang baru dikurasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pelatihan *combined-domain* secara signifikan meningkatkan ketahanan model di berbagai kondisi akustik.

acl:2026.chipsal-1.7.title: Cross-Domain Evaluation of Transformer-Based Models for Punjabi Speech Emotion Recognition
acl:2026.chipsal-1.7.venue: Proceedings of the Second workshop on Challenges in Processing South Asian Languages (CHiPSAL2026)

acl:2026.chipsal-1.9.abstract: Despite the growing progress in Natural Language Inference (NLI) research, resources for the Bengali language remain extremely limited. Existing Bengali NLI datasets exhibit several inconsistencies, including annotation errors, ambiguous sentence pairs, and inadequate linguistic diversity, which hinder effective model training and evaluation. To address these limitations, we introduce BNLI, a refined and linguistically curated Bengali NLI dataset designed to support robust language understanding and inference modeling. The dataset was constructed through a rigorous annotation pipeline emphasizing semantic clarity and balance across entailment, contradiction, and neutrality classes. We benchmarked BNLI using a suite of state-of-the-art transformer-based architectures, including multilingual and Bengali-specific models, to assess their ability to capture complex semantic relations in Bengali text. The experimental findings highlight the improved reliability and interpretability achieved with BNLI, establishing it as a strong foundation for advancing research in Bengali and other low-resource language inference tasks. The link to the BNLI dataset: https://github.com/FarahHaque/BNLI-Dataset.git
acl:2026.chipsal-1.9.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Second workshop on Challenges in Processing South Asian Languages (CHiPSAL2026)

glossary.explanation_id: Tugas dalam *model bahasa* untuk menentukan apakah suatu hipotesis benar, salah, atau netral berdasarkan sebuah premis.
Metode untuk mengukur tingkat kemiripan makna antara dua teks atau kalimat.
Arsitektur *model bahasa* modern yang mengandalkan mekanisme *attention* untuk memproses data sekuensial.
Hasil atau *model* rujukan standar yang digunakan untuk membandingkan kinerja *model* baru.
Tahap pelatihan awal *model* pada korpus data teks skala besar sebelum dilakukan *fine-tuning*.

background.en: Natural Language Inference is a core task in natural language understanding, but resources for the Bengali language remain extremely limited. Existing Bengali datasets suffer from annotation errors, ambiguous sentence pairs, inadequate linguistic diversity, and inaccurate machine translations, which hinder effective model training and evaluation.
background.id: *Natural Language Inference* adalah tugas inti dalam pemahaman bahasa alami, namun sumber daya untuk bahasa Bengali masih sangat terbatas. Korpus bahasa Bengali yang ada menderita kesalahan anotasi, pasangan kalimat yang ambigu, keragaman linguistik yang tidak memadai, dan terjemahan mesin yang tidak akurat, yang menghambat pelatihan dan evaluasi *model* secara efektif.

contributions.en: The paper introduces BNLI, a refined and linguistically curated Bengali NLI dataset constructed through a rigorous multi-stage pipeline ensuring semantic clarity and balanced class representation. It provides comprehensive benchmark evaluations using multiple transformer-based architectures to establish reliable baselines for future research.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan BNLI, *dataset* NLI Bengali yang dimurnikan dan dikurasi secara linguistik yang dibangun melalui *pipeline* multi-tahap yang ketat untuk memastikan kejelasan semantik dan representasi kelas yang seimbang. Makalah ini menyediakan evaluasi *benchmark* komprehensif menggunakan berbagai arsitektur berbasis *transformer* untuk menetapkan *baseline* yang andal bagi penelitian masa depan.

future_work.en: A key future direction is the development of a Bengali foundation model leveraging this dataset for large-scale pretraining and downstream reasoning tasks. The dataset also supports applications in natural language inference and can be utilized to train LLMs for meaningful sentence generation in Bengali.
future_work.id: Arah masa depan yang utama adalah pengembangan *foundation model* bahasa Bengali dengan memanfaatkan *dataset* ini untuk *pre-training* skala besar dan tugas penalaran hilir. *Dataset* ini juga mendukung aplikasi dalam *natural language inference* dan dapat digunakan untuk melatih *large language model* untuk pembuatan kalimat yang bermakna dalam bahasa Bengali.

method.en: The dataset was constructed in three stages: selecting premises from the SNLI corpus and translating them into Bengali, having 60 native students compose corresponding hypotheses using premise-scene descriptions, and performing validation using Semantic Textual Similarity analysis and human review by five linguists. The authors benchmarked BNLI using various models including LSTM, BERT, BanglaBERT, RoBERTa, MultiBERT, and LLaMA-2.
method.id: *Dataset* dibangun dalam tiga tahap: memilih premis dari korpus SNLI dan menerjemahkannya ke dalam bahasa Bengali, meminta 60 mahasiswa penutur asli menyusun hipotesis menggunakan deskripsi adegan premis, dan melakukan validasi menggunakan analisis *Semantic Textual Similarity* serta tinjauan manusia oleh lima ahli linguistik. Para penulis menguji *benchmark* BNLI menggunakan berbagai *model* termasuk LSTM, BERT, BanglaBERT, RoBERTa, MultiBERT, dan LLaMA-2.

related_work.en: Major NLI datasets exist for high-resource languages such as English, Arabic, and Chinese, alongside multilingual benchmarks like XNLI and INDICXNLI. In contrast, prior Bengali NLI datasets are typically small in scale or derived from machine-translated English benchmarks, and they suffer from semantic inconsistencies, mistranslations, and incorrect entailment labeling.
related_work.id: *Dataset* NLI utama ada untuk bahasa berpenghormatan tinggi seperti bahasa Inggris, Arab, dan Mandarin, di samping *benchmark* multibahasa seperti XNLI dan INDICXNLI. Sebaliknya, *dataset* NLI Bengali sebelumnya biasanya berskala kecil atau diturunkan dari *benchmark* bahasa Inggris hasil *terjemahan mesin*, serta menderita inkonsistensi semantik, salah terjemahan, dan pelabelan *entailment* yang salah.

results.en: Transformer-based models substantially outperform traditional LSTM architectures on the BNLI dataset. RoBERTa and BERT Base deliver strong results, while LLaMA-2 achieves the highest overall F1-score of 79.13 percent, demonstrating superior cross-lingual reasoning and robust generalization compared to other models.
results.id: *Model* berbasis *transformer* secara substansial mengungguli arsitektur LSTM tradisional pada *dataset* BNLI. RoBERTa dan BERT Base memberikan hasil yang kuat, sementara LLaMA-2 mencapai skor F1 keseluruhan tertinggi sebesar 79,13 persen, menunjukkan penalaran lintas bahasa yang unggul dan generalisasi yang tangguh dibandingkan *model* lain.

tldr.en: This paper introduces BNLI, a linguistically refined Bengali natural language inference dataset designed to address inconsistencies in prior resources. Experimental evaluations using state-of-the-art transformer models demonstrate improved reliability, with large language models achieving superior cross-lingual reasoning.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan BNLI, sebuah korpus *Natural Language Inference* bahasa Bengali yang dimurnikan secara linguistik untuk mengatasi inkonsistensi pada sumber daya sebelumnya. Evaluasi eksperimental menggunakan model *transformer* terkini menunjukkan keandalan yang lebih baik, dengan *large language model* mencapai penalaran lintas bahasa yang unggul.

acl:2026.chipsal-1.9.title: BNLI: A Linguistically-Refined Bengali Dataset for Natural Language Inference
acl:2026.chipsal-1.9.venue: Proceedings of the Second workshop on Challenges in Processing South Asian Languages (CHiPSAL2026)

acl:2026.computel-1.1.abstract: While machine learning approaches dominate contemporary NLP research, a critical gap exists between published models and tools actually used by target communities (Gessler & von der Wense, 2024). This paper presents two morphological parsers for Media Lengua (ISO 639-3: mue), an endangered mixed language of Ecuador, demonstrating that a JavaScript rule-based system (98.6% accuracy) can outperform a CRF model (95.7% F1) while offering immediate community accessibility.Not all language structures permit straightforward rule-based parsing; however, when a language’s morphology allows for this approach with competitive accuracy, we argue that it should be preferred for its practical advantages: immediate browser-based deployment, transparency, zero infrastructure requirements, and long-term maintainability. Our rule-based parser runs entirely in the browser, is freely available online, and can be adapted to other Quechuan languages. In contrast, while the CRF model performs well on benchmarks, it requires additional infrastructure to become accessible.Our comparison highlights the need to evaluate NLP tools not only on accuracy metrics but also on accessibility and real-world adoption, which is particularly crucial for endangered language communities where sustainable, community-accessible tools can support language documentation, education, and revitalization.
acl:2026.computel-1.1.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.1.title: Morphological Parsing for Media Lengua: When Accessibility Matters More Than State-of-the-Art
acl:2026.computel-1.1.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.10.abstract: The use of ASR models in endangered language documentation has grown in popularity given the bottleneck of manual speech transcription. Meta’s Massively Multilingual Speech (MMS) model is particularly popular for its extensibility to low-resource languages. However, it is mostly trained on read speech data from the Bible, meaning it may not perform well on other domains. We evaluated this model on data collected as part of a larger language documentation and revitalization project focused on Akuzipik, a polysynthetic Alaska Native language. We also finetuned and evaluated the model on a small (1h) collection of speech. The original model performed well on a dataset that roughly matched the Bible training data in domain and writing style but struggled on a separate collection of spontaneous speech. Performance on spontaneous speech improved after finetuning on a sample of our full dataset, and error rates reduced less dramatically after finetuning only on read speech. Both finetuning scenarios show promise for future model improvement, especially considering the relative ease of collecting read speech data. This experiment confirms the challenge of transcribing spontaneous speech with the MMS ASR model but provides hope for improving model performance for language documentation purposes, even with scarce data.
acl:2026.computel-1.10.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.10.title: Addressing Domain Mismatch in ASR for Akuzipik Language Documentation
acl:2026.computel-1.10.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.11.abstract: This paper investigates the challenges of low-resource machine translation for ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi (Hawaiian), a critically endangered Polynesian language. We compile a corpus of publicly available Hawaiian-English bitext and investigate the effectiveness of neural sequence-to-sequence models and large language models for translating Hawaiian. To address data scarcity, we employ various data augmentation techniques, including backtranslation, multilingual training using parallel corpora in related languages, and leveraging dictionary entries. Our experiments demonstrate that multilingual training significantly improves model performance, particularly when incorporating bitext from related Polynesian languages. Fine-tuned large language models were not able to outperform mBART, highlighting that smaller and simpler models are still relevant, especially in low-resource scenarios.
acl:2026.computel-1.11.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.11.title: Low-Resource Methods for Hawaiian Machine Translation
acl:2026.computel-1.11.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.13.abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) has made significant progress in recent years, largely driven by large-scale pretrained models and vast textual and multimodal corpora. However, these advances remain unevenly distributed, disproportionately benefiting high-resource languages while Indigenous and endangered languages—especially those employing diverse and less widely supported writing systems—remain underrepresented. This paper examines the role of writing system diversity in NLP, with a focus on Indigenous and endangered languages. We propose a theoretical framework that accounts for variation across writing systems and its implications for computational modeling. Specifically, we (i) provide an overview of writing system diversity, (ii) synthesize available computational resources, and (iii) present a structured analysis of challenges in modeling, tokenization, and evaluation.Our analysis shows that writing system diversity reveals structural biases embedded in current NLP pipelines. We conclude by identifying key open challenges and outlining directions for future research toward more inclusive, script-aware NLP approaches that better account for writing system variation.
acl:2026.computel-1.13.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.13.title: Indigenous Writing Systems Matter: Rethinking NLP beyond Alphabetic Bias through Script-Aware Modeling
acl:2026.computel-1.13.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.15.abstract: Despite decades of progress in human language technology (HLT) and growing research interest in endangered languages, practical uptake of HLT in documentary linguistics workflows remains rare. In this opinion piece, we report on a structured dialogue among approximately twenty academics convened to diagnose why this gap persists. Across all topics, we identify a recurring structural problem, which we call the missing middle: despite the existence of many potentially useful HLTs, the connective infrastructure necessary to make them genuinely accessible to linguists and language communities does not exist. We report the details of our discussion and make four specific recommendations for how those active in language documentation and HLT research might orient their future work.
acl:2026.computel-1.15.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.15.title: The Missing Middle: Language Documentation Needs Better Infrastructure, Not Better Models
acl:2026.computel-1.15.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.16.abstract: We investigate how training languages should be selected for cross-lingual IPA ASR on unseen languages. Using Common Voice audio and Vox Communis phonetic transcripts, we train multilingual IPA-based ASR models for Upper Sorbian, Luganda, and Tatar under three linguistically motivated selection strategies: genealogical relatedness, geographic proximity, and phonological inventory overlap. We compare these strategies to a random baseline and evaluate performance with phone error rate. Linguistically informed selection generally improves transfer, but no single strategy is consistently optimal. Geographic proximity performs best for Luganda, phonological overlap is slightly best for Tatar, and none of the proposed strategies outperform random selection for Upper Sorbian. The results suggest that linguistic similarity aids low-resource ASR transfer, but that the most useful dimension of similarity varies by target language.
acl:2026.computel-1.16.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.16.title: Aspects of Selecting the Right ASR Training Languages for Under-Resourced Languages
acl:2026.computel-1.16.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.17.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables ASR models to transcribe unseen languages by conditioning on a handful of audio-transcript pairs at inference time, with no fine-tuning. This is appealing for language documentation, where transcribed data is scarce and recording conditions vary across sessions. We evaluate ICL on Panãra (Northern Jê, Brazil), a language with a complex practical orthography in which diacritics encode phonemic contrasts, across seven fieldwork recordings varying in speaker, narrative, and recording context. We find substantial within-language variation in transcription accuracy unexplained by any single recording-level factor, and show that diacritics are a systematic bottleneck with pronounced differences across diacritic types. An orthographic manipulation experiment further shows that how diacritics are represented in context transcriptions substantially affects model performance. These results highlight orthographic complexity and recording-level variation as key practical challenges for ICL-assisted fieldwork transcription.
acl:2026.computel-1.17.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.17.title: Bottlenecks of In-Context Learning for Fieldwork ASR: A Case-study of Panãra
acl:2026.computel-1.17.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.18.abstract: This paper presents the development of an online multimodal corpus toolkit designed for data-driven language learning in Hawaiian. The toolkit supports corpus linguistics analyses including concordance/KWIC (Key Word In Context) searches, frequency analysis, collocation analyses, and complex queries with n-grams and regex pattern matching. Specifically designed for educators, students, and parents within the Hawaiian community, this easy-to-use tool facilitates a data-driven language learning process by enabling users to explore authentic language data, identify patterns, and develop deeper understanding of Hawaiian language structures through computational methods. By integrating corpus-based approaches into language education, this toolkit contributes significantly to preserving and promoting Hawaiian language learning and supports the broader community’s efforts in language revitalization.
acl:2026.computel-1.18.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.18.title: Developing A Hawaiian Corpus Toolkit for Data-Driven Language Learning
acl:2026.computel-1.18.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.19.abstract: Voice Activity Detection (VAD) is the first step in a workflow intended for the automated transcription of Indigenous and low-resource languages. However, VAD’s effectiveness when detecting voices in fieldwork settings remains untested. Fieldwork recordings have very different noise and interference conditions from the datasets that mainstream VAD models have been trained for, and so they might fail when confronted with this type of linguistic data. This paper tests different algorithms using data from two typologically distinct Indigenous languages: Bribri from Costa Rica and Cook Islands Māori from Polynesia. We compare energy-based methods (PyDub), GMM-based methods (WebRTC VAD), and two neural-network based methods (Silero and SpeechBrain) against human-annotated transcriptions. Our results indicate that hybrid architectures like that of SpeechBrain obtain the best results (89% accuracy for Bribri and 94% for Cook Islands Māori). However, no system performed well when tagging non-speech segments, which might indicate a bias towards marking the natural noise in a fieldwork setting as a false-positive for voice. With these findings we hope to inform the selection of VAD tools when implementing ASR workflows.
acl:2026.computel-1.19.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.19.title: Voice Activation Detection for Transcription of Indigenous Languages
acl:2026.computel-1.19.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.2.abstract: This paper gives an overview of our activities in developing automatic speech recognition (ASR) and text-to-speech (TTS) systems for the preservation and revitalization of the Ainu language, once spoken in the Hokkaido area of Japan, and listed as “severely endangered” of extinction. With a large pretrained model, a high-performing ASR system can be trained even with five hours of speech from a few speakers. It has been used to streamline the transcription and archiving of old recordings. A TTS system is also developed and used for revitalizing the speech of old folktales whose audio is missing. It is also used to provide a reference for speaking practice for new Ainu speakers. Speech technologies are important for endangered languages because their cultures have typically been passed down orally, and our efforts will be useful for passing them on to the future.
acl:2026.computel-1.2.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.2.title: Speech Recognition and Synthesis Technologies Applied to Preservation and Revitalization of the Ainu Language
acl:2026.computel-1.2.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.3.abstract: While several pre-trained multilingual models are actively used for fine-tuning on under-resourced and endangered languages, it remains unclear which architectures perform better and what factors explain their varying performance across languages. Although this question may be less pressing for languages with adequate resources, it is critical for endangered language communities, where limited time and funding to experiment with multiple model options are available (Jimerson et al., 2023). We compare the performance of two ASR architectures, Wav2Vec2 and Whisper, on a Dënë Sųłıné dataset. This language and dataset present several challenges common to under-resourced and endangered languages: unstandardized orthography, pronunciation variation, and phonological and morphosyntactic structures that differ from the major languages represented in the multilingual datasets used for pre-training large ASR models. Although Wav2Vec2 reportedly outperforms Whisper in low-resource settings (see e.g., Coto-Solano et al., 2024; Nahabwe et al., 2025; Williams et al., 2023), our study shows that Whisper yields significantly better results on the Dënë Sųłıné dataset. These findings suggest that model performance may depend not only on architecture, dataset size, or typological features of language, but also on dataset-specific characteristics. In our case, Whisper showed better adaptability to a dataset with inconsistent spelling and pronunciation. Further verification across similarly inconsistent datasets is required to assess the generalizability of this result.
acl:2026.computel-1.3.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.3.title: Choosing an ASR model for Dënë Sųłıné: Navigating polysynthesis and unstandardized orthography
acl:2026.computel-1.3.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.4.abstract: Endangered-language teaching often faces two practical bottlenecks: the scarcity of experts able to produce pedagogical grammars, and the dependence of most approaches on expert linguistic annotation. We present a human-in-the-loop system for extremely low-resource languages that addresses both constraints by combining lightweight concept-based annotation, typological inference, structured sentence-pair augmentation, document retrieval, and constrained language model generation. Rather than aiming to produce definitive grammatical descriptions, the system generates revisable grammar lesson drafts grounded in heterogeneous evidence, including elicited sentence pairs, free translation pairs, and descriptive documents. The interface is designed so that speakers, teachers, and other language practitioners without formal linguistic training can contribute usable data, inspect intermediate inferences, control source selection and generate draft grammar lessons. We describe the architecture, user workflows, and initial deployment experience in real-world revitalization settings. The contribution of the paper is an implemented workflow for early pedagogical draft generation under extreme data scarcity, not a controlled evaluation of pedagogical effectiveness.
acl:2026.computel-1.4.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.4.title: An Interactive System for Generating Revisable Grammar Lessons for Extremely Low-Resource Languages Without Expert Annotation
acl:2026.computel-1.4.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.5.abstract: We conduct Automatic speech recognition (ASR) experiments on the Common Voice Spontaneous Speech dataset by Mozilla Data Collective, consisting of 21 low-resource languages across four continents of the world. We fine-tune popular multilingual speech models on all languages of this dataset, and observe that while a single-best-model solution doesn’t exist, the Massively Multilingual Speech model and Whisper achieve superior performance on certain languages. Through n-gram language modeling decoding experiments, we observe a significant improvement in error rate over greedy decoding by up to 27.3%. We follow our experiments with a close linguistic error analysis of the best performing models on Scots (sco) and Nubi (kcn) - two of the languages in our dataset, with very little prior audio and text modeling research. We highlight the morphosyntactic errors induced during speech recognition and perform a holistic analysis of these languages. We finally advocate for the importance of building efficient and accurate ASR tools for modeling speech in endangered languages with scarce resources, and their applications to language revitalization, language learning assistance, and accessibility.
acl:2026.computel-1.5.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.5.title: Voices from the Margins: Modeling Linguistic Diversity in Spontaneous Speech for Low-Resource Languages
acl:2026.computel-1.5.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.7.abstract: This paper presents a digital ecosystem designed for Avar, a morphologically rich and vulnerable Northeast Caucasian language. Addressing the common bottleneck where lexical resources, corpora, and computational tools are developed in isolation or are entirely absent, we propose the “generate-verify” workflow. By developing a scalable, rule-based computational architecture, our system specifically targets the challenges of low-resource settings, overcoming data sparsity to generate over one million inflected forms from a static dictionary of 14,700 entries.Furthermore, by coupling morphological generation with corpus verification, we introduce a dynamic method to rapidly analyze and expand endangered language data. This approach transforms static linguistic documentation into active language reclamation tools, supporting dictionary lookup and the creation of silver-standard annotations for downstream NLP. The platform also serves as a unified model for the collection, management, and mobilization of fragmented language data, ensuring that the resulting resources are directly accessible and beneficial to the speaker community. Ultimately, AvarLab provides a practical, adaptable pathway for building sustainable digital infrastructure by fostering interaction among documentary linguists, computer scientists, and native speakers.
acl:2026.computel-1.7.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.7.title: AvarLab: An Integrated Digital Ecosystem for Avar, a Morphologically Rich Low-Resource Language
acl:2026.computel-1.7.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.8.abstract: In this short paper, we present the first prototype of a mobile application to help preserve and revitalise the endangered language and cultural heritage of the speakers of Dzardzongke, a Tibetic language spoken in South Mustang, Nepal. With this pilot study, we provide a collaborative and highly accessible solution to revitalisation that has potential for any community interested in preserving their language and culture.
acl:2026.computel-1.8.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.8.title: Revitalising Endangered Languages and Cultural Heritage through Language Technology: A Pilot Study for Dzardzongke
acl:2026.computel-1.8.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.computel-1.9.abstract: Annotation tools are foundational infrastructure for language documentation, yet few comprehensive surveys have evaluated the tool landscape specifically from a documentary linguistics perspective. We survey 98 annotation tools across dimensions critical to language documentation workflows: annotation support, collaboration features, active learning, cost and openness, and institutional sustainability. Of the 44 tools both free and accessible for evaluation, only 15 support morpheme segmentation and glossing, and only 6 combine morphological annotation with remote collaboration at no cost. We identify a structural gap between the current tools and the requirements of field linguists working with endangered and Indigenous languages. While many NLP tools prioritize scalable annotation for high-resource settings, documentary linguists need interlinear glossed text (IGT) support and community-accessible interfaces. We taxonomise the tool landscape, present a multi-dimensional feature matrix, suggest current tools for language documentation, and conclude with concrete recommendations for tool developers and the documentary linguistics community.
acl:2026.computel-1.9.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)
acl:2026.computel-1.9.title: Annotation Tools for Language Documentation: A Survey of Capabilities, Gaps, and Morphological Support
acl:2026.computel-1.9.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-9)

acl:2026.conll-main.17.abstract: Low-resource language varieties used by specific groups remain neglected in the development of Multilingual Language Models. A great deal of cross-lingual research focuses on inter-lingual language transfer which strives to align allied varieties and minimize differences between them. However, for low-resource varieties, linguistic dissimilarity is also an important cue allowing generalization to unseen varieties. Unlike prior approaches, we propose a two-stage Language Generalization framework that focuses on capturing variety-specific cues while also exploiting rich overlap offered by high-resource source variety. First, we propose TOPPing, a source-selection method specifically designed for low-resource varieties. Second, we suggest a lightweight VAÇAÍ-Bowl architecture that learns variety-specific attributes with one branch while a parallel branch captures variety-invariant attributes using adversarial training. We evaluate our framework on structural prediction tasks, which are among the few tasks available, as proxy for performance on other downstream tasks. Using VAÇAÍ-Bowl with TOPPing yields an average 54.62% improvement in the dependency parsing task, which serves as a proxy for performance on other downstream tasks across 10 low-resource varieties.
acl:2026.conll-main.17.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 30th Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
acl:2026.conll-main.17.title: Harnessing Linguistic Dissimilarity for Language Generalization on Unseen Low-Resource Varieties
acl:2026.conll-main.17.venue: Proceedings of the 30th Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning

acl:2026.conll-main.29.abstract: Visual Word Sense Disambiguation (Visual-WSD) requires ranking the correct image for an ambiguous word given a short trigger phrase. For low-resource languages, it is bottle­necked by scarce sense-level benchmarks and limited sense-aligned multimodal supervision. We study Ukrainian and (i) extend the Ukrainian Visual-WSD benchmark from 87 to 381 instances and benchmark multilingual CLIP checkpoints and multimodal large models, and (ii) introduce two scalable Wikipedia-derived dataset construction methods. Using compute-efficient adaptation we fine-tune a multilingual CLIP backbone and show that sense-grounded supervision drives the improvements: combining our two Wikipedia-derived datasets improves HIT@1 from 37.00% to 43.05%.
acl:2026.conll-main.29.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 30th Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
acl:2026.conll-main.29.title: From Sparse to Sense-Grounded: Wikipedia Training for Ukrainian Visual-WSD
acl:2026.conll-main.29.venue: Proceedings of the 30th Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning

acl:2026.customnlp4u-1.13.abstract: Research in language documentation has the potential to benefit from integration of ASR models, especially through the assisted transcription of recordings with audio. Recent advancements in ASR for low-resource languages demonstrate the ability to adapt general, multilingual models for unseen languages with limited fine-tuning data, supporting the creation of custom ASR models. However, resources are still required to collect and prepare the fine-tuning data, necessitating exploration of optimization of resource allocation within the process of data collection and preparation. This paper outlines important considerations for the collection and preparation of data for customizing an ASR model for use in language documentation projects. With the development of a Lamkang ASR model as an example, prioritization of tasks within a language documentation project is outlined by analyzing the relative impact of time spent on transcription correction versus time spent on manual alignment on ASR model performance. Results from this research suggest prioritization of transcription correction over manual-alignment of data and suggest fine-tuning multilingual ASR systems produces superior results to zero-shot ASR models, despite recent advancements in the technology.
acl:2026.customnlp4u-1.13.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Second Workshop on Customizable NLP: Progress and Challenges in Customizing NLP for a Domain, Application, Group, or Individual (CustomNLP4U)
acl:2026.customnlp4u-1.13.title: Customizing ASR for Language Documentation and Resource Prioritization
acl:2026.customnlp4u-1.13.venue: Proceedings of the Second Workshop on Customizable NLP: Progress and Challenges in Customizing NLP for a Domain, Application, Group, or Individual (CustomNLP4U)

acl:2026.determit-1.5.abstract: Reliable Text Difficulty Assessment is a prerequisite for valid text simplification workflows and personalized learning applications. However, the development of robust assessment models is severely hindered by a critical bottleneck: the scarcity of expert-annotated corpora containing fine-grained difficulty levels (e.g., CEFR), particularly for lower-resource languages. This paper addresses this data scarcity problem in the context of a low-resource European language. We propose a cross-lingual data augmentation strategy that leverages machine translation to transfer labeled resources from high-resource languages to the target low-resource language. We train BERT-based regression models to predict difficulty scores and investigate whether synthetic, translated data can effectively supplement native training sets. Our experiments demonstrate that augmenting scarce native data with machine-translated corpora significantly improves the accuracy of difficulty estimation, offering a viable solution for languages lacking extensive expert annotations.
acl:2026.determit-1.5.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 2nd Workshop on Evaluating Text Difficulty in a Multilingual Context (DeTermIt! 2026)

glossary.explanation_id: Proses penyesuaian lanjutan pada *pretrained model* menggunakan data spesifik untuk tugas tertentu.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain kekurangan sumber daya data beranotasi yang memadai untuk pelatihan model.
Tugas *machine learning* untuk memprediksi nilai kontinu berdasarkan variabel masukan.
Teknik penambahan data latih tiruan atau modifikasi untuk memperbesar ukuran dan keragaman dataset.
Model standar atau sederhana yang digunakan sebagai pembanding untuk mengukur peningkatan dari model baru yang diusulkan.
Studi eksperimental dengan menghapus atau mengubah komponen tertentu dari sistem untuk mengukur kontribusinya.
Teknik yang digunakan untuk mencegah *overfitting* pada model *machine learning* dengan membatasi kompleksitasnya.

background.en: Reliable text difficulty assessment is essential for text simplification and personalized learning applications. However, building robust assessment models is severely hindered by the scarcity of expert-annotated corpora containing fine-grained difficulty levels, especially for lower-resource European languages like Finnish. This paper addresses this critical data scarcity problem by exploring cross-lingual transfer techniques.
background.id: Penilaian tingkat kesulitan teks yang andal sangat penting untuk alur kerja simplifikasi teks dan aplikasi pembelajaran yang dipersonalisasi. Namun, pengembangan model penilaian yang tangguh sangat terhambat oleh kelangkaan korpus beranotasi pakar yang memuat tingkat kesulitan yang rinci, terutama untuk bahasa-bahasa Eropa *low-resource* seperti bahasa Finlandia. Makalah ini mengatasi masalah kelangkaan data yang krusial ini dengan mengeksplorasi teknik transfer lintas-bahasa.

contributions.en: The paper introduces a cross-lingual data augmentation strategy that leverages machine translation to transfer expert-annotated readability resources from a high-resource language, Russian, to a low-resource target language, Finnish. It constructs a comprehensive Finnish dataset combining native and translated texts spanning all CEFR levels. Additionally, it investigates the impact of label injection and label-wise proportional sampling strategies on regression model performance and cross-lingual generalization.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan strategi augmentasi data lintas-bahasa yang memanfaatkan *machine translation* untuk mentransfer sumber daya keterbacaan beranotasi pakar dari bahasa *high-resource*, yaitu bahasa Rusia, ke bahasa target *low-resource*, yaitu bahasa Finlandia. Makalah ini menyusun korpus bahasa Finlandia komprehensif yang menggabungkan teks asli dan terjemahan yang mencakup seluruh tingkat CEFR. Selain itu, penelitian ini menyelidiki dampak dari strategi *label injection* dan *label-wise proportional sampling* pada kinerja model regresi dan generalisasi lintas-bahasa.

future_work.en: The authors plan to integrate feature-based and Transformer-based models to improve interpretability and explore methods to provide reasonable guarantees that machine translation preserves readability levels. They also aim to study multilingual difficulty models to identify language-independent features.
future_work.id: Para penulis berencana untuk mengintegrasikan model berbasis fitur dan berbasis *Transformer* guna meningkatkan kemudahan interpretasi dan mengeksplorasi metode untuk memberikan jaminan yang wajar bahwa *machine translation* mempertahankan tingkat keterbacaan. Mereka juga bertujuan untuk mempelajari model kesulitan multilingua untuk mengidentifikasi fitur yang bebas bahasa.

method.en: The authors compile a Finnish dataset combining native texts from five sources and machine-translated texts derived from Russian corpora using OpusMT models. The final dataset contains 12,865 texts mapped onto a continuous numerical scale ranging from 1 to 6 to preserve relative order. They train a BERT-based regression model, specifically TurkuNLP/bert-base-finnish-cased-v1 for Finnish and ai-forever/ruBert-large for Russian, fine-tuned with a regression objective. The evaluation uses metrics including mean squared error, root mean square error, mean absolute error, and coefficient of determination.
method.id: Para penulis menyusun dataset bahasa Finlandia yang menggabungkan teks asli dari lima sumber dan teks hasil *machine translation* yang berasal dari korpus bahasa Rusia menggunakan model OpusMT. Dataset akhir berisi 12.865 teks yang dipetakan ke skala numerik kontinu dari 1 hingga 6 untuk mempertahankan urutan relatif. Mereka melatih model regresi berbasis BERT, khususnya TurkuNLP/bert-base-finnish-cased-v1 untuk bahasa Finlandia dan ai-forever/ruBert-large untuk bahasa Rusia, yang di-*fine-tune* dengan tujuan regresi. Evaluasi menggunakan metrik termasuk *mean squared error*, *root mean square error*, *mean absolute error*, dan koefisien determinasi.

related_work.en: Estimating text difficulty has a long history, starting from early formula-based approaches like Flesch-Kincaid and the Lexile framework, which relied on surface-level features and failed to capture deeper lexical or syntactic complexity. Subsequent supervised systems incorporated richer handcrafted linguistic features, while recent neural approaches and fine-tuned BERT models substantially outperformed feature-based baselines. Furthermore, large language models have been evaluated on readability tasks with competitive results. Despite these advancements, a persistent bottleneck across all approaches remains the scarcity of expert-annotated corpora.
related_work.id: Estimasi kesulitan teks memiliki sejarah panjang, dimulai dari pendekatan berbasis rumus awal seperti Flesch-Kincaid dan kerangka kerja Lexile, yang mengandalkan fitur tingkat permukaan dan gagal menangkap kompleksitas leksikal atau sintaksis yang lebih dalam. Sistem terawasi berikutnya memasukkan fitur linguistik buatan tangan yang lebih kaya, sementara pendekatan neural modern dan model BERT yang telah di-*fine-tune* mengungguli garis dasar berbasis fitur secara substansial. Selain itu, *large language model* telah dievaluasi pada tugas keterbacaan dengan hasil yang kompetitif. Meskipun ada kemajuan ini, hambatan yang persisten di semua pendekatan tetaplah kelangkaan korpus beranotasi pakar.

results.en: The experiments show that incorporating machine-translated data from Russian substantially improves text difficulty prediction for Finnish compared to training on native data alone. Training exclusively on translated data yields poor results when tested on native text with an R2 of 18.24 percent, while combining native and translated data achieves a high R2 of 96.01 percent. Furthermore, ablation studies reveal that adding mid-level translated texts or applying a 40 percent proportional sampling yields the strongest performance and optimal regularization.
results.id: Eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa memasukkan data hasil *machine translation* dari bahasa Rusia secara substansial meningkatkan prediksi kesulitan teks untuk bahasa Finlandia dibandingkan dengan pelatihan menggunakan data asli saja. Pelatihan secara eksklusif pada data terjemahan menghasilkan kinerja yang buruk ketika diuji pada teks asli dengan R2 sebesar 18,24 persen, sementara menggabungkan data asli dan terjemahan mencapai R2 yang tinggi sebesar 96,01 persen. Lebih lanjut, studi ablasi mengungkapkan bahwa penambahan teks terjemahan tingkat menengah atau penerapan *proportional sampling* sebesar 40 persen menghasilkan kinerja terkuat dan regularisasi yang optimal.

tldr.en: This paper proposes a cross-lingual data augmentation strategy using machine translation to address data scarcity in text difficulty assessment for low-resource languages. The experiments demonstrate that augmenting scarce native data with translated corpora significantly improves prediction accuracy and model robustness.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan strategi augmentasi data lintas-bahasa menggunakan *machine translation* untuk mengatasi kelangkaan data dalam penilaian tingkat kesulitan teks pada bahasa *low-resource*. Eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa penambahan data asli yang langka dengan korpus terjemahan secara signifikan meningkatkan akurasi prediksi dan ketahanan model.

acl:2026.determit-1.5.title: Translation as Augmentation: Effect of Translated Data on Assessment of Difficulty
acl:2026.determit-1.5.venue: Proceedings of the 2nd Workshop on Evaluating Text Difficulty in a Multilingual Context (DeTermIt! 2026)

acl:2026.dialres-1.1.abstract: The growing interest of Natural Language Processing (NLP) in minority languages has not yet bridged the gap in the preservation of oral linguistic heritage. In particular, extemporaneous poetry — a performative genre based on real-time improvisation, metrical-rhetorical competence — remains a largely unexplored area of computational linguistics. This methodological gap necessitates the creation of specific resources to document and analyse the structures of improvised poetry. This is the context in which A Bolu was created, the first structured corpus of extemporaneous poetry dedicated to cantada logudorese, a variant of the Sardinian language. The dataset comprises 2,835 stanzas for a total of 141,321 tokens. The study presents the architecture of the corpus and applies a multidimensional analysis combining descriptive statistical indices and computational linguistics techniques to map the characteristics of the poetic text. The results indicate that the production of Sardinian extemporaneous poets is characterised by recurring patterns that support Parry and Lord’s theory of formulaicity. This evidence not only provides a new key to understanding oral creativity, but also offers a significant contribution to the development of NLP tools that are more inclusive and sensitive to the specificities of less widely spoken languages.
acl:2026.dialres-1.1.journal_ref: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective
acl:2026.dialres-1.1.title: A Bolu: A Structured Dataset for the Computational Analysis of Sardinian Improvisational Poetry
acl:2026.dialres-1.1.venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective

acl:2026.dialres-1.13.abstract: Formosan languages are a critically endangered branch of the Austronesian family spoken in Taiwan, and many of their dialects remain poorly understood and computationally understudied. Subgrouping relationships in these languages are often contested and unresolved. We provide the first evaluation of the ePark corpus as a dialectal NLP resource, identifying its strengths and gaps for future NLP work, and present the first large-scale corpus-based computational analysis of dialect similarity across all officially recognized Formosan languages. We use the ePark corpus to analyze 42 dialects in 16 Formosan languages, and through word-level TF-IDF cosine similarity, Jaccard similarity over shared vocabulary, and Levenshtein distance, we quantify pairwise dialectal relationships within the Amis, Atayal, Seediq, Bunun, Paiwan, Rukai, and Puyuma languages. We find that simple lexical similarity methods can recover and confirm linguistically established dialectal subgroupings. We find that in multiple cases the two metrics diverge, offering insights on contested subgroupings such as Mantauran Rukai. This work establishes a scalable methodological framework for dialectometry in low-resource languages, demonstrates the value of the ePark corpus for Formosan NLP research, and encourages future work in NLP on Formosan dialects.
acl:2026.dialres-1.13.journal_ref: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective

glossary.explanation_id: Dialektometri adalah metode kuantitatif dalam linguistik untuk mengukur jarak atau kesamaan linguistik antara berbagai dialek menggunakan data korpus.
Kesamaan kosinus TF-IDF adalah ukuran kemiripan antara dua dokumen berdasarkan bobot frekuensi kata dan kemiringan sudut vektornya.
Kesamaan Jaccard adalah metrik statistik yang digunakan untuk mengukur kemiripan dan keragaman sampel himpunan data.
Jarak Levenshtein adalah ukuran string untuk mengukur perbedaan antara dua urutan karakter melalui jumlah minimum penyuntingan.
Rasio token-tipe adalah metrik keanekaragaman leksikal yang dihitung dari jumlah total kata dibagi dengan jumlah kata unik dalam korpus.
Tingkat hapax adalah proporsi kata dalam korpus yang hanya muncul sekali, yang menunjukkan tingkat kekosongan atau kejarangan data.
*Cross-dialect transfer learning* adalah teknik *transfer learning* di mana model yang dilatih pada satu dialek diadaptasi untuk digunakan pada dialek lain.
Dendrogram adalah diagram pohon yang menunjukkan susunan hierarki dan pengelompokan berdasarkan tingkat kemiripan.

background.en: Formosan languages form a critically endangered branch of the Austronesian family spoken in Taiwan, yet many of their dialects remain poorly understood and computationally understudied. Subgrouping relationships within these languages are often contested and unresolved, while developing language technology is vital for preservation and revitalization efforts.
background.id: Bahasa-bahasa Formosa merupakan cabang dari rumpun Austronesia yang terancam punah di Taiwan, namun banyak dialeknya masih kurang dipahami dan belum banyak diteliti secara komputasi. Hubungan subkelompok dalam bahasa-bahasa ini sering kali diperdebatkan dan belum terselesaikan, sementara pengembangan teknologi bahasa sangat penting untuk upaya preservasi dan revitalisasi.

contributions.en: The paper provides the first evaluation of the ePark corpus as a dialectal NLP resource and presents the first large-scale corpus-based computational analysis of dialect similarity across all officially recognized Formosan languages. It establishes a scalable methodological framework for dialectometry in low-resource languages.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyajikan evaluasi pertama terhadap korpus ePark sebagai sumber daya *NLP* dialektal dan menampilkan analisis komputasi berbasis korpus berskala besar yang pertama untuk kesamaan dialek di seluruh bahasa Formosa yang diakui secara resmi. Penelitian ini membangun kerangka kerja metodologis yang dapat diskalakan untuk dialektometri pada bahasa-bahasa *low-resource*.

future_work.en: Limitations include the reliance on lexical similarity measures as a single dimension of linguistic relatedness, the absence of morphological segmentation beyond word-level tokenization, and the restriction to officially recognized dialects in ePark. Future work should incorporate phonological and morphological features, develop morphological analysis tools, extend work to downstream tasks like automatic speech recognition and cross-dialect transfer learning, and compare lexical measures against neural and embedding-based approaches.
future_work.id: Keterbatasan penelitian mencakup ketergantungan pada ukuran kesamaan leksikal sebagai satu dimensi keterkaitan linguistik, ketiadaan segmentasi morfologis di luar tokenisasi tingkat kata, serta pembatasan pada dialek yang diakui secara resmi di ePark. Pekerjaan masa depan harus memasukkan fitur fonologis dan morfologis, mengembangkan alat analisis morfologis, memperluas pekerjaan ke tugas hilir seperti *automatic speech recognition* dan *cross-dialect transfer learning*, serta membandingkan ukuran leksikal dengan pendekatan berbasis saraf dan *embedding*.

method.en: The study utilizes the ePark corpus covering 42 dialects across 16 Formosan languages, containing 2,680,175 tokens. The preprocessing pipeline converts text to lowercase, removes punctuation, normalizes whitespace, and performs word-level tokenization. Three lexical similarity measures are computed: word-level TF-IDF cosine similarity, Jaccard similarity over shared vocabulary, and character-level Levenshtein distance, accompanied by bootstrap confidence intervals.
method.id: Studi ini menggunakan korpus ePark yang mencakup 42 dialek dari 16 bahasa Formosa dengan total 2.680.175 token. Alur pra-pemrosesan mengubah teks menjadi huruf kecil, menghapus tanda baca, menormalisasi spasi, dan melakukan tokenisasi tingkat kata. Tiga ukuran kesamaan leksikal dihitung yaitu kesamaan kosinus TF-IDF tingkat kata, kesamaan Jaccard pada kosakata bersama, dan jarak Levenshtein tingkat karakter, yang disertai dengan interval kepercayaan *bootstrap*.

related_work.en: Previous computational dialectology research utilized methods such as Levenshtein distance, autoencoders, Jaccard similarity, and vector space models across various language families. While NLP research on Formosan languages is beginning through machine translation benchmarks and speech representation models, dialectal relationships within these languages have not been studied previously.
related_work.id: Penelitian dialektologi komputasi sebelumnya menggunakan metode seperti jarak Levenshtein, *autoencoder*, kesamaan Jaccard, dan *vector space model* di berbagai rumpun bahasa. Meskipun penelitian *NLP* pada bahasa Formosa mulai berkembang melalui *benchmark* terjemahan mesin dan model representasi ujaran, hubungan dialektal dalam bahasa-bahasa ini belum pernah diteliti sebelumnya.

results.en: The results demonstrate that simple lexical similarity methods can recover and confirm linguistically established dialectal subgroupings, such as in Seediq and Bunun. Furthermore, metrics diverge in multiple cases, providing insights into contested subgroupings like Mantauran Rukai, where Seediq dialects exhibit the highest internal similarity and Atayal and Rukai show the greatest internal diversity.
results.id: Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa metode kesamaan leksikal sederhana dapat memulihkan dan mengonfirmasi subkelompok dialek yang telah ditetapkan secara linguistik, seperti pada bahasa Seediq dan Bunun. Selain itu, metrik berselisih pada beberapa kasus, memberikan wawasan tentang subkelompok yang diperdebatkan seperti Rukai Mantauran, di mana dialek Seediq menunjukkan kesamaan internal tertinggi sementara Atayal dan Rukai menunjukkan keragaman internal terbesar.

tldr.en: This paper evaluates the ePark corpus as a dialectal NLP resource and presents a large-scale computational analysis of dialect similarity across Formosan languages. The findings show that simple lexical similarity methods can effectively recover and confirm linguistically established dialectal subgroupings.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengevaluasi korpus ePark sebagai sumber daya *NLP* dialektal dan menyajikan analisis komputasi skala besar mengenai kesamaan dialek di seluruh bahasa Formosa. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa metode kesamaan leksikal sederhana dapat memulihkan dan mengonfirmasi subkelompok dialek yang telah ditetapkan secara linguistik.

acl:2026.dialres-1.13.title: Dialectometry and Evaluation of the ePark Corpus for Low-Resource Formosan Language Dialects
acl:2026.dialres-1.13.venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective

acl:2026.dialres-1.25.abstract: Alsatian is a regional low-resource language spoken in a majority-language context. In order to create a voice dataset suited for training automatic speech recognition and speech-to-text models, we launched a crowdsourcing campaign on the platform Mozilla Common Voice. We describe sociolinguistic issues we ran into, such as participants’ perception of their own language and its role in the AI landscape, which are vital to address to raise the participation in the crowdsourcing effort. We found that the participants are often confused about NLP and AI tools, and have a strong interested in preserving their language.
acl:2026.dialres-1.25.journal_ref: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective
acl:2026.dialres-1.25.title: Sociolinguistic aspects of crowdsourcing for a vocal corpus of Alsatian
acl:2026.dialres-1.25.venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective

acl:2026.dialres-1.32.abstract: This paper presents a knowledge management framework for the digital preservation of Aromanian, an endangered Eastern Romance language spoken across the Balkans, combined with the first systematic evaluation of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models on Aromanian dialectal speech. The proposed three-module framework encompasses localization of existing resources, distribution through digital platforms, and creation of new linguistic content through technological innovation. Empirical analysis of knowledge management practices among 176 respondents validates the framework design, revealing that information quality (28.3%) and personal utility (24.1%) are the most valued criteria for knowledge sharing, while digital information seeking (27.1%) is the dominant behaviour. Within this framework, we evaluate models from the OpenAI Whisper family across three sizes (medium, large-v2, large-v3) and multiple language settings on two Aromanian varieties: Gramosteanj and Crushova. All configurations yield word error rates (WER) above 88%, with character error rates (CER) as low as 34% under optimal conditions, indicating partial phonotactic capture despite word-level failure. The Latin language setting with large-v3 consistently achieves the best results. Romanization of non-Latin script output substantially reduces CER, confirming script mismatch as a major error source. These findings underscore the limitations of current pretrained ASR models for endangered languages and the need for dedicated resources and adaptation strategies within a broader language preservation framework
acl:2026.dialres-1.32.journal_ref: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective
acl:2026.dialres-1.32.title: Digital Preservation of Aromanian Through Knowledge Management and Automatic Speech Recognition Evaluation
acl:2026.dialres-1.32.venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective

acl:2026.dialres-1.5.abstract: Automatic speech recognition models are typically trained with data of standard languages. However, their performance degrades when dealing with non-standard dialectal speech. In this paper, we present the first evaluation of an automatic speech recognition system for Basque, a low-resource language, based on spontaneous broadcast speech with high representation of dialectal speech. It relies on a 140-h manually annotated propietary corpus of television programs broadcast by Basque Radio Television, including dialect-level labels, as well as standardized and pseudo-phonetic transcriptions. We find that recognition performance significantly degrades for dialectal compared to standard speech, for all dialects present in our corpus. Subsequently, we provide a quantitative analysis of phonological phenomena based on single-word substitution errors, and identify 52 recurrent phenomena, grouped into sound deletions, epentheses, and substitutions. We further show a modest but statistically significant correlation between the number of phonological phenomena in an utterance and its recognition error rate. Our findings highlight the limitations of dialect-agnostic evaluation and motivate linguistically informed, dialect-aware strategies for automatic speech recognition in low-resource and typologically diverse languages.
acl:2026.dialres-1.5.journal_ref: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective

glossary.explanation_id: Teknologi *machine learning* yang mampu mengenali dan mentranskripsikan suara manusia menjadi teks tertulis.
Metrik evaluasi yang mengukur persentase kesalahan kata antara transkripsi otomatis dan transkripsi acuan.
Metrik evaluasi yang menghitung tingkat galat berdasarkan perbedaan karakter individual antara teks hipotesis dan referensi.
Arsitektur *neural network* yang menggabungkan mekanisme konvolusi dan *self-attention* untuk tugas *automatic speech recognition*.
Uji statistik non-parametrik yang digunakan untuk membandingkan dua atau lebih kelompok sampel independen.
Fenomena fonologis berupa penambahan bunyi atau fonem ke dalam suatu kata.

background.en: Automatic speech recognition models are typically trained on standard language varieties and experience performance degradation when applied to non-standard dialectal speech. Despite the social and ethical implications of dialectal natural language processing, research in automatic speech recognition has largely focused on high-resource languages, leaving low-resource and typologically diverse languages like Basque underexplored. Basque exhibits high dialectal variability in phonetics and phonology, posing challenges for speech technologies.
background.id: Model *automatic speech recognition* umumnya dilatih pada varietas bahasa standar dan mengalami penurunan performa ketika diterapkan pada wicara berdialek non-standar. Terlepas dari implikasi sosial dan etika dari *natural language processing* berdialek, penelitian pada *automatic speech recognition* sebagian besar berfokus pada bahasa bersumber daya tinggi, sehingga mengabaikan bahasa bersumber daya rendah dan beragam secara tipologis seperti bahasa Basque yang menunjukkan variabilitas dialek yang tinggi dalam fonetik dan fonologi.

contributions.en: The paper contributes the first dialect-aware evaluation of Basque automatic speech recognition using a 140-hour proprietary corpus of television broadcast speech with manual annotations, dialect labels, and both standardized and pseudo-phonetic transcriptions. Furthermore, it provides a systematic documentation and quantitative analysis of 52 recurrent phonological phenomena across Basque dialects and links them to recognition error rates.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyumbangkan evaluasi *automatic speech recognition* bahasa Basque yang sadar dialek pertama menggunakan korpus berpemilik berdurasi 140 jam dari wicara siaran televisi dengan anotasi manual, label dialek, serta transkripsi terstandarisasi dan pseudo-fonetik. Selain itu, makalah ini menyediakan dokumentasi sistematis dan analisis kuantitatif dari 52 fenomena fonologis berulang di berbagai dialek bahasa Basque serta menghubungkannya dengan tingkat galat pengenalan.
