future_work.en: The authors note limitations including the underrepresentation of northern dialects like Lapurdian and Lower Navarrese, the absence of Souletin in the dataset, and challenges in defining subdialectal boundaries and consistent speaker-level dialect usage. Future efforts should prioritize targeted data collection for northern and less represented dialects as well as informal and spontaneous speech.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat keterbatasan termasuk kurangnya representasi dialek utara seperti Lapurdian dan Lower Navarrese, ketiadaan dialek Souletin dalam dataset, serta tantangan dalam mendefinisikan batas subdialek dan penggunaan dialek tingkat penutur yang konsisten. Upaya di masa mendatang harus memprioritaskan pengumpulan data yang ditargetkan untuk dialek utara dan yang kurang terwakili serta wicara informal dan spontan.

method.en: The study uses a 140-hour proprietary dataset of Basque television broadcasts containing standardized and pseudo-phonetic transcriptions. The evaluation employs a Conformer-Transducer automatic speech recognition model from the NVIDIA NeMo framework, specifically stt_eu_conformer_transducer_large_v2, trained on 772 hours of Basque speech. Evaluation metrics include word error rate and character error rate, accompanied by non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis tests and Dunn post-hoc pairwise comparisons with Holm correction.
method.id: Penelitian ini menggunakan dataset berpemilik berdurasi 140 jam dari siaran televisi bahasa Basque yang berisi transkripsi terstandarisasi dan pseudo-fonetik. Evaluasi ini menggunakan model *automatic speech recognition* *Conformer-Transducer* dari kerangka kerja *NVIDIA NeMo*, secara spesifik stt_eu_conformer_transducer_large_v2, yang dilatih pada 772 jam wicara bahasa Basque. Metrik evaluasi mencakup *word error rate* dan *character error rate*, disertai dengan uji non-parametrik Kruskal-Wallis dan perbandingan berpasangan *post-hoc* Dunn dengan koreksi Holm.

related_work.en: Prior research has documented automatic speech recognition performance degradation for non-white speakers and non-standard varieties across various languages, predominantly focusing on English. In the context of Basque, while some corpora and natural language processing resources exist for dialects, speech processing resources remain underexplored, often containing limited spontaneous speech or lacking proper dialectal representation.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya telah mendokumentasikan penurunan performa *automatic speech recognition* untuk penutur non-kulit putih dan varietas non-standar di berbagai bahasa, yang sebagian besar berfokus pada bahasa Inggris. Dalam konteks bahasa Basque, meskipun beberapa korpus dan sumber daya *natural language processing* untuk dialek telah ada, sumber daya pengolahan wicara masih kurang dieksplorasi, sering kali berisi wicara spontan yang terbatas atau kekurangan representasi dialek yang memadai.

results.en: Recognition performance is significantly better for Standard Basque compared to all other dialects, with Gipuzkoan and Biscayan showing high error rates and Biscayan exhibiting the highest character error rate and most phonological phenomena. A modest yet statistically significant correlation (r = .216, p < .001) was found between the number of phonological phenomena in an utterance and its character error rate, confirming that phonological variability contributes to recognition errors.
results.id: Performa pengenalan secara signifikan lebih baik untuk bahasa Basque Standar dibandingkan dengan semua dialek lainnya, di mana dialek Gipuzkoan dan Biscayan menunjukkan tingkat galat yang tinggi dan Biscayan menampilkan *character error rate* tertinggi serta fenomena fonologis terbanyak. Korelasi yang moderat namun signifikan secara statistik (r = .216, p < .001) ditemukan antara jumlah fenomena fonologis dalam sebuah ujaran dan *character error rate*-nya, yang mengonfirmasi bahwa variabilitas fonologis berkontribusi pada galat pengenalan.

tldr.en: This paper presents the first automatic speech recognition evaluation for Basque dialects using a 140-hour spontaneous broadcast speech corpus. The findings reveal that recognition performance significantly degrades for dialectal speech, driven by the accumulation of phonological phenomena.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan evaluasi *automatic speech recognition* pertama untuk dialek bahasa Basque menggunakan korpus wicara siaran spontan berdurasi 140 jam. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa performa pengenalan menurun secara signifikan pada wicara berdialek, yang didorong oleh akumulasi fenomena fonologis.

acl:2026.dialres-1.5.title: Phonologically-aware Automatic Speech Recognition Evaluation of Low-Resource Languages: The Case of Basque Dialects
acl:2026.dialres-1.5.venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Dialects in NLP — A Resource Perspective

acl:2026.dmr-1.14.abstract: We present the Sema system for the DMR 2026 shared task on parsing from natural language to . Our approach relies on parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Qwen3-4B with a multistage training procedure. We first train on a capped subset of the noisy training data, then continue training on the clean split, and finally fine-tune a dedicated stage for word-to-node alignment prediction. The system generates sentence-level graphs, selected document-level information, and alignments in separate steps, followed by rule-based post-processing to satisfy the official evaluation format. Results show that the approach is viable across several languages and exhibits promising transfer to Italian despite the absence of Italian data for fine-tuning , while very low-resource languages remain challenging.
acl:2026.dmr-1.14.journal_ref: Proceedings of The Seventh International Workshop on Designing Meaning Representations (DMR 2026) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.dmr-1.14.title: Sema System for the DMR 2026 Shared Task: Multistage UMR Parsing with Qwen3-4B
acl:2026.dmr-1.14.venue: Proceedings of The Seventh International Workshop on Designing Meaning Representations (DMR 2026) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.1.abstract: The rapid growth of social media platforms has led to a substantial increase in user-generated content, including abusive and offensive language. Detecting abusive content becomes particularly challenging in low-resource and code-mixed language settings such as Telugu-English social media text. Code-mixed content involves transliteration, inconsistent spelling variations, informal expressions, and frequent language switching within a single sentence. This paper focuses on detecting abusive content in Telugu-English code-mixed comments using both traditional machine learning and transformer-based deep learning models. The proposed approach incorporates preprocessing strategies to normalize transliterations and spelling variations, hybrid feature extraction techniques combining TF-IDF and FastText embeddings, and fine-tuning of multilingual transformer models. The study addresses challenges such as morphological complexity, contextual ambiguity, and limited annotated data in low-resource NLP environments.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.1.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.1.title: Abusive Content Detection in Telugu-English Code-Mixed Social Media Using Hybrid Transformer Architectures
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.1.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.15.abstract: Political sentiment analysis aims to automatically identify opinions and attitudes expressed in political discourse on social media platforms. This paper presents an overview of the TamilPoliSent 2026 shared task on multiclass political sentiment analysis in Tamil, organized as part of DravidianLangTech@ACL 2026. The task focuses on categorizing Tamil comments from X (formerly Twitter) into seven sentiment classes: Substantiated, Sarcastic, Opinionated, Positive, Negative, Neutral, and None of the above. The dataset consists of 5,440 annotated Tamil tweets collected from political discussions on social media. Participants were provided with labeled training and development datasets, while the test set was used for final evaluation.A total of 22 teams participated in the shared task and explored a wide range of modeling approaches including classical machine learning methods, transformer-based architectures, hybrid lexical–contextual models, and ensemble frameworks. System performance was evaluated using Macro F1-score to ensure balanced evaluation across all sentiment categories. The best-performing system achieved a Macro F1-score of 0.3935.The results highlight several challenges in Tamil political sentiment analysis, including class imbalance, sarcasm, informal writing styles, and semantic overlap between sentiment categories. The shared task demonstrates that transformer-based models combined with class-balanced learning and hybrid representations are effective for handling fine-grained political sentiment classification in low-resource languages. These findings contribute to advancing research in political discourse analysis and natural language processing for Tamil and other under-resourced languages.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.15.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.15.title: TamilPoliSent 2026: A Shared Task report on Multiclass Political Sentiment Analysis in Tamil
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.15.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.17.abstract: Low-resource languages pose significant challenges for speech technology due to linguistic variation and limited annotated resources. One such language is Tamil, which is a morphologically rich language with significant dialectal variations, which makes Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and dialect classification a challenging task. In this article, we introduce a shared-task system for handling Speech Processing in Tamil Language covering both ASR and Dialect classification. We use the Whisper Large-v3 multilingual model in a zero-shot setting without task-specific fine-tuning. For dialect classification, we employ a pre-trained Wav2Vec2 model to extract acoustic features and mean and standard deviation pooling to create utterance-level representations, with an XGBoost model trained for four-way prediction of dialects. Experiments on 579 Tamil speech samples resulted in a word error rate (WER) of 0.61, highlighting the difficulty of the dialectal ASR problem in low- resource setting. The dialect classification system obtained an accuracy of 0.49 and a macro F1 score of 0.41, and there was a certain amount of confusion between the dialect classes. The proposed system is purely based on the standard pretrained models without adaptation, but has produced a benchmark that can be replicated in the multilingual speech representation evaluation of Tamil low-resource scenarios. The results also indicate the need for additional strategies to improve the robustness of the model and stronger baseline models and improved methods for embedding-based dialect classification for future research.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.17.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.17.title: AITamilDialect@DravidianLangTech 2026: Zero-Shot Whisper and Wav2Vec2 Embedding-Based Tamil Speech Recognition and Dialect Classification.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.17.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.25.abstract: Prompt recovery in large language models (LLMs) is the task of inferring the communicative intent and stylistic framing of the original instruction from model-generated output. This task is especially challenging for low-resource Dravidian languages such as Telugu, where agglutinative morphology, register variation, and scarce annotated data complicate stylistic modelling. In this paper, we present our system for the Shared Task on Prompt Recovery for LLM in Telugu at DravidianLangTech @ ACL 2026, which aims to classify Telugu transcript excerpts into nine communicative style categories: Formal, Informal, Optimistic, Pessimistic, Humorous, Serious, Inspiring, Authoritative, and Persuasive.We have implemented a transformer-based approach using ai4bharat/IndicBERTv2-MLM-only, MuRIL-base and Telugu-BERT for Telugu communicative style classification. Our system fine-tunes the pretrained Indic language training samples to capture stylistic patterns in Telugu transcripts. Our approach achieved a macro F1 score of 0.2993 on the evaluation set, demonstrating the potential of Indic-focused pretrained models for stylistic analysis in low-resource language settings.Controlled ablations reveal that label smoothing benefits stronger Indic backbones but degrades weaker ones, and that surface linguistic feature augmentation does not complement rich contextual representations on small datasets.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.25.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.25.title: Cuet Yet Another Baseline@DravidianLangTech 2026: Shared Task on Prompt Recovery for LLM in Telugu
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.25.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.32.abstract: The low-resource dialectal Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) in languages like Tamil is a critical issue because of phonological differences, lack of labeled data and because of the differences in the acoustic of speech patterns among regions. This paper will introduce a dialect-conscious Tamil ASR model that is trained on the Conformer-CTC-BPE-Large framework via the NVIDIA NeMo framework. This model is an integration of convolutional subsampling, multi-head self-attention, and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) decoding along with a BPE tokenizer to make possible both efficient end-to-end speech recognition. The system is tested on the audio recordings of dialectal Tamil, in which mono-channel audio normalization and batch transcription are used. Our findings indicate that even using large pretrained Conformer models, dialectal ASR tasks are successfully implemented even in zero-shot. Transcriptions generated are examined and the challenges associated with the dialectal differences and acoustic models, and we comment on the possible future directions of enhancing data-efficient adaptation in low-resource speech recognition.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.32.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.32.title: Dialectmind@DravidianLang Tech 2026: Zero-Shot Dialectal Tamil Automatic Speech Recognition Using a Large Pretrained Conformer Model
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.32.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.34.abstract: Many social media platforms have users who have normalized the abuse of women online, creating a need for systems that automatically detect such activity. For low-resource, regional languages like Tamil, which has informal writing styles, spelling variations, dialectal differences, and culturally specific expressions, it becomes a challenge to correctly detect abusive comments. In this work, a transformer-based approach for binary classification of Tamil comments into abusive and non-abusive categories is done using the DravidianLangTech dataset. The proposed system fine-tunes MuRIL(a multilingual transformer pretrained for Indian languages), enabling effective contextual representation with minimal preprocessing. To improve the transparency of the system, a post-hoc Explainable AI component is incorporated. A perturbation-based method using log-odds differences identifies words that significantly influence the predictions. Experimental findings indicate that the model reaches a validation accuracy exceeding 81% while also exhibiting a strong macro-F1 score. This research shows that utilizing contextual multilingual representations alongside simple interpretability methods offers a viable and effective approach for detecting abusive text in Tamil. The implementation of our system is publicly available at https://github.com/mirud5173/Abusive-Tamil-Comment-Detection-using-Transformer-Models
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.34.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.34.title: DLRG@DravidianLangTech 2026: Explainable Transformer-Based Detection of Abusive Tamil Text Targeting Women on Social Media
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.34.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.37.abstract: Recovering writing style prompts in low resource languages has been daunting due to diverse morphology, culturally cognizant language patterns and deficient annotated resources. As previous works have predominantly focused on binary sentiment or single attribute transfer, extensive multi-class style classification in under-resourced languages like Telegu has been vastly underexplored. In this study, we have addressed this chasm through the Telugu Prompt-Style Recovery Shared Task at DravidianLangTech@ACL 2026 (Premjith et al., 2026), framing prompt reconstruction as a nine-class classification problem with Formal, Informal, Optimistic, Pessimistic, Humorous, Serious, Inspiring, Authoritative and Persuasive as prompt styles. We have evaluated three input configurations—Change Style, Original Transcripts and Merged input style—while training three transformer based models-MuRIL, XLM-RoBERTa and IndicBERT v2 under identical conditions. Our most promising model, IndicBERT v2 with partial layer freezing and weighted cross-entropy loss, has obtained a macro-F1 of 0.2987 and accuracy of 0.299. The Change Style configuration has significantly outperformed Original and Merged inputs, indicating that explicit style changes have made tonal and meaning cues more distinctive. These results have showcased the importance of language-specific pretraining and careful input design for style-sensitive NLP in low-resource settings, ultimately securing 1st rank on the shared task.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.37.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.37.title: ERROR_500@DravidianLangTech2026: Automatic Prompt Style Classification in Telugu Using Transformer-Based Language Models
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.37.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.38.abstract: The increasing prevalence of social media has also correlated with an increase in abusive content targeting women, particularly for regional languages such as Tamil. The automatic identification of abusive content is critical for the creation of safer online spaces. In this paper, we focus on the abusive text detection of women in the context of binary text classification. We evaluated the performance of the proposed system on the abusive text detection of women using the IndicBERT, MuRIL, and Tamil-BERT models. Additionally, we propose the use of grapheme-aware normalization for the proposed system. Grapheme-aware normalization aims to maintain the structural integrity of Tamil characters at the Unicode level. The experimental results reveal that the proposed system using the Tamil-BERT model with grapheme-aware normalization achieves the best performance among the evaluated models. The proposed system achieved the third position in the shared task.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.38.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.38.title: HNK@DravidianLangTech 2026: Investigating Grapheme-Level Normalization for Abusive Tamil Text Classification
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.38.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.42.abstract: Identifying the structure of detailed sentences which show glimpses of various annotation cues, in a low resource language that is morphological rich like Telugu is a challenge. Standard baseline architectures like Multi Layer Perceptrons (MLP) struggle with low resource languages. This paper details our proposed solution for the Telugu Prompt-Style Recovery Shared Task at DravidianLangTech @ ACL 2026. We propose a Two-Stream Cross-Attention architecture that uses a shared MuRIL encoder to calculate the relationship between an original transcript and its style-shifted counterpart, helping the MLP to distinguish the styles better and catch the differences better. Through experimentation we have found out that this proposed model handles the signal dilution of the individual labels better than the rest. Our best-performing system achieved a Macro F1-score of 0.2588 on the test set, securing 2nd place out of 13 teams. We have concluded that the local transformation is the main driver for the style recovery in this task. For reproducibility, we release our implementation and experimental setup on GitHub.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.42.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.42.title: JerinWarriors@DravidianLangTech 2026: A Two-Stream Cross-Attention Approach for Prompt Recovery in Telugu
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.42.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.47.abstract: Hope speech refers to online expressions that promote positivity, encouragement, and social harmony. It fosters inclusivity and resilience, making it particularly valuable in culturally diverse and code-mixed communities. Detecting hope speech is an emerging area in computational linguistics, aimed at supporting healthier digital interactions and improving accessibility for vulnerable groups.While most of the hope speech detection work has been focused on high-resource languages, low- resource languages such as Tulu remains unexplored. In this paper, we - Team MUCS, describe our proposed system submitted to the first shared task on Hope Speech Detection in Code-Mixed Tulu, organized by DravidianLangTech@ACL 2026. As there are no pretrained language models for Tulu, we explored multiple hand crafted features - word n-grams (n = 1, 3), character n-grams (n = 1, 3), syllable n-grams (n = 1, 3) and sub-words, to train ensemble of classical Machine Learning (ML) models: i) Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB) and Logistic Regression (LR) classifiers and ii) k Nearest Neighbor (kNN) and Decision Tree (DT) classifiers, both with soft-voting. Experimental results demonstrate that feature integration effectively captures lexical, sub-lexical, and phonological cues in noisy code-mixed text. The system achieves competitive performance on both development and test datasets, highlighting the effectiveness of feature-based approaches for hope speech detection in code-mixed Tulu.An ablation study is also conducted to evaluate the contribution of multiple feature sets for hope speech detection.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.47.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.47.title: MUCS@Dravidianlangtech@ACL2026: Hope Speech Detection in Code-Mixed Tulu Language Using Multiple Features
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.47.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.48.abstract: The proliferation of misogynistic content on social media platforms is a serious problem that requires the development of automated detection systems, which is a challenging task for low-resource languages like Tamil. This study investigates the effectiveness of multilingual transformer models for identifying abusive Tamil text targeting women in social media. Results indicate that such models achieve strong baseline performance on this task. Furthermore, an ensemble of two best performing models was found to improve the classification performance further. The results also highlighted the significance of domain-specific pre-training for improving classifier performance. The best performing ensemble model achieved a weighted F1 score of 0.83 on the test set, placing our approach in first position in the shared task.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.48.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.48.title: NITC-HSR@DravidianLangTech 2026: Ensembling Multilingual Transformer Models for Detecting Abusive Tamil Text Targeting Women on Social Media
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.48.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.53.abstract: Internet memes have become a dominant and highly accessible medium for political discourse on social media. However, their multimodal nature—combining culturally specific visual symbols with code-mixed text—presents a significant challenge for automated content analysis, particularly in low-resource languages. In this study, we describe the system submitted by team RMS for the Multi-Level Political Meme Classification shared task at DravidianLangTech @ ACL 2026, focusing exclusively on the Tamil language track. We propose a robust late-fusion multimodal architecture that leverages a pre-trained ResNet-50 network for visual feature extraction and a Transformer-based model (MuRIL) for processing code-mixed Tamil text. The modalities are aligned using bidirectional cross-modal attention and combined using a Gated Multimodal Unit, allowing the model to dynamically weight the importance of visual versus textual cues. Our system ranked 11th on the official leaderboard with a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.7382. Through detailed error analysis, we demonstrate that while our gated fusion approach excels at identifying explicit trolling stances, it struggles with complex target resolution when visual and textual cues contradict.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.53.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.53.title: RMS@DravidianLangTech 2026: Multimodal Gated Fusion for Hierarchical Tamil Political Meme Classification
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.53.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.54.abstract: Political memes are widely used to express opinions, sarcasm, and ideological narratives on social media platforms. However, detecting political trolling in low-resource languages such as Tamil and Malayalam remains challenging due to limited datasets and tools. To address this problem, DravidianLangTech@ACL 2026 organized a shared task on hierarchical political meme classification.This work explores text-only models, classical multimodal fusion, and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for Tamil and Malayalam political meme classification. Our experiments include IndicBERTv2, XLM-RoBERTa, EfficientNet-based multimodal fusion, and Qwen-VL models. Among the submitted systems, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct with 4-bit QLoRA fine-tuning achieved competitive performance, ranking 3rd in the Malayalam track and 4th in the Tamil track based on weighted-F1 score. Additional post-evaluation experiments with Qwen3-VL-8B further improved macro-F1 performance, highlighting the effectiveness of VLMs for low-resource multilingual political meme classification.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.54.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.54.title: Semantica@DravidianLangTech 2026: Vision-Language Models for Hierarchical Political Meme Classification in Tamil and Malayalam
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.54.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.62.abstract: It is difficult to detect abusive language, particularly in social networks for low-resource languages like Tamil. Spelling errors, informal expressions and code-mixing make it even more challenging to read text from social media. The current work proposes a multilingual transformer-based approach to detect abusive content in Tamil text. A pretrained XLM-RoBERTa model is used to learn contextual and semantic representations from the input text. This is a general pipeline comprising preprocessing, tokenization, and binary classification (abusive / non-abusive). Experiments are performed on Tamil social media datasets that have abusive and non-abusive data. The results reveal that multilingual transformer models achieve good performance in low-resource scenarios. The proposed model attains an F1-score of 78.64%, which shows the potential of using cross-lingual pretrained models for the detection of abusive Tamil language.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.62.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.62.title: TAMILGOODBADTXT@DravidianLangTech 2026:A Multilingual Transformer-Based Approach for Abusive Language Identification in Tamil Social Media
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.62.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.67.abstract: Abusive comment detection in low-resource languages poses significant challenges, particularly when targeting gender-based abuse on social media platforms. This work presents our system for ’Abusive Tamil text targeting women on social media’ at DravidianLangTech@ACL 2026. We introduce nine handcrafted lexicon features integrated with pretrained multilingual transformer embeddings and evaluate their effectiveness in classifying Tamil online comments as abusive or non-abusive. To better understand their impact, we compare model performance with and without these lexical attributes across multiple transformer architectures. Our best-performing model, XLM-RoBERTa-Large, achieved a macro F1-score of 81.71%, securing 15th rank in the competition. The findings indicate that larger multilingual models generalize more effectively to unseen data compared to smaller domain-specific models, while the addition of lexical features yields only mild gains.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.67.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.67.title: TriVector@DravidianLangTech 2026: Abusive Tamil Text Detection on Social Media Using Lexicon-Augmented Transformers
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.67.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.70.abstract: While Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems have shown impressive performance in languages having sufficient annotated speech data like English, their performance is still limited for low-resource, dialect rich languages like Tamil. Tamil poses further challenges because of its extremely high regional variation in dialects that manifest in varying vocabulary, pronunciations, and even syntactic structures. To address these challenges, we present a unified framework WhisTam based on the Whisper medium model, which performs speech transcription and dialect classification jointly within a single system. Our method is evaluated against speech samples from four regional dialects and achieves a macro F1-score of 0.53 and a Word Error Rate (WER) of 0.55 for dialect classification and transcription respectively, ranking 2nd in the dialect classification task and 3rd in the transcription task in the DravidianLangTech@ACL 2026 shared task on Dialect-based Speech Recognition and Classification in Tamil. These findings emphasize the challenges in dialectal Tamil ASR as well as the promise of multi-task learning for low-resource languages. Our implementation is publicly available at: https://github.com/rwd51/DravidianLangTech-Wave2Word.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.70.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.70.title: Wave2Word@DravidianLangTech 2026: WhisTam: A unified framework for dialect based Tamil speech recognition and classification
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.70.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.8.abstract: This paper introduces Thiruppugazh-KG, a semantically annotated dataset and knowledge graph derived from the Thiruppugazh corpus, a 14th-century collection of 1,335 Tamil devotional hymns composed by Arunagirinathar. The dataset includes annotations for entities, devotional themes, mythological events, philosophical concepts, imagery, and sacred locations mentioned in each hymn. Using these annotations, we construct a Neo4j-based knowledge graph that models relationships between hymns and their associated cultural and narrative elements. Graph analytics, including PageRank, are applied to identify prominent entities and sacred locations within the corpus. The resulting resource provides a structured representation of Tamil devotional literature and supports computational analysis of cultural texts in low-resource languages.
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.8.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.8.title: Thiruppugazh-KG Dataset: A Manually Annotated Resource for Computational Analysis of Tamil Devotional Literature
acl:2026.dravidianlangtech-1.8.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Speech, Vision, and Language Technologies for Dravidian Languages

acl:2026.eamt-1.10.abstract: Code-mixed and Romanized texts are widely used in digital content, yet they remain largely underexplored for many low-resource languages, including Sinhala. The scarcity of high-quality parallel data has limited progress on downstream tasks, such as machine translation and transliteration. We introduce SinMix2Mono, the largest manually annotated parallel training dataset, followed by the first gold standard benchmark and code-mixed transliteration ambiguity corpora for code-mixed romanized Sinhala to Sinhala conversion. The dataset comprises approximately 25,000 real-world sentences collected from social media, covering diverse domains and authentic code-mixing patterns. To ensure high-quality translations, we used an annotation pipeline that combined rule-based transliteration, LLM-assisted translation, and human validation. The golden test dataset, which includes 2549 sentences, and the code-mixed transliteration ambiguity test were validated by three annotators, yielding Gwet’s AC1 scores of 0.7465 and 0.7068, respectively. We benchmarked nine systems, including statistical, neural and commercial LLMs. SinMix2Mono provides a robust training and evaluation resource, establishing a strong benchmark for future research on Sinhala code-mixed translation and transliteration.
acl:2026.eamt-1.10.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 26th Annual Conference of the European Association for Machine Translation (Volume 1)

glossary.explanation_id: Transliterasi adalah proses mengubah teks dari satu sistem tulisan ke sistem tulisan lainnya berdasarkan korespondensi fonetik tanpa mengubah bahasanya.
Code-mixed mengacu pada fenomena pencampuran dua bahasa atau lebih dalam satu ucapan atau percakapan secara bergantian.
Low-resource merujuk pada bahasa atau domain yang memiliki ketersediaan data pelatihan dan sumber daya komputasi yang sangat terbatas.
Benchmark adalah standar atau uji acuan yang digunakan untuk mengevaluasi dan membandingkan performa berbagai model atau sistem secara objektif.
Fine-tuning adalah proses melatih ulang model terlatih (pretrained model) menggunakan data tambahan agar kinerjanya optimal pada tugas spesifik tertentu.
Zero-shot adalah metode pengujian di mana model harus menyelesaikan tugas baru tanpa diberikan contoh demonstrasi terlebih dahulu di dalam *prompt*.
Few-shot adalah metode evaluasi di mana model diberikan beberapa contoh teladan di dalam *prompt* sebelum diminta untuk memproses data pengujian.
Encoder-decoder adalah arsitektur *neural network* yang memetakan teks masukan menjadi representasi perantara melalui *encoder* sebelum menghasilkan teks keluaran melalui *decoder*.

background.en: Code-mixed and romanized texts are widely used in digital content and social media platforms, yet they remain largely underexplored for low-resource languages such as Sinhala. The severe scarcity of high-quality parallel data has hindered progress on downstream tasks such as machine translation and transliteration. Addressing this gap requires robust resources capable of handling noisy, non-standard text formats that mix native script transliterations with embedded English words.
background.id: Teks *code-mixed* dan romanisasi banyak digunakan pada konten digital dan platform media sosial, namun masih belum banyak dieksplorasi untuk bahasa *low-resource* seperti bahasa Sinhala. Kelangkaan data paralel berkualitas tinggi yang parah telah menghambat kemajuan pada tugas *downstream* seperti terjemahan mesin dan transliterasi. Mengatasi kesenjangan ini memerlukan sumber daya yang tangguh yang mampu menangani format teks yang bising dan non-standar yang mencampurkan transliterasi aksara asli dengan kata-kata bahasa Inggris yang disematkan.

contributions.en: This study introduces SinMix2Mono, comprising approximately 25,000 real-world sentences collected from social media across diverse domains. It provides the first manually annotated gold standard dataset for code-mixed romanized Sinhala translation, a dedicated code-mixed transliteration ambiguity dataset, and a rigorous benchmark of nine diverse systems ranging from rule-based approaches to neural models and commercial large language models.
contributions.id: Studi ini memperkenalkan SinMix2Mono, yang mencakup sekitar 25.000 kalimat dunia nyata yang dikumpulkan dari media sosial di berbagai domain. Studi ini menyediakan *dataset* *gold-standard* beranotasi manual pertama untuk terjemahan bahasa Sinhala romanisasi *code-mixed*, *dataset* ambiguitas transliterasi *code-mixed* khusus, dan *benchmark* ketat dari sembilan sistem berbeda mulai dari pendekatan *rule-based* hingga model *neural* dan *large language model* komersial.

future_work.en: The authors note that the dataset is restricted to Latin source text and Sinhala Unicode targets with filtered emojis and special characters. Future work should focus on expanding the dataset to improve both scale and linguistic diversity.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa *dataset* ini terbatas pada teks sumber Latin dan target Sinhala Unicode dengan emoji serta karakter khusus yang telah difilter. Penelitian mendatang harus berfokus pada perluasan *dataset* untuk meningkatkan skala dan keragaman linguistik.

method.en: Data collection leveraged an automated algorithm to scrape YouTube comments combined with filtered instances from the Swa-Bhasha dataset. The annotation pipeline integrated trigram-based rule transliteration, LLM-assisted translation using Claude models with few-shot prompting, and meticulous human validation by native speakers. Evaluation utilized SacreBLEU, chrF++, and BERTScore metrics across baseline systems, zero-shot and few-shot LLMs, and fine-tuned encoder-decoder models.
method.id: Pengumpulan data memanfaatkan algoritma otomatis untuk mengeruk komentar YouTube yang dikombinasikan dengan instance yang difilter dari *dataset* Swa-Bhasha. *Pipeline* anotasi mengintegrasikan transliterasi aturan berbasis trigram, terjemahan berbantuan *large language model* menggunakan model Claude dengan *few-shot prompting*, dan validasi manusia yang teliti oleh penutur asli. Evaluasi menggunakan metrik SacreBLEU, chrF++, dan BERTScore pada sistem *baseline*, *large language model* *zero-shot* dan *few-shot*, serta model *encoder-decoder* yang telah di-*fine-tune*.

related_work.en: Prior research on Sinhala has largely focused on native transliteration datasets, such as the SwaBhasha series and various ambiguity evaluation sets, which lack support for broader code-mixing or translation settings. Existing code-mixed datasets for other low-resource languages, including Hindi and Urdu corpora like PHINC and HinGE, demonstrate the utility of social media data for similar tasks. However, prior code-mixed Sinhala resources remain extremely limited in scale and predominantly isolated to single studies.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya mengenai bahasa Sinhala sebagian besar berfokus pada *dataset* transliterasi asli, seperti seri SwaBhasha dan berbagai set evaluasi ambiguitas, yang kurang mendukungh pengaturan *code-mixed* atau terjemahan yang lebih luas. *Dataset* *code-mixed* yang ada untuk bahasa *low-resource* lainnya, termasuk korpus bahasa Hindi dan Urdu seperti PHINC dan HinGE, menunjukkan kegunaan data media sosial untuk tugas serupa. Meskipun demikian, sumber daya *code-mixed* bahasa Sinhala sebelumnya tetap sangat terbatas dalam skalanya dan sebagian besar terisolasi pada studi tunggal.

results.en: Neural machine translation models fine-tuned on the SinMix2Mono corpus achieved the highest overall performance, with Swa-Bhasha mBART reaching a BLEU score of 49.70 and BERTScore of 81.19. Commercial LLMs like Gemini 2.5 Flash-lite and Qwen-3 Max showed competitive performance and benefited significantly from few-shot prompting, whereas traditional rule-based and statistical trigram models performed poorly.
results.id: Model terjemahan mesin *neural* yang di-*fine-tune* pada korpus SinMix2Mono mencapai performa keseluruhan tertinggi, di mana Swa-Bhasha mBART mencapai skor BLEU sebesar 49,70 dan BERTScore sebesar 81,19. *Large language model* komersial seperti Gemini 2.5 Flash-lite and Qwen-3 Max menunjukkan performa yang kompetitif dan mendapat manfaat signifikan dari *few-shot prompting*, sedangkan model berbasis aturan tradisional dan trigram statistik memiliki performa yang buruk.

tldr.en: This paper introduces SinMix2Mono, the largest parallel training dataset and gold standard benchmark for translating and transliterating code-mixed romanized Sinhala into native Sinhala. Evaluation across nine systems demonstrates that neural models and fine-tuned architectures significantly outperform traditional rule-based and statistical approaches.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan SinMix2Mono, *dataset* pelatihan paralel dan *benchmark* *gold-standard* terbesar untuk menerjemahkan dan mentransliterasikan bahasa Sinhala romanisasi *code-mixed* ke dalam bahasa Sinhala asli. Evaluasi pada sembilan sistem menunjukkan bahwa model *neural* dan arsitektur *fine-tuning* mengungguli pendekatan *rule-based* dan statistik tradisional secara signifikan.

acl:2026.eamt-1.10.title: SinMix2Mono: A Dataset for Code-mixed Romanized Sinhala Translation and Transliteration
acl:2026.eamt-1.10.venue: Proceedings of the 26th Annual Conference of the European Association for Machine Translation (Volume 1)

acl:2026.eamt-1.13.abstract: Most machine translation datasets come with a certain level of noise, and strategies for handling such data need to be robust and efficient. Data selection and filtering are challenging and may depend on expensive language-specific tools that are not necessarily available, especially for low-resource languages. This paper looks at training strategies that combine cheap heuristic filters with curriculum learning to implement iterative procedures that robustly operate on raw noisy data without expensive prior preprocessing and data selection. The intuition is that we can cluster data into buckets with varying noise levels and use different sets of buckets at different stages of MT model training. We test various strategies and compare them to pre-filtering approaches for a diverse set of low-resource languages and conclude that curriculum learning can improve robustness but does not necessarily lead to improved translation performance. Overall, the experiments demonstrate the importance of proper experimental workflows, which cannot easily generalize from one language pair and scenario to another.
acl:2026.eamt-1.13.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 26th Annual Conference of the European Association for Machine Translation (Volume 1)

glossary.explanation_id: Sebuah strategi pelatihan *machine learning* di mana data diberikan secara bertahap mulai dari contoh yang paling mudah hingga yang paling sulit.
Pendekatan berbasis aturan sederhana yang cepat dan murah secara komputasi tanpa memerlukan pelatihan model yang kompleks.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain memiliki ketersediaan data dan sumber daya komputasi yang sangat terbatas.
Algoritma *unsupervised machine learning* yang mengelompokkan data ke dalam sejumlah *cluster* berdasarkan kemiripan fitur.
Kumpulan teks yang terdiri dari kalimat-kalimat dalam satu bahasa beserta terjemahannya yang sepadan dalam bahasa lain.
Arsitektur jaringan saraf tiruan yang dilatih untuk merekonstruksi data masukan aslinya.

background.en: Most machine translation datasets contain significant levels of noise from web crawls, requiring robust and efficient strategies for handling such data. Data selection and filtering remain challenging and often rely on expensive language-specific tools that are unavailable for low-resource languages. The paper addresses the gap in operating on raw noisy data without expensive prior preprocessing by proposing iterative training strategies.
background.id: Sebagian besar *dataset* *machine translation* mengandung tingkat kebisingan yang signifikan dari *web crawl*, sehingga memerlukan strategi yang tangguh dan efisien untuk menangani data tersebut. Seleksi dan *filtering* data tetap menjadi tantangan dan sering kali mengandalkan alat spesifik bahasa yang mahal dan tidak tersedia untuk bahasa *low-resource*. Makalah ini mengatasi celah dalam mengoperasikan data bising mentah tanpa pra-pemrosesan awal yang mahal dengan mengusulkan strategi pelatihan iteratif.

contributions.en: The paper introduces an unsupervised data cleaning approach combining heuristic scores, K-means clustering, and multi-stage curriculum learning to divide noisy data into buckets of varying noise levels without requiring clean training data. It evaluates adaptive self-paced learning strategies across diverse low-resource language pairs, demonstrating that heuristic-based curriculum methods can avoid pitfalls like language identification failures.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan pendekatan pembersihan data nir-awas (*unsupervised*) yang menggabungkan skor *heuristic*, *K-means clustering*, dan *curriculum learning* multi-tahap untuk membagi data bising ke dalam *bucket* dengan tingkat kebisingan bervariasi tanpa memerlukan data latihan yang bersih. Pendekatan ini mengevaluasi strategi *self-paced learning* adaptif di berbagai pasangan bahasa *low-resource*, yang menunjukkan bahwa metode *curriculum* berbasis *heuristic* dapat menghindari kendala seperti kegagalan identifikasi bahasa.

future_work.en: The authors suggest studying the proposed curriculum learning method for language pairs not covered by pretrained cleaning models, exploring alternative ways of combining heuristic filtering with curriculum learning, and conducting more thorough analyses of overall energy consumption.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyarankan untuk mempelajari metode *curriculum learning* yang diusulkan untuk pasangan bahasa yang tidak tercakup oleh *pretrained model* pembersihan, mengeksplorasi cara alternatif untuk menggabungkan *heuristic filtering* dengan *curriculum learning*, serta melakukan analisis yang lebih menyeluruh mengenai konsumsi energi secara keseluruhan.

method.en: The authors use the raw HPLT v1.2 parallel datasets for English paired with Basque, Irish, Macedonian, Nynorsk, and Swahili. After exact and near-duplicate removal, sentence pairs are scored using OpusFilter heuristic features without thresholds, standardized, and clustered via K-means into buckets sorted by cleanness. Models are trained using MarianNMT with a Transformer base architecture, evaluating strategies like Baby Steps and adaptive self-paced learning against baselines such as Bicleaner AI and static OpusFilter configurations.
method.id: Para penulis menggunakan *dataset* paralel mentah HPLT v1.2 untuk bahasa Inggris yang dipasangkan dengan bahasa Basque, Irlandia, Makedonia, Nynorsk, dan Swahili. Setelah penghapusan duplikat persis dan hampir persis, pasangan kalimat dinilai menggunakan fitur *heuristic* OpusFilter tanpa *threshold*, distandarisasi, dan dikelompokkan melalui *K-means* ke dalam *bucket* yang diurutkan berdasarkan kebersihan. Model dilatih menggunakan MarianNMT dengan arsitektur dasar *Transformer*, mengevaluasi strategi seperti *Baby Steps* dan *self-paced learning* adaptif terhadap *baseline* seperti Bicleaner AI dan konfigurasi statis OpusFilter.

related_work.en: Previous data cleaning methods involve inexpensive heuristics from the Moses framework and OpusFilter, hard rule filters from Bicleaner, or state-of-the-art neural classifiers like Bicleaner AI, dual conditional cross-entropy, and sentence embedding similarities. While neural methods require significant computational resources and clean parallel data for training, existing curriculum learning approaches such as those by Kocmi and Bojar, Platanios et al., and Mohiuddin et al. organize data by difficulty or use pre-calculated cleanness scores with continuous schedulers.
related_work.id: Metode pembersihan data sebelumnya melibatkan *heuristic* murah dari *framework* Moses dan OpusFilter, *filter* aturan keras dari Bicleaner, atau *neural classifier* canggih seperti Bicleaner AI, *dual conditional cross-entropy*, dan kemiripan *sentence embedding*. Meskipun metode neural memerlukan sumber daya komputasi yang besar dan data paralel bersih untuk pelatihan, pendekatan *curriculum learning* yang ada seperti oleh Kocmi dan Bojar, Platanios et al., serta Mohiuddin et al. mengorganisasikan data berdasarkan tingkat kesulitan atau menggunakan skor kebersihan pra-hitung dengan *continuous scheduler*.

results.en: Bicleaner AI and static OpusFilter achieve high COMET scores across most language pairs, showing that simple heuristics can rival neural methods. However, static OpusFilter completely fails on Nynorsk due to language identification errors mislabeling it as Norwegian, whereas curriculum learning methods successfully utilize data that would otherwise be discarded, mitigating such failures despite achieving lower overall translation performance compared to direct filtering.
results.id: Bicleaner AI dan OpusFilter statis mencapai skor COMET yang tinggi di sebagian besar pasangan bahasa, menunjukkan bahwa *heuristic* sederhana dapat bersaing dengan metode neural. Namun, OpusFilter statis mengalami kegagalan total pada bahasa Nynorsk karena kesalahan identifikasi bahasa yang melabelinya sebagai Norwegia, sedangkan metode *curriculum learning* berhasil memanfaatkan data yang seharusnya dibuang, memitigasi kegagalan tersebut meskipun mencapai performa terjemahan secara keseluruhan yang lebih rendah dibandingkan *filtering* langsung.

tldr.en: This paper investigates training strategies combining cheap heuristic filters with curriculum learning to handle noisy machine translation datasets. The experiments conclude that curriculum learning improves robustness but does not necessarily enhance translation performance.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti strategi pelatihan yang menggabungkan *heuristic filter* murah dengan *curriculum learning* untuk menangani *dataset* *machine translation* yang bising. Eksperimen menyimpulkan bahwa *curriculum learning* meningkatkan ketahanan tetapi tidak selalu memperbaiki performa terjemahan.

acl:2026.eamt-1.13.title: The Challenge of Finding Robust and Efficient Strategies for Training Machine Translation Models with Noisy Data
acl:2026.eamt-1.13.venue: Proceedings of the 26th Annual Conference of the European Association for Machine Translation (Volume 1)

acl:2026.eamt-1.20.abstract: EU legislation is equally authentic and legally binding in all 24 official languages, rendering high-quality translation a legal obligation rather than a mere choice. Therefore, high-quality language technology supporting translation processes in all EU languages are essential for language professionals at the European Parliament (EP). This paper investigates whether domain-specific fine-tuning of an open-weight Large Language Model (LLM) yields consistently larger quality gains on legislative text compared to generic text, in all 23 EU target languages from English. We evaluate ten experimental conditions: base model, in-domain and cross-domain fine-tuning, sequential generic-then-legislative fine-tuning, and zero-shot Claude Sonnet 4.6 as a proprietary reference. We analyse BLEU, chrF, TER, and COMET metrics on nearly 700,000 segments. Results confirm the hypothesis for all 23 languages: legislative fine-tuning enhances BLEU by +12.30 compared to +7.10 for generic fine-tuning, demonstrating a consistent advantage of +5.20 BLEU in all the metrics. The fine-tuned EuroLLM-22B decisively outperforms Claude Sonnet 4.6, Anthropic’s latest frontier model, on both domains, highlighting that targeted adaptation of a smaller open-weight model can surpass a state-of-the-art proprietary system. Cross-domain transfer within institutional domain is positive for all languages, with no catastrophic forgetting. Low-resource languages such as Irish and Maltese benefit the most from fine-tuning, while a divergence between BLEU and COMET rankings for some languages underlines the need of evaluation metrics alongside traditional measures.
acl:2026.eamt-1.20.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 26th Annual Conference of the European Association for Machine Translation (Volume 1)

glossary.explanation_id: Proses melatih ulang *large language model* yang sudah ada menggunakan *data* domain khusus untuk meningkatkan kinerjanya pada tugas tertentu.
Fenomena di mana sebuah model kehilangan kemampuan atau pengetahuan lamanya setelah mempelajari *data* atau tugas baru.
Metode evaluasi di mana model diminta menyelesaikan tugas tanpa diberikan contoh demonstrasi sebelumnya di dalam *prompt*.
Status model kecerdasan buatan di mana bobot parameternya dibagikan secara publik agar dapat diunduh dan dimodifikasi.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain memiliki ketersediaan *data* latih dan sumber daya digital yang sangat terbatas.
Teknik *parameter-efficient fine-tuning* yang melatih matriks peringkat rendah untuk membekukan sebagian besar parameter model utama.

background.en: The European Union operates under full multilingualism, requiring legislation to be equally authentic and legally binding in 24 official languages. This creates an immense translation challenge for the European Parliament, where precision, consistency, and terminological exactness are legally mandated. While general-purpose large language models offer promising translation baselines, legislative texts possess rigid structural conventions, specialized terminology, and precise cross-references that distinguish them from general text. The paper addresses whether general-purpose models can adequately handle these demands without domain-specific adaptation.
background.id: Uni Eropa beroperasi di bawah prinsip multilingualisme penuh, yang mewajibkan undang-undang memiliki keaslian dan kekuatan hukum yang setara dalam 24 bahasa resmi. Hal ini menciptakan tantangan terjemahan yang luar biasa bagi Parlemen Eropa, di mana presisi, konsistensi, dan ketepatan terminologi diwajibkan secara hukum. Meskipun *large language model* serbaguna menawarkan *baseline* terjemahan yang menjanjikan, teks legislatif memiliki konvensi struktural yang kaku, terminologi khusus, dan rujukan silang yang presisi, yang membedakannya dari teks umum. Makalah ini membahas apakah model serbaguna mampu menangani tuntutan tersebut secara memadai tanpa adaptasi spesifik domain.

contributions.en: The paper makes three primary contributions to institutional translation research. First, it provides a rigorous experimental design to measure the differential impact of domain adaptation in a multilingual setting across 24 official EU languages. Second, it produces parallel evaluation datasets for both legislative and generic institutional domains. Third, it offers practical guidance for institutional translation services considering the integration of fine-tuned open-weight models into their production workflows.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memberikan tiga kontribusi utama untuk penelitian terjemahan institusional. Pertama, makalah ini menyediakan desain eksperimen yang ketat untuk mengukur dampak diferensial dari adaptasi domain dalam pengaturan multilinguasa di 24 bahasa resmi Uni Eropa. Kedua, makalah ini menghasilkan *dataset* evaluasi paralel untuk domain legislatif maupun institusional generik. Ketiga, makalah ini menawarkan panduan praktis bagi layanan terjemahan institusional yang mempertimbangkan integrasi model *open-weight* yang telah di-*fine-tuning* ke dalam alur kerja produksi mereka.

future_work.en: The authors outline several directions for future research, including integrating the produced datasets into the AI4TRAD project for systematic translation bias analysis, conducting human evaluations with specialized translators for qualitative assessment of legal equivalence, exploring retrieval-augmented generation and alternative prompt strategies, and extending the framework to smaller model architectures and non-European foundational models.
future_work.id: Para penulis menggariskan beberapa arah untuk penelitian masa depan, termasuk mengintegrasikan *dataset* yang dihasilkan ke dalam proyek *AI4TRAD* untuk analisis bias terjemahan secara sistematis, melakukan evaluasi manusia dengan penerjemah spesialis untuk penilaian kualitatif atas ekuivalensi hukum, mengeksplorasi *retrieval-augmented generation* serta strategi *prompt* alternatif, dan memperluas kerangka kerja ke arsitektur model yang lebih kecil serta model dasar non-Eropa.

method.en: The study uses EuroLLM-22B as the base model and evaluates ten experimental conditions, including base model evaluation, in-domain fine-tuning, cross-domain fine-tuning, sequential generic-then-legislative fine-tuning, and zero-shot Claude Sonnet 4.6 as a proprietary reference. The researchers construct two parallel corpora of nearly 600,000 segments each in 24 languages, extracting data from EUramis translation memories while strictly controlling for segment length distributions and applying a four-stage filtering pipeline to eliminate noise and duplicates. Fine-tuning is performed efficiently using LoRA adapters on attention projection matrices.
method.id: Studi ini menggunakan *EuroLLM-22B* sebagai model dasar dan mengevaluasi sepuluh kondisi eksperimental, termasuk evaluasi model dasar, *fine-tuning* dalam domain, *fine-tuning* lintas domain, *fine-tuning* sekuensial generik ke legislatif, serta *Claude Sonnet 4.6* dengan pendekatan *zero-shot* sebagai pembanding komersial. Para peneliti membangun dua korpus paralel dengan hampir 600.000 segmen masing-masing dalam 24 bahasa, mengekstrak data dari memori terjemahan *EUramis* sembari mengontrol distribusi panjang segmen secara ketat dan menerapkan tahapan penyaringan empat tahap untuk menghilangkan derau serta duplikat. *Fine-tuning* dilakukan secara efisien menggunakan adaptor *LoRA* pada matriks proyeksi atensi.

related_work.en: Prior research in neural machine translation extensively examines domain adaptation through data-centric, model-centric, and inference-time methods, noting that in-domain adaptation often risks catastrophic forgetting. Studies on legal translation highlight the critical importance of consistent terminology and demonstrate that fine-tuned models significantly outperform models trained from scratch. Furthermore, previous initiatives such as the Neural Translation for the European Union project and various European multilingual NLP resources established foundations for institutional translation, while recent parameter-efficient methods like LoRA made large model adaptation computationally feasible.
related_work.id: Penelitian terdahulu dalam *neural machine translation* secara ekstensif mengkaji adaptasi domain melalui metode yang berpusat pada data, model, dan waktu inferensi, dengan catatan bahwa adaptasi dalam domain sering kali berisiko memicu *catastrophic forgetting*. Studi tentang terjemahan hukum menyoroti pentingnya konsistensi terminologi dan menunjukkan bahwa model yang di-*fine-tuning* mengungguli model yang dilatih dari awal secara signifikan. Selain itu, inisiatif sebelumnya seperti proyek *Neural Translation for the European Union* dan berbagai sumber daya *NLP* multilingualisme Eropa membangun fondasi untuk terjemahan institusional, sementara metode efisiensi parameter terkini seperti *LoRA* membuat adaptasi model besar menjadi layak secara komputasi.

results.en: Experiments across nearly 700,000 evaluated segments confirm the central hypothesis: legislative fine-tuning enhances BLEU by +12.30 compared to +7.10 for generic fine-tuning, yielding a consistent +5.20 advantage across BLEU, chrF, TER, and COMET. Sequential fine-tuning achieves the highest legislative score at 63.17 BLEU. Furthermore, the fine-tuned EuroLLM-22B decisively outperforms Claude Sonnet 4.6 by over 8 BLEU points on legislative text. Cross-domain transfer shows no catastrophic forgetting, and lower-resource languages such as Irish and Maltese experience the largest gains.
results.id: Eksperimen pada hampir 700.000 segmen yang dievaluasi mengonfirmasi hipotesis utama: *fine-tuning* legislatif meningkatkan skor *BLEU* sebesar +12.30 dibandingkan +7.10 untuk *fine-tuning* generik, menghasilkan keunggulan konsisten sebesar +5.20 di seluruh metrik *BLEU*, *chrF*, *TER*, dan *COMET*. *Fine-tuning* sekuensial mencapai skor legislatif tertinggi sebesar 63.17 *BLEU*. Lebih lanjut, *EuroLLM-22B* yang telah di-*fine-tuning* secara telak mengungguli *Claude Sonnet 4.6* dengan selisih lebih dari 8 poin *BLEU* pada teks legislatif. Transfer lintas domain menunjukkan tidak adanya *catastrophic forgetting*, dan bahasa-bahasa dengan sumber daya rendah seperti bahasa Irlandia serta bahasa Malta memperoleh peningkatan terbesar.

tldr.en: This paper investigates whether domain-specific fine-tuning of an open-weight large language model yields larger quality gains on legislative translation compared to generic text across 23 European Union languages. Results demonstrate that legislative fine-tuning consistently outperforms generic fine-tuning and surpasses state-of-the-art proprietary models without catastrophic forgetting.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyelidiki apakah *fine-tuning* spesifik domain pada *large language model* *open-weight* menghasilkan peningkatan kualitas yang lebih besar pada terjemahan legislatif dibandingkan teks generik di 23 bahasa Uni Eropa. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa *fine-tuning* legislatif secara konsisten mengungguli *fine-tuning* generik serta melampaui model komersial mutakhir tanpa mengalami *catastrophic forgetting*.

acl:2026.eamt-1.20.title: One Size Does Not Fit All: Why EU Legislative Translation Demands Domain-Specific Fine-Tuning of LLMs
acl:2026.eamt-1.20.venue: Proceedings of the 26th Annual Conference of the European Association for Machine Translation (Volume 1)

acl:2026.eamt-1.23.abstract: Term injection in machine translation is undergoing a paradigm shift in the era of large language models (LLMs). Although recent shared-task results suggest near-saturation for sentence-level term injection from pre-defined glossaries, it remains unclear whether this also holds in more challenging settings. We address this question with a custom test set for legal translation from Italian into South Tyrolean German, a non-dominant and under-resourced language variety. We cover three terminology challenges: simple term injection, localisation of abbreviated forms, and homonym disambiguation. We focus on Reasoning Models (RMs) leveraging Test-Time Scaling, comparing them with different architectures and contributing a human analysis of reasoning traces. We find that reasoning offers little benefit for simple term insertion, but yields clear gains for semantically complex cases such as homonym disambiguation. However, human evaluation of reasoning traces shows that these gains do not necessarily reflect robust and factually grounded translation-specific reasoning. We further show that without external terminological resources, even state-of-the-art RMs struggle to retrieve correct terminology for a non-dominant variety, while NMT small models remain competitive when trained on in-domain bilingual corpora. Based on these findings, we propose data collection strategies for inducing translation-specific reasoning, frameworks for adapting to and evaluating terminology across many language varieties, and terminology challenges beyond simple term injection.

glossary.explanation_id: Metode alokasi komputasi tambahan saat *inference* untuk meningkatkan kemampuan pemecahan masalah pada *large language model*.
Proses pengelompokan bentuk infleksi suatu kata sehingga dapat dianalisis sebagai item tunggal berdasarkan bentuk dasarnya.
Basis data terstruktur yang menyimpan istilah khusus beserta definisi, konteks penggunaan, dan padanannya.
Proses pelatihan lanjutan pada *model bahasa* yang sudah dilatih sebelumnya menggunakan data domain tertentu.
Serangkaian langkah penalaran perantara yang dihasilkan oleh *large language model* sebelum mencapai jawaban akhir.
Pendekatan *terjemahan mesin* yang menggunakan jaringan saraf tiruan untuk memprediksi kemungkinan seluruh kalimat.

background.en: Term injection in machine translation has reached near-saturation for sentence-level tasks using pre-defined glossaries, but its effectiveness in more challenging settings remains unclear. Legal translation into non-dominant and under-resourced language varieties, such as South Tyrolean German from Italian, requires strict adherence to system-bound legal terminology and regional variation. Without proper guidance, models tend to override non-dominant variants with dominant ones, posing severe risks of misunderstandings, financial loss, or legal liability.
background.id: Penyuntikan istilah dalam terjemahan mesin telah mencapai titik jenuh untuk tugas tingkat kalimat menggunakan glosarium pra-definisi, namun keefektifannya dalam pengaturan yang lebih menantang masih belum jelas. Penerjemahan hukum ke dalam variasi bahasa yang non-dominan dan minim sumber daya, seperti bahasa Jerman Tirol Selatan dari bahasa Italia, memerlukan kepatuhan ketat pada terminologi hukum yang terikat sistem dan variasi regional. Tanpa panduan yang tepat, model cenderung menimpa varian non-dominan dengan varian dominan, yang menimbulkan risiko kesalahpahaman, kerugian finansial, atau tanggung jawab hukum.

contributions.en: The paper contributes a custom test set called LegISTyr for legal translation from Italian to South Tyrolean German, covering simple term injection, abbreviated forms, and homonym disambiguation. It evaluates reasoning models against other architectures using automated metrics and a qualitative human evaluation of reasoning traces. Furthermore, it proposes data collection strategies for translation-specific reasoning, variety-aware terminology adaptation frameworks, and knowledge-based terminology learning from structured termbases.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyumbangkan *test set* khusus bernama LegISTyr untuk penerjemahan hukum dari bahasa Italia ke bahasa Jerman Tirol Selatan, yang mencakup penyuntikan istilah sederhana, bentuk singkatan, dan disambiguasi homonim. Makalah ini mengevaluasi *reasoning model* terhadap arsitektur lain menggunakan metrik otomatis dan evaluasi manusia kualitatif terhadap jejak penalaran. Selanjutnya, makalah ini mengusulkan strategi pengumpulan data untuk penalaran khusus terjemahan, kerangka kerja adaptasi terminologi yang sadar variasi, dan pembelajaran terminologi berbasis pengetahuan dari *termbase* terstruktur.

future_work.en: The authors suggest developing variety-aware terminology injection systems, leveraging structured knowledge from termbases for knowledge-based terminology learning, and adopting data collection methods like think-aloud protocols and translation difficulty estimators to improve adaptive compute allocation in reasoning models.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyarankan pengembangan sistem penyuntikan terminologi yang sadar variasi, memanfaatkan pengetahuan terstruktur dari *termbase* untuk pembelajaran terminologi berbasis pengetahuan, serta mengadopsi metode pengumpulan data seperti *think-aloud protocol* dan estimator kesulitan terjemahan untuk meningkatkan alokasi komputasi adaptif pada *reasoning model*.

method.en: The authors evaluate closed and open models, including Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1, and GPT models, alongside specialized neural machine translation systems fine-tuned on an in-house corpus of South Tyrolean legal sentence pairs. Evaluation relies on a custom four-step term-matching pipeline that handles lemmatization, compound splitting, and fuzzy matching, combined with MetricX-24-XL for fluency. A qualitative human evaluation is conducted by legal translators using a taxonomy of reasoning patterns and flaws.
method.id: Para penulis mengevaluasi model tertutup dan terbuka, termasuk Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1, dan model GPT, beserta sistem *neural machine translation* khusus yang telah melalui *fine-tuning* pada korpus internal yang terdiri dari pasangan kalimat hukum Tirol Selatan. Evaluasi mengandalkan *pipeline* pencocokan istilah empat langkah khusus yang menangani *lemmatization*, pemisahan kata majemuk, dan *fuzzy matching*, yang dikombinasikan dengan MetricX-24-XL untuk kelancaran. Evaluasi manusia kualitatif dilakukan oleh penerjemah hukum menggunakan taksonomi pola dan kelemahan penalaran.

related_work.en: Prior research has explored term injection through shared tasks and prompt-based methods, indicating high sentence-level saturation. Other studies have examined reasoning large language models, test-time scaling, and reinforcement learning for logical and mathematical tasks, while early translation studies focused on think-aloud protocols and translation difficulty. However, existing work has largely overlooked the challenges of non-dominant language varieties and the factual grounding of internal reasoning traces in specialized translation.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya telah mengeksplorasi penyuntikan istilah melalui *shared task* dan metode berbasis *prompt*, yang mengindikasikan kejenuhan tingkat kalimat yang tinggi. Studi lain telah menguji *large language model* penalar, *test-time scaling*, dan *reinforcement learning* untuk tugas logika dan matematika, sementara studi terjemahan awal berfokus pada *think-aloud protocol* dan kesulitan penerjemahan. Namun, pekerjaan yang ada sebagian besar mengabaikan tantangan variasi bahasa non-dominan dan landasan faktual dari jejak penalaran internal dalam terjemahan khusus.

results.en: Reasoning offers little benefit for simple term injection and abbreviation tasks, where models already achieve near-perfect rates, but yields clear gains for homonym disambiguation. However, human evaluation reveals that reasoning traces often exhibit unfaithfulness, rumination, and lack factual grounding. Without external resources, state-of-the-art reasoning models struggle with non-dominant terminology, whereas small neural machine translation models trained on parallel corpora remain highly competitive.
results.id: Penalaran memberikan sedikit manfaat untuk tugas penyuntikan istilah sederhana dan singkatan, di mana model telah mencapai tingkat kesempurnaan yang tinggi, namun memberikan peningkatan yang jelas untuk disambiguasi homonim. Namun, evaluasi manusia mengungkapkan bahwa jejak penalaran sering kali menunjukkan ketidaksetiaan, perenungan berlebihan, dan kurangnya landasan faktual. Tanpa sumber daya eksternal, *reasoning model* tercanggih kesulitan dengan terminologi non-dominan, sedangkan model *neural machine translation* kecil yang dilatih pada korpus paralel tetap sangat kompetitif.

tldr.en: This paper investigates reasoning models using test-time scaling for legal terminology translation into a non-dominant language variety. The authors find that while reasoning helps in semantically complex tasks, reasoning traces often lack factual grounding and robustness.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti *reasoning model* yang menggunakan *test-time scaling* untuk penerjemahan terminologi hukum ke dalam variasi bahasa non-dominan. Para penulis menemukan bahwa meskipun penalaran membantu dalam tugas yang kompleks secara semantis, jejak penalaran seringkali kurang memiliki landasan faktual dan ketahanan.

acl:2026.eamt-1.23.title: Beyond Simple Term Injection: Reasoning Models for Legal Translation in a Non-Dominant Language Variety
acl:2026.eamt-1.23.venue: Proceedings of the 26th Annual Conference of the European Association for Machine Translation (Volume 1)

acl:2026.eamt-1.3.abstract: Effective communication in asylum reception settings requires reliable machine translation (MT) across many languages, including low-resource ones. Using data from the MaTIAS project, we compare retrieval-augmented LLM translation with adaptive Neural MT across 14 target languages with varying resource levels. Working with a very small translation memory of only 358 sentences, we evaluate fuzzy match (FM) augmentation as an in-context learning strategy for open-source and commercial LLMs and benchmark these against ModernMT with and without domain adaptation. In the LLM setting, FM-based example selection consistently outperforms random selection and zero-shot prompting, with the largest gains for low-resource languages. Adaptive NMT retains an overall advantage, although Gemini Pro approaches its performance and outperforms it on 6 of 14 languages, highlighting a trade-off between translation quality and data sovereignty in privacy-sensitive contexts. These findings show that FM augmentation remains effective under severe data constraints and emphasise the importance of language-specific evaluation in multilingual MT.
