Kesenjangan ini membatasi ketererapan global dan berisiko memperkuat ketidaksetaraan linguistik dalam teknologi digital.

contributions.en: The paper presents LLM Probe, a lexicon-based assessment framework designed to systematically evaluate the linguistic skills of large language models across four areas: lexical alignment, part-of-speech recognition, morphosyntactic probing, and translation accuracy. Additionally, the authors construct a manually annotated benchmark dataset comprising 7,234 bidirectional English-Tigrinya and Tigrinya-English phrase pairs enriched with morphosyntactic annotations and high inter-annotator agreement.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyajikan LLM Probe, sebuah *framework* *evaluasi* berbasis leksikon yang dirancang untuk menilai keterampilan linguistik *large language model* di empat area: *lexical alignment*, pengenalan *part-of-speech*, *probing* morfosintaksis, dan akurasi terjemahan. Selain itu, para penulis menyusun *dataset* *benchmark* beranotasi manual yang terdiri dari 7.234 pasangan frasa dwibahasa.

future_work.en: The authors identify several limitations, including limited model coverage that excludes proprietary models, domain and register constraints restricting evaluation to general-purpose text, manual annotation bottlenecks, prompt sensitivity, and language-specific tooling gaps. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset to include domain-specific vocabulary, dialectal variation, and informal registers, as well as incorporating additional evaluation dimensions such as semantic similarity and cross-lingual transfer capabilities.
future_work.id: Para penulis mengidentifikasi beberapa keterbatasan, termasuk cakupan *model* yang terbatas yang tidak mencakup *model* berpemilik, kendala domain dan register, hambatan *anotasi* manual, sensitivitas *prompt*, dan kesenjangan alat bantu spesifik bahasa. Pekerjaan masa depan akan berfokus pada perluasan *dataset* untuk mencakup kosakata khusus domain, variasi dialek, dan register informal.

method.en: The evaluation pipeline assesses diverse open-source large language models spanning causal language models like Falcon-10B, Gemma, Mistral-7B, and Qwen-7B, alongside sequence-to-sequence models like mT5 and ByT5. Evaluations were executed on a high-performance computing cluster using greedy sampling with zero temperature for deterministic outputs. The newly constructed benchmark dataset supports bidirectional evaluation and is stored in a structured JSON format.
method.id: Alur *evaluasi* menilai berbagai *large language model* *open-source* yang mencakup *causal language model* seperti Falcon-10B, Gemma, Mistral-7B, dan Qwen-7B, serta *model* *sequence-to-sequence* seperti mT5 dan ByT5. *Evaluasi* dijalankan pada klaster komputasi berkinerja tinggi menggunakan *greedy sampling* dengan suhu nol untuk menghasilkan keluaran yang deterministik.

related_work.en: Previous evaluation efforts include specialized frameworks such as Eka Eval for Indian languages and GlotEval for massively multilingual evaluations, alongside various multilingual probing approaches. However, these evaluations frequently highlight performance disparities, and traditional benchmarks often rely on data already present in pretraining sets, leading to inflated performance metrics. Furthermore, current evaluators exhibit biases toward high-resource languages and require calibration against native speaker judgments.
related_work.id: Upaya *evaluasi* sebelumnya mencakup *framework* khusus seperti Eka Eval untuk bahasa-bahasa di India dan GlotEval untuk *evaluasi* *multilingual*, serta berbagai pendekatan *probing*. Kendati demikian, *benchmark* tradisional sering kali mengandalkan data yang sudah ada dalam *pretraining set*, yang menyebabkan metrik kinerja menjadi terlalu tinggi.

results.en: Experimental results reveal notable differences in performance across linguistic tasks, showing that sequence-to-sequence models like ByT5 and mT5 excel in morphosyntactic analysis and translation quality with higher BLEU scores. Conversely, causal models demonstrate strong performance in lexical alignment but exhibit weaker translation accuracy. Confusion matrix analysis for part-of-speech tagging indicates that models frequently confuse nouns with verbs and adjectives due to overlapping contextual cues and morphological markers.
results.id: Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan perbedaan kinerja yang mencolok di berbagai tugas linguistik, di mana *model* *sequence-to-sequence* seperti ByT5 dan mT5 unggul dalam analisis morfosintaksis dan kualitas terjemahan dengan skor BLEU yang lebih tinggi. Sebaliknya, *causal model* menunjukkan kinerja yang kuat dalam *lexical alignment* tetapi memiliki akurasi terjemahan yang lebih lemah.

tldr.en: This paper introduces LLM Probe, a lexicon-based framework for systematically evaluating large language models in low-resource and morphologically rich languages. The evaluation reveals that sequence-to-sequence architectures generally excel in morphosyntactic analysis and translation quality, whereas causal models perform well in lexical alignment.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan LLM Probe, sebuah *framework* berbasis leksikon untuk mengevaluasi *large language model* secara sistematis pada bahasa *low-resource* dan kaya morfologi. Evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa arsitektur *sequence-to-sequence* umumnya unggul dalam analisis morfosintaksis dan kualitas terjemahan, sementara *causal model* berkinerja baik dalam *lexical alignment*.

acl:2026.llms4ssh-1.24.title: LLM Probe: Evaluating LLMs for Low-Resource Languages
acl:2026.llms4ssh-1.24.venue: Proceedings of Shaping Multilingual, Multimodal AI for the Social Sciences and Humanities (LLMs4SSH) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.llms4ssh-1.8.abstract: Multilingual large language models (LLMs) often exhibit emergent ‘shadow’ capabilities in languages without official support, yet their performance on these languages remains uneven and under-measured. This is particularly acute for morphosyntactically rich minority languages such as Scottish Gaelic, where translation benchmarks fail to capture structural competence. We introduce GaelEval, the first multi-dimensional benchmark for Gaelic, comprising: (i) an expert-authored morphosyntactic MCQA task; (ii) a culturally-grounded translation benchmark and (iii) a large-scale cultural knowledge Q&A task. Evaluating 19 LLMs against a fluent-speaker human baseline (n = 30), we find that Gemini 3 Pro Preview achieves 83.3% accuracy on the linguistic task, surpassing the human baseline (78.1%). Proprietary models consistently outperform open-weight systems, and in-language (Gaelic) prompting yields a small but stable advantage (+2.4pp). On the cultural task, leading models exceed 90% accuracy, though most systems perform worse under Gaelic prompting and absolute scores are inflated relative to the manual benchmark. Overall, GaelEval reveals that frontier models achieve above-human performance on several dimensions of Gaelic grammar, demonstrates the effect of Gaelic prompting and shows a consistent performance gap favouring proprietary over open-weight models.
acl:2026.llms4ssh-1.8.journal_ref: Proceedings of Shaping Multilingual, Multimodal AI for the Social Sciences and Humanities (LLMs4SSH) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.llms4ssh-1.8.title: GaelEval: Benchmarking LLM Performance for Scottish Gaelic
acl:2026.llms4ssh-1.8.venue: Proceedings of Shaping Multilingual, Multimodal AI for the Social Sciences and Humanities (LLMs4SSH) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.lrec-1.109.abstract: Decoder-only language models can be adapted to diverse tasks through instruction finetuning, but the extent to which this generalizes at small scale for low-resource languages remains unclear. We focus on the languages of South Africa, where we are not aware of a publicly available decoder-only model that explicitly targets all eleven official written languages, nine of which are low-resource. We introduce MzansiText, a curated multilingual pretraining corpus with a reproducible filtering pipeline, and MzansiLM, a 125M-parameter language model trained from scratch. We evaluate MzansiLM on natural language understanding and generation using three adaptation regimes: monolingual task-specific finetuning, multilingual task-specific finetuning, and general multi-task instruction finetuning. Monolingual task-specific finetuning achieves strong performance on data-to-text generation, reaching 20.65 BLEU on isiXhosa and competing with encoder-decoder baselines over ten times larger. Multilingual task-specific finetuning benefits closely related languages on topic classification, achieving 78.5% macro-F1 on isiXhosa news classification. While MzansiLM adapts effectively to supervised NLU and NLG tasks, few-shot reasoning remains challenging at this model size, with performance near chance even for much larger decoder-only models. We release MzansiText and MzansiLM to provide a reproducible decoder-only baseline and clear guidance on adaptation strategies for South African languages at small scale.
acl:2026.lrec-1.109.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

glossary.explanation_id: Arsitektur *neural network* yang hanya menggunakan komponen *decoder* dari model transformator untuk menghasilkan teks secara autoregresif.
Proses pelatihan lanjutan pada model bahasa menggunakan instruksi berbasis teks dan respons untuk meningkatkan kemampuan generalisasi pada berbagai tugas.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain memiliki ketersediaan data digital, korpus, dan alat pemrosesan bahasa alami yang sangat terbatas.
Unit teks terkecil yang diproses oleh *tokenizer* dalam model bahasa, yang dapat berupa kata, bagian kata, atau karakter.
Kemampuan model bahasa untuk menyelesaikan tugas penalaran baru hanya dengan diberikan beberapa contoh demonstrasi di dalam *prompt*.
Metrik evaluasi yang menghitung rerata skor *F1* dari setiap kelas secara merata tanpa memandang frekuensi kemunculan kelas tersebut.
Metode *parameter-efficient fine-tuning* yang membekukan bobot asli model dan melatih matriks peringkat rendah (*low-rank*) tambahan.
Proses mendeteksi dan menghapus dokumen atau teks duplikat dari korpus data pelatihan untuk menghindari bias dan meningkatkan kualitas.

background.en: Decoder-only language models can be adapted to diverse tasks through instruction fine-tuning, but the extent to which this generalizes at a small scale for low-resource languages remains unclear. The authors focus on the languages of South Africa, a linguistically diverse nation with eleven official written languages, nine of which are low-resource. Prior research on African languages has historically been dominated by encoder-only and encoder-decoder models, leaving a gap for publicly available decoder-only models that explicitly target all official South African languages.
background.id: Model bahasa *decoder-only* dapat diadaptasi ke berbagai tugas melalui *instruction fine-tuning*, namun sejauh mana hal ini dapat digeneralisasikan pada skala kecil untuk bahasa *low-resource* masih belum jelas. Para penulis berfokus pada bahasa-bahasa di Afrika Selatan, sebuah negara dengan keragaman linguistik tinggi yang memiliki sebelas bahasa resmi tertulis, di mana sembilan di antaranya termasuk *low-resource*. Penelitian sebelumnya mengenai bahasa-bahasa Afrika secara historis didominasi oleh model *encoder-only* dan *encoder-decoder*, sehingga menyisakan celah bagi model *decoder-only* publik yang secara eksplisit menargetkan seluruh bahasa resmi Afrika Selatan.

contributions.en: This paper contributes MzansiText, a curated multilingual pretraining corpus with a reproducible preparation pipeline covering all eleven official written South African languages. It also introduces MzansiLM, a 125M-parameter decoder-only model trained from scratch on MzansiText. Furthermore, the study provides a systematic comparison of different instruction fine-tuning approaches across available tasks for South African languages, revealing where decoder-only models excel and where they fall short.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyumbangkan MzansiText, korpus *pretraining* multibahasa kurasi dengan pipa persiapan yang dapat direproduksi yang mencakup kesebelas bahasa resmi tertulis Afrika Selatan. Makalah ini juga memperkenalkan MzansiLM, sebuah model *decoder-only* berparameter 125M yang dilatih dari awal pada MzansiText. Selain itu, penelitian ini menyediakan perbandingan sistematis dari berbagai pendekatan *instruction fine-tuning* di berbagai tugas yang tersedia untuk bahasa-bahasa Afrika Selatan, mengungkapkan di mana model *decoder-only* unggul dan di mana model tersebut masih memiliki kekurangan.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss future work in detail.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan masa depan secara rinci.

method.en: The pretraining corpus MzansiText is constructed by aggregating public sources such as mC4, CulturaX, WURA, Glot500, NCHLT Text, CC100, ParaCrawl, and Inkuba-Mono, followed by a deterministic multi-stage filtering and deduplication pipeline using Datatrove. MzansiLM is built using the MobileLLM 125M architecture with a LLaMA-style decoder stack and a 65,536-token BPE tokenizer. The authors evaluate MzansiLM under three adaptation regimes: monolingual task-specific fine-tuning, multilingual task-specific fine-tuning, and general multi-task instruction fine-tuning using LoRA for parameter-efficient adaptation.
method.id: Korpus *pretraining* MzansiText dibangun dengan menggabungkan sumber publik seperti mC4, CulturaX, WURA, Glot500, NCHLT Text, CC100, ParaCrawl, dan Inkuba-Mono, diikuti oleh pipa penyaringan dan *deduplication* multi-tahap deterministik menggunakan Datatrove. MzansiLM dibangun menggunakan arsitektur MobileLLM 125M dengan tumpukan *decoder* bergaya LLaMA dan sebuah *tokenizer* BPE berukuran 65.536 token. Para penulis mengevaluasi MzansiLM di bawah tiga rezim adaptasi: *fine-tuning* spesifik tugas monolingual, *fine-tuning* spesifik tugas multibahasa, dan *instruction fine-tuning* multi-tugas umum menggunakan LoRA untuk adaptasi yang efisien parameter.

related_work.en: Current research in African NLP increasingly explores decoder-only architectures, with examples including InkubaLM, AfroLlama-V1, and LughaLlama, though open-weight baselines remain predominantly encoder-only and encoder-decoder models like AfriBERTa, AfroXLMR, and AfriTeVa. The authors identify three major gaps in prior literature: existing decoder-only models cover only subsets of South African languages rather than all eleven, systematic comparisons across different adaptation strategies are seldom performed, and evaluation is often limited to broad benchmarks that exclude lower-resource languages.
related_work.id: Penelitian terkini dalam NLP Afrika semakin banyak mengeksplorasi arsitektur *decoder-only*, dengan contoh seperti InkubaLM, AfroLlama-V1, dan LughaLlama, meskipun *baseline* berbobot terbuka sebagian besar tetap berupa model *encoder-only* dan *encoder-decoder* seperti AfriBERTa, AfroXLMR, dan AfriTeVa. Para penulis mengidentifikasi tiga celah utama dalam literatur sebelumnya: model *decoder-only* yang ada hanya mencakup sebagian kecil bahasa Afrika Selatan dan bukan kesebelasnya, perbandingan sistematis antar strategi adaptasi jarang dilakukan, dan evaluasi sering kali terbatas pada *benchmark* luas yang mengecualikan bahasa-bahasa dengan sumber daya lebih rendah.

results.en: Monolingual task-specific fine-tuning achieves strong performance on data-to-text generation, reaching 20.65 BLEU on isiXhosa and competing with encoder-decoder baselines over ten times larger. Multilingual task-specific fine-tuning benefits closely related Bantu languages on topic classification, achieving 78.5 percent macro-F1 on isiXhosa news classification. However, few-shot reasoning and reading comprehension remain challenging at this model size, with performance staying near chance level across decoder-only models below 70B parameters.
results.id: *Fine-tuning* spesifik tugas monolingual mencapai performa yang kuat pada generasi *data-to-text*, mencapai 20,65 BLEU pada bahasa isiXhosa dan bersaing dengan *baseline encoder-decoder* yang ukurannya sepuluh kali lebih besar. *Fine-tuning* spesifik tugas multibahasa memberikan keuntungan bagi bahasa-bahasa Bantu yang berkerabat dekat pada klasifikasi topik, mencapai 78,5 persen *macro-F1* pada klasifikasi berita isiXhosa. Meskipun demikian, penalaran *few-shot* dan pemahaman bacaan tetap menantang pada ukuran model ini, dengan performa yang berada di sekitar tingkat peluang (*chance level*) di antara model *decoder-only* di bawah parameter 70B.

tldr.en: This paper introduces MzansiText and MzansiLM, a multilingual pretraining corpus and a 125M-parameter decoder-only model for all eleven official written languages of South Africa. The findings show that while task-specific fine-tuning achieves strong performance on generation and sequence labelling, few-shot reasoning remains challenging at this scale.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan MzansiText dan MzansiLM, sebuah korpus *pretraining* multibahasa dan model *decoder-only* berparameter 125M untuk kesebelas bahasa resmi tertulis di Afrika Selatan. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa meskipun *fine-tuning* spesifik tugas mencapai performa yang kuat pada generasi dan pelabelan sekuens, penalaran *few-shot* tetap menantang pada skala ini.

acl:2026.lrec-1.109.title: MzansiText and MzansiLM: An Open Corpus and Decoder-Only Language Model for South African Languages
acl:2026.lrec-1.109.venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

acl:2026.lrec-1.112.abstract: We investigate high-accuracy and speaker-robust automatic speech recognition (ASR) models by leveraging pretrained models for endangered languages in Japan — Ryukyuan (Shuri dialect) and Ainu (Saru dialect) — to support language and cultural preservation. In particular, this study presents the first experimental study on building and evaluating an ASR model for the Ryukyuan language. Specifically, we compare existing multilingual pretrained models, Whisper and XLS-R, with our in-house Japanese-focused model (JP-90k) pretrained solely on a large-scale weakly-supervised Japanese dataset. These models were fine-tuned on up to 10 and 32 hours of Ryukyuan and Ainu data, respectively. As a result, JP-90k consistently outperformed other models of the similar size in both languages. In addition, it demonstrated a remarkable advantage when training data was very limited, i.e., an hour or less. These findings suggest that large-scale pretraining on a language closely related to the target ones can yield robust low-resource ASR, including for unseen speakers and out-of-domain conditions. Furthermore, we found that all pretrained models achieved convergence in ASR accuracy with as little as 3-5 hours of fine-tuning data for both languages.

glossary.explanation_id: Teknologi komputasi yang mengonversi sinyal suara ucapan menjadi teks tertulis.
Proses melatih ulang model praterlatih menggunakan *dataset* target spesifik untuk tugas tertentu.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain kekurangan data pelatihan digital yang memadai.
Fungsi *loss* yang digunakan dalam model pengenalan suara untuk menangani data urutan tanpa penjajaran eksplisit.
Metrik evaluasi yang mengukur rasio kesalahan karakter antara transkripsi hipotesis model dan referensi.

background.en: Endangered languages suffer from a severe scarcity of transcribed audio data, making them low-resource in automatic speech recognition. Preserving languages like Ryukyuan and Ainu is crucial for cultural heritage, but manual transcription requires scarce experts and is costly. This study addresses the data-scarcity problem by applying pretrained speech models to the Shuri dialect of Ryukyuan and the Saru dialect of Ainu.
background.id: Bahasa yang terancam punah mengalami kelangkaan data audio beranotasi yang parah, menjadikannya *low-resource* dalam pengenalan suara otomatis. Pelestarian bahasa seperti Ryukyuan dan Ainu sangat penting untuk warisan budaya, tetapi transkripsi manual memerlukan tenaga ahli yang langka dan berbiaya tinggi. Studi ini mengatasi masalah kelangkaan data dengan menerapkan model suara praterlatih pada dialek Shuri dari bahasa Ryukyuan dan dialek Saru dari bahasa Ainu.

contributions.en: The main contributions are threefold. First, this is the first experimental study to build and evaluate an automatic speech recognition model for the Ryukyuan language. Second, the authors demonstrate that the Japanese-focused JP-90k model outperforms comparable multilingual models on both Ryukyuan and Ainu. Third, the study shows that 3 to 5 hours of fine-tuning data is sufficient for pretrained models to achieve stable recognition accuracy.
contributions.id: Kontribusi utama mencakup tiga hal. Pertama, ini adalah studi eksperimental pertama yang membangun dan mengevaluasi model pengenalan suara otomatis untuk bahasa Ryukyuan. Kedua, para penulis mendemonstrasikan bahwa model JP-90k yang berfokus pada bahasa Jepang mengungguli model multibahasa yang sebanding pada bahasa Ryukyuan dan Ainu. Ketiga, studi ini menunjukkan bahwa data *fine-tuning* sebanyak 3 hingga 5 jam sudah cukup bagi model praterlatih untuk mencapai akurasi pengenalan yang stabil.

future_work.en: For future work, the authors plan to pursue higher accuracy by integrating multilingual and Japanese-focused pretrained models. They also aim to extend automatic speech recognition development to other dialects of Ryukyuan and Ainu that are even more severely resource-scarce.
future_work.id: Untuk pekerjaan masa depan, para penulis berencana mengejar akurasi yang lebih tinggi dengan mengintegrasikan model praterlatih multibahasa dan yang berfokus pada bahasa Jepang. Mereka juga bertujuan memperluas pengembangan pengenalan suara otomatis ke dialek lain dari bahasa Ryukyuan dan Ainu yang bahkan memiliki sumber daya yang lebih langka.

method.en: The study evaluates three pretrained models: XLS-R, Whisper, and an in-house Japanese-focused model called JP-90k pretrained on 90,251 hours of weakly-supervised Japanese data. A model trained from scratch is also used as a baseline. The models were fine-tuned using syllable-level phonemic transcriptions on datasets comprising up to 10 hours of Ryukyuan and 32 hours of Ainu speech, using cross-entropy or connectionist temporal classification loss.
method.id: Studi ini mengevaluasi tiga model praterlatih: XLS-R, Whisper, dan model buatan sendiri yang berfokus pada bahasa Jepang bernama JP-90k yang dilatih pada 90.251 jam data bahasa Jepang dengan *weak supervision*. Model yang dilatih dari awal juga digunakan sebagai baseline. Model-model tersebut di-*fine-tune* menggunakan transkripsi fonem tingkat suku kata pada korpus yang mencakup hingga 10 jam suara Ryukyuan dan 32 jam suara Ainu, menggunakan *loss function* *cross-entropy* atau *connectionist temporal classification*.

related_work.en: Prior low-resource automatic speech recognition research relies on multilingual pretraining frameworks such as Whisper and XLS-R. While these models leverage massive multilingual data, other studies debate whether data quantity or linguistic proximity to the target language is more crucial. Furthermore, previous Ainu automatic speech recognition either lacked pretrained models or focused on fine-tuning without systematic comparison against related-language pretraining.
related_work.id: Penelitian pengenalan suara otomatis *low-resource* sebelumnya mengandalkan kerangka kerja praterlatih multibahasa seperti Whisper dan XLS-R. Meskipun model ini memanfaatkan data multibahasa yang masif, studi lain memperdebatkan apakah jumlah data atau kedekatan linguistik dengan bahasa target lebih krusial. Selain itu, pengenalan suara otomatis Ainu sebelumnya kurang memiliki model praterlatih atau hanya berfokus pada *fine-tuning* tanpa perbandingan sistematis terhadap praterlatih bahasa serumpun.

results.en: The JP-90k model consistently achieved the best character error rate on both Ryukyuan and Ainu evaluation splits among comparable models. Its advantage became especially pronounced when training data was reduced to one hour or less, outperforming even the much larger Whisper-L model. Error analysis revealed that while JP-90k excels overall, it struggles with Japanese-non-contrastive phonemes like semivowels, showing that multilingual and language-focused pretraining are complementary.
results.id: Model JP-90k secara konsisten mencapai *character error rate* terbaik pada split evaluasi Ryukyuan dan Ainu di antara model yang sebanding. Keunggulannya menjadi sangat nyata ketika data pelatihan dikurangi menjadi satu jam atau kurang, bahkan mengungguli model Whisper-L yang jauh lebih besar. Analisis kesalahan mengungkapkan bahwa meskipun JP-90k unggul secara keseluruhan, model ini mengalami kesulitan dengan fonem yang tidak kontras dalam bahasa Jepang seperti semivokal, yang menunjukkan bahwa praterlatih multibahasa dan berfokus bahasa saling melengkapi.

tldr.en: This paper investigates pretrained models for automatic speech recognition of endangered Ryukyuan and Ainu languages. The results demonstrate that a Japanese-focused model outperforms multilingual models, especially in low-resource settings.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti model praterlatih untuk pengenalan suara otomatis pada bahasa Ryukyuan dan Ainu yang terancam punah. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa model berfokus bahasa Jepang mengungguli model multibahasa, terutama pada pengaturan *low-resource*.

acl:2026.lrec-1.112.title: Adapting Pretrained Models to Endangered Languages in Japan: A Comparative Study on Ryukyuan and Ainu Speech Recognition
