Although existing natural language processing tools can accurately detect mutated forms, they lack the ability to explain why a mutation occurs, leaving a significant gap in pedagogical applications and computational linguistics for low-resource languages.
background.id: Mutasi konsonan awal adalah ciri morfofonologis yang menentukan dalam bahasa Wales di mana konsonan pertama dari suatu kata berubah berdasarkan konteks gramatikalnya. Meskipun perangkat *natural language processing* yang ada dapat mendeteksi bentuk mutasi dengan akurat, perangkat tersebut tidak memiliki kemampuan untuk menjelaskan mengapa mutasi terjadi, sehingga meninggalkan celah yang signifikan dalam aplikasi pedagogis dan linguistik komputasi untuk bahasa *low-resource*.

contributions.en: This paper makes three primary contributions: defining the novel task of mutation trigger labelling, introducing a new taxonomy covering underlying grammatical categories and syntactic configurations, and exploring two preliminary computational approaches using Constraint Grammar rules and few-shot prompting with large language models.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memberikan tiga kontribusi utama: mendefinisikan tugas baru berupa *mutation trigger labelling*, memperkenalkan taksonomi baru yang mencakup kategori gramatikal mendasar dan konfigurasi sintaksis, serta mengeksplorasi dua pendekatan komputasi awal menggunakan aturan *Constraint Grammar* dan *prompting* *few-shot* dengan *large language model*.

future_work.en: The authors identify limitations regarding the reliance on upstream tools, scarcity of fully labelled corpora, and copyright restrictions on grammar datasets. Future work includes integrating dependency parsing models like UDPipe to incorporate syntactic information and improve the detection of morphosyntactic mutation triggers.
future_work.id: Para penulis mengidentifikasi keterbatasan terkait ketergantungan pada perangkat hulu, kelangkaan *korpus* beranotasi penuh, dan pembatasan hak cipta pada *data* gramatika. Pekerjaan masa depan mencakup pengintegrasian model *parsing* dependensi seperti UDPipe untuk menyertakan informasi sintaksis dan meningkatkan deteksi pemicu mutasi morfofonologis.

method.en: The evaluation dataset is compiled from grammar reference books by D.A. Thorne and the CorCenCC corpus. Two unsupervised strategies are tested: a rule-based model utilising 234 Constraint Grammar rules to append trigger tags, and large language models evaluated in few-shot settings using prompts with defined taxonomies and examples.
method.id: Data *evaluasi* dikompilasi dari buku referensi gramatika oleh D.A. Thorne dan *korpus* CorCenCC. Dua strategi *unsupervised* diuji: model berbasis aturan yang memanfaatkan 234 aturan *Constraint Grammar* untuk menambahkan *tag* pemicu, dan *large language model* yang dievaluasi dalam pengaturan *few-shot* menggunakan *prompt* dengan taksonomi dan contoh yang ditentukan.

related_work.en: Previous research in Welsh natural language processing includes early rule-based machine translation systems like Apertium-cy, part-of-speech taggers such as CyTag2 using Constraint Grammar rules, and corpora like CorCenCC. However, these tools are limited to surface-level tokenisation, lemmatisation, and tagging without capturing the causal mechanisms behind mutations.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya dalam *natural language processing* bahasa Wales mencakup sistem *terjemahan mesin* berbasis aturan awal seperti Apertium-cy, *tagger* *part-of-speech* seperti CyTag2 yang menggunakan aturan *Constraint Grammar*, serta *korpus* seperti CorCenCC. Namun, perangkat ini terbatas pada *tokenisasi* tingkat permukaan, * lemmatisasi*, dan *tagging* tanpa menangkap mekanisme kausal di balik mutasi.

results.en: The rule-based model achieves 94% accuracy in mutation detection and 65% accuracy in trigger labelling with high precision, whereas Claude matches the rule-based mutation detection accuracy and outperforms GPT in trigger prediction. Qualitative analysis reveals that rule errors primarily stem from upstream tagger mistakes and limitations in handling complex syntactic dependencies.
results.id: Model berbasis aturan mencapai akurasi 94% dalam deteksi mutasi dan 65% dalam penandaan pemicu dengan presisi tinggi, sedangkan Claude menyamai akurasi deteksi mutasi berbasis aturan dan mengungguli GPT dalam prediksi pemicu. Analisis kualitatif mengungkapkan bahwa kesalahan aturan terutama berasal dari kesalahan *tagger* hulu dan keterbatasan dalam menangani ketergantungan sintaksis yang kompleks.

tldr.en: This paper introduces the task of mutation trigger labelling in Welsh to explain the grammatical or lexical causes of initial consonant mutations. The results show that a rule-based system achieves high precision, while large language models struggle with multi-label reasoning.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan tugas *mutation trigger labelling* pada bahasa Wales untuk menjelaskan penyebab gramatikal atau leksikal dari mutasi konsonan awal. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem berbasis aturan mencapai presisi tinggi, sedangkan *large language model* mengalami kesulitan dalam penalaran *multi-label*.

acl:2026.lrec-1.911.title: Unsupervised Labelling of Mutation Triggers in Welsh
acl:2026.lrec-1.911.venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

acl:2026.lrec-1.912.abstract: In this paper, we present a new Universal Dependencies treebank for Uzbek language(UzUDT) developed as a gold-standard resource with full manual annotation. The treebank includes 684 sentences (7,582 tokens) from Uzbek literary texts, and is larger and more domain-diverse than the existing Uzbek UD treebank. The corpus was developed through rigorous multi-annotator adjudication, achieving very high inter-annotator agreement (multi-rater agreement coefficients >0.90) across lemmatization, PoS tagging, and morphological features. Alongside comprehensive corpus profiling, we establish robust computational baselines by evaluating graph-based (Stanza) and transition-based (spaCy) parsing architectures using both static and monolingual contextual embeddings. Our evaluations reveal a critical architectural trade-off for low-resource agglutinative parsing: joint transition-based models excel at morphosyntactic tagging, whereas graph-based models remain strictly superior for resolving complex structural dependencies. Furthermore, we demonstrate that cross-treebank data augmentation yields substantial, synergistic accuracy gains. The resource provides a much-needed high-quality treebank for Uzbek to assist in developing better NLP tools and to enable linguistic research in the low-resource language
acl:2026.lrec-1.912.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

glossary.explanation_id: Sebuah korpus teks yang dianotasikan dengan informasi struktur sintaksis atau dependensi.
Proses pengelompokan bentuk infleksi suatu kata sehingga dapat dianalisis sebagai bentuk tunggal dasarnya.
Tugas NLP untuk menganalisis struktur gramatikal suatu kalimat dan menetapkan hubungan antarkata.
Jenis bahasa di mana kata-kata dibentuk dengan menggabungkan morfem-morfem imbuhan tanpa mengubah bentuk dasarnya secara signifikan.
Representasi vektor kata yang dinamis berdasarkan konteks kalimat di sekitarnya.
Teknik memperbesar ukuran dan keragaman *dataset* pelatihan dengan menambahkan data baru atau gabungan.

background.en: Uzbek is a low-resource Turkic language that historically suffered from a lack of core NLP resources, particularly dependency treebanks. The first publicly available Uzbek UD treebank, Uzbek-UT, was limited in size, genre, and domain coverage, consisting mainly of news and fiction texts. This scarcity of robust and diverse annotated data constrains the effective training of taggers, parsers, and language models for Uzbek, creating an urgent need for a larger, higher-quality, and domain-diverse resource.
background.id: Bahasa Uzbek adalah bahasa Turkik *low-resource* yang secara historis kekurangan sumber daya NLP inti, terutama *dependency treebank*. *Treebank* UD bahasa Uzbek pertama yang tersedia untuk umum, yaitu Uzbek-UT, memiliki ukuran, genre, dan cakupan domain yang terbatas, yang sebagian besar terdiri dari teks berita dan fiksi. Kelangkaan data beranotasi yang kuat dan beragam ini membatasi pelatihan *tagger*, *parser*, dan *model bahasa* yang efektif untuk bahasa Uzbek, sehingga menciptakan kebutuhan mendesak akan sumber daya yang lebih besar, berkualitas tinggi, dan beragam domain.

contributions.en: The authors introduce UzUDT, a new gold-standard Universal Dependencies treebank for Uzbek containing 684 sentences and 7,582 tokens sourced from literary texts. The corpus features rigorous multi-annotator adjudication with high inter-annotator agreement coefficients exceeding 0.90. Additionally, the paper establishes robust computational baselines by evaluating graph-based and transition-based parsing architectures with static and contextual embeddings, and demonstrates significant accuracy gains through cross-treebank data augmentation.
contributions.id: Para penulis memperkenalkan UzUDT, sebuah *treebank* *Universal Dependencies* berstandar emas baru untuk bahasa Uzbek yang berisi 684 kalimat dan 7.582 *token* yang bersumber dari teks sastra. Korpus ini menampilkan adjudikasi multi-anotator yang ketat dengan koefisien *inter-annotator agreement* yang tinggi melebihi 0,90. Selain itu, makalah ini menetapkan *baseline* komputasi yang kuat dengan mengevaluasi arsitektur *parsing* berbasis *graph* dan berbasis *transition* menggunakan *embedding* statis dan kontekstual, serta mendemonstrasikan peningkatan akurasi yang signifikan melalui *data augmentation* lintas *treebank*.

future_work.en: The authors plan to scale the resource beyond literary text by incorporating additional genres such as news, web text, and social media using model-assisted annotation and LLM-assisted syntactic annotation, combined with automatic UD validation and human-in-the-loop review.
future_work.id: Para penulis berencana untuk menskalakan sumber daya ini melampaui teks sastra dengan memasukkan genre tambahan seperti berita, teks web, dan media sosial menggunakan *model-assisted annotation* dan *LLM-assisted syntactic annotation*, yang dikombinasikan dengan validasi UD otomatis dan ulasan *human-in-the-loop*.

method.en: The corpus was compiled by selecting self-contained sentences from literary works and annotating them in INCEpTION according to Universal Dependencies guidelines through a double-annotation setting and adjudication. For evaluation, the authors tested a graph-based pipeline using Stanza and a transition-based pipeline using spaCy. These architectures were evaluated using static FastText embeddings and monolingual contextual TahrirchiBERT embeddings, both on standalone UzUDT data and on a merged dataset combining UzUDT and Uzbek-UT.
method.id: Korpus disusun dengan memilih kalimat mandiri dari karya sastra dan menganotasikannya di INCEpTION sesuai pedoman *Universal Dependencies* melalui pengaturan *double-annotation* dan adjudikasi. Untuk evaluasi, para penulis menguji *pipeline* berbasis *graph* menggunakan Stanza dan *pipeline* berbasis *transition* menggunakan spaCy. Arsitektur ini dievaluasi menggunakan *embedding* statis FastText dan *embedding* kontekstual monolingual TahrirchiBERT, baik pada data UzUDT mandiri maupun pada *dataset* gabungan yang menggabungkan UzUDT dan Uzbek-UT.

related_work.en: Prior computational efforts for Uzbek include an old morphological parser built in Prolog, rule-based tools such as UzbekTagger and UzMorphAnalyzer, and the recently released Uzbek-UT treebank containing 500 sentences from news and fiction domains. However, these existing resources remain small, genre-limited, and lack comprehensive morphosyntactic annotations for complex literary structures such as converb chains and possessor agreements.
related_work.id: Upaya komputasi sebelumnya untuk bahasa Uzbek mencakup *morphological parser* lama yang dibangun dengan Prolog, alat berbasis aturan seperti UzbekTagger dan UzMorphAnalyzer, serta *treebank* Uzbek-UT yang baru dirilis yang berisi 500 kalimat dari domain berita dan fiksi. Namun, sumber daya yang ada ini tetap kecil, terbatas genrenya, dan kurang memiliki anotasi morfosintaksis yang komprehensif untuk struktur sastra yang kompleks seperti rantai *converb* dan persetujuan kepemilikan.

results.en: Experiments reveal a critical architectural trade-off: joint transition-based models (spaCy) excel at morphosyntactic tagging with the highest UPOS accuracy of 89.18% on merged data, whereas graph-based models (Stanza) remain vastly superior for structural parsing, achieving a Labeled Attachment Score of 63.81%. Replacing static embeddings with TahrirchiBERT consistently improved performance, and cross-treebank data augmentation yielded substantial accuracy gains, particularly boosting Stanza graph-based LAS by 10 to 11 points.
results.id: Eksperimen mengungkapkan pertukaran arsitektural yang krusial: model gabungan berbasis *transition* (spaCy) unggul dalam *morphosyntactic tagging* dengan akurasi UPOS tertinggi sebesar 89,18% pada data gabungan, sedangkan model berbasis *graph* (Stanza) jauh lebih superior untuk *parsing* struktural, mencapai *Labeled Attachment Score* sebesar 63,81%. Mengganti *embedding* statis dengan TahrirchiBERT secara konsisten meningkatkan performa, dan *data augmentation* lintas *treebank* menghasilkan peningkatan akurasi yang substansial, terutama mendongkrak LAS berbasis *graph* Stanza sebesar 10 hingga 11 poin.

tldr.en: This paper presents UzUDT, a new Universal Dependencies treebank for the Uzbek language annotated with full morphosyntactic structure. The evaluations reveal an architectural trade-off where transition-based models excel at tagging while graph-based models are superior for structural parsing.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan UzUDT, sebuah *treebank* *Universal Dependencies* baru untuk bahasa Uzbek yang dianotasikan dengan struktur morfosintaksis lengkap. Evaluasi menunjukkan adanya pertukaran arsitektural di mana model berbasis *transition* unggul dalam *tagging* sedangkan model berbasis *graph* lebih superior untuk *parsing* struktural.

acl:2026.lrec-1.912.title: UzUDT: Uzbek Universal Dependencies Treebank
acl:2026.lrec-1.912.venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

acl:2026.lrec-1.916.abstract: Low German (Low Saxon, ISO 639-2 nds) is an underresourced West Germanic language spoken in Northern Germany (Plattdütsch), in the Netherlands (Nedersaksisch) and in an international diaspora (Plautdietsch, Pomerano, etc.). As a minority language, it is under pressure from the respective national languages, and considered threatened. Although NLP and digital language resources might play a role in facilitating the use of the language on the web and to support intergenerational transmission, no NLP tools are known to exist, and no adequate corpora that such tools could be trained on. This paper describes the construction of a novel corpus of North Markian, a dialect of East Low German, its morphosyntactic annotation and morphological analysis, and in particular explores methods to bootstrap and develop such resources in the face of a complete lack of training data.
acl:2026.lrec-1.916.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference
acl:2026.lrec-1.916.title: Towards the Morphological Annotation of North Markian (Low German)
acl:2026.lrec-1.916.venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

acl:2026.lrec-1.919.abstract: Collecting and annotating morphological data present significant challenges, requiring linguistic expertise, methodological rigour, and substantial resources. These barriers are particularly acute for low-resource languages and varieties. To accelerate this process, we introduce CommonMorph, a comprehensive platform that streamlines morphological data collection development through a three-tiered approach: expert linguistic definition, contributor elicitation, and community validation. The platform minimises manual work by incorporating active learning, annotation suggestions, and tools to import and adapt materials from related languages. It accommodates diverse morphological systems, including fusional, agglutinative, and root-and-pattern morphologies. Its open-source design and UniMorph-compatible outputs ensure accessibility and interoperability with NLP tools. Our platform is accessible at https://common-morph.com, offering a replicable model for preserving linguistic diversity through collaborative technology.
acl:2026.lrec-1.919.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference
acl:2026.lrec-1.919.title: CommonMorph: Participatory Morphological Documentation Platform
acl:2026.lrec-1.919.venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

acl:2026.lrec-1.922.abstract: Precision computational grammars encode detailed linguistic analyses and compositional semantics that support rigorous investigation of grammatical phenomena, but their development requires substantial expertise and maintenance. To ensure long-term sustainability and accessibility of these resources, we present the DELPH-IN Grammary, a curated collection of twenty three HPSG grammars spanning seventeen languages and eight language families. The repository includes mature broad-coverage grammars (English, German, Japanese, Norwegian, Spanish) with associated treebanks, as well as grammars for typologically diverse and less-resourced languages. Each grammar is standardized with metadata, compiled using the ACE parser/generator, and loaded into the Linguistic Type Database for detailed inspection. Following FAIR principles, all resources are version-controlled and archived on Zenodo with annual releases synchronized to community development cycles. The Grammary enables reproducible grammar research, cross-linguistic typological studies, semantic parsing development, and grammar engineering pedagogy, providing the depth and theoretical grounding that complements data-driven approaches in computational linguistics. Our goal is to establish a sustainable model for preserving these valuable resources which bridge the critical gap between theoretical linguistics and empirical corpus based research. The Grammary is available at https://github.com/delph-in/grammary (Zenodo doi: zenodo.18945956).
acl:2026.lrec-1.922.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

glossary.explanation_id: Sebuah kerangka kerja linguistik berbasis batasan yang sangat leksikalisasi untuk menentukan properti sintaksis dan semantik bahasa.
Sebuah representasi semantik komposisional yang datar dan tidak terspesifikasi secara berlebihan yang digunakan dalam semua *grammar* DELPH-IN.
Sebuah *parser* dan *generator* yang efisien yang menerapkan *grammar* DELPH-IN ke kalimat-kalimat suatu bahasa.
Prinsip tata kelola data ilmiah yang memastikan sumber daya dapat ditemukan, dapat diakses, dapat beroperasi, dan dapat digunakan kembali.
Sebuah *korpus* teks yang dianotasi dengan struktur analisis sintaksis atau semantik.
Basis data berbasis web untuk memeriksa dan menjelajahi *grammar* dan *treebank* secara mendetail.

background.en: Precision computational grammars encode detailed linguistic analyses and compositional semantics that support rigorous investigation of grammatical phenomena. However, their development requires substantial expertise, continuous maintenance, and significant labor, often putting them at odds with the pace of software development and funding cycles. To preserve these valuable resources and enhance their accessibility, the authors address the gap between theoretical linguistics and empirical corpus-based research.
background.id: *Grammar* komputasi presisi mengenkode analisis linguistik mendetail dan semantik komposisional yang mendukung investigasi ketat terhadap fenomena gramatikal. Namun, pengembangannya membutuhkan keahlian yang substansial, pemeliharaan berkelanjutan, dan tenaga kerja yang signifikan, yang seringkali tidak sejalan dengan laju pengembangan perangkat lunak dan siklus pendanaan. Untuk melestarikan sumber daya berharga ini dan meningkatkan aksesibilitasnya, para penulis mengatasi kesenjangan antara linguistik teoretis dan riset berbasis *korpus* empiris.

contributions.en: The main contribution is the DELPH-IN Grammary, an open-source repository containing a standardized collection of twenty-three HPSG grammars across seventeen languages and eight language families. The repository includes metadata enrichment, automated compilation using the ACE parser/generator, local or upstream code repairs for legacy grammars, and integration with the Linguistic Type Database and pydelphin for interactive web exploration. All resources follow FAIR principles and are version-controlled and archived on Zenodo.
contributions.id: Kontribusi utama dari makalah ini adalah DELPH-IN Grammary, sebuah repositori sumber terbuka yang berisi koleksi terstandarisasi dari dua puluh tiga *grammar* HPSG di tujuh belas bahasa dan delapan famili bahasa. Repositori ini mencakup pengayaan *metadata*, kompilasi otomatis menggunakan *parser* atau *generator* ACE, perbaikan kode lokal atau hulu untuk *grammar* warisan, serta integrasi dengan *Linguistic Type Database* dan pydelphin untuk eksplorasi web interaktif. Semua sumber daya mengikuti prinsip *FAIR* serta dikontrol versinya dan diarsipkan di Zenodo.

future_work.en: The authors note limitations including lower coverage on unseen text compared to statistical parsers, limited linguistic diversity across only seventeen languages with gaps in certain regions, and the requirement of substantial background expertise in HPSG, MRS, and DELPH-IN tooling. Future work includes compiling all grammars with the LKB development environment, establishing annual releases synchronized with the DELPH-IN Summit, and using tools developed for Universal Dependencies to make syntax trees and semantic dependencies graph-searchable.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat beberapa keterbatasan termasuk cakupan yang lebih rendah pada teks yang belum terlihat dibandingkan dengan *parser* statistik, keragaman linguistik yang terbatas di hanya tujuh belas bahasa dengan celah di wilayah tertentu, serta persyaratan keahlian latar belakang yang substansial dalam *tooling* HPSG, MRS, dan DELPH-IN. Pekerjaan di masa mendatang mencakup pengkompilasian semua *grammar* dengan lingkungan pengembangan LKB, pembentukan rilis tahunan yang disinkronkan dengan DELPH-IN Summit, dan penggunaan *tool* yang dikembangkan untuk Universal Dependencies agar pohon sintaksis dan dependensi semantik dapat dicari melalui grafik.

method.en: The authors surveyed literature and repositories to locate the most recent versions of all known DELPH-IN grammars, recording canonical URLs and retrieval instructions. They enriched each grammar with minimal metadata, applied necessary code repairs to ensure successful compilation under current toolchains, and added sample sentences for demonstration. All grammars were then loaded into the Linguistic Type Database and compiled using the ACE parser/generator, with the final collection compressed and archived on Zenodo with annual releases planned.
method.id: Para penulis mensurvei literatur dan repositori untuk menemukan versi terbaru dari semua *grammar* DELPH-IN yang diketahui, mencatat URL kanonis dan instruksi pengambilan. Mereka memperkaya setiap *grammar* dengan *metadata* minimal, menerapkan perbaikan kode yang diperlukan untuk memastikan kompilasi yang sukses di bawah *toolchain* saat ini, dan menambahkan kalimat sampel untuk demonstrasi. Semua *grammar* kemudian dimuat ke dalam *Linguistic Type Database* dan dikompilasi menggunakan *parser* atau *generator* ACE, dengan koleksi akhir yang dikompresi dan diarsipkan di Zenodo dengan rencana rilis tahunan.

related_work.en: The authors compare their work with other projects developing broad-coverage computational grammars grounded in linguistic theory, such as CoreGram, ParGram, Grammatical Framework, and Universal Dependencies. While projects like CoreGram and ParGram build parallel or theory-grounded grammars, their resources are often not openly released or lack online exploration tools. Universal Dependencies offers broad multilingual treebanks but focuses on surface syntactic structures without model-theoretic constraints or compositional semantics, making these collections complementary to the DELPH-IN approach.
related_work.id: Para penulis membandingkan karya mereka dengan proyek lain yang mengembangkan *grammar* komputasi cakupan luas yang didasarkan pada teori linguistik, seperti CoreGram, ParGram, Grammatical Framework, dan Universal Dependencies. Meskipun proyek seperti CoreGram dan ParGram membangun *grammar* paralel atau berlandaskan teori, sumber daya mereka seringkali tidak dirilis secara terbuka atau kurang memiliki alat eksplorasi daring. Universal Dependencies menawarkan *treebank* multinasional yang luas tetapi berfokus pada struktur sintaksis permukaan tanpa batasan teoretis model atau semantik komposisional, menjadikan koleksi-koleksi ini komplementer terhadap pendekatan DELPH-IN.

results.en: The Grammary successfully compiles and organizes twenty-three grammars covering seventeen languages and eight language families, featuring mature broad-coverage grammars such as the English Resource Grammar, German Grammar, Jacy for Japanese, Norsource for Norwegian, and Spanish Resource Grammar, alongside grammars for typologically diverse and less-resourced languages. The integration with the Linguistic Type Database provides a web interface allowing users to inspect lexical entries, derivation trees, and semantic representations without local installation.
results.id: DELPH-IN Grammary berhasil mengompilasi dan mengorganisasi dua puluh tiga *grammar* yang mencakup tujuh belas bahasa dan delapan famili bahasa, menampilkan *grammar* cakupan luas yang matang seperti English Resource Grammar, German Grammar, Jacy untuk bahasa Jepang, Norsource untuk bahasa Norwegia, dan Spanish Resource Grammar, beserta *grammar* untuk bahasa-bahasa yang beragam secara tipologis dan memiliki sumber daya terbatas. Integrasi dengan *Linguistic Type Database* menyediakan antarmuka web yang memungkinkan pengguna untuk memeriksa entri leksikal, pohon derivasi, dan representasi semantik tanpa instalasi lokal.

tldr.en: This paper presents the DELPH-IN Grammary, a curated repository of twenty-three HPSG grammars spanning seventeen languages and eight language families. The repository ensures long-term sustainability and accessibility by standardizing resources, compiling them with the ACE parser, and archiving them on Zenodo following FAIR principles.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan DELPH-IN Grammary, sebuah repositori terkurasi yang terdiri dari dua puluh tiga *grammar* HPSG yang mencakup tujuh belas bahasa dan delapan famili bahasa. Repositori ini memastikan keberlanjutan dan aksesibilitas jangka panjang dengan menstandarisasi sumber daya, mengkompilasinya menggunakan *parser* ACE, dan mengarsipkannya di Zenodo mengikuti prinsip *FAIR*.

acl:2026.lrec-1.922.title: The DELPH-IN Grammary: A Curated Repository of Grammars and Treebanks
acl:2026.lrec-1.922.venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

acl:2026.lrec-1.93.abstract: Euskorpora is a pioneering initiative designed to establish a comprehensive digital infrastructure for the development of speech and language technologies in Basque. Built upon European, Spanish, and Basque strategies, it addresses the scarcity of linguistic data, foundational models, and technological resources for this non-Indo-European, low-resourced language. The project integrates large-scale data collection from public institutions and private organisations, creating extensive multimodal corpora that cover the linguistic, dialectal, and domain diversity of Basque. These resources support the training of open language models for speech, translation, and language understanding, as well as the establishment of an interoperable infrastructure aligned with European initiatives such as the European Language Data Space (LDS). By combining linguistic research, artificial intelligence, and data governance, Euskorpora ensures the digital sovereignty and inclusion of the Basque language within the global AI ecosystem. Beyond its regional focus, it stands as a transferable model for advancing linguistic diversity, technological innovation, and equitable digital transformation in multilingual Europe.
acl:2026.lrec-1.93.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference
acl:2026.lrec-1.93.title: Euskorpora: A Strategic Framework for Digital Sovereignty and Linguistic Inclusion of Basque in the Era of AI
acl:2026.lrec-1.93.venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

acl:2026.lt4hala-1.12.abstract: Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging is a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing, yet its performance on historical low-resource languages is still underexplored, particularly in the context of large generative models. While recent studies have demonstrated strong results for Large Language Models (LLMs) on modern languages and contemporary low-resource settings, their effectiveness for historical varieties remains unclear. Moreover, genre-specific structural variation, which may substantially affect tagging performance, has received limited attention. This study evaluates the zero- and few-shot POS tagging performance of two generative models on four historical Germanic low-resource languages across two literary genres. Their performance is benchmarked against fine-tuned BERT models. To contextualize the performance on historical data, the models are also evaluated on two modern languages. The results show that fine-tuned encoder models consistently outperform generative models across all settings. The performance of the LLMs on historical languages is substantially lower compared to that on modern languages, suggesting limited representation of these varieties in pretraining data. Furthermore, error analysis reveals structural output inconsistencies in LLM predictions that require additional post-processing. These findings highlight the limitations of zero- and few-shot generative models for historical low-resource POS tagging and underline the importance of task-specific fine-tuning.
acl:2026.lt4hala-1.12.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fourth Workshop on Language Technologies for Historical and Ancient Languages (LT4HALA 2026) @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Proses pemberian label kategori kata pada setiap *token* di dalam teks berdasarkan konteks gramatikalnya.
Pengaturan evaluasi di mana *model* melakukan tugas tanpa diberikan contoh demonstrasi di dalam *prompt*.
Pengaturan evaluasi di mana *model* diberikan beberapa contoh demonstrasi di dalam *prompt* sebelum melakukan tugas.
Proses pelatihan lanjutan pada *model* prarilis menggunakan data khusus untuk tugas tertentu.
Arsitektur *model* *neural* *network* yang memetakan urutan teks masukan menjadi representasi vektor terkontekstualisasi.
Sistem atau *model* pembanding standar yang digunakan untuk mengukur kinerja *model* baru.
Unit teks terkecil, seperti kata atau sub-kata, yang diproses oleh *model* bahasa.
Proses mencocokkan kembali *token* atau struktur teks hasil prediksi dengan data referensi emas.

background.en: Part-of-speech tagging is a fundamental task in natural language processing, but its performance on historical low-resource languages remains underexplored, especially for generative models. While large language models achieve strong results on modern languages and contemporary low-resource settings, their effectiveness on historical varieties is unclear. Furthermore, genre-specific structural variation that may substantially affect tagging performance has received limited attention in previous research.
background.id: *Part-of-speech* *tagging* adalah tugas mendasar dalam pengolahan bahasa alami, namun performanya pada bahasa historis *low-resource* masih kurang dieksplorasi, terutama untuk *model* generatif. Meskipun *large language model* mencapai hasil yang kuat pada bahasa modern dan pengaturan *low-resource* kontemporer, efektivitasnya pada ragam historis masih belum jelas. Selain itu, variasi struktural spesifik genre yang dapat memengaruhi performa *tagging* secara substansial hanya mendapat sedikit perhatian dalam penelitian sebelumnya.

contributions.en: This study evaluates the zero- and few-shot part-of-speech tagging performance of two generative models, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509, on four historical Germanic low-resource languages across poetry and prose genres. Their performance is benchmarked against fine-tuned Multilingual BERT models and contextualized using evaluations on two modern Germanic languages. The work also provides a thorough error analysis detailing structural output errors and formatting schema violations.
contributions.id: Studi ini mengevaluasi performa *part-of-speech* *tagging* *zero-shot* dan *few-shot* dari dua *model* generatif, yaitu Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct dan Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509, pada empat bahasa Jermanik historis *low-resource* di genre puisi dan prosa. Performa mereka diuji terhadap *model* Multilingual BERT yang telah di-*fine-tune* dan dikontekstualisasikan menggunakan evaluasi pada dua bahasa Jermanik modern. Karya ini juga menyediakan analisis kesalahan menyeluruh yang merinci kesalahan struktural keluaran dan pelanggaran skema pemformatan.

future_work.en: The authors state that future work will extend this investigation to additional natural language processing tasks and explore the fine-tuning of generative large language models to assess whether task-specific adaptation can improve performance.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyatakan bahwa penelitian di masa mendatang akan memperluas investigasi ini ke tugas pengolahan bahasa alami tambahan dan mengeksplorasi *fine-tuning* pada *large language model* generatif untuk menilai apakah adaptasi spesifik tugas dapat meningkatkan performa.

method.en: The study utilizes historical corpora for Old English, Old High German, Old Saxon, and Old Norse, alongside modern English and German corpora, covering both poetry and prose genres. All tags were mapped to Universal Dependencies part-of-speech tag sets. The generative models were evaluated using zero- and few-shot prompting strategies with greedy decoding without additional task-specific fine-tuning. Multilingual BERT models were fine-tuned as encoder baselines using the MaChAmp toolkit with a seq task type. A robust post-processing pipeline was implemented to handle structural validation, annotation mapping, and token alignment.
method.id: Studi ini memanfaatkan *korpus* historis untuk bahasa Inggris Kuno, Jerman Hulu Kuno, Sachsen Kuno, dan Nordik Kuno, beserta *korpus* bahasa Inggris dan Jerman modern, yang mencakup genre puisi dan prosa. Semua label dipetakan ke set label *part-of-speech* Universal Dependencies. *Model* generatif dievaluasi menggunakan strategi *prompting* *zero-shot* dan *few-shot* dengan *greedy* *decoding* tanpa *fine-tuning* spesifik tugas tambahan. *Model* Multilingual BERT di-*fine-tune* sebagai *baseline* *encoder* menggunakan perangkat MaChAmp dengan tipe tugas *seq*. Alur kerja *post-processing* yang tangguh diimplementasikan untuk menangani validasi struktural, pemetaan *anotasi*, dan *alignment* *token*.

related_work.en: Previous studies have investigated the abilities of large language models on part-of-speech tagging as part of broader linguistic surveys or specific modern tasks. A smaller number of works have examined low-resource historical languages, such as 16th-century Latin, Medieval Romance languages, and historical Chinese sources, showing that language variation, non-standard orthography, and diachronic changes present significant challenges. However, no prior studies have evaluated generative models on the four historical Germanic low-resource languages examined in this work using traditional POS datasets.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya telah menyelidiki kemampuan *large language model* pada *part-of-speech* *tagging* sebagai bagian dari survei linguistik yang lebih luas atau tugas modern tertentu. Sejumlah kecil karya telah meneliti bahasa historis *low-resource*, seperti bahasa Latin abad ke-16, bahasa Roman Abad Pertengahan, dan sumber Tiongkok kuno, yang menunjukkan bahwa variasi bahasa, ortografi non-standar, dan perubahan diakronik menghadirkan tantangan yang signifikan. Namun, belum ada penelitian sebelumnya yang mengevaluasi *model* generatif pada keempat bahasa historis Jermanik *low-resource* yang diteliti dalam karya ini menggunakan *dataset* POS tradisional.

results.en: The results demonstrate that fine-tuned encoder models consistently outperform generative models across all languages and genres, with accuracy exceeding 0.90 for Multilingual BERT. Generative models achieve substantially lower scores on historical languages compared to modern ones, indicating limited pretraining representation. Furthermore, error analysis reveals that generative models suffer from frequent structural output inconsistencies and schema violations, requiring extensive post-processing.
results.id: Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa *model* *encoder* yang telah di-*fine-tune* secara konsisten mengungguli *model* generatif di semua bahasa dan genre, dengan akurasi melampaui 0,90 untuk Multilingual BERT. *Model* generatif mencapai skor yang secara substansial lebih rendah pada bahasa historis dibandingkan bahasa modern, yang mengindikasikan representasi *pretraining* yang terbatas. Selain itu, analisis kesalahan mengungkapkan bahwa *model* generatif mengalami inkonsistensi struktur keluaran yang sering terjadi dan pelanggaran skema, sehingga memerlukan *post-processing* ekstensif.

tldr.en: This paper evaluates the zero- and few-shot part-of-speech tagging performance of generative large language models on historical Germanic low-resource languages across different genres. The results show that fine-tuned encoder models consistently outperform generative models, which suffer from poor performance on historical varieties and structural output inconsistencies.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengevaluasi performa *part-of-speech* *tagging* dalam pengaturan *zero-shot* dan *few-shot* dari *large language model* generatif pada bahasa Jermanik historis *low-resource* di berbagai genre. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa *model* *encoder* yang telah di-*fine-tune* secara konsisten mengungguli *model* generatif yang mengalami performa buruk pada ragam historis serta inkonsistensi struktur keluaran.

acl:2026.lt4hala-1.12.title: POS Tagging with Generative LLMs for Historical Germanic Low-Resource Languages: An Evaluation Against Fine-Tuned BERT
acl:2026.lt4hala-1.12.venue: Proceedings of the Fourth Workshop on Language Technologies for Historical and Ancient Languages (LT4HALA 2026) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.lt4hala-1.45.abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) for low-resource languages remains challenging due to limited annotated data and linguistic characteristics such as rich morphology and flexible word order. In this work, we propose a probing-based method that leverages the contextual knowledge encoded in pretrained language models to detect entities. Our approach uses a substitution strategy in which words in a sentence are replaced, one by one, with candidate entities of predefined entity types, referred to as probes. By measuring how well the probes of a certain entity type fit the surrounding context of the replaced word, we estimate the compatibility between the replaced word and the entity type. The resulting compatibility scores can be used either as a standalone zero-shot NER model or as an auxiliary feature during NER model decoding. We evaluate our method on the Latin dataset provided in the Fourth Workshop on Language Technologies for Historical and Ancient Languages (LT4HALA). Our system ranked second in the coarse-grained NER task. For the fine-grained NER task, where no training data were available, we relied exclusively on the proposed scoring method without any model training and achieved third place. These results demonstrate that contextual probing can provide an effective signal for NER in low-resource settings.
acl:2026.lt4hala-1.45.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fourth Workshop on Language Technologies for Historical and Ancient Languages (LT4HALA 2026) @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Tugas *Natural Language Processing* untuk mengidentifikasi dan mengklasifikasikan entitas bernomor atau bernama ke dalam kategori yang telah ditentukan.
Metrik yang digunakan untuk memperkirakan probabilitas kemunculan suatu token dalam konteks tertentu berdasarkan *model bahasa* bertopeng.
Entitas representatif yang telah ditentukan sebelumnya dan digunakan sebagai pengganti dalam strategi substitusi untuk menguji kompatibilitas kontekstual.
Nilai mentah yang dihasilkan oleh lapisan terakhir *model* sebelum diterapkan fungsi aktivasi seperti *softmax*.
Ukuran jarak edit untuk mengkuantifikasi perbedaan antara dua string teks berdasarkan jumlah operasi minimum.

background.en: Named Entity Recognition for low-resource languages remains challenging due to limited annotated training data and complex linguistic characteristics such as rich morphology and flexible word order. While standard approaches rely on fine-tuning pretrained language models, their performance heavily depends on the size and quality of available training data, making them less effective for ancient or historical languages like Latin.
background.id: *Named Entity Recognition* untuk bahasa *low-resource* masih menjadi tantangan akibat terbatasnya data pelatihan beranotasi serta karakteristik linguistik yang kompleks seperti morfologi yang kaya dan susunan kata yang fleksibel. Meskipun pendekatan standar mengandalkan *fine-tuning* *model bahasa* prapelatihan, kinerjanya sangat bergantung pada ukuran dan kualitas data pelatihan yang tersedia, sehingga kurang efektif untuk bahasa kuno atau historis seperti bahasa Latin.

contributions.en: The paper introduces a probing-based method using a substitution strategy to estimate compatibility between sentence words and predefined entity probes via pseudo-log-likelihood scores. This compatibility score serves either as a standalone zero-shot NER model without requiring any training data or as an auxiliary feature to guide decoding during the fine-tuning of NER models. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by ranking second in coarse-grained NER and third in fine-grained NER at the LT4HALA workshop.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan metode berbasis *probing* menggunakan strategi substitusi untuk memperkirakan kompatibilitas antara kata-kata dalam kalimat dan *probe* entitas pradefinisi melalui skor *pseudo-log-likelihood*. Skor kompatibilitas ini berfungsi baik sebagai *model* *zero-shot* *NER* mandiri tanpa memerlukan data pelatihan maupun sebagai fitur tambahan untuk memandu *decoding* selama *fine-tuning* *model* *NER*. Para penulis mendemonstrasikan keefektifan pendekatan ini dengan meraih peringkat kedua pada *NER* berbutir kasar dan peringkat ketiga pada *NER* berbutir halus di lokakarya LT4HALA.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss future work in detail.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan masa depan secara rinci.

method.en: The method computes a compatibility score for each word position and entity type using the Pseudo-Log-Likelihood metric derived from pretrained language models like LaBERTa and LatinBERT. For the supervised coarse-grained task, the compatibility scores are integrated into fine-tuned LaBERTa logits using a gating threshold. For the zero-shot fine-grained task, the standalone scoring method evaluates lists of probes across all pairs of top- and sub-level entity categories without model training. Evaluation is performed on five Latin datasets under strict and fuzzy precision, recall, and F1 metrics.
method.id: Metode ini menghitung skor kompatibilitas untuk setiap posisi kata dan jenis entitas menggunakan metrik *Pseudo-Log-Likelihood* yang diturunkan dari *model bahasa* prapelatihan seperti LaBERTa dan LatinBERT. Untuk tugas berbutir kasar tersupervisi, skor kompatibilitas diintegrasikan ke dalam *logit* LaBERTa yang telah di-*fine-tune* menggunakan ambang batas *gating*. Untuk tugas berbutir halus *zero-shot*, metode penentuan skor mandiri mengevaluasi daftar *probe* di semua pasangan kategori entitas tingkat atas dan sub-tingkat tanpa pelatihan model. Evaluasi dilakukan pada lima *korpus* bahasa Latin di bawah metrik *precision*, *recall*, dan *F1* dengan pengaturan *strict* dan *fuzzy*.

related_work.en: Prior research on Latin Named Entity Recognition explored traditional sequence-labelling techniques like Conditional Random Fields and rule-based methods, as well as multilingual or Latin-pretrained transformer models. Other recent studies explored probing and few-shot techniques such as point in-context learning, natural language definitions of entity types, and embedding-based similarity retrieval. However, these prior probing models primarily focus on prompting or similarity between candidate entities and type definitions rather than leveraging sentence context as the primary signal.
related_work.id: Penelitian terdahulu tentang *Named Entity Recognition* bahasa Latin mengeksplorasi teknik pelabelan sekuens tradisional seperti *Conditional Random Fields* dan metode berbasis aturan, serta *model* *transformer* multibahasa atau yang diprapelatihan untuk bahasa Latin. Studi terbaru lainnya mengeksplorasi teknik *probing* dan *few-shot* seperti *point in-context learning*, definisi bahasa alami untuk jenis entitas, dan temu kembali kemiripan berbasis *embedding*. Namun, model *probing* terdahulu tersebut terutama berfokus pada *prompting* atau kemiripan antara entitas kandidat dan definisi jenis alih-alih memanfaatkan konteks kalimat sebagai sinyal utama.

results.en: On Task 1 coarse-grained NER, LaBERTa integrated with the proposed probabilistic scoring achieved an F1 score of 0.714 under strict evaluation, ranking second in the competition. On Task 2 fine-grained NER with no training data, the zero-shot probing method achieved an F1 score of 0.129 strict and ranked third. Additional experiments show that adding the proposed probabilistic scoring method consistently improves fine-tuning performance for both LaBERTa and LatinBERT.
results.id: Pada Tugas 1 *NER* berbutir kasar, LaBERTa yang diintegrasikan dengan penentuan skor probabilitas yang diusulkan mencapai skor *F1* sebesar 0,714 di bawah evaluasi *strict*, menempati peringkat kedua dalam kompetisi. Pada Tugas 2 *NER* berbutir halus tanpa data pelatihan, metode *probing* *zero-shot* mencapai skor *F1* *strict* sebesar 0,129 dan menempati peringkat ketiga. Eksperimen tambahan menunjukkan bahwa penambahan metode penentuan skor probabilitas yang diusulkan secara konsisten meningkatkan kinerja *fine-tuning* untuk LaBERTa dan LatinBERT.

tldr.en: This paper proposes a contextual probing method to detect named entities in low-resource languages using pretrained language models. The approach achieves competitive results on Latin Named Entity Recognition tasks in both zero-shot and supervised settings.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan metode *probing* kontekstual untuk mendeteksi entitas bernama pada bahasa *low-resource* menggunakan *model bahasa* prapelatihan. Pendekatan ini mencapai hasil yang kompetitif pada tugas *Named Entity Recognition* bahasa Latin baik dalam pengaturan *zero-shot* maupun tersupervisi.

acl:2026.lt4hala-1.45.title: Contextual Probing for Low-Resource Named Entity Recognition in Latin
acl:2026.lt4hala-1.45.venue: Proceedings of the Fourth Workshop on Language Technologies for Historical and Ancient Languages (LT4HALA 2026) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.lt4hala-1.7.abstract: This project addresses the general absence of Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools when it comes to historical languages as a subset of low-resource languages that is relevant to an array of academic disciplines from linguistics to textual criticism. In particular, we train an Ancient Hebrew language model, BEReshiT, as well as BEReshiT-morph, a submodel for morphological annotation. BEReshiT is achieved through the fine-tuning of DictaBERT, a state-of-the-art model for Modern Hebrew that has also proved useful in Biblical Hebrew tasks. Layer freezing is applied in order to achieve maximal results and gain insight about the adaptation process. In the context of an elaborate cloze test, BEReshiT demonstrates increased performance and notions of the Ancient Hebrew language compared to the source model as well as a selection of additional relevant models. The submodel BEReshiT-morph performs highly on tasks of morphological classification, reaching an F1 score of 0.97 for part-of-speech (POS) tagging. We will release the main and morphological models as well as the datasets used at training and evaluation.
acl:2026.lt4hala-1.7.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fourth Workshop on Language Technologies for Historical and Ancient Languages (LT4HALA 2026) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.lt4hala-1.7.title: BEReshiT: an Ancient Hebrew Model based on DictaBERT
acl:2026.lt4hala-1.7.venue: Proceedings of the Fourth Workshop on Language Technologies for Historical and Ancient Languages (LT4HALA 2026) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.ltedi-1.1.abstract: Bangla memes are widely used on social media to express humor and social commentary, yet computational analysis of gender bias in Bangla memes remains largely unexplored. In this work, we present a multimodal framework for detecting gender bias in Bangla memes by jointly analyzing textual and visual con tent. We construct a dataset of 6,846 Bangla and Banglish code-mixed memes annotated into three categories: male-biased, female biased, and neutral. For textual representation, we use BanglishBERT, while visual features are extracted using ConvNeXt, and the two modalities are fused for final classification. Our best-performing model, ConvNeXt + BanglishBERT, achieves accuracy of 0.67 and an F1-score of 0.63, outperforming several multimodal baselines. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of multimodal learning for understanding culturally nuanced and code-mixed meme content in low-resource languages. Code and data available at this link
acl:2026.ltedi-1.1.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion
acl:2026.ltedi-1.1.title: Behind the Laughter: Uncovering Gender Bias in Code-Mixed Bangla Memes
acl:2026.ltedi-1.1.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion

acl:2026.ltedi-1.10.abstract: While automatic text summarization has achieved remarkable success in English,extending these capabilities to low-resource languages remains a significantchallenge due to the scarcity of labeled training data. We propose atranslation-augmented approach to multilingual summarization: we systematicallytranslate high-quality English summarization corpora into low-resource targetlanguages using NLLB-200, and use the resulting parallel data to train andevaluate sequence-to-sequence models. We experiment across three typologicallydiverse languages—Swahili, Hausa, and Afrikaans—comparing monolingualfine-tuning (MONO), cross-lingual transfer (XLT), and joint multilingualtraining (TAMT) on mBART-large-50. Monolingual fine-tuning achieves the bestperformance for Swahili (ROUGE-L 13.9) and Afrikaans (ROUGE-L 15.7),surpassing the Lead-3 baseline in both cases, while cross-lingual transferremains strongest for Hausa (ROUGE-L 14.5). We show that native language tokenavailability in mBART-50 is a critical determinant of fine-tuning performance,and characterize the conditions under which the theoretically expectedTAMT > MONO > XLT ordering breaks down. We release our dataset, code, andevaluation infrastructure to support future research on low-resourcemultilingual summarization.
acl:2026.ltedi-1.10.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion
acl:2026.ltedi-1.10.title: Translation-Augmented Multilingual Summarization for Low-Resource Languages
acl:2026.ltedi-1.10.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion

acl:2026.ltedi-1.16.abstract: Online hate speech is spreading rapidly, creating significant challenge, particularly in low-resource language such as Tamil. Lack of developed automated content moderation systems makes it difficult to control harmful content effectively. In this study, we propose a computational framework for generating Counter Narratives (CNs) using classical NLP techniques. With this, we leverage TF-IDF features with n-grams to identify the labels as Homophobic or Transphobic. Span detection is performed with TF-IDF features with n-grams and Machine learning models. Counter narratives are then retrieved by computing cosine similarity, ensuring semantic alignment and contextual relevance. Evaluation on the expanded human curated dataset demonstrates that our approach produces contextually appropriate and semantically coherent counter narratives. Notably, the proposed system is submitted at Task 2 shown a overall average score of 80.40 % for Tamil and 77.29 % for English and secured first and fourth rank respectively. GitHub: https://github.com/kannanrrk/Span-Counter-Feature-Based
acl:2026.ltedi-1.16.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion
acl:2026.ltedi-1.16.title: DLRG@LT-EDI 2026: Automating Counter-Narratives for Homophobic and Transphobic Comments
acl:2026.ltedi-1.16.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion

acl:2026.ltedi-1.22.abstract: Over the past decade, the rapid advancement of LLMs has significantly improved natural language generation. However, these models often inherit and amplify gender biases present in large-scale training data, leading to stereotypical associations, androcentric language, and misgendering. Such biases can negatively impact applications in education, healthcare, legal systems, and automated content generation. In this paper, we address this issue as defined in the shared task LT-EDI on Gender-Inclusive Language Generation. The task focuses on rewriting gender-biased sentences into inclusive, gender-neutral alternatives while preserving meaning. We propose a retrieval-augmented framework combining lexical replacement, semantic retrieval, and controlled instruction-tuned generation. An edit-distance constraint and self-evaluation step ensure minimal, coherent, and bias-free outputs. We also present zero-shot adaptation for low resource language. The implementation code available here https://github.com/SupriyaChanda/gilg-ltedi-acl2026.git.
acl:2026.ltedi-1.22.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion
acl:2026.ltedi-1.22.title: JustGen@LT-EDI 2026: Controlled Gender Inclusive and Bias-Aware Language Generation using LLMs
acl:2026.ltedi-1.22.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion

acl:2026.ltedi-1.25.abstract: The problem of harmful online discourse against the LGBTQ+ community is still a concern on social media platforms. Although hate speech detection is a well-explored area, the task of constructive counter-narrative generation is still an emerging field of research, especially in the multilingual and low-resource settings. Counter-narratives are designed to counter harmful discourse with respectful and empathetic responses, as opposed to mere content deletion. In this paper, the model proposes a zero-shot multilingual system for counter-narrative generation in English and Tamil. The proposed system employs the pretrained google/flan-t5-base transformer model guided by rubric-aligned prompts to encourage politeness, contextual relevance, and non-toxic response generation. The system operates in a zero-shot setting without task-specific fine-tuning and uses beam search decoding for controlled response generation. On the English test data, the system scored an overall score of 70.33 per cent with a contextual coherence score of 81.82 per cent. On the Tamil test data, the system scored an overall score of 33.57 per cent with significantly lower scores on coherence and quality. These findings indicate that structured prompting can facilitate safe and coherent generation in English, but also underscore the challenges of zero-shot multilingual models in low-resource language scenarios.
acl:2026.ltedi-1.25.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion
acl:2026.ltedi-1.25.title: RspectNLP@LT-EDI 2026:Rubric-Driven Prompting for Safe Multilingual Counter Narrative Generation
acl:2026.ltedi-1.25.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion

acl:2026.ltedi-1.3.abstract: Multilingual Natural Language Understanding (NLU) systems often struggle to adapt when new languages or new semantic labels are introduced with only a few annotated examples. This challenge is particularly pronounced for low-resource languages, where limited supervision and evolving label spaces make conventional joint-label classification approaches unstable. Most existing multilingual NLU models treat each language-semantic pair as an independent class, entangling linguistic and semantic representations and hindering few-shot adaptation. We propose Dual-Axis Compositional Few-Shot Learning, a framework that explicitly factorizes the representation space into linguistic and semantic embedding axes, enabling independent modeling of language variation and domain-intent semantics. Joint representations are constructed compositionally through multiplicative interaction of axis-specific embeddings, allowing controlled adaptation when either the language set or the semantic label space evolves. The framework integrates factorized prototype learning, axis-structured contrastive alignment, and disentanglement regularization using HSIC-based statistical independence and Jacobian-based cross-axis decorrelation. Experiments on six low-resource Indic languages spanning Indo-Aryan and Dravidian families (Hindi, Bengali, Sanskrit, Assamese, Tamil, and Telugu) demonstrate strong performance under two structured generalization regimes. The model achieves 81.12% accuracy when adapting to few-shot languages with known semantics and 63.5% accuracy when learning new semantic classes from few-shot examples, along with an accuracy of 89.56% on known language and seen semantics. These results show that axis-factorized representations enable stable compositional generalization, offering a promising direction for scalable multilingual NLU in linguistically diverse low-resource settings.
acl:2026.ltedi-1.3.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion
acl:2026.ltedi-1.3.title: Dual-Axis Compositional Contrastive Few-Shot Learning using Prototypes Across Linguistic and Semantic Dimensions for Indic Low-Resource Multilingual NLU
acl:2026.ltedi-1.3.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion

acl:2026.ltedi-1.9.abstract: The rapid expansion of social media platforms has led to a significant increase in the spread of harmful content, including misogynistic, homophobic, and transphobic memes. Detecting such content is challenging because memes often combine textual and visual elements and frequently appear in multilingual and culturally diverse contexts. This study proposes a multimodal transformer-based framework for multilingual harmful meme classification that integrates textual and visual representations to improve detection performance. The proposed architecture employs XLM-RoBERTa for multilingual text encoding and the Swin Transformer for hierarchical visual feature extraction. A cross-attention fusion mechanism is introduced to enable meaningful interaction between textual and visual modalities. The fused representation is then processed through a classification layer to perform multi-class prediction. Experiments are conducted across multiple datasets covering eight languages and three harmful content categories: misogyny, homophobia/transphobia, and hate speech. The model is evaluated using the macro-F1 score and demonstrates consistent improvements over baseline multimodal systems across both high-resource and low-resource languages. The results highlight the effectiveness of transformer-based multimodal architectures in capturing implicit and contextual harmful signals present in memes. The study contributes to the development of robust multilingual systems for harmful content detection and supports efforts toward creating safer and more inclusive online environments.
acl:2026.ltedi-1.9.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion
acl:2026.ltedi-1.9.title: Multimodal Transformer Framework for Multilingual Harmful Meme Classification
acl:2026.ltedi-1.9.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth Workshop on Language Technology for Equality, Diversity, Inclusion

acl:2026.mellm-1.12.abstract: Recent advances in multilingual representation learning aim to bridge the performance gap between high- and low-resource languages, yet their ability to preserve affective meaning across languages remains underexplored, particularly for underrepresented languages like Bengali. This research addresses cross-lingual sentiment misalignment between Bengali and English by introducing a controlled benchmarking framework evaluating four multilingual transformer models on parallel Bengali-English sentence pairs, stratified by dialect, to assess their representational stability. We demonstrate that a compressed model architecture exhibits a 28.7% “Sentiment Inversion Rate,” fundamentally misinterpreting positive semantics as negative (or vice versa). Consequently, we identify a cross-lingual sentiment skew that we call “Asymmetric Empathy”, where models systematically dampen or artificially amplify the affective weight of Bengali text relative to its exact English counterpart. Finally, we expose a key vulnerability regarding dialectal representation: a “Modern Bias” in the regional model, which exhibits a 57% increase in alignment error when processing the formal Bengali register compared to modern colloquial text. As foundational encoders continue to serve as safety classifiers and reward models for LLM pipelines, cross-lingual reliability becomes a critical concern. We therefore advocate for the integration of “Affective Stability” metrics into future cross-lingual benchmarks to detect and penalize polarity inversions, particularly in low-resource settings.
acl:2026.mellm-1.12.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)
acl:2026.mellm-1.12.title: Cross-Lingual Sentiment Misalignment: Auditing Multilingual Language Models for Inversion Risk, Dialectal Representation, and Affective Stability
acl:2026.mellm-1.12.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)

acl:2026.mellm-1.14.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) is commonly used to improve reasoning performance in large language models. We investigate its impact in multilingual contexts by systematically constraining reasoning steps across languages with varying resource levels. This study evaluates two models on two benchmarks with seven languages, comparing constrained CoT depth against zero-shot and free-CoT baselines. We demonstrate that increasing the number of reasoning steps does not consistently improve accuracy across various languages. While high-resource and mid-resource languages remain stable, low-resource languages often experience a decline in performance as the number of reasoning steps increases. We attribute this decline to error accumulation and reasoning noise, which are amplified under deeper reasoning in low-resource languages. These findings indicate that CoT is not inherently beneficial, but its effectiveness is significantly influenced by the interaction between reasoning steps and language resource availability.
acl:2026.mellm-1.14.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)
acl:2026.mellm-1.14.title: Do Thoughts Depth Affect Multilingual Reasoning?
acl:2026.mellm-1.14.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)

acl:2026.mellm-1.18.abstract: We present Polyglot-Lion, a family of compact multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) models tailored for the linguistic landscape of Singapore, covering English, Mandarin, Tamil, and Malay. Our models are obtained by fine-tuning Qwen3-ASR-0.6B and Qwen3-ASR-1.7B exclusively on publicly available speech corpora, using a balanced sampling strategy that equalizes the number of training utterances per language and deliberately omits language-tag conditioning so that the model learns to identify languages implicitly from audio. On 12 benchmarks spanning the four target languages, Polyglot-Lion-1.7B achieves an average error rate of 14.85, competitive with MERaLiON-2-10B-ASR (14.32) - a model 6x larger - while incurring a training cost of 81 on a single RTX PRO 6000 GPU. Inference throughput is approximately 20x faster than MERaLiON at 0.10 s/sample versus 2.02 s/sample. These results demonstrate that linguistically balanced fine-tuning of moderate-scale pretrained models can yield deployment-ready multilingual ASR at a fraction of the cost of larger specialist systems.
acl:2026.mellm-1.18.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)
acl:2026.mellm-1.18.title: Polyglot-Lion: Efficient Multilingual ASR for Singapore via Balanced Fine-Tuning of Qwen3-ASR
acl:2026.mellm-1.18.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)

acl:2026.mellm-1.19.abstract: Multilingual retrieval increasingly underpins cross-lingual question answering and retrieval-augmented generation. Strong zero-shot scores on multilingual benchmarks are often taken as evidence that current encoders transfer reliably across many languages. We argue that this assumption breaks down for underrepresented, morphologically rich languages, and use Amharic as a diagnostic case. Under a shared passage retrieval protocol covering dense, late-interaction, learned sparse, and cross-encoder paradigms, we compare zero-shot multilingual retrievers, Amharic-fine-tuned multilingual retrievers, and monolingual Amharic retrievers. The strongest zero-shot multilingual retriever underperforms the strongest monolingual Amharic first-stage retriever by 23% relative MRR@10. Fine-tuning two recent multilingual embedding models on the same Amharic supervision yields 32–60% relative MRR@10 gains over zero-shot, but the best Amharic-fine-tuned multilingual model remains below the strongest monolingual Amharic retriever. These findings indicate that zero-shot multilingual retrieval is not a sufficient proxy for equitable information access in the LLM era: for underrepresented languages, retrieval must be evaluated and adapted in language rather than inferred from aggregate multilingual benchmarks. To foster future research, we publicly release our trained models, dataset, and codebase at https://github.com/rasyosef/amharic-neural-ir.
acl:2026.mellm-1.19.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)
acl:2026.mellm-1.19.title: The Multilingual Curse at the Retrieval Layer: Evidence from Amharic
acl:2026.mellm-1.19.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)

acl:2026.mellm-1.2.abstract: Inspired by linguistic Olympiads, extremely low-resource language reasoning presents a unique challenge that enables models to solve problems without prior knowledge. This task mirrors the Rosetta Stone decipherment process, where the goal is to induce and apply linguistic rules from minimal context. Existing methods mainly rely on naive in-context learning that fails to handle the complexity and diversity of language rules. To mitigate this issue, we propose a framework that combines dynamic knowledge construction with task-aware evidence augmentation. First, we use large language models (LLMs) to generate a diverse set of task-specific examples that instantiate potential linguistic rules for the target low-resource language. Second, we apply a semantic retrieval mechanism to select the most relevant examples as evidence for each test query, preventing context overload and ensuring focused, analogical reasoning. Our method shifts from learning language distributions to dynamically discovering and applying rules. Experimental results on the LINGOLY and Linguini benchmark show that our approach achieves competitive performance across various LLMs, outperforming existing baselines. More importantly, our framework advances extremely low-resource reasoning and provides a generalizable framework for rule induction under knowledge constraints.
acl:2026.mellm-1.2.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)
acl:2026.mellm-1.2.title: Evidence-Augmented Generation Reasoning for Extremely Low-Resource Language Decipherment
acl:2026.mellm-1.2.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)

acl:2026.mellm-1.20.abstract: Emotion detection is an important text classification task with applications in sentiment analysis, social media monitoring, human-computer interaction, and affective language understanding. However, Punjabi written in the Shahmukhi script remains severely under-resourced for emotion detection, with limited benchmark-style resources available for supervised evaluation. This paper introduces ShahiEmotion, a new Punjabi Shahmukhi emotion detection dataset containing 30379 sentence-level instances annotated with seven emotion categories: sadness, surprise, happiness, anger, neutral, fear, and disgust. The dataset is designed to support research in a low-resource setting characterized by script-specific challenges, lexical variation, and substantial class imbalance. We establish baseline results using several pretrained transformer-based models and formulate emotion detection as a sentence-level classification task. In particular, we fine-tune multilingual BERT, multilingual DistilBERT, XLM-RoBERTa, and Urdu RoBERTa under the same training and evaluation setting using standard cross-entropy loss. Experimental results show that XLM-RoBERTa provides the strongest overall performance among the compared models. The best model achieves 77.95% accuracy, 58.47% macro-F1, and 77.60% weighted-F1 on the test set. The dataset, evaluation protocol, and baseline results introduced in this work are intended to support future research on Punjabi Shahmukhi emotion analysis and low-resource NLP.
acl:2026.mellm-1.20.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)
acl:2026.mellm-1.20.title: ShahiEmotion: A Benchmark Dataset for Punjabi Shahmukhi Emotion Detection
acl:2026.mellm-1.20.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)

acl:2026.mellm-1.8.abstract: Chain-of-thought reasoning improves the performance of large language models on complex tasks but often produces overly verbose outputs, leading to increased inference cost. This issue is exacerbated in multilingual settings, where differences in tokenization and linguistic structure result in inconsistent compression performance across languages. Existing methods are largely English-centric and tend to suffer from accuracy degradation, especially in low-resource languages.We propose \textbf{M}ultilingual \textbf{C}hain-of-thought Compression via Cross-lingual \textbf{D}istillation \textbf{(MCD)}, a unified framework that addresses these challenges through both data construction and optimization. MCD builds a cross-lingually aligned dataset using a translation-with-verification pipeline and difficulty-aware sampling, and employs a reinforcement training strategy that combines supervised fine-tuning with direct preference optimization to encourage concise yet sufficient reasoning.Experiments on multilingual mathematical benchmarks show that MCD consistently reduces reasoning length while maintaining competitive accuracy, and significantly improves robustness in low-resource languages.
acl:2026.mellm-1.8.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)
acl:2026.mellm-1.8.title: Multilingual Chain-of-Thought Compression via Cross-Lingual Distillation
acl:2026.mellm-1.8.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)

acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.15.abstract: Identifying intertextual parallels is central to philology, traditionally requiring labor-intensive manual analysis. While digitized historical corpora enable automated approaches using semantic sentence embeddings, training such models requires large annotated datasets, which are scarce for low-resource languages. We address this challenge by introducing a scalable automatic annotation pipeline for training semantic embedding models for Classical Tibetan. Our method combines unsupervised contrastive bootstrapping with iterative pair mining, generating silver-standard similarity labels through two complementary annotation strategies: (1) an ensemble of embedding models and rerankers, and (2) an LLM-as-a-judge committee using best–worst scaling. When combined with a domain-specific, gold-standard annotated dataset for sequential fine-tuning, the resulting text-similarity model achieves a state-of-the-art Spearman correlation of 0.864 on the STS task. This enables effective semantic search in Classical Tibetan and provides a framework for automatic supervision in low-resource languages used in digital humanities. We will make our code, dataset, and trained model publicly available upon publication.
acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.15.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Natural Language Processing for the Digital Humanities
acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.15.title: Scaling Sentence Similarity for Classical Tibetan with Automatic Annotations
acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.15.venue: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Natural Language Processing for the Digital Humanities

acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.16.abstract: Historical corpora for Tagalog remain limited, particularly texts produced during the Martial Law period under the dictatorship of Ferdinand Marcos Sr. (1972–1986). Much of this material remains undigitized, restricting computational analysis of a significant period in Philippine political history. To support research on historical Tagalog texts, we introduce PHMartialLawNER, a gold-standard named entity recognition corpus constructed from newspapers and underground publications of the Martial Law era. The corpus includes approximately 13k extracted sentence segments (362,000 tokens), consolidated into 8k annotated text spans through a semi-automatic pipeline with manual validation. The reliability of the annotation is measured using Cohen’s \kappa, reaching 0.86 on all tokens and 0.72 on annotated tokens, with a pairwise F1-score of 0.74. The schema defines historically relevant entity categories including Person (Individual, Collective), Organization (Political, Government, Other), Event (Local, International), Production (Media, Government, Doctrine), as well as Time, Numerical Statistics, Location, and Object entities, specifically identifying weapon artifacts. We establish baseline performance using GLiNER variants, calamanCy models, and transformer-based architectures under zero-shot and few-shot settings. The PHMartialLawNER corpus will be publicly released to support Tagalog NLP, historical text processing, and digital humanities research.
acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.16.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Natural Language Processing for the Digital Humanities
acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.16.title: PHMartialLawNER: A Tagalog Named Entity Recognition Corpus for the Philippine Martial Law Era
acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.16.venue: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Natural Language Processing for the Digital Humanities

acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.6.abstract: Ancient and endangered languages pose a unique challenge for NLP: their datasets are inherently scarce, difficult to expand, and built from formulaic corpora—making data-quality issues especially consequential yet rarely audited. Motivated by the need to understand what current NMT can realistically achieve for such languages, we investigate hieroglyphic-to-German translation, where a recent study reported 61.5 BLEU using fine-tuned M2M-100. Our reproduction yields only 37.0 BLEU with the released model. Investigating this gap, we find 32% of test targets appear identically in training (16/50; 50% under 8-gram overlap at 70% threshold). This contamination inflates scores dramatically: contaminated samples achieve up to 83.8 BLEU / 0.924 COMET-22 versus 30.9–39.2 BLEU / 0.622–0.676 COMET-22 on clean samples across five model configurations spanning two architectures. Document-level decontamination reduces contaminated BLEU by only 4.6 points because 8/16 targets persist via other source documents—target-level deduplication is required. We release a decontaminated 34-sample test set and establish corrected baselines (30.9–39.2 BLEU), providing a realistic assessment of NMT capability for this endangered writing system.
acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.6.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Natural Language Processing for the Digital Humanities
acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.6.title: Data Contamination in Neural Hieroglyphic Translation: A Reproducibility Study
acl:2026.nlp4dh-1.6.venue: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Natural Language Processing for the Digital Humanities

acl:2026.nlp4ecology-1.7.abstract: Climate change discourse has expanded substantially in recent decades, yet computational analyses remain concentrated on high-resource languages. In this paper, we construct a longitudinal Vietnamese climate news corpus and examine thematic structure and temporal evolution in a lower-resource setting. The corpus comprises 10,401 articles published between 2004 and 2026 and is systematically preprocessed using linguistically informed word segmentation. To ensure domestic relevance, we apply transformer-based Named Entity Recognition and construct a geographically grounded subset of 4,501 Vietnam-focused documents. We analyze this dataset using both Latent Dirichlet Allocation and BERTopic.
