Results reveal stable thematic dimensions alongside longitudinal shifts from event-driven pollution reporting toward governance- and energy-centered narratives. Embedding-based modeling achieves higher semantic coherence while maintaining comparable topic diversity. The main contribution of this work is thus the compilation of a structured Vietnamese climate corpus and a systematic analysis of discourse evolution in an underrepresented language context.
acl:2026.nlp4ecology-1.7.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 2nd Workshop on Ecology, Environment, and Natural Language Processing

glossary.explanation_id: Latent Dirichlet Allocation adalah model probabilistik generatif yang digunakan dalam *topic modeling* untuk menemukan struktur tematik tersembunyi di dalam sekumpulan dokumen.
BERTopic adalah teknik *topic modeling* berbasis *embedding* yang memanfaatkan representasi *transformer* dan klusterisasi densitas untuk menangkap kemiripan semantik antar dokumen.
Named Entity Recognition adalah tugas NLP untuk mengidentifikasi dan mengklasifikasikan entitas bernama seperti lokasi, organisasi, atau orang di dalam teks.
UMAP adalah algoritma yang digunakan untuk reduksi dimensi dengan mempertahankan struktur semantik global dari data berdimensi tinggi.
HDBSCAN adalah algoritma klusterisasi berbasis densitas hierarkis yang mengelompokkan data serupa sekaligus membiarkan titik-titik derau tidak ditetapkan ke kluster manapun.
c-TF-IDF adalah varian dari *TF-IDF* yang dihitung pada tingkat kluster untuk mengekstrak kata-kata yang paling khas bagi setiap topik di dalam *BERTopic*.
NPMI adalah metrik evaluasi yang mengukur kekuatan asosiasi kata dinormalisasi untuk menilai koherensi lokal dari kata-kata representatif suatu topik.

background.en: Climate change discourse has grown substantially, yet computational analyses remain heavily concentrated on high-resource languages like English. This leaves a significant gap in understanding environmental narratives in low-resource contexts, where linguistic, cultural, and institutional factors differ. Furthermore, the Vietnamese language presents unique challenges such as multi-syllabic word segmentation, lexical ambiguity, and limited domain-specific resources, which complicate preprocessing and make standard coherence metrics behave unreliably.
background.id: Diskursus perubahan iklim telah berkembang pesat, namun analisis komputasi masih sangat terkonsentrasi pada bahasa-bahasa sumber daya tinggi seperti bahasa Inggris. Hal ini menyisakan celah yang signifikan dalam memahami narasi lingkungan pada konteks *low-resource*, di mana faktor linguistik, kultural, dan institusional berbeda. Selain itu, bahasa Vietnam menghadirkan tantangan unik seperti segmentasi kata bersuku kata banyak, ambiguitas leksikal, dan terbatasnya sumber daya spesifik domain, yang mempersulit prapemrosesan dan membuat metrik koherensi standar berperilaku tidak andal.

contributions.en: The paper makes three primary contributions: first, it introduces a structured longitudinal Vietnamese climate news corpus spanning over two decades from 2004 to 2026; second, it provides a systematic methodological comparison between probabilistic Latent Dirichlet Allocation and embedding-based BERTopic in a low-resource language; and third, it critically evaluates topic coherence metrics, demonstrating how standard measures can underestimate topic quality in Vietnamese due to surface-level co-occurrence limitations.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memberikan tiga kontribusi utama: pertama, memperkenalkan korpus berita iklim bahasa Vietnam longitudinal terstruktur yang mencakup lebih dari dua dekade dari tahun 2004 hingga 2026; kedua, menyediakan perbandingan metodologis yang sistematis antara *Latent Dirichlet Allocation* probabilistik dan *BERTopic* berbasis *embedding* dalam bahasa *low-resource*; dan ketiga, mengevaluasi secara kritis metrik koherensi topik, yang menunjukkan bagaimana ukuran standar dapat meremehkan kualitas topik dalam bahasa Vietnam karena keterbatasan ko-okurensi tingkat permukaan.

future_work.en: The authors note several limitations, including the reliance on mainstream national media which may introduce structural bias and underrepresent local perspectives, potential noise introduced by automatic word segmentation, limited domain-specific pretrained models in Vietnamese, and the lack of human qualitative validation. Future directions include extending the corpus to regional outlets and social media, employing dynamic topic modeling for fine-grained temporal analysis, applying domain-adaptive pretraining, and integrating sentiment or uncertainty modeling.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat beberapa keterbatasan, termasuk ketergantungan pada media nasional arus utama yang dapat memperkenalkan bias struktural dan kurang merepresentasikan perspektif lokal, potensi noise yang diperkenalkan oleh segmentasi kata otomatis, terbatasnya model praterlatih spesifik domain dalam bahasa Vietnam, dan kurangnya validasi kualitatif oleh manusia. Arah masa depan meliputi memperluas korpus ke outlet regional dan media sosial, menerapkan *dynamic topic modeling* untuk analisis temporal yang lebih rinci, menerapkan *domain-adaptive pretraining*, serta mengintegrasikan pemodelan sentimen atau ketidakpastian.

method.en: The authors construct a corpus of 10,401 articles from major Vietnamese news outlets using automated scraping and preprocess the text using vncorenlp for linguistically informed word segmentation, along with stopword removal and frequency-based dictionary filtering. They apply a transformer-based Named Entity Recognition model to extract a geographically grounded subset of 4,501 Vietnam-focused documents. For modeling, they implement Latent Dirichlet Allocation with 15 passes and asymmetric priors, alongside BERTopic using sentence-transformers, UMAP for dimensionality reduction, HDBSCAN for clustering, and c-TF-IDF for representation. Model evaluation utilizes topic coherence metrics including cv and NPMI, alongside Jaccard-based topic diversity.
method.id: Para penulis membangun korpus yang terdiri dari 10.401 artikel dari outlet berita utama Vietnam menggunakan *scraping* otomatis dan memprapemrosesan teks menggunakan vncorenlp untuk segmentasi kata yang diinformasikan secara linguistik, beserta penghapusan *stopword* dan pemfilteran kamus berbasis frekuensi. Mereka menerapkan model *Named Entity Recognition* berbasis *transformer* untuk mengekstrak subset yang berpijak secara geografis sejumlah 4.501 dokumen yang berfokus pada Vietnam. Untuk pemodelan, mereka mengimplementasikan *Latent Dirichlet Allocation* dengan 15 putaran dan *prior* asimetris, beserta *BERTopic* menggunakan *sentence-transformers*, UMAP untuk reduksi dimensi, HDBSCAN untuk klusterisasi, dan c-TF-IDF untuk representasi. Evaluasi model menggunakan metrik koherensi topik termasuk cv dan NPMI, beserta keragaman topik berbasis Jaccard.

related_work.en: Prior computational analyses of climate discourse have applied NLP to policy documents, institutional texts, and social media platforms using approaches such as Latent Dirichlet Allocation and embedding-based models like BERTopic. In low-resource settings, recent studies have introduced datasets or hybrid models for languages like Bengali, but typically focus on single methods with limited comparative evaluation. For Vietnamese, climate communication research has relied almost entirely on qualitative approaches without large-scale computational analysis or systematic longitudinal comparisons.
related_work.id: Analisis komputasi terdahulu mengenai diskursus iklim telah menerapkan NLP pada dokumen kebijakan, teks institusional, dan platform media sosial menggunakan pendekatan seperti *Latent Dirichlet Allocation* dan model berbasis *embedding* seperti *BERTopic*. Dalam pengaturan *low-resource*, studi-studi terbaru telah memperkenalkan dataset atau model hibrida untuk bahasa seperti bahasa Bengali, namun biasanya berfokus pada metode tunggal dengan evaluasi komparatif yang terbatas. Untuk bahasa Vietnam, penelitian komunikasi iklim hampir sepenuhnya mengandalkan pendekatan kualitatif tanpa analisis komputasi berskala besar atau perbandingan longitudinal yang sistematis.

results.en: Both LDA and BERTopic identify six coherent topics centered on pollution, energy transition, adaptation, and policy. Longitudinal analysis reveals that early media attention focused on event-driven pollution crises, which later shifted toward institutional governance, international commitments, and energy transition narratives. Quantitatively, BERTopic achieves higher semantic coherence with a cv score of 0.66 and an NPMI of 0.18 compared to LDA's 0.55 and 0.06, while both maintain high topic diversity above 0.93. The authors interpret the low NPMI scores for LDA as a metric mismatch rather than poor topic quality, driven by lexical synonymy and corpus sparsity in Vietnamese.
results.id: Baik LDA maupun *BERTopic* mengidentifikasi enam topik koheren yang berpusat pada polusi, transisi energi, adaptasi, dan kebijakan. Analisis longitudinal mengungkapkan bahwa perhatian media awal berfokus pada krisis polusi berbasis kejadian, yang kemudian bergeser menuju tata kelola institusional, komitmen internasional, dan narasi transisi energi. Secara kuantitatif, *BERTopic* mencapai koherensi semantik yang lebih tinggi dengan skor cv sebesar 0,66 dan NPMI sebesar 0,18 dibandingkan dengan LDA yang masing-masing 0,55 dan 0,06, sementara keduanya mempertahankan keragaman topik yang tinggi di atas 0,93. Para penulis menginterpretasikan skor NPMI yang rendah untuk LDA sebagai ketidakcocokan metrik daripada kualitas topik yang buruk, yang didorong oleh sinonimi leksikal dan sparsitas korpus dalam bahasa Vietnam.

tldr.en: This paper constructs a longitudinal Vietnamese climate news corpus and applies comparative topic modeling to examine thematic structures and temporal evolution. The main finding reveals stable thematic dimensions alongside a shift from event-driven pollution reporting to governance- and energy-centered narratives.
tldr.id: Artikel ini membangun sebuah korpus berita iklim bahasa Vietnam yang longitudinal dan menerapkan *topic modeling* komparatif untuk meneliti struktur tematik serta evolusi temporalnya. Temuan utamanya mengungkapkan dimensi tematik yang stabil seiring dengan pergeseran dari pelaporan polusi berbasis kejadian menuju narasi yang berpusat pada tata kelola dan energi.

acl:2026.nlp4ecology-1.7.title: Ecological Discourse Modeling in a Low-Resource Setting: A Longitudinal Vietnamese Climate Corpus with Comparative Topic Modeling
acl:2026.nlp4ecology-1.7.venue: Proceedings of the 2nd Workshop on Ecology, Environment, and Natural Language Processing

acl:2026.nlpaics-1.24.abstract: A common assumption in low-resource NLP is that cross-lingual transfer from a related language can substitute for target-language annotation when labelled data is scarce. We test this assumption for offensive content detection across five Indic languages by evaluating all twenty directed transfer pairs from a LLaMA3.1-8B model fine-tuned with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on the MACD benchmark. Only three of twenty pairs achieve tolerable transfer loss below 15%, all involving Malayalam as the source language. Telugu is the hardest transfer target (average loss 33.8%), while Malayalam is the most transferable source (average loss 16.8%). Confusion-matrix analysis reveals two distinct failure modes: Tamiland Kannada-trained models are conservative under-flaggers that miss 73–82% of offensive content with near-zero false alarms, while Malayalam-trained models are aggressive flaggers that miss far less (39%) but over-flag at 21%. These patterns do not follow typological structure: a Spearman correlation between URIEL typological similarity and transfer F1 yields ρ = −0.254 (p = 0.281), failing to conf irm the typological hypothesis. Our results indicate that cross-lingual shortcuts are unreliable for this task and that language-specific annotation cannot be avoided by appealing to linguistic family membership.
acl:2026.nlpaics-1.24.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Second International Conference on Natural Language Processing and Artificial Intelligence for Cyber Security

glossary.explanation_id: Teknik mentransfer pengetahuan dari model yang dilatih pada satu bahasa ke bahasa target yang berbeda.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain memiliki ketersediaan data latih dan sumber daya komputasi yang sangat terbatas.
Proses melatih ulang model terlatih (*pretrained model*) menggunakan data baru agar sesuai dengan tugas spesifik.
Evaluasi model pada tugas atau bahasa baru tanpa memberikan contoh pelatihan sebelumnya.
Metode *parameter-efficient fine-tuning* yang melatih matriks peringkat rendah alih-alih seluruh parameter *large language model*.
Standar atau kumpulan data standar yang digunakan untuk mengevaluasi dan membandingkan performa model.
Model atau metode dasar yang digunakan sebagai titik perbandingan untuk mengukur peningkatan performa.
Arsitektur model bahasa yang hanya menggunakan komponen *encoder*, biasanya digunakan untuk tugas pemahaman teks.

background.en: Building offensive content detection systems for low-resource languages is resource-intensive and requires substantial annotation effort. A common assumption is that cross-lingual transfer from a related language can serve as a substitute for target-language data. This is particularly intuitive in the Indic context where multiple languages share morphological structures or contact features.
background.id: Membangun sistem deteksi konten ofensif untuk bahasa *low-resource* memerlukan banyak sumber daya dan upaya anotasi yang besar. Anggapan umum adalah bahwa *cross-lingual transfer* dari bahasa terkait dapat menjadi pengganti data bahasa target. Hal ini sangat intuitif dalam konteks bahasa India di mana berbagai bahasa berbagi struktur morfologi atau fitur kontak.

contributions.en: The paper provides the first complete directed transfer matrix across five Indic languages on a single benchmark, accompanied by a quantitative typological control. The contribution is empirical and cautionary, demonstrating that language-specific annotation cannot be avoided by appealing to linguistic family membership.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyajikan matriks *transfer* terarah yang lengkap pertama di lima bahasa India pada satu *benchmark*, disertai dengan kontrol tipologis kuantitatif. Kontribusinya bersifat empiris dan memperingatkan bahwa anotasi spesifik bahasa tidak dapat dihindari dengan mengandalkan keanggotaan rumpun bahasa.

future_work.en: The authors note limitations including the binary label taxonomy of the MACD dataset and the limited statistical power of the URIEL control across twenty data points. They suggest that replication of the experiments on encoder-only models such as XLM-R and IndicBERT is the most important direction for follow-up work.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat keterbatasan termasuk taksonomi label biner dari *dataset* MACD dan daya statistik kontrol URIEL yang terbatas pada dua puluh titik data. Mereka menyarankan bahwa replikasi eksperimen pada model *encoder-only* seperti XLM-R dan IndicBERT adalah arah terpenting untuk pekerjaan lanjutan.

method.en: The authors use the MACD dataset containing user-generated comments annotated for offensive versus non-offensive content. They fine-tune LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct on each language independently using LoRA across all twenty directed zero-shot cross-lingual transfer pairs. Transfer loss is computed relative to monolingual baselines, and typological control is evaluated using URIEL feature vectors via lang2vec.
method.id: Para penulis menggunakan *dataset* MACD yang berisi komentar buatan pengguna yang dianotasi untuk konten ofensif versus non-ofensif. Mereka melakukan *fine-tuning* pada LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct di setiap bahasa secara independen menggunakan *LoRA* di seluruh dua puluh pasangan *cross-lingual transfer zero-shot* terarah. *Transfer loss* dihitung relatif terhadap *baseline* monolingual, dan kontrol tipologis dievaluasi menggunakan vektor fitur URIEL melalui lang2vec.

related_work.en: Prior research demonstrates that cross-lingual transfer correlates with typological proximity on structural NLP tasks. However, for pragmatically motivated tasks such as offensive language detection, previous studies suggest that cultural rather than structural factors play a larger role. Existing work on Indic offensive language detection has largely focused on monolingual or code-mixed settings, while cross-lingual studies typically cover only a partial subset of pairs without quantitative typological controls.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya menunjukkan bahwa *cross-lingual transfer* berkorelasi dengan kedekatan tipologis pada tugas NLP struktural. Namun, untuk tugas yang dimotivasi secara pragmatis seperti deteksi bahasa ofensif, studi terdahulu menyarankan bahwa faktor budaya alih-alih struktural memainkan peran yang lebih besar. Pekerjaan yang ada mengenai deteksi bahasa ofensif di India sebagian besar berfokus pada pengaturan monolingual atau *code-mixed*, sementara studi lintas bahasa biasanya hanya mencakup sebagian kecil pasangan tanpa kontrol tipologis kuantitatif.

results.en: Only three of the twenty directed transfer pairs achieve tolerable transfer loss below 15 percent, all of which use Malayalam as the source language. Telugu proves to be the hardest transfer target, while Malayalam is the most transferable source. Confusion-matrix analysis shows distinct failure modes where Tamil and Kannada models act as conservative under-flaggers, whereas Malayalam models over-flag. Furthermore, URIEL typological similarity fails to predict transfer performance.
results.id: Hanya tiga dari dua puluh pasangan *transfer* terarah yang mencapai *transfer loss* yang dapat ditoleransi di bawah 15 persen, yang semuanya menggunakan bahasa Malayalam sebagai bahasa sumber. Telugu terbukti menjadi target *transfer* yang paling sulit, sementara Malayalam adalah sumber yang paling dapat ditransfer. Analisis *confusion-matrix* menunjukkan mode kegagalan yang berbeda di mana model Tamil dan Kannada bertindak sebagai *under-flagger* yang konservatif, sedangkan model Malayalam melakukan *over-flag*. Lebih lanjut, kesamaan tipologis URIEL gagal memprediksi performa *transfer*.

tldr.en: This paper evaluates cross-lingual transfer for offensive content detection across five Indic languages using fine-tuned LLaMA-3.1-8B models. The results show that cross-lingual shortcuts are largely unreliable and do not correlate with typological similarity.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengevaluasi *cross-lingual transfer* untuk deteksi konten ofensif di lima bahasa India menggunakan model LLaMA-3.1-8B yang telah di-*fine-tune*. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa jalan pintas lintas bahasa sebagian besar tidak dapat diandalkan dan tidak berkorelasi dengan kesamaan tipologis.

acl:2026.nlpaics-1.24.title: Does Hate Transfer? Cross-Lingual Generalisation of Offensive Content Detection Across Indic Languages
acl:2026.nlpaics-1.24.venue: Proceedings of the Second International Conference on Natural Language Processing and Artificial Intelligence for Cyber Security

acl:2026.nonliteral-1.8.abstract: Metonymy, often considered as a figurative trope, is a frequently occurring linguistic phenomenon in which an entity is replaced by a semantically related entity. Named entities are commonly used to refer to associated concepts. For instance, in the sentence India signed a treaty, the geographical name India stands metonymically for the government rather than the physical location. This study develops a hybrid architecture to classify literal and metonymic usages of named entities in Marathi language using small data. The approach integrates Pustejovsky’s Generative Lexicon framework with linguistic features, including part-of-speech tags, named entity labels, and lemmas. The model is evaluated on 890 sentences and achieved F1 scores of 66.98% and 71.97% for literal and metonymic instances, respectively. The study highlights the effectiveness of the features in capturing metonymic contexts, though precision remains a target for improvement. Ablation results confirm that the Formal and Constitutive Qualia roles are the most critical components for detecting metonymic shifts, while the Telic role introduces modest noise in the present corpus. This experiment shows the scope for developing hybrid models for learning non-literal language using small data, which could be beneficial for less-explored and low-resource languages.
acl:2026.nonliteral-1.8.journal_ref: Proceedings of Learning Non-Literal Expressions with Small Data @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.nonliteral-1.8.title: A Hybrid Architecture for Metonymy Detection in Marathi
acl:2026.nonliteral-1.8.venue: Proceedings of Learning Non-Literal Expressions with Small Data @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.nslp-1.15.abstract: Scientific Information Extraction (IE), which identifies entities and their relations from scientific texts, is essential for building Scientific Knowledge Graphs (SciKGs) that encode structured knowledge and enable applications such as semantic search, question answering, and literature reasoning. Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities in processing unstructured text, yet most advances focus on English, with limited exploration for less-resourced languages like Portuguese. The reliability of generative LLMs, including Portuguese-targeted models like the sovereign AMALIA, for structured extraction of scientific knowledge from literature text remains underexplored. We evaluate low- to mid-scale generative LLMs (8–12B parameters) on scientific Named Entity Recognition (NER) and Relation Extraction (RE), using a Portuguese-translated dataset of computer science article abstracts. Overall, our results show moderate performance and indicate that the adaptation strategy has a greater impact than model choice: prompting yields unstable performance and poor RE scores, while fine-tuning consistently improves both NER and RE and reduces cross-model variability. These findings suggest that, at this scale, prompting alone is insufficient for SciKG construction and underscore the need for supervised adaptation. We provide a detailed error analysis and outline directions for advancing Portuguese scientific IE.
acl:2026.nslp-1.15.journal_ref: Proceedings of Natural Scientific Language Processing (NSLP) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.nslp-1.15.title: Evaluating Generative Large Language Models for Portuguese Scientific Information Extraction
acl:2026.nslp-1.15.venue: Proceedings of Natural Scientific Language Processing (NSLP) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.osact-1.6.abstract: Image captioning plays a crucial role in numerous applications, including educational systems. However, ensuring caption quality remains a significant challenge, particularly for morphologically rich, low-resource languages such as Arabic. We investigate an evaluation of Arabic image captioning using state-of-the-art multimodal foundation models. We systematically assess the performance of leading models—Gemini, Gemma, LLaMA, and Fanar. Our evaluation framework employs a diverse set of metrics spanning rule-based, learnable, visually-grounded, and LLM-based approaches to capture semantic accuracy, linguistic fluency, and hallucination detection. Experiments are conducted on two benchmark datasets: Flickr8k-Arabic and JEEM. Our findings reveal significant performance variations across models and evaluation metrics, highlighting the need for Arabic-specific optimization in multimodal architectures.
acl:2026.osact-1.6.journal_ref: The 7th Workshop on Open-Source Arabic Corpora and Processing Tools (OSACT7) with 5 Shared Tasks
acl:2026.osact-1.6.title: How Foundation Models Behave for Arabic Image Captioning?
acl:2026.osact-1.6.venue: The 7th Workshop on Open-Source Arabic Corpora and Processing Tools (OSACT7) with 5 Shared Tasks

acl:2026.pressmint-1.8.abstract: Digitized literary corpora of the 19th century largely focus on standalone volumes, sidelining the broader and more diverse literary production of the period. Fiction published in less enduring formats – such as novellas and serialized pieces in newspapers – remains underexplored, particularly for low-resource languages like Danish, despite the growing availability of digitized newspaper archives. This paper addresses that gap by identifying and tagging fiction in Danish newspapers (1666–1850). We (1) present a manually annotated dataset of 1,831 articles with both binary (fiction/nonfiction) and fine-grained subcategories (travelogue, biography, essay), and (2) evaluate a document-embedding classifier that achieves an F1-score of up to 0.89 for the fiction/nonfiction distinction. Building on this pipeline, we further provide two resources for future research: (a) fiction probability scores for nearly five million newspaper articles (n=4,898,084), and (b) a small, cleaned, and curated subset of newspaper fiction (n=139), intended as a growing resource.
acl:2026.pressmint-1.8.journal_ref: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Creating Interoperable Corpora of Historical Newspapers
acl:2026.pressmint-1.8.title: A Growing Literature of the Public Sphere: Fiction in Danish Newspapers (1666–1850)
acl:2026.pressmint-1.8.venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop on Creating Interoperable Corpora of Historical Newspapers

acl:2026.rail-1.1.abstract: This paper presents a manually annotated morpho-syntactic corpus of Ògè, an under-resourced indigenous language spoken in Nigeria. The corpus consists of ten folk narratives (approximately 4,667 tokens) collected for the investigation of nominal structure. Annotation is expert-driven and includes token-level part-of-speech tagging together with a structured Determiner Phrase (DP) classification framework designed to capture language-specific nominal configurations. The scheme distinguishes between bare nouns and modified noun phrases, reflecting a central structural property of Ògè: noun forms remain morphologically stable across contexts, while modifiers exhibit formal and positional variation contributing to reference, specificity, and discourse prominence. The DP classification layer encodes both simple and complex nominal constructions, enabling systematic analysis of internal phrase structure. Designed as a reusable digital resource, the corpus supports morphosyntactic tagging, noun phrase boundary detection, and modeling of nominal structure in low-resource NLP settings. The annotated dataset will be made publicly available through the SADiLaR repository. This work demonstrates how descriptive linguistic analysis can inform annotation design and provides a replicable framework for developing structured resources for under-resourced African languages. Keywords: Ògè, low-resource NLP, annotated corpus, nominal structure, African languages
acl:2026.rail-1.1.journal_ref: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Sebuah frasa dalam teori sintaksis yang memiliki *determiner* sebagai kepala atau unsur penentunya.
Proses pelabelan setiap kata dalam teks dengan kelas kata yang sesuai seperti nomina atau verba.
Bentuk nomina yang muncul tanpa modifikasi atau penentu tambahan dalam konteks sintaksis lokal.

background.en: Many African indigenous languages remain severely under-resourced in terms of publicly available linguistic data and computational tools. Ògè, an indigenous Benue-Congo language spoken in Nigeria, exemplifies this gap as it lacks digitally accessible annotated resources, limiting both descriptive linguistic research and computational modeling.
background.id: Banyak bahasa adat di Afrika masih sangat kekurangan sumber daya berupa data linguistik dan alat komputasi yang tersedia untuk umum. Bahasa Ògè, sebuah bahasa adat dari rumpun Benue-Congo yang dituturkan di Nigeria, mencerminkan kesenjangan ini karena tidak memiliki sumber daya beranotasi yang dapat diakses secara digital, sehingga membatasi penelitian linguistik deskriptif dan pemodelan komputasi.

contributions.en: The paper contributes a manually annotated corpus of ten Ògè folk narratives comprising approximately 4,667 tokens. It introduces a structured Determiner Phrase classification framework designed to capture language-specific nominal configurations, explicitly distinguishing between bare nouns and modified noun phrases.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyumbangkan sebuah korpus beranotasi manual yang terdiri dari sepuluh narasi rakyat Ògè dengan sekitar 4.667 token. Makalah ini memperkenalkan kerangka klasifikasi *Determiner Phrase* terstruktur yang dirancang untuk menangkap konfigurasi nominal spesifik bahasa, serta secara eksplisit membedakan antara nomina telanjang dan frasa nomina termodifikasi.

future_work.en: Future work will extend the annotation framework to further texts within the broader archive of Ògè data and deposit the annotated corpus in the SADiLaR repository.
future_work.id: Penelitian mendatang akan memperluas kerangka anotasi ke teks-teks lain dalam arsip data Ògè yang lebih luas dan mendepositokan korpus beranotasi tersebut ke dalam repositori SADiLaR.

method.en: The corpus was annotated manually using an expert-driven approach informed by descriptive analysis of Ògè nominal structure. Each token received part-of-speech tagging, and a structured Determiner Phrase framework was applied to encode both simple and complex nominal constructions, distinguishing between bare nouns and various modifier combinations.
method.id: Korpus dianotasi secara manual menggunakan pendekatan berbasis pakar yang didasarkan pada analisis deskriptif struktur nominal Ògè. Setiap token diberi *part-of-speech tagging*, dan kerangka *Determiner Phrase* terstruktur diterapkan untuk mengodekan konstruksi nominal sederhana maupun kompleks, dengan membedakan nomina telanjang dan berbagai kombinasi modifikator.

related_work.en: Previous research emphasizes that annotation frameworks designed for high-resource languages often fail to capture the structural properties of under-resourced languages. While multilingual initiatives like Universal Dependencies provide cross-linguistic infrastructure, language-specific adaptation remains essential because available corpora for African indigenous languages lack fine-grained nominal distinctions.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya menekankan bahwa kerangka anotasi yang dirancang untuk bahasa *high-resource* sering kali gagal menangkap properti struktural bahasa dengan sumber daya terbatas. Meskipun inisiatif multilingual seperti Universal Dependencies menyediakan infrastruktur lintas bahasa, adaptasi khusus bahasa tetap esensial karena korpus yang tersedia untuk bahasa adat Afrika masih kurang memiliki pembedaan nominal yang mendalam.

results.en: Preliminary analysis of the annotated corpus shows that bare nouns frequently occur in discourse-given contexts, while modified DPs appear in environments requiring disambiguation or emphasis. The results demonstrate that Ògè nominal modification relies on compositional structure rather than morphological alternation.
results.id: Analisis awal terhadap korpus beranotasi menunjukkan bahwa nomina telanjang sering muncul dalam konteks yang sudah diketahui dalam wacana, sementara *Determiner Phrase* termodifikasi muncul di lingkungan yang membutuhkan disinflasi makna atau penekanan. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa modifikasi nominal Ògè bergantung pada struktur komposisional alih-alih perubahan morfologis.

tldr.en: This paper presents a manually annotated morpho-syntactic corpus of the Ògè language focusing on nominal structure. The resulting dataset provides a reusable resource for low-resource natural language processing and linguistic research.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan korpus morfo-sintaksis bahasa Ògè beranotasi manual dengan fokus pada struktur nominal. Kumpulan data tersebut menyediakan sumber daya yang dapat digunakan kembali untuk *natural language processing* *low-resource* dan penelitian linguistik.

acl:2026.rail-1.1.title: A Morpho-Syntactically Annotated Corpus of Ògè Folk Narratives with a Focus on Nominal Structure
acl:2026.rail-1.1.venue: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.rail-1.12.abstract: The development of Natural Language Processing (NLP) resources for African indigenous languages remains constrained by limited data availability, fragmented expertise, and a lack of sustainable, locally grounded infrastructures for enabling language research. While much existing work focuses on producing discrete resources such as corpora or lexicons, less attention has been paid to the social, institutional, and methodological conditions that enable such resources to be created, maintained, and sustained. This paper presents the Hundzula Retreat for NLP and Linguistics as a retreat-based resource infrastructure model that addresses these constraints. We conceptualise Hundzula not as a once-off event, but as a structured, upstream research infrastructure that facilitates human capacity development, interdisciplinary collaboration between linguistics and NLP, ethical data practices, and the early-stage incubation of language resources for African indigenous languages. Drawing on evidence from multiple iterations of the retreat, we describe the design principles, workflows, and governance mechanisms that support resource development, including training pipelines, human-in-the-loop methodologies, and collaborative project formation. Rather than focusing on already formalised outputs, the paper foregrounds the infrastructural conditions that make such outputs possible within under-resourced contexts. In doing so, the paper shifts attention from outputs to the enabling ecosystems required for their production. We argue that retreat-based infrastructures constitute an essential but under-recognised category of language resources and demonstrate how the Hundzula model can be adapted and replicated in other low-resourced language contexts. The paper contributes a transferable framework for sustainable NLP resource development grounded in African linguistic realities.
acl:2026.rail-1.12.journal_ref: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa kekurangan data, alat komputasi, dan sumber daya digital yang memadai untuk pengembangan *natural language processing*.
Metodologi yang melibatkan intervensi dan keahlian manusia secara aktif dalam proses pelatihan atau pengembangan *model* dan data.
Kumpulan teks atau data ujaran dalam jumlah besar yang disusun secara sistematis untuk analisis linguistik dan pelatihan *model bahasa*.
Kumpulan kosakata atau daftar kata beserta informasi leksikalnya yang digunakan dalam suatu bahasa.
Proses penyesuaian lanjutan pada *model* pralatih menggunakan data spesifik domain agar kinerjanya meningkat pada tugas tertentu.
Teknik memperbesar ukuran dan keragaman *dataset* pelatihan secara buatan untuk meningkatkan ketahanan *model*.
Sistem percakapan otomatis berbasis komputer yang dirancang untuk berinteraksi dengan pengguna menggunakan bahasa alami.
Standar atau kumpulan *dataset* baku yang digunakan untuk mengevaluasi dan membandingkan kinerja berbagai *model* secara objektif.

background.en: The development of natural language processing resources for African indigenous languages is severely constrained by limited data availability, fragmented expertise, and a lack of sustainable, locally grounded infrastructures. Existing efforts often focus on producing discrete artifacts like corpora or lexicons in isolation, while neglecting the social, institutional, and methodological conditions necessary to create and sustain them. Consequently, African languages face persistent skills gaps, weak interdisciplinary collaboration between linguistics and computer science, and insufficient attention to ethical and contextual considerations in data creation.
background.id: Pengembangan sumber daya *natural language processing* untuk bahasa-bahasa pribumi Afrika sangat terkendala oleh ketersediaan data yang terbatas, keahlian yang terfragmentasi, dan kurangnya infrastruktur yang berkelanjutan serta berakar secara lokal. Upaya yang ada sering kali berfokus pada produksi artefak diskrit seperti korpus atau leksikon secara terisolasi, sementara mengabaikan kondisi sosial, institusional, dan metodologis yang diperlukan untuk menciptakan dan mempertahankannya. Akibatnya, bahasa-bahasa Afrika menghadapi kesenjangan keterampilan yang persisten, kolaborasi interdisipliner yang lemah antara linguistik dan ilmu komputer, serta perhatian yang tidak memadai terhadap pertimbangan etis dan kontekstual dalam pembuatan data.

contributions.en: This paper introduces the Hundzula Retreat as an infrastructural resource model that addresses core constraints in African natural language processing by shifting attention from finished outputs to enabling ecosystems. Its main contributions include documenting the retreat as an institutional framework, proposing a transferable five-layer model encompassing human capacity, collaborative networks, resource pipelines, governance and ethics, and sustainability, and providing a foundational framework for sustainable NLP resource development grounded in linguistic realities.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan Hundzula Retreat sebagai model sumber daya infrastruktur yang mengatasi kendala inti dalam *natural language processing* Afrika dengan mengalihkan perhatian dari keluaran akhir ke ekosistem pendukung. Kontribusi utamanya meliputi pendokumentasian *retreat* sebagai kerangka kerja institusional, pengajuan model lima lapisan yang dapat ditransfer yang mencakup kapasitas manusia, jaringan kolaboratif, *resource pipeline*, tata kelola dan etika, serta keberlanjutan, dan penyediaan kerangka kerja dasar untuk pengembangan sumber daya *NLP* yang berkelanjutan yang berakar pada realitas linguistik.

future_work.en: The authors note that the study does not offer a formal longitudinal comparison across all editions, treat the fifth iteration as a mature instance without implementing fully formalised design-science methodology, and argue for model transferability conceptually rather than empirically. Future work could extend this research by evaluating the model across different settings, conducting systematic evaluations of downstream outputs, and tracing the progression of retreat-incubated projects into formalised NLP resources.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa penelitian ini tidak menawarkan perbandingan longitudinal formal di semua edisi, memperlakukan iterasi kelima sebagai instansi matang tanpa mengimplementasikan metodologi *design-science* yang sepenuhnya diformalisasi, dan berargumen untuk transferabilitas model secara konseptual alih-alih empiris. Pekerjaan di masa mendatang dapat memperluas penelitian ini dengan mengevaluasi model di berbagai pengaturan, melakukan evaluasi sistematis terhadap keluaran hilir, dan melacak perkembangan proyek inkubasi *retreat* menjadi sumber daya *NLP* yang diformalisasi.

method.en: The authors adopt a design-science case study approach focusing on the fifth edition of the Hundzula Retreat, a four-day intensive programme integrating linguistic complexity, corpus building, ethical data practices, and applied NLP techniques. The initiative operationalizes a human-in-the-loop methodology through formal training sessions, collaborative project incubation, and mentored research activities. The conceptualized model is structured across five interacting layers: the Human Capacity Layer, the Collaborative Network Layer, the Resource Pipeline Layer, the Governance and Ethical Layer, and the Sustainability Layer.
method.id: Para penulis mengadopsi pendekatan studi kasus *design-science* yang berfokus pada edisi kelima Hundzula Retreat, sebuah program intensif empat hari yang mengintegrasikan kompleksitas linguistik, pembangunan korpus, praktik data etis, dan teknik *NLP* terapan. Inisiatif ini mengoperasionalkan metodologi *human-in-the-loop* melalui sesi pelatihan formal, inkubasi proyek kolaboratif, dan kegiatan penelitian dengan mentor. Model yang dikonseptualisasikan disusun dalam lima lapisan yang berinteraksi: *Human Capacity Layer*, *Collaborative Network Layer*, *Resource Pipeline Layer*, *Governance and Ethical Layer*, dan *Sustainability Layer*.

related_work.en: Prior research highlights that existing language resources are frequently developed through different institutions and in isolation, leading to duplication of effort and limited sustainability. Studies such as those by Siminyu et al., Nahar et al., and various initiative reports emphasize the fragmentation inherent in African NLP research. Additionally, prior literature notes that ethical and cultural considerations specific to African contexts are often treated as secondary concerns, and that infrastructural outcomes must be assessed beyond mere dataset size or model performance.
related_work.id: Penelitian terdahulu menyoroti bahwa sumber daya bahasa yang ada sering kali dikembangkan melalui institusi yang berbeda dan secara terisolasi, yang mengarah pada duplikasi upaya dan keberlanjutan yang terbatas. Studi seperti yang dilakukan oleh Siminyu et al., Nahar et al., dan berbagai laporan inisiatif menekankan fragmentasi yang melekat dalam penelitian *NLP* Afrika. Selain itu, literatur sebelumnya mencatat bahwa pertimbangan etis dan kontekstual yang khusus untuk konteks Afrika sering kali diperlakukan sebagai kekhawatiran sekunder, dan bahwa hasil infrastruktur harus dinilai melampaui ukuran *dataset* atau performa *model* semata.

results.en: The paper does not provide quantitative benchmark evaluations or performance metrics, as the Hundzula Retreat prioritizes upstream capacity building, collaboration, and project incubation over the immediate production of finished datasets. Instead, qualitative results demonstrate that the retreat successfully fosters interdisciplinary engagement between linguists and computer scientists, facilitates the initiation of resource pipelines for under-documented varieties such as Sepitori and Khelobedu, and establishes enduring research networks that reduce fragmentation across institutions.
results.id: Makalah ini tidak memberikan evaluasi *benchmark* kuantitatif atau metrik performa, karena Hundzula Retreat memprioritaskan pembangunan kapasitas hulu, kolaborasi, dan inkubasi proyek daripada produksi langsung *dataset* jadi. Sebagai gantinya, hasil kualitatif menunjukkan bahwa *retreat* tersebut berhasil menumbuhkan keterlibatan interdisipliner antara ahli linguistik dan ilmuwan komputer, memfasilitasi inisiasi *resource pipeline* untuk varietas yang kurang didokumentasikan seperti Sepitori dan Khelobedu, serta membentuk jaringan penelitian abadi yang mengurangi fragmentasi antar institusi.

tldr.en: This paper presents the Hundzula Retreat as a structured infrastructure model for African natural language processing. The work demonstrates that retreat-based frameworks effectively support human capacity building, interdisciplinary collaboration, and sustainable resource development in low-resource settings.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mempresentasikan Hundzula Retreat sebagai model infrastruktur terstruktur untuk *natural language processing* bahasa-bahasa Afrika. Penelitian ini mendemonstrasikan bahwa kerangka kerja berbasis *retreat* secara efektif mendukung pengembangan kapasitas manusia, kolaborasi interdisipliner, dan pengembangan sumber daya yang berkelanjutan pada pengaturan *low-resource*.

acl:2026.rail-1.12.title: The Hundzula Retreat-Based Infrastructure Model for African Natural Language Processing
acl:2026.rail-1.12.venue: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.rail-1.3.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are trained on data contributed by low-resource language communities, including curated datasets such as MasakhaNER and MAFAND-MT, yet the linguistic knowledge encoded in these models remains accessible only through commercial APIs. This paper investigates whether strategic prompting can extract usable text data from LLMs for two West African languages: Hausa (Afroasiatic, approximately 80 million speakers) and Fongbe (Niger-Congo, approximately 2 million speakers). We systematically compare six elicitation task types: creative writing, functional text, structured knowledge, dialogue, topic-switching probes, and constrained generation across two commercial LLMs (GPT-4o Mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash). Generated outputs are evaluated on linguistic accuracy, lexical diversity, domain coverage, and code-switching rates through automatic metrics assessment. Our findings reveal that elicitation strategy significantly affects output quality and that optimal strategies differ by language: Hausa benefits from volume-maximizing tasks such as functional text and dialogue, while Fongbe requires constraint-heavy prompts that enforce monolingual output. GPT-4o Mini extracts 6–41x more usable target-language words per API call than Gemini, though Gemini achieves higher language purity for Fongbe on constrained tasks. We provide a practical framework for low-resource language communities to maximize usable data extraction from LLMs and release all generated corpora and code.
acl:2026.rail-1.3.journal_ref: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Proses memanggil atau mengeluarkan respons atau data tertentu dari *large language model* menggunakan *prompt* yang dirancang secara khusus.
Tanda grafis yang ditambahkan pada huruf untuk menunjukkan pengucapan atau nada tertentu, yang sangat penting dalam bahasa seperti Fongbe.
Fenomena beralih di antara dua atau lebih bahasa atau dialek dalam satu percakapan atau teks yang sama.
Unit teks terkecil yang diproses oleh *tokenizer* dalam model bahasa, yang bisa berupa kata utuh atau bagian dari kata.
Tugas atau aplikasi hilir yang menggunakan model atau representasi data yang telah dilatih sebelumnya untuk menyelesaikan masalah spesifik.
Kondisi di mana *large language model* menghasilkan ulang teks pelatihan secara persis alih-alih menghasilkan teks baru.
Kumpulan teks terstruktur dalam jumlah besar yang biasanya digunakan untuk penelitian linguistik atau pelatihan *machine learning*.
Model atau metode standar yang digunakan sebagai titik perbandingan untuk mengukur performa metode baru yang diusulkan.

background.en: Natural language processing technologies remain largely inaccessible to speakers of most African languages due to severe data scarcity, despite large language models being trained on web-scale data contributed by these communities. While these commercial models absorb valuable linguistic knowledge, it flows back to the communities only through paid application programming interfaces. This creates a critical bootstrapping problem where low-resource language communities struggle to collect expensive and slow text data for building NLP systems.
background.id: Teknologi *natural language processing* sebagian besar tetap tidak dapat diakses oleh penutur sebagian besar bahasa Afrika karena kelangkaan data yang parah, meskipun *large language model* dilatih pada data berskala web yang disumbangkan oleh komunitas-komunitas ini. Meskipun model komersial ini menyerap pengetahuan linguistik yang berharga, pengetahuan tersebut hanya mengalir kembali ke komunitas melalui *application programming interface* berbayar. Hal ini menciptakan masalah *bootstrapping* yang krusial di mana komunitas bahasa *low-resource* kesulitan mengumpulkan data teks yang mahal dan lambat untuk membangun sistem NLP.

contributions.en: This work introduces a systematic taxonomy of large language model elicitation strategies evaluated across six task types for two typologically distinct West African languages, Hausa and Fongbe. It provides an empirical comparison of two commercial models showing significant efficiency differences and language-specific optimal strategies. Additionally, the authors deliver a practical framework and publicly release all generated corpora and code to enable replication.
contributions.id: Karya ini memperkenalkan taksonomi sistematis dari strategi *elicitation* *large language model* yang dievaluasi di enam jenis tugas untuk dua bahasa Afrika Barat yang secara tipologi berbeda, yaitu Hausa dan Fongbe. Penelitian ini menyediakan perbandingan empiris dari dua model komersial yang menunjukkan perbedaan efisiensi yang signifikan serta strategi optimal khusus bahasa. Selain itu, para penulis menghadirkan kerangka kerja praktis dan merilis semua korpus serta kode yang dihasilkan untuk publik guna memungkinkan replikasi.

future_work.en: The authors acknowledge limitations including evaluation restricted to two commercial models, reliance entirely on automatic metrics without human evaluation, modest sample sizes, and the use of English-only prompts. Future work will include additional models such as Claude Sonnet and open-weight variants, human evaluation with native speakers, downstream utility testing on benchmarks like MasakhaNER 2.0 and MasakhaPOS, target-language prompting experiments, and extension to further African languages.
future_work.id: Para penulis mengakui keterbatasan termasuk evaluasi yang terbatas pada dua model komersial, ketergantungan sepenuhnya pada metrik otomatis tanpa evaluasi manusia, ukuran sampel yang sederhana, dan penggunaan *prompt* khusus bahasa Inggris. Pekerjaan masa depan akan mencakup model tambahan seperti Claude Sonnet dan varian *open-weight*, evaluasi manusia dengan penutur asli, pengujian utilitas *downstream* pada *benchmark* seperti MasakhaNER 2.0 dan MasakhaPOS, eksperimen *prompting* dalam bahasa target, dan perluasan ke bahasa Afrika lainnya.

method.en: The study designs a controlled experiment sending six task types consisting of creative writing, functional text, structured knowledge, dialogue, topic-switching probes, and constrained generation to GPT-4o Mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash. All prompts are written in English with placeholders for language and cultural context, totaling 600 API calls across both models and languages. Outputs are evaluated using automatic assessment metrics for output validity, lexical diversity, language fidelity via GlotLID, diacritic analysis, repetition detection, and reference overlap.
method.id: Studi ini merancang eksperimen terkontrol dengan mengirimkan enam jenis tugas yang terdiri dari *creative writing*, *functional text*, *structured knowledge*, *dialogue*, *topic-switching probes*, dan *constrained generation* ke GPT-4o Mini dan Gemini 2.5 Flash. Semua *prompt* ditulis dalam bahasa Inggris dengan *placeholder* untuk bahasa dan konteks budaya, dengan total 600 panggilan API di kedua model dan bahasa. Keluaran dievaluasi menggunakan metrik penilaian otomatis untuk validitas keluaran, keragaman leksikal, fidelitas bahasa melalui GlotLID, analisis diakritik, deteksi pengulangan, dan *reference overlap*.

related_work.en: Previous research has examined large language models for low-resource languages primarily through machine translation or data augmentation for specific downstream tasks, such as the Fikira dataset which generated reasoning data without comparing task types. Studies like those by Robinson and Hendy showed that standard models degrade significantly for underrepresented languages lacking web presence. However, a critical gap persists because prior work investigates model performance on translation rather than identifying which prompting strategies maximize the extraction of usable language data.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya telah mengkaji *large language model* untuk bahasa *low-resource* terutama melalui *machine translation* atau *data augmentation* untuk tugas *downstream* tertentu, seperti dataset Fikira yang menghasilkan data penalaran tanpa membandingkan jenis tugas. Studi seperti yang dilakukan oleh Robinson dan Hendy menunjukkan bahwa model standar menurun secara signifikan untuk bahasa kurang terwakili yang minim kehadiran web. Namun, celah kritis tetap ada karena pekerjaan sebelumnya menyelidiki kinerja model pada terjemahan daripada mengidentifikasi strategi *prompting* mana yang memaksimalkan ekstraksi data bahasa yang dapat digunakan.

results.en: GPT-4o Mini achieves 100 percent validity across all conditions and is significantly more efficient, extracting 6 times more usable Hausa words and 41 times more Fongbe words per API call than Gemini. Optimal strategies differ by language, where Hausa benefits from volume-maximizing tasks like functional text and dialogue, while Fongbe requires constraint-heavy prompts to enforce monolingual output and diacritic accuracy. Furthermore, all models exhibit low reference overlap and repetition rates, indicating novel text generation rather than mere memorization.
results.id: GPT-4o Mini mencapai validitas 100 persen di semua kondisi dan jauh lebih efisien, mengekstrak kata Hausa 6 kali lebih banyak dan kata Fongbe 41 kali lebih banyak per panggilan API dibandingkan Gemini. Strategi optimal berbeda menurut bahasa, di mana Hausa diuntungkan oleh tugas yang memaksimalkan volume seperti teks fungsional dan dialog, sementara Fongbe membutuhkan *prompt* dengan kendala berat untuk menegakkan keluaran monolingual dan keakuratan diakritik. Lebih lanjut, semua model menunjukkan tingkat *reference overlap* dan pengulangan yang rendah, yang mengindikasikan pembuatan teks baru alih-alih sekadar memorisasi.

tldr.en: This paper investigates how strategic prompting can extract usable text data from large language models for two West African languages. The findings reveal that optimal elicitation strategies depend heavily on the language and model chosen.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyelidiki bagaimana *prompting* strategis dapat mengekstrak data teks yang dapat digunakan dari *large language model* untuk dua bahasa Afrika Barat. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa strategi *elicitation* yang optimal sangat bergantung pada bahasa dan model yang dipilih.

acl:2026.rail-1.3.title: Mining Large Language Models for Low-Resource Language Data: Comparing Elicitation Strategies for Hausa and Fongbe
acl:2026.rail-1.3.venue: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.rail-1.4.abstract: Cross-lingual transfer learning enables building NLP systems for low-resource languages by leveraging data from higher-resource languages. A critical but understudied question for African languages is: which source languages should be selected for multi-source transfer? We present a systematic comparison of four source language selection strategies: random selection (baseline), genetic distance based on language family trees, geographic distance based on speaker locations, and embedding similarity from multilingual models. We evaluate these strategies on Named Entity Recognition, Part-of-Speech tagging, and sentiment analysis across five typologically diverse African target languages (Hausa, Yoruba, Swahili, Igbo, Kinyarwanda) using three multilingual models. We further investigate how the number of source languages affects transfer performance. Our experiments reveal that no single strategy dominates across tasks: geographic distance leads on sequence labeling tasks while embedding similarity is most effective for sentiment analysis, and all informed strategies consistently outperform random selection.
acl:2026.rail-1.4.journal_ref: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Tugas pemrosesan bahasa alami untuk mengidentifikasi dan mengklasifikasikan entitas bernama seperti nama orang, lokasi, atau organisasi di dalam *korpus* teks.
Proses pemberian label kategori gramatikal atau kelas kata kepada setiap token dalam sebuah kalimat.
Pengaturan evaluasi di mana model diuji pada suatu tugas atau bahasa tanpa pelatihan atau *fine-tuning* sebelumnya pada data target tersebut.
Model bahasa yang telah dilatih pada data dari berbagai bahasa untuk memungkinkan transfer pengetahuan lintas bahasa.
Proses penyesuaian bobot pada *large language model* yang sudah dilatih sebelumnya menggunakan data spesifik untuk suatu tugas.

background.en: Building natural language processing systems for low-resource languages remains challenging, particularly for over 2,000 languages spoken across Africa that exhibit high typological diversity. Cross-lingual transfer learning offers a promising solution by leveraging labeled data from higher-resource languages, but a critical and understudied question remains: which source languages should practitioners select for multi-source transfer?
background.id: Pembangunan sistem pemrosesan bahasa alami untuk bahasa-bahasa *low-resource* tetap menjadi tantangan, terutama bagi lebih dari 2.000 bahasa yang dituturkan di seluruh Afrika yang menunjukkan keragaman tipologis tinggi. *Cross-lingual transfer learning* menawarkan solusi menjanjikan dengan memanfaatkan data beranotasi dari bahasa dengan sumber daya lebih tinggi, namun pertanyaan krusial yang belum banyak diteliti tetap ada: bahasa sumber mana yang harus dipilih praktisi untuk *transfer* multisumber?

contributions.en: The paper makes three main contributions: it provides the first systematic comparison of genetic, geographic, and embedding-based source selection strategies specifically for African languages; it investigates the effect of the number of source languages in zero-shot settings; and it analyzes strategy effectiveness across different tasks and model architectures to offer actionable guidance for practitioners.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memberikan tiga kontribusi utama: menyajikan perbandingan sistematis pertama dari strategi pemilihan sumber genetik, geografis, dan berbasis *embedding* secara khusus untuk bahasa Afrika; menyelidiki pengaruh jumlah bahasa sumber dalam pengaturan *zero-shot*; serta menganalisis efektivitas strategi di berbagai tugas dan arsitektur model untuk menawarkan panduan praktis bagi para praktisi.

future_work.en: The authors note several limitations, including not controlling for total training data quantity in the primary strategy comparison, relying on a single random seed for genetic and geographic comparisons due to GPU constraints, evaluating only three models, and using FLORES-200 parallel sentences which may not capture domain-specific similarity for tasks like sentiment analysis.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat beberapa keterbatasan, termasuk tidak mengontrol total kuantitas data latih dalam perbandingan strategi utama, mengandalkan satu *random seed* tunggal untuk perbandingan genetik dan geografis karena keterbatasan GPU, hanya mengevaluasi tiga model, dan menggunakan kalimat paralel FLORES-200 yang mungkin tidak menangkap kemiripan spesifik domain untuk tugas seperti analisis sentimen.

method.en: The study evaluates four selection strategies—random baseline, genetic distance, geographic distance, and embedding similarity using cosine gap on FLORES-200 sentences—across three tasks: Named Entity Recognition using MasakhaNER 2.0, Part-of-Speech tagging using MasakhaPOS, and sentiment analysis using AfriSenti. Evaluations are performed on five African target languages using three multilingual models, namely AfroXLMR, AfriBERTa, and Serengeti, while also varying the number of source languages from one to five.
method.id: Studi ini mengevaluasi empat strategi pemilihan—dasar acak, jarak genetik, jarak geografis, dan kemiripan *embedding* menggunakan *cosine gap* pada kalimat FLORES-200—di tiga tugas: *Named Entity Recognition* menggunakan MasakhaNER 2.0, *Part-of-Speech tagging* menggunakan MasakhaPOS, and analisis sentimen menggunakan AfriSenti. Evaluasi dilakukan pada lima bahasa target Afrika menggunakan tiga *multilingual model*, yaitu AfroXLMR, AfriBERTa, dan Serengeti, serta memvariasikan jumlah bahasa sumber dari satu hingga lima.

related_work.en: Prior work on source language selection has explored typological approaches using genetic distance and linguistic databases like URIEL, geographic distance reflecting speaker proximity and language contact, and embedding similarity computed directly from multilingual model representations. However, most research has focused on European and Asian languages, leaving systematic comparisons for African languages and the evaluation of optimal source counts largely unaddressed.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya mengenai pemilihan bahasa sumber telah mengeksplorasi pendekatan tipologis menggunakan jarak genetik dan basis data linguistik seperti URIEL, jarak geografis yang mencerminkan kedekatan penutur dan kontak bahasa, serta kemiripan *embedding* yang dihitung langsung dari representasi *multilingual model*. Namun, sebagian besar penelitian berfokus pada bahasa Eropa dan Asia, sehingga perbandingan sistematis untuk bahasa Afrika dan evaluasi jumlah sumber optimal sebagian besar belum terselesaikan.

results.en: The results demonstrate that no single strategy dominates across all tasks: geographic distance achieves the best performance on sequence labeling tasks like Named Entity Recognition and Part-of-Speech tagging, whereas embedding similarity leads on sentiment analysis. All informed strategies consistently outperform random selection, and increasing the number of source languages up to K equals 5 generally improves transfer performance.
results.id: Hasil menunjukkan bahwa tidak ada satu strategi tunggal yang mendominasi di semua tugas: jarak geografis mencapai performa terbaik pada tugas pelabelan urutan seperti *Named Entity Recognition* dan *Part-of-Speech tagging*, sedangkan kemiripan *embedding* unggul pada analisis sentimen. Semua strategi berinformasi secara konsisten mengungguli pemilihan acak, dan meningkatkan jumlah bahasa sumber hingga K sama dengan 5 secara umum meningkatkan performa *transfer*.

tldr.en: This paper presents a systematic comparison of four source language selection strategies for multi-source cross-lingual transfer to African languages. The experiments reveal that geographic distance is most effective for sequence labeling tasks, whereas embedding similarity leads on sentiment analysis.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan perbandingan sistematis dari empat strategi pemilihan bahasa sumber untuk *transfer* lintas bahasa multisumber ke bahasa-bahasa di Afrika. Eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa jarak geografis paling efektif untuk tugas pelabelan urutan, sedangkan kemiripan *embedding* unggul pada analisis sentimen.

acl:2026.rail-1.4.title: Comparing Source Language Selection Strategies for Multi-Source Cross-Lingual Transfer to African Languages
acl:2026.rail-1.4.venue: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.rail-1.5.abstract: In this work we introduce a collection of monolingual embedding models for ten South African languages in four different architectures. To determine the quality of the embedding models we evaluate the embeddings on two sequence-labelling tasks, namely Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging and Named Entity Recognition (NER). Languages are grouped into conjunctive (isiNdebele, isiXhosa, isiZulu, and Siswati), disjunctive (Sepedi, Sesotho, Setswana, Tshivenḓa, and Xitsonga), and Afrikaans to establish the influence of training data set size and typology on the quality of the different embeddings. To isolate representation effects we train BiLSTM-CRF taggers, while keeping the architecture, data splits, and training budget fixed, varying only the input imbedding representations, namely GloVe, fastText, Flair, and RoBERTa. In our experiments, GloVe lags behind fastText, Flair, and the transformer-based models, confirming that static word-level vectors are less suited to morphologically complex, low-resource languages. Subword-aware embeddings such as fastText remain a reliable and computationally efficient baseline, while Flair is the most competitive overall across both POS tagging and NER tasks.
acl:2026.rail-1.5.journal_ref: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.rail-1.5.title: Benchmarking Text Embedding Models for South African Languages
acl:2026.rail-1.5.venue: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.rail-1.6.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has been used to improve the accuracy and transparency of outputs produced by large language models (LLMs) by integrating external knowledge; however, applying RAG to low-resource languages presents unique challenges, including poor embedding representations, low retrieval quality, and semantic gaps caused by the scarcity of digital documents. In this research, we address these challenges for a selected low-resource language, Amharic, by using translative and debate-based RAG techniques to improve retrieval and reasoning. This paper outlines the key problems and research gaps in applying RAG to low-resource languages and introduces a method to enhance RAG performance for Amharic. Additionally, we introduce the first comprehensive Amharic Retrieval-Augmented Generation Benchmark (ARGB), designed to capture grammatical, cultural, and writing-system-specific constraints of the Amharic language. ARGB evaluates not only retrieval and generation quality, but also noise robustness, counterfactual robustness, negative rejection, and multi-source information integration, providing a holistic assessment of RAG capabilities. The dataset, which spans a wide range of categories, is evaluated using multiple evaluation metrics. Furthermore, we demonstrate that, using our dataset, translation-based and debate-based methods substantially improve various aspects of RAG pipeline assessment in the Amharic language. This work aims to improve the reliability, accessibility, and inclusiveness of AI systems for Amharic speakers while providing a scalable framework for other low-resource languages. Current progress on the code and benchmark can be found on this GitHub link: link.
acl:2026.rail-1.6.journal_ref: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.rail-1.6.title: Improving Amharic Information Retrieval with Translative and Multi-Agent Debate Retrieval Augmented Generation
acl:2026.rail-1.6.venue: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.rail-1.7.abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) for low-resource languages remains challenging due to limited annotated data and high linguistic variability. In this work, we investigate parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies for Cape Verdean Creole ASR using the Wav2Vec 2.0 XLSR model. We evaluate the impact of structured layer freezing on model performance, training stability, and computational efficiency. Experiments conducted on a newly curated Santiago-dialect dataset show that full fine-tuning achieves the best absolute performance (WER 0.212, CER 0.120). However, several freezing configurations achieve comparable recognition performance while substantially reducing the number of trainable parameters and exhibiting more stable convergence. These results highlight a trade-off between adaptability and efficiency, showing that selective freezing can serve as an effective regularization strategy in low-resource settings. This work provides practical insights into parameter-efficient adaptation for under-resourced Creole languages.
acl:2026.rail-1.7.journal_ref: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Wav2Vec 2.0 adalah model *self-supervised learning* terkemuka yang dikembangkan oleh Facebook AI Research untuk memproses *waveform* audio mentah menjadi representasi akustik.
XLSR adalah ekstensi multibahasa dari *Wav2Vec 2.0* yang dirancang untuk mempelajari representasi akustik lintas bahasa pada berbagai *low-resource* *language*.
Word Error Rate adalah metrik evaluasi utama dalam *ASR* yang mengukur jumlah kesalahan tingkat kata berupa substitusi, penghapusan, dan penyisipan.
Character Error Rate adalah metrik evaluasi yang menghitung kesalahan pada tingkat karakter untuk memberikan analisis yang lebih rinci mengenai akurasi subkata.

Connectionist Temporal Classification adalah fungsi kerugian dan lapisan decoding yang memungkinkan jaringan saraf melatih tugas pengurutan tanpa memerlukan penyejajaran manual antara label dan input audio.
Layer freezing adalah teknik menjaga bobot pada *layer* model tertentu agar tetap konstan dan tidak diperbarui selama proses *fine-tuning*.
Fine-tuning adalah proses melatih ulang model praterlatih pada *dataset* hilir tertentu untuk menyesuaikannya dengan tugas target.
Data augmentation adalah teknik buatan untuk memperbesar ukuran dan keragaman *dataset* pelatihan dengan memodifikasi sampel yang ada.

background.en: Automatic speech recognition for low-resource languages remains challenging due to limited annotated data and high linguistic variability, a disparity particularly pronounced for Creole languages that lack standardized orthography. Cape Verdean Creole exemplifies these challenges with substantial phonetic, lexical, and orthographic variation across dialects. This work addresses the research gap in adapting large pre-trained multilingual speech models to such under-resourced languages while balancing performance, computational efficiency, and training stability.
background.id: *Automatic speech recognition* untuk bahasa *low-resource* masih menjadi tantangan akibat keterbatasan data beranotasi dan variabilitas linguistik yang tinggi, sebuah kesenjangan yang sangat terlihat pada bahasa-bahasa Kreol yang tidak memiliki ortografi baku. Kreol Tanjung Verde merepresentasikan tantangan-tantangan ini dengan variasi fonetik, leksikal, dan ortografis yang besar antar dialek. Karya ini mengatasi celah penelitian dalam mengadaptasi *large-scale* *model bahasa* multibahasa praterlatih ke bahasa-bahasa dengan sumber daya terbatas tersebut sekaligus menjaga keseimbangan antara performa, efisiensi komputasi, and stabilitas pelatihan.

contributions.en: This paper makes two primary contributions to the field. First, it introduces a new, curated speech dataset of 1,787 recordings comprising approximately 2 hours of audio for the Santiago dialect of Cape Verdean Creole, adding to the growing body of resources for African-influenced languages. Second, it provides an empirically validated, parameter-efficient adaptation strategy through structured layer freezing for large self-supervised speech models in a low-resource context, demonstrating how selective freezing acts as an effective regularization mechanism.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memberikan dua kontribusi utama pada bidang ini. Pertama, makalah ini memperkenalkan *dataset* ucapan baru yang dikurasi sebanyak 1.787 rekaman dengan durasi sekitar 2 jam untuk dialek Santiago dari Kreol Tanjung Verde, menambah sumber daya yang terus berkembang untuk bahasa-bahasa berakar Afrika. Kedua, makalah ini menyediakan strategi adaptasi yang tervalidasi secara empiris dan efisien parameter melalui *layer freezing* terstruktur untuk *model bahasa* ucapan *self-supervised* berskala besar dalam konteks *low-resource*, yang menunjukkan bagaimana *selective freezing* bertindak sebagai mekanisme *regularization* yang efektif.

future_work.en: The authors state that their conclusions are limited by the size and scope of the dataset, noting that future work should explore larger and more diverse corpora representing other dialects and domains, as well as investigate alternative parameter-efficient approaches such as adapters and LoRA.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyatakan bahwa kesimpulan mereka dibatasi oleh ukuran dan cakupan *dataset*, serta mencatat bahwa pekerjaan di masa depan harus mengeksplorasi korpus yang lebih besar dan lebih beragam yang merepresentasikan dialek dan domain lain, serta menyelidiki pendekatan alternatif yang efisien parameter seperti *adapters* dan *LoRA*.

method.en: The study utilizes a newly curated corpus of 1,787 speech recordings from the Santiago dialect of Cape Verdean Creole, accompanied by a custom phonetic normalization dictionary to map spelling variations and online data augmentation. The baseline ASR system is built upon the Wav2Vec 2.0 large-XLSR architecture initialized from the XLSR-CORAA checkpoint, featuring a 24-layer Transformer encoder and a Connectionist Temporal Classification head. The adaptation methodology systematically varies the depth of structured layer freezing, evaluating configurations from full fine-tuning to freezing various subsets of upper Transformer layers.
method.id: Studi ini menggunakan korpus ucapan yang baru dikurasi sebanyak 1.787 rekaman dari dialek Santiago bahasa Kreol Tanjung Verde, disertai dengan kamus *phonetic normalization* khusus untuk memetakan variasi ejaan serta *data augmentation* daring. Sistem *ASR* dasar dibangun di atas arsitektur *Wav2Vec 2.0 large-XLSR* yang diinisialisasi dari *checkpoint* *XLSR-CORAA*, yang menampilkan *encoder* *Transformer* 24 *layer* dan sebuah kepala *Connectionist Temporal Classification*. Metodologi adaptasi secara sistematis memvariasikan kedalaman *layer freezing* terstruktur, mengevaluasi konfigurasi mulai dari *fine-tuning* penuh hingga pembekuan berbagai subset *layer* *Transformer* atas.

related_work.en: Recent advances in self-supervised learning, particularly Wav2Vec 2.0 and its cross-lingual extensions like XLSR, have improved ASR performance in resource-constrained scenarios by learning universal acoustic representations. However, excessive fine-tuning on limited datasets often leads to overfitting, unstable convergence, and catastrophic forgetting. Previous studies suggest that selective layer freezing can help preserve universal acoustic-phonetic representations in lower Transformer layers while adapting higher layers, though its application to Creole languages remains underexplored.
related_work.id: Kemajuan terkini dalam *self-supervised learning*, khususnya *Wav2Vec 2.0* dan ekstensi lintas bahasanya seperti *XLSR*, telah meningkatkan performa *ASR* pada skenario keterbatasan sumber daya dengan mempelajari representasi akustik universal. Namun, *fine-tuning* berlebihan pada dataset terbatas sering kali menyebabkan *overfitting*, konvergensi yang tidak stabil, dan *catastrophic forgetting*. Studi-studi sebelumnya menunjukkan bahwa *selective layer freezing* dapat membantu mempertahankan representasi akustik-fonetik universal pada *layer* *Transformer* bawah sembari mengadaptasi *layer* atas, meskipun penerapannya pada bahasa Kreol masih belum banyak dieksplorasi.

results.en: Experiments show that while full fine-tuning achieves the best absolute performance with a Word Error Rate of 0.212 and Character Error Rate of 0.120, several selectively frozen configurations achieve comparable recognition performance while substantially reducing trainable parameters and exhibiting more stable convergence. Moderate freezing depths, such as F>14 to F>15, attain nearly identical final WER values of 0.213 while significantly lowering computational costs. The authors interpret these findings as evidence of a trade-off where selective layer freezing acts as an effective regularizer against lexical overfitting in low-resource settings.
results.id: Eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa meskipun *fine-tuning* penuh mencapai performa absolut terbaik dengan *Word Error Rate* sebesar 0,212 dan *Character Error Rate* sebesar 0,120, beberapa konfigurasi yang dibekukan secara selektif mencapai performa pengenalan yang sebanding sekaligus mengurangi parameter terlatih secara substansial dan menunjukkan konvergensi yang lebih stabil. Kedalaman pembekuan moderat, seperti F>14 hingga F>15, memperoleh nilai *WER* akhir yang hampir identik yaitu 0,213 sembari menurunkan biaya komputasi secara signifikan. Para penulis menginterpretasikan temuan ini sebagai bukti adanya *trade-off* di mana *selective layer freezing* bertindak sebagai *regularizer* yang efektif terhadap *overfitting* leksikal pada pengaturan *low-resource*.

tldr.en: This paper investigates parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategies for automatic speech recognition in Cape Verdean Creole using the Wav2Vec 2.0 XLSR model. The results show that structured layer freezing achieves competitive recognition performance while substantially reducing trainable parameters and improving training stability.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti strategi *fine-tuning* yang efisien parameter untuk *automatic speech recognition* pada bahasa Kreol Tanjung Verde menggunakan model *Wav2Vec 2.0 XLSR*. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa *layer freezing* terstruktur mencapai performa pengenalan yang kompetitif sekaligus mengurangi parameter terlatih secara substansial dan meningkatkan stabilitas pelatihan.

acl:2026.rail-1.7.title: Less can be More: Towards a Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Wav2Vec2 XLSR for Low-Resource Cape Verdean Creole ASR
acl:2026.rail-1.7.venue: Proceedings of Resources for African Indigenous Languages (RAIL) 2026 @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.rail-1.8.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated in multilingual settings, yet their inference behavior in low-resource African languages remains underexplored especially under pure prompting without fine-tuning. We present a systematic study of prompting strategies for Natural Language Inference (NLI) in Swahili, Yoruba, and Hausa using the AfriXNLI benchmark. We evaluate five prompting strategies Baseline (zero-shot), Script-Aware, Language Specific, Contrastive, and Native-Label Self-Translation (NL-STP) across two mid-sized open weight models (Llama3.2-3B and Gemma3-4B). To isolate the effect of prompt design, the effect of few-shot examples and Chain-of-Thought reasoning is eliminated in our study. We find a significant difference in performance of class wise across strategies with highly neutral class collapse and high prediction skew in some configurations. Contrastive prompting proves to be the most reliable and steadily improving strategy over language and model and has better balance of class behavior and balance of overall accuracy gains. Notably, well-constructed prompts are sufficient to beat more powerful baselines that are provided with few-shot prompts and Chain-of-Thought prompts. We have found that prompt formulation is essential to multilingual NLI with low-resource languages and that language aware decision structuring can be used to meaningfully enhance robustness in resource challenged settings.
