acl:2026.sigul-1.5.abstract: We present mobile and desktop keyboards for Idu Mishmi, an endangered Trans-Himalayan language spoken by approximately 11,000 people in Arunachal Pradesh, India. A Latin-based orthography, the Idu Azobra, was developed in 2018, but no digital input tools existed to use it. The orthography requires characters absent from standard keyboards, including schwa (ə), retracted vowels (ə̱, o̱, u̱), nasalized vowels, and accented forms, several of which involve multi-codepoint Unicode sequences that default keyboards do not support. Developed with the Idu Mishmi community, the keyboards comprise: (1) an Android mobile keyboard, published on the Google Play Store, and (2) a Windows desktop keyboard distributed as a single portable executable. Both tools support the complete character inventory, and operate fully offline with zero network permissions. The Android keyboard has been adopted by community leaders and teachers who currently know and actively use the Idu Azobra orthography. The Windows keyboard is currently undergoing testing with community leaders. We describe the design, implementation, and deployment as a replicable model for other endangered language communities.
acl:2026.sigul-1.5.journal_ref: Proceedings of the SIGUL 2026 Joint Workshop with ELE, EURALI, and DCLRL: Towards Inclusivity and Equality: Language Resources and Technologies for Under-Resourced and Endangered Languages
acl:2026.sigul-1.5.title: Keyboards for the Endangered Idu Mishmi Language
acl:2026.sigul-1.5.venue: Proceedings of the SIGUL 2026 Joint Workshop with ELE, EURALI, and DCLRL: Towards Inclusivity and Equality: Language Resources and Technologies for Under-Resourced and Endangered Languages

acl:2026.sigul-1.6.abstract: We investigate multilingual sentiment analysis and interpretability across high- and low-resource languages, focusing on Amharic, English, German, and Hausa. Our study evaluates encoder-only transformer models for both sequence-level sentiment classification and token-level attribution using Captum. Additionally, we assess zero- and few-shot decoder-only models for sequence-level sentiment prediction. Our results show that few-shot decoder-only models outperform encoder-only models on token-level sentiment classification in most languages, with the exception of Hausa, where a multilingual encoder-based model leads. For sequence-level sentiment classification, encoder-only models generally achieve strong performance across most languages, but decoder-only models are highly competitive, and may even surpass encoders, in the high-resource settings (German, English) and low-resource scenarios, depending on the prompting strategy. These findings highlight the utility of combining fine-tuned transformer models with prompt- based large language models to build interpretable sentiment analysis systems across both low- and high-resource languages. The SAINT dataset, annotation guideline, and evaluation scripts can be found at https://github.com/uhh-hcds/SAINT.
acl:2026.sigul-1.6.journal_ref: Proceedings of the SIGUL 2026 Joint Workshop with ELE, EURALI, and DCLRL: Towards Inclusivity and Equality: Language Resources and Technologies for Under-Resourced and Endangered Languages

glossary.explanation_id: Proses penyesuaian bobot pada *pre-trained model* menggunakan *data* spesifik untuk tugas tertentu.
Kemampuan *large language model* untuk melakukan tugas tanpa pelatihan atau contoh sebelumnya.
Metode *prompting* yang memberikan beberapa contoh demonstrasi kepada model sebelum melakukan *inference*.
Komponen yang memecah teks menjadi unit subkata atau token yang dapat diproses oleh model.
Arsitektur *transformer* yang hanya menggunakan bagian *encoder* untuk representasi teks.
Arsitektur *transformer* generatif yang dirancang untuk menghasilkan teks secara autoregresif.
Kumpulan *data* terstruktur yang digunakan untuk melatih dan mengevaluasi *model bahasa*.
Standar evaluasi yang digunakan untuk mengukur dan membandingkan performa berbagai *model*.

background.en: Sentiment analysis is an essential tool across business intelligence and social science research, but deploying these models in real-world applications requires not only high predictive accuracy but also interpretability and transparency. While transformer models have significantly improved sentiment classification in high-resource languages like English and German, many low- and medium-resource languages remain underrepresented. This lack of linguistic infrastructure can obscure biases and systematic errors, creating an urgent need to evaluate how models perform across diverse language settings.
background.id: *Sentiment analysis* adalah alat yang esensial dalam bidang *business intelligence* dan riset ilmu sosial, namun penerapan model-model ini memerlukan akurasi prediktif yang tinggi serta *interpretability* dan transparansi. Meskipun model *transformer* telah meningkatkan klasifikasi sentimen secara signifikan pada bahasa *high-resource* seperti bahasa Inggris dan Jerman, banyak bahasa *low-resource* dan *medium-resource* yang masih kurang terwakili sehingga dapat mengaburkan bias dan kesalahan sistematis.

contributions.en: The authors introduce SAINT, a new annotated multilingual sentiment explainability dataset covering Amharic, English, German, and Hausa. They provide a comprehensive comparative analysis of sentiment explainability using encoder-only fine-tuned models and decoder-only models under zero-shot and few-shot settings, highlighting the challenges and differences in interpretability across languages, resource levels, and model types.
contributions.id: Para penulis memperkenalkan SAINT, sebuah *dataset* penjelasan sentimen multilinguistik beranotasi baru yang mencakup bahasa Amharika, Inggris, Jerman, dan Hausa. Mereka menyajikan analisis komparatif yang komprehensif mengenai *explainability* sentimen menggunakan model *encoder-only* yang telah di-*fine-tune* dan model *decoder-only* dalam pengaturan *zero-shot* dan *few-shot*.

future_work.en: The authors note limitations including the reliance on a single expert annotator per language, small dataset sizes for training encoder-only models, and limited LLM selections and contextual learning samples. Future work includes adding more annotators to assess inter-annotator agreement, exploring multitasking approaches to integrate sentiment and span-level tasks, and investigating better alignment between model attributions and human rationales.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat keterbatasan termasuk ketergantungan pada satu anotator ahli per bahasa, ukuran *dataset* yang relatif kecil untuk melatih model *encoder-only*, serta pemilihan *large language model* dan sampel pembelajaran kontekstual yang terbatas. Pekerjaan di masa mendatang mencakup penambahan lebih banyak anotator untuk menilai *inter-annotator agreement* dan menjelajahi pendekatan *multitasking*.

method.en: The study evaluates encoder-only transformer models and decoder-only large language models across Amharic, English, German, and Hausa. Expert annotators built the SAINT dataset using a customized Potato annotation tool. Encoder models were evaluated using monolingual and multilingual fine-tuning strategies alongside Captum for token-level attribution using Integrated Gradients, while decoder models were tested using zero-shot and few-shot prompting strategies.
method.id: Studi ini mengevaluasi model *transformer* *encoder-only* dan *large language model* *decoder-only* pada bahasa Amharika, Inggris, Jerman, dan Hausa. *Dataset* SAINT dikumpulkan oleh anotator ahli menggunakan alat anotasi Potato yang disesuaikan. Model *encoder* dievaluasi menggunakan strategi *fine-tuning* *monolingual* dan *multilingual* beserta Captum untuk atribusi tingkat token menggunakan *Integrated Gradients*, sementara model *decoder* diuji dengan strategi *prompting* *zero-shot* dan *few-shot*.

related_work.en: Previous research has progressed from lexicon-based and classical machine learning approaches to deep learning and transformer-based architectures. However, prior work on multilingual sentiment classification has given much less attention to model interpretability, often relying on computationally expensive and model-agnostic methods like LIME and SHAP or focusing solely on monolingual settings that do not generalize well to cross-lingual or token-level insights.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya telah berkembang dari pendekatan berbasis leksikon dan *machine learning* klasik ke arsitektur *deep learning* dan *transformer*. Namun, pekerjaan terdahulu pada klasifikasi sentimen multilinguistik jarang memperhatikan *interpretability* model dan sering kali bergantung pada metode yang mahal secara komputasi serta *model-agnostic* seperti LIME dan SHAP.

results.en: For sequence-level sentiment classification, encoder-only models like AfroXLMR-Social achieved strong performance across languages, while decoder-only models such as GPT-4o-mini were highly competitive and matched or surpassed encoders in high-resource and certain low-resource settings. For token-level classification, few-shot decoder-only models generally outperformed encoder-only models in most languages, except for Hausa where multilingual encoder-based models led.
results.id: Untuk klasifikasi sentimen tingkat sekuens, model *encoder-only* seperti AfroXLMR-Social mencapai performa yang kuat di berbagai bahasa, sementara model *decoder-only* seperti GPT-4o-mini sangat kompetitif dan mampu menyamai atau melampaui *encoder*. Untuk klasifikasi tingkat token, model *decoder-only* dengan *few-shot* secara umum mengungguli model *encoder-only* pada sebagian besar bahasa, kecuali pada bahasa Hausa.

tldr.en: This paper investigates multilingual sentiment analysis and model interpretability across high- and low-resource languages using both encoder-only and decoder-only transformer models. The results show that few-shot decoder-only models frequently outperform encoder-only models on token-level classification, while both architectures achieve strong performance on sequence-level classification depending on the language and strategy.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti analisis *sentiment analysis* multilinguistik dan *interpretability* model lintas bahasa *high-resource* dan *low-resource* menggunakan model *transformer* *encoder-only* dan *decoder-only*. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa model *decoder-only* dengan *few-shot* sering kali mengungguli model *encoder-only* pada klasifikasi tingkat token, sementara kedua arsitektur mencapai performa yang kuat pada klasifikasi tingkat sekuens tergantung pada bahasa dan strategi yang digunakan.

acl:2026.sigul-1.6.title: SAINT: Multilingual Span-Level Interpretability for Sentiment Analysis
acl:2026.sigul-1.6.venue: Proceedings of the SIGUL 2026 Joint Workshop with ELE, EURALI, and DCLRL: Towards Inclusivity and Equality: Language Resources and Technologies for Under-Resourced and Endangered Languages

acl:2026.sigul-1.7.abstract: Safety evaluation of Large Language Models (LLMs) has largely focused on high-resource languages, leaving low-resource languages critically underserved. We present AlbanianLLMSafety, the first publicly available safety evaluation dataset for LLMs in Albanian, a linguistically distinct low-resource language with approximately 7.5 million speakers across Albania, Kosovo, North Macedonia, and the diaspora. The dataset contains 2,951 prompts spanning 11 safety categories, including self-harm, violence, racist content, child exploitation, and radicalization, with an average of 268 prompts per category. Each prompt is provided in Albanian with an English reference translation and a detailed category label. This resource addresses a significant gap in safety evaluation infrastructure for low-resource languages and provides an essential benchmark for developing safer, more inclusive LLMs. The dataset will be provided upon request to support safety evaluation, fine-tuning, red-teaming, and guardrail development for Albanian-speaking communities.
acl:2026.sigul-1.7.journal_ref: Proceedings of the SIGUL 2026 Joint Workshop with ELE, EURALI, and DCLRL: Towards Inclusivity and Equality: Language Resources and Technologies for Under-Resourced and Endangered Languages
acl:2026.sigul-1.7.title: AlbanianLLMSafety: A Safety Evaluation Dataset for Large Language Models in Albanian
acl:2026.sigul-1.7.venue: Proceedings of the SIGUL 2026 Joint Workshop with ELE, EURALI, and DCLRL: Towards Inclusivity and Equality: Language Resources and Technologies for Under-Resourced and Endangered Languages

acl:2026.sigul-1.8.abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) bridges the gap between computer vision and natural language processing, yet progress remains largely confined to high-resource languages. For low-resource languages like Urdu, research is severely hindered by the total absence of large-scale reasoning-based datasets. To address this critical gap, we introduce the first synthetic Urdu VQA dataset modeled after the CLEVR framework, specifically designed to evaluate complex, multi-step visual reasoning. We conduct a rigorous comparative analysis using both transformer-based architectures (VisualBERT, LXMERT, ViLT) and neuro-symbolic models. Our results demonstrate that the neuro-symbolic approach achieves a superior accuracy of 85.3%, outperforming the strongest transformer baseline by 7.1% while maintaining competitive processing efficiency. This work establishes a primary benchmark for Urdu VQA, demonstrating that hybrid reasoning architectures provide a robust and scalable solution for advancing multimodal AI in under-resourced linguistic contexts.
acl:2026.sigul-1.8.journal_ref: Proceedings of the SIGUL 2026 Joint Workshop with ELE, EURALI, and DCLRL: Towards Inclusivity and Equality: Language Resources and Technologies for Under-Resourced and Endangered Languages

glossary.explanation_id: Pendekatan hibrida yang menggabungkan kemampuan persepsi dari *neural network* dengan penalaran formal serta transparansi dari *symbolic AI*.
Representasi terstruktur yang mengkodekan objek visual, atribut fisik, serta koordinat spasial di dalam suatu citra.
Proses menyelaraskan representasi fitur dari modalitas visual dan tekstual agar saling terhubung secara akurat.
Teknik pengambilan sampel untuk memastikan distribusi jawaban yang seimbang dan mengurangi bias dalam *dataset*.
Proses memecah teks menjadi unit-unit kecil yang disebut *token* seperti kata atau sub-kata untuk diproses oleh *model bahasa*.

background.en: Visual Question Answering bridges computer vision and natural language processing, but progress is largely confined to high-resource languages. For low-resource languages such as Urdu, research is severely hindered by rich morphological structures, complex syntax, and the total absence of large-scale reasoning-based datasets.
background.id: *Visual Question Answering* menjembatani *computer vision* dan *natural language processing*, namun kemajuannya sebagian besar terbatas pada bahasa *high-resource*. Untuk bahasa *low-resource* seperti bahasa Urdu, penelitian sangat terhambat oleh struktur morfologi yang kaya, sintaksis yang kompleks, dan ketiadaan total *dataset* berbasis penalaran berskala besar.

contributions.en: The paper makes two primary contributions to multimodal AI. First, it introduces Urdu-CLEVR, the first human-verified, complexity-controlled VQA benchmark for the Urdu language using a structured template-based generation process. Second, it establishes the first relational VQA benchmarks for Urdu, demonstrating that neuro-symbolic architectures significantly outperform transformer-based models.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memberikan dua kontribusi utama bagi *multimodal* *AI*. Pertama, makalah ini memperkenalkan *Urdu-CLEVR*, *benchmark* *VQA* pertama yang diverifikasi oleh manusia dan dikontrol kompleksitasnya untuk bahasa Urdu menggunakan proses *generation* berbasis templat terstruktur. Kedua, makalah ini menetapkan *benchmark* *VQA* relasional pertama untuk bahasa Urdu, yang menunjukkan bahwa arsitektur *neuro-symbolic* mengungguli model berbasis *transformer* secara signifikan.

future_work.en: The authors note that the use of synthetic images and template-based question generation may not fully reflect the linguistic diversity of natural Urdu discourse. Future work should focus on extending these reasoning tasks to more diverse, naturalistic visual and linguistic settings while addressing potential semantic drift in spatial attributes.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa penggunaan citra sintetis dan *generation* pertanyaan berbasis templat mungkin belum sepenuhnya mencerminkan keragaman linguistik dari wacana bahasa Urdu alami. Penelitian masa depan harus berfokus pada perluasan tugas penalaran ini ke dalam *setting* visual dan linguistik yang lebih beragam dan naturalistik sekaligus mengatasi potensi *semantic drift* pada atribut spasial.

method.en: The methodology comprises dataset synthesis modeled after the CLEVR framework, cross-modal alignment involving specialized preprocessing to map Urdu text to visual features, and evaluation of three transformer models alongside a neuro-symbolic framework. The pipeline uses structured scene graphs, 90 question families, NLTK tokenization, and Unicode standardization.
method.id: Metodologi ini mencakup sintesis *dataset* yang dimodelkan setelah kerangka *CLEVR*, *cross-modal alignment* yang melibatkan *preprocessing* khusus untuk memetakan teks bahasa Urdu ke fitur visual, serta *evaluasi* tiga model *transformer* beserta kerangka *neuro-symbolic*. *Pipeline* ini menggunakan *scene graph* terstruktur, 90 famili pertanyaan, *tokenization* NLTK, dan standardisasi Unicode.

related_work.en: Prior research on VQA divides benchmarks into synthetic diagnostic reasoning datasets like CLEVR, real-world perception datasets like VQA 2.0 and GQA, and knowledge-intensive datasets like FVQA and OK-VQA. However, these existing benchmarks are predominantly English-centric, lacking support for Urdu linguistic complexities, explicit reasoning programs, and bias-controlled evaluation in under-resourced contexts.
related_work.id: Penelitian terdahulu tentang *VQA* membagi *benchmark* menjadi *dataset* *synthetic diagnostic reasoning* seperti *CLEVR*, *dataset* persepsi dunia nyata seperti *VQA 2.0* dan *GQA*, serta *dataset* intensif pengetahuan seperti *FVQA* dan *OK-VQA*. Namun, *benchmark* yang ada sebagian besar berpusat pada bahasa Inggris, sehingga kurang mendukung kompleksitas linguistik bahasa Urdu, program penalaran eksplisit, dan *evaluasi* yang terkontrol dari bias dalam konteks *low-resource*.

results.en: The neuro-symbolic model achieves an accuracy of 85.3% on Urdu-CLEVR, significantly outperforming transformer-based architectures such as VisualBERT at 72.5%, ViLT at 74.6%, and LXMERT at 78.2%. The results demonstrate that while purely neural transformers struggle with rich morphology and lack of pretraining corpora in low-resource settings, neuro-symbolic models provide superior robustness and interpretability.
results.id: Model *neuro-symbolic* mencapai akurasi sebesar 85,3% pada *Urdu-CLEVR*, mengungguli arsitektur berbasis *transformer* seperti *VisualBERT* sebesar 72,5%, *ViLT* sebesar 74,6%, dan *LXMERT* sebesar 78,2% secara signifikan. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa sementara *transformer* murni berbasis neural mengalami kesulitan dengan morfologi yang kaya dan kurangnya korpus pra-pelatihan dalam *setting* *low-resource*, model *neuro-symbolic* memberikan ketahanan dan *interpretability* yang superior.

tldr.en: This paper introduces Urdu-CLEVR, the first synthetic visual question answering dataset for Urdu designed to evaluate multi-step visual reasoning. The evaluation shows that a neuro-symbolic approach significantly outperforms transformer-based models in this low-resource setting.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan *Urdu-CLEVR*, *dataset* *visual question answering* sintetis pertama untuk bahasa Urdu yang dirancang untuk mengevaluasi penalaran visual multi-langkah. Hasil *evaluasi* menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan *neuro-symbolic* mengungguli model berbasis *transformer* secara signifikan dalam *setting* *low-resource*.

acl:2026.sigul-1.8.title: Urdu-CLEVR: A Novel Benchmark for Visual Reasoning in an Under-Resourced Linguistic Context
acl:2026.sigul-1.8.venue: Proceedings of the SIGUL 2026 Joint Workshop with ELE, EURALI, and DCLRL: Towards Inclusivity and Equality: Language Resources and Technologies for Under-Resourced and Endangered Languages

acl:2026.slide-1.10.abstract: This paper presents a two-stage training approach to improve the performance of Slovene large language models on lexicographic question-answering tasks. We developed a comprehensive lexical pretraining corpus containing 356,294 Slovene word entries. We constructed the corpus by converting structured data from multiple lexicographic sources into markdown format. Additionally, we created a question-answering dataset with 10,485 QA pairs from diverse sources, including automatically generated questions, a linguistic advisory portal, and community forums. Using the Slovenian GaMS model (based on Gemma 2 9B) and GaMS 3 model (based on Gemma 3 12B), we performed continued pretraining on the lexical corpus, followed by instruction fine-tuning with our QA dataset combined with translated general-domain questions. We compared results to different model configurations. Our results demonstrate significant improvements (text similarity increasing from 0.226 to 0.542, BERTScore F1 of 0.915) in answering Slovene lexicographic questions, validating the effectiveness of domain-specific continued pretraining for low-resource languages.
acl:2026.slide-1.10.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Workshop on Structured Linguistic Data and Evaluation (SLiDE)
acl:2026.slide-1.10.title: Improving Slovene Language Models for Lexicographic Question Answering through Continued Pretraining and Instruction Fine-Tuning
acl:2026.slide-1.10.venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Structured Linguistic Data and Evaluation (SLiDE)

acl:2026.speakable-1.14.abstract: Multi-modal Speech Language Models (SpeechLMs) are a recent advancement in natural language processing. These SpeechLMs are instruction-tuned and optimized for general tasks. Their usefulness for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), particularly in relatively low-resource scenarios, remains largely understudied. This work developed SpeechLM for ASR in Basque and Maltese and studied the impact of language-adapted Large Language Model (LLM) and speech encoder within the SpeechLM for ASR. Using supervised learning, we fine-tuned LLaMA-Omni, a SpeechLM, for ASR. We have conducted comprehensive hyperparameter tuning and experimented with language-adapted SpeechLM components to improve performance and evaluated our best models on in-distribution datasets for both languages and an out-of-distribution dataset for Basque. LLaMA-Omni achieved 8.09% WER in Basque and 25.65% WER for Maltese on average across multiple test splits. The in-distribution results show that SpeechLM outperforms a fine-tuned ASR system under specific constraints, whereas it underperforms the baseline model on out-of-distribution Basque, indicating weaker overall robustness. We also find that a language-adapted LLM within SpeechLM improves in out-of-distribution settings when compared to the off-the-shelf LLM within SpeechLM.
acl:2026.speakable-1.14.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Metrik metrik evaluasi yang mengukur persentase kesalahan kata antara transkripsi teks hasil *model* dan transkripsi referensi.
Proses melatih ulang *large language model* atau *model* terlatih pada *dataset* spesifik untuk meningkatkan kinerja pada tugas tertentu.
Metode pembelajaran mesin di mana *model* dilatih menggunakan *dataset* beranotasi yang memiliki pasangan input dan target yang benar.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain memiliki ketersediaan *data* dan sumber daya komputasi yang sangat terbatas.
Komponen dalam *model* wicara yang bertugas mengekstrak fitur akustik dari sinyal audio mentah atau bentuk gelombang.
Kondisi pengujian di mana *dataset* evaluasi memiliki karakteristik akustik atau domain yang berbeda jauh dari *data* pelatihan.
Pendekatan transfer pengetahuan atau pelatihan yang melibatkan lebih dari satu bahasa.

background.en: Multi-modal Speech Language Models are a recent advancement in natural language processing, optimized for general instruction-following tasks. However, their usefulness for Automatic Speech Recognition, particularly in relatively low-resource scenarios, remains largely understudied. This paper addresses this gap by investigating how these architectures perform in under-resourced environments and examining the impact of language-adapted components.
background.id: *Multi-modal speech language model* merupakan kemajuan terkini dalam pengolahan bahasa alami yang dioptimalkan untuk tugas-tugas *instruction-following* secara umum. Namun, kegunaannya untuk *automatic speech recognition*, terutama dalam skenario *low-resource*, sebagian besar masih belum banyak diteliti. Makalah ini membahas kesenjangan tersebut dengan meneliti bagaimana arsitektur ini bekerja di lingkungan *low-resource* dan mengkaji dampak dari komponen yang diadaptasi ke bahasa tertentu.

contributions.en: The paper provides the first systematic evaluation of speech language model-based automatic speech recognition in low-resource language settings using Basque and Maltese. It isolates the effect of language adaptation at different system components by introducing Latxa-Omni with a language-adapted large language model and experimenting with adapted speech encoders. Furthermore, it conducts a data scarcity analysis to demonstrate how training data size impacts model performance.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyajikan evaluasi sistematis pertama mengenai *automatic speech recognition* berbasis *speech language model* dalam pengaturan bahasa *low-resource* menggunakan bahasa Basque dan bahasa Maltese. Penelitian ini mengisolasi efek adaptasi bahasa pada komponen sistem yang berbeda dengan memperkenalkan Latxa-Omni yang menggunakan *large language model* beradaptasi bahasa dan bereksperimen dengan *speech encoder* yang diadaptasi. Selain itu, penelitian ini melakukan analisis kelangkaan data untuk menunjukkan bagaimana ukuran data pelatihan memengaruhi kinerja model.

future_work.en: Future work should focus on optimizing adapter designs and exploring cross-lingual transfer mechanisms to reduce the data burden for speech language model adaptation, ultimately moving toward a more holistic integration of language-specific linguistic knowledge within the framework.
future_work.id: Penelitian mendatang harus berfokus pada pengoptimalan desain *adapter* dan mengeksplorasi mekanisme transfer lintas bahasa untuk mengurangi beban data bagi adaptasi *speech language model*, yang pada akhirnya mengarah pada integrasi pengetahuan linguistik khusus bahasa yang lebih holistik di dalam kerangka kerja.

method.en: The authors fine-tuned LLaMA-Omni using supervised learning on extensive corpora for Basque and Maltese. They conducted three main experiments exploring off-the-shelf adaptation, replacing the large language model with a Basque-specific instruction-tuned model named Latxa-Omni, and swapping the speech encoder with a language-adapted version. They also performed a controlled experiment using a reduced 35-hour Basque corpus to study data scarcity. Evaluation was performed using Word Error Rate on in-distribution datasets and the Faktoria out-of-distribution dataset for Basque.
method.id: Para penulis melakukan *fine-tuning* pada LLaMA-Omni menggunakan *supervised learning* pada korpus ekstensif untuk bahasa Basque dan bahasa Maltese. Mereka melakukan tiga eksperimen utama yang mengeksplorasi *off-the-shelf adaptation*, mengganti *large language model* dengan model *instruction-tuned* khusus bahasa Basque bernama Latxa-Omni, serta menukar *speech encoder* dengan versi yang diadaptasi ke bahasa. Mereka juga melakukan eksperimen terkontrol menggunakan korpus bahasa Basque yang dikurangi menjadi 35 jam untuk mempelajari kelangkaan data. Evaluasi dilakukan menggunakan *Word Error Rate* pada *dataset* *in-distribution* dan *dataset* *out-of-distribution* Faktoria untuk bahasa Basque.

related_work.en: Recent progress in speech language models has enabled end-to-end speech understanding and generation without relying on traditional cascaded pipelines. Systems such as LLaMA-Omni, Soundwave, EchoX, and GLM-4 Voice have proposed novel architectures toward low-latency speech interaction. However, their evaluation remains restricted to speech-to-text instruction-following and generative tasks in high-resource languages like English, leaving low-resource downstream tasks such as automatic speech recognition largely unexplored.
related_work.id: Kemajuan terkini pada *speech language model* telah memungkinkan pemahaman dan pembuatan ucapan *end-to-end* tanpa mengandalkan *pipeline* terenkripsi tradisional. Sistem seperti LLaMA-Omni, Soundwave, EchoX, dan GLM-4 Voice telah mengusulkan arsitektur baru untuk interaksi suara berlatensi rendah. Namun, evaluasinya tetap terbatas pada tugas *speech-to-text instruction-following* dan generatif dalam bahasa *high-resource* seperti bahasa Inggris, sehingga tugas hilir *low-resource* seperti *automatic speech recognition* sebagian besar masih belum dieksplorasi.

results.en: On Basque in-distribution test sets, LLaMA-Omni outperformed the whisper-large-v3 baseline by 22%, achieving an average Word Error Rate of 8.09%, while Latxa-Omni achieved 7.98%. Conversely, Maltese models exhibited a performance degradation of approximately 50% due to data scarcity. In out-of-distribution evaluations for Basque, traditional baselines outperformed all speech language model variants, though models with language-adapted components showed better robustness and generalizability than off-the-shelf variants.
results.id: Pada perangkat pengujian *in-distribution* bahasa Basque, LLaMA-Omni mengungguli *baseline* *whisper-large-v3* sebesar 22%, mencapai rata-rata *Word Error Rate* sebesar 8,09%, sementara Latxa-Omni mencapai 7,98%. Sebaliknya, model bahasa Maltese menunjukkan penurunan kinerja sekitar 50% karena kelangkaan data. Dalam evaluasi *out-of-distribution* untuk bahasa Basque, *baseline* tradisional mengungguli semua varian *speech language model*, meskipun model dengan komponen yang diadaptasi ke bahasa menunjukkan ketahanan dan kemampuan generalisasi yang lebih baik daripada varian *off-the-shelf*.

tldr.en: This paper investigates the adaptability of multi-modal speech language models for automatic speech recognition in low-resource languages like Basque and Maltese. The findings show that while speech language models can outperform traditional baselines with sufficient data, they are highly sensitive to data scarcity and out-of-distribution shifts.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti adaptabilitas dari *multi-modal speech language model* untuk *automatic speech recognition* pada bahasa *low-resource* seperti bahasa Basque dan bahasa Maltese. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa meskipun *speech language model* dapat mengungguli *baseline* tradisional ketika data mencukupi, model tersebut sangat sensitif terhadap kelangkaan data dan pergeseran *out-of-distribution*.

acl:2026.speakable-1.14.title: SpeechLM for Automatic Speech Recognition in Low-resource Languages
acl:2026.speakable-1.14.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.15.abstract: This study explores how bilingual fine-tuning affects automatic speech recognition (ASR) in low-resource languages. We evaluate this method across nine linguistically and geographically diverse language pairs, covering a range of language families and writing systems. To distinguish the two languages, during training, we pre-pend each input text with a language identification token. At inference, the model jointly predicts both the language and transcription from the speech input alone. As texts for which the language is incorrectly determined show low ASR performance, we also conduct a follow-up experiment in which the language identification token is provided both during training and inference. Our results show that bilingual fine-tuning can be beneficial when language identification accuracy is high, and that in cases where language identification performance is low, including the language identification token at inference helps to improve ASR performance.
acl:2026.speakable-1.15.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: *Fine-tuning* adalah proses melatih ulang model *pre-trained* pada dataset tertentu untuk tugas hilir tertentu.
Bahasa *low-resource* adalah bahasa yang memiliki ketersediaan data teks atau audio beranotasi yang sangat terbatas untuk pelatihan komputer.
*Inference* adalah tahap di mana model yang sudah dilatih digunakan untuk menghasilkan prediksi pada data baru.
Sebuah *utterance* adalah segmen atau ucapan suara tunggal yang digunakan sebagai unit data dalam korpus ucapan.
*Down-sampling* adalah proses mengurangi jumlah sampel data agar ukurannya seragam di antara kelompok yang dibandingkan.
*Cross-lingual transfer* adalah metode memanfaatkan pengetahuan yang dipelajari dari suatu bahasa untuk membantu tugas pada bahasa lain.
*Word error rate* adalah metrik evaluasi yang mengukur tingkat kesalahan kata pada transkripsi otomatis dibandingkan dengan referensi.
Sebuah *baseline* adalah model standar atau metode pembanding yang digunakan untuk mengukur efektivitas metode baru.

background.en: Automatic speech recognition has progressed rapidly, but much of that progress remains limited to high-resource languages such as English due to data scarcity and dialectal variation. A promising approach to address this challenge is cross-lingual transfer learning, where knowledge from high-resource languages supports low-resource ones. However, it remains unclear whether bilingual fine-tuning with explicit language identification consistently improves automatic speech recognition across diverse linguistic contexts, as prior work has not systematically examined this approach across language families, scripts, or varying degrees of linguistic similarity.
background.id: Pengenalan ucapan otomatis telah berkembang pesat, tetapi sebagian besar kemajuan tersebut tetap terbatas pada bahasa *high-resource* seperti bahasa Inggris karena kelangkaan data dan variasi dialek. Pendekatan yang menjanjikan untuk mengatasi tantangan ini adalah *cross-lingual transfer learning*, di mana pengetahuan dari bahasa *high-resource* mendukung bahasa *low-resource*. Namun, masih belum jelas apakah *fine-tuning* bilingual dengan *language identification* yang eksplisit secara konsisten meningkatkan pengenalan ucapan otomatis di berbagai konteks linguistik, karena penelitian sebelumnya belum secara sistematis menguji pendekatan ini di berbagai *family*, aksara, atau tingkat kemiripan linguistik.

contributions.en: This work investigates when and under what conditions bilingual fine-tuning using two related languages with explicit language identification tokens benefits low-resource languages. The study evaluates this approach across nine typologically diverse pairs of related languages spanning five language families and multiple writing systems, and assesses the robustness of observed gains using random subsets of data.
contributions.id: Penelitian ini menyelidiki kapan dan dalam kondisi apa *fine-tuning* bilingual menggunakan dua bahasa yang berkerabat dengan token *language identification* yang eksplisit memberikan manfaat bagi bahasa *low-resource*. Studi ini mengevaluasi pendekatan tersebut di sembilan pasangan bahasa berkerabat yang secara tipologis beragam, mencakup lima *family* bahasa dan berbagai sistem penulisan, serta menilai ketahanan peningkatan yang diamati menggunakan *subset* data secara acak.

future_work.en: The authors state that they did not investigate why language identification performance was lower for some language pairs, nor did they examine the effect of model architecture, the fine-tuning approach, the stopping criterion, or whether the bilingual approach resulted in new mistakes compared to the monolingual model when language identification was correctly identified. These questions are left for future work.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyatakan bahwa mereka tidak menyelidiki mengapa performa *language identification* lebih rendah untuk beberapa pasangan bahasa, dan mereka juga tidak menguji efek arsitektur model, pendekatan *fine-tuning*, kriteria penghentian (*stopping criterion*), atau apakah pendekatan bilingual menghasilkan kesalahan baru dibandingkan dengan model *monolingual* ketika *language identification* diidentifikasi dengan benar. Pertanyaan-pertanyaan ini diserahkan untuk penelitian di masa mendatang.

method.en: The authors fine-tuned the pre-trained XLS-R 1B model, based on the Wav2Vec 2.0 architecture, by freezing the convolutional feature encoder and updating only the transformer layers. They used Common Voice 17.0 datasets, down-sampling both languages in each pair to 3000 utterances to avoid bias. During training, a language identification token was pre-pended to each input text. At inference, the model jointly predicted the language and transcription. A follow-up experiment also tested providing the correct language identification at inference using a language-specific bias embedding added to the connectionist temporal classification logits.
method.id: Para penulis melakukan *fine-tuning* pada model *pre-trained* XLS-R 1B yang berbasis arsitektur Wav2Vec 2.0, dengan membekukan *convolutional feature encoder* dan hanya memperbarui *layer* *transformer*. Mereka menggunakan dataset Common Voice 17.0, melakukan *down-sampling* pada kedua bahasa di setiap pasangan menjadi 3000 *utterance* untuk menghindari bias. Selama pelatihan, token *language identification* ditambahkan di awal setiap teks masukan. Pada saat *inference*, model secara bersamaan memprediksi bahasa dan transkripsi. Eksperimen lanjutan juga menguji penyediaan *language identification* yang benar pada saat *inference* menggunakan *bias embedding* khusus bahasa yang ditambahkan ke *logit* *connectionist temporal classification*.

related_work.en: Prior studies have explored language-aware and language-agnostic multilingual fine-tuning strategies to enable cross-lingual transfer in automatic speech recognition. Other works explicitly incorporated language information using external language identification, meta-learning frameworks, adapter-based methods, and multi-task learning setups with auxiliary connectionist temporal classification objectives or hierarchical softmax structures. Additionally, recent work showed that Frisian automatic speech recognition performance improves when multilingual fine-tuning corpora are augmented with pre-pended language identification tokens. However, these prior works did not systematically examine the approach across diverse linguistic similarities, writing scripts, or language families.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya telah mengeksplorasi strategi *multilingual* *fine-tuning* yang sadar bahasa dan agnostik bahasa untuk mengaktifkan *cross-lingual transfer* dalam pengenalan ucapan otomatis. Penelitian lain secara eksplisit memasukkan informasi bahasa menggunakan identifikasi bahasa eksternal, kerangka kerja *meta-learning*, metode berbasis *adapter*, dan pengaturan *multi-task learning* dengan tujuan *connectionist temporal classification* tambahan atau struktur *hierarchical softmax*. Selain itu, penelitian terbaru menunjukkan bahwa performa pengenalan ucapan otomatis bahasa Frisia meningkat ketika korpus *multilingual* *fine-tuning* ditambah dengan token *language identification* di awal. Namun, penelitian-penelitian terdahulu ini tidak secara sistematis menguji pendekatan tersebut di berbagai kemiripan linguistik, aksara penulisan, atau *family* bahasa.

results.en: The evaluation shows a diverse pattern where a small majority of language pairs exhibit positive word error rate improvements, while others show negative improvements, strongly associating performance gains with language identification accuracy. Specifically, language pairs with high language identification accuracy above 95 percent achieved clear improvements, whereas lower accuracy limited or counteracted the benefits. Furthermore, a follow-up experiment demonstrated that explicitly providing the correct language identification at inference successfully improved performance for language pairs with lower language identification accuracy.
results.id: Evaluasi menunjukkan pola yang beragam di mana sebagian kecil mayoritas pasangan bahasa menunjukkan peningkatan *word error rate* yang positif, sementara yang lain menunjukkan peningkatan negatif, yang mengaitkan peningkatan performa secara kuat dengan akurasi *language identification*. Secara khusus, pasangan bahasa dengan akurasi *language identification* yang tinggi di atas 95 persen mencapai peningkatan yang jelas, sedangkan akurasi yang lebih rendah membatasi atau menetralkan manfaat tersebut. Selain itu, eksperimen lanjutan menunjukkan bahwa secara eksplisit menyediakan *language identification* yang benar pada saat *inference* berhasil meningkatkan performa untuk pasangan bahasa dengan akurasi *language identification* yang lebih rendah.

tldr.en: This study explores how bilingual fine-tuning affects automatic speech recognition in low-resource languages across nine diverse language pairs. The results show that bilingual fine-tuning is beneficial when language identification accuracy is high, and providing the language identification token at inference helps improve performance when accuracy is low.
tldr.id: Studi ini mengeksplorasi bagaimana *fine-tuning* bilingual memengaruhi pengenalan ucapan otomatis pada bahasa *low-resource* di sembilan pasang bahasa yang beragam. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa *fine-tuning* bilingual bermanfaat ketika akurasi *language identification* tinggi, dan menyediakan token *language identification* pada saat *inference* membantu meningkatkan performa ketika akurasi rendah.

acl:2026.speakable-1.15.title: Improving Low-resource ASR Using Bilingual Fine-tuning with Language Identification: A Cross-linguistic Evaluation
acl:2026.speakable-1.15.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.16.abstract: This study presents our attempt on applying Query by Example - Spoken Term Detection methodologies to a real-world, low-resource scenario: building an audio-based query functionality for the diasporan Teochew dictionary WhatTCSay. This functionality enables users to retrieve dictionary entries without prior knowledge of the writing systems in Teochew, thereby enhancing the accessibility of the dictionary and facilitating language revitalization efforts within Teochew communities. To address the retrieval task, we investigate two approaches: (i) an ASR-based approach using text-to-text matching, and (ii) a Dynamic Time Warping (DTW)-based acoustic framework for audio-to-audio retrieval. In the first approach, we compare an automatic romanization of the spoken query against the gold romanization from the dictionary; in the second, we directly match the user’s spoken query against audio recordings from the dictionary pronounced by a native speaker. Retrieval performance is evaluated using recall at rank k. Results show that text-to-text matching achieves better performance than audio-to-audio matching; however, the two approaches were not optimized under fully comparable conditions, as the ASR-based approach benefited from additional optimization, which was not equally available for the DTW method.

acl:2026.speakable-1.16.title: Leveraging Speech Models for Audio-based Lexical Retrieval in Dictionaries: The Case of the Teochew Language
acl:2026.speakable-1.16.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.17.abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) for low-resource languages remains challenging due to limited labeled data. Although multilingual models and the inclusion of related auxiliary languages enable cross-lingual transfer, it is still unclear how introducing cross-lingual information at different training stages-pre-training versus fine-tuning-affects downstream performance. Prior work largely treats transfer as a single-stage optimization problem without disentangling stage effects. We present a stage-aware analysis of cross-lingual transfer for Faroese ASR using related auxiliary languages and Wav2Vec 2.0 XLS-R models. We systematically compare two complementary adaptation pipelines: (i) cross-lingual supervised fine-tuning and (ii) cross-lingual continuous pre-training prior to fine-tuning. Both strategies are evaluated under a unified setup with controlled model architectures, balanced representation of auxiliary languages, and identical evaluation protocols. Results demonstrate that cross-lingual transfer is stage-dependent. Supervised adaptation optimizes in-domain accuracy, while pretraining-level adaptation enhances robustness and reduces Character Error Rate (CER). Auxiliary language effects vary across pipelines, reinforcing the idea that transfer effectiveness depends on when and how cross-lingual information is introduced. Comparisons with large-scale multilingual ASR models highlight trade-offs between model scale and explicit, small-scale domain-aware adaptation. These findings suggest that effective cross-lingual transfer for Faroese low-resource ASR is inherently stage-dependent rather than a single-step design choice.
acl:2026.speakable-1.17.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Proses melatih ulang *pretrained model* yang sudah ada menggunakan data spesifik tugas tertentu untuk meningkatkan akurasi.
Tahap awal pelatihan model pada korpus data berskala besar agar mempelajari representasi umum sebelum disesuaikan ke tugas hilir.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau tugas memiliki ketersediaan data beranotasi yang sangat terbatas.
Standar atau kumpulan data evaluasi yang digunakan untuk mengukur dan membandingkan performa berbagai model.
Unit teks terkecil yang diproses oleh model bahasa setelah melalui proses *tokenization*.
Komponen yang memecah teks mentah menjadi urutan token yang dapat dipahami oleh model.
Kemampuan model untuk melakukan tugas baru tanpa memerlukan contoh pelatihan atau penyesuaian khusus sebelumnya.
Model bahasa berukuran sangat besar yang dilatih pada korpus masif untuk memahami dan menghasilkan teks.

background.en: Automatic speech recognition for low-resource languages remains a significant challenge due to the scarcity of annotated data and domain mismatch between training and real-world deployment. Faroese, a Scandinavian language with roughly 70,000 speakers, exemplifies these difficulties because available labeled data is insufficient for generalizing beyond clean read speech. While multilingual models and related auxiliary languages can facilitate cross-lingual transfer, it remains unclear how introducing auxiliary information at different training stages affects downstream performance.
background.id: Pengenalan suara otomatis untuk bahasa *low-resource* tetap menjadi tantangan besar akibat kurangnya data beranotasi dan ketidakcocokan *domain* antara pelatihan dan penerapan di dunia nyata. Bahasa Faroese, sebuah bahasa Skandinavia dengan sekitar 70.000 penutur, mencerminkan kesulitan ini karena data beranotasi yang tersedia belum mencukupi untuk generalisasi di luar *read speech* yang bersih. Meskipun *multilingual model* dan bahasa bantu terkait dapat memfasilitasi transfer *cross-lingual*, masih belum jelas bagaimana pengenalan informasi bantu pada tahap pelatihan yang berbeda memengaruhi performa hilir.

contributions.en: This study contributes a systematic, stage-aware analysis of cross-lingual transfer for Faroese automatic speech recognition using Wav2Vec 2.0 XLS-R models. The primary contributions include a unified comparison between supervised cross-lingual fine-tuning and continuous self-supervised pre-training, the creation of a challenging new out-of-domain parliamentary benchmark named FO-Parl-Eval-2h10m, and the public release of newly trained models and full replication pipelines.
contributions.id: Studi ini berkontribusi melalui analisis yang sistematis dan *stage-aware* terhadap transfer *cross-lingual* untuk *automatic speech recognition* bahasa Faroese menggunakan model Wav2Vec 2.0 XLS-R. Kontribusi utamanya meliputi perbandingan terpadu antara *supervised cross-lingual fine-tuning* dan *continuous self-supervised pre-training*, pembuatan *benchmark* parlementer *out-of-domain* baru yang menantang bernama FO-Parl-Eval-2h10m, serta rilis publik untuk model yang baru dilatih dan *pipeline* replikasi lengkap.

future_work.en: The authors note several limitations, including computational constraints that restrict model sizes and limit continuous pre-training to a single model variant, a focus on a single target language, and domain overlap between the pre-training data and the parliamentary evaluation set. Future work could validate these findings on other low-resource languages and scale up model sizes.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat beberapa keterbatasan, termasuk kendala komputasi yang membatasi ukuran model dan membatasi *continuous pre-training* pada satu varian model saja, fokus pada satu bahasa target tunggal, serta adanya tumpang tindih *domain* antara data *pre-training* dan *set* evaluasi parlementer. Penelitian masa depan dapat memvalidasi temuan ini pada bahasa *low-resource* lainnya dan meningkatkan skala ukuran model.

method.en: The research evaluates two complementary adaptation pipelines using Wav2Vec 2.0 XLS-R architectures. Pipeline A performs supervised cross-lingual fine-tuning on auxiliary languages followed by Faroese-only continued fine-tuning, using 100 hours of data per stage. Pipeline B introduces cross-lingual continuous pre-training on 1,000 hours of unlabeled parliamentary speech containing mixed Scandinavian languages prior to 100 hours of Faroese supervised fine-tuning. Evaluation is conducted on the official Ravnursson test split and the new FO-Parl-Eval-2h10m parliamentary benchmark, alongside comparisons with baseline Whisper and Omnilingual models.
method.id: Penelitian ini mengevaluasi dua *pipeline* adaptasi komplementer menggunakan arsitektur Wav2Vec 2.0 XLS-R. *Pipeline* A melakukan *supervised cross-lingual fine-tuning* pada bahasa bantu yang diikuti oleh *continued fine-tuning* khusus bahasa Faroese, menggunakan 100 jam data per tahap. *Pipeline* B memperkenalkan *continuous pre-training* *cross-lingual* pada 1.000 jam *unlabeled* *speech* parlementer yang mencakup campuran bahasa Skandinavia sebelum dilakukan *supervised fine-tuning* bahasa Faroese selama 100 jam. Evaluasi dilakukan pada *split* pengujian resmi Ravnursson dan *benchmark* parlementer baru FO-Parl-Eval-2h10m, disertai perbandingan dengan model *baseline* Whisper dan Omnilingual.

related_work.en: Prior research on multilingual ASR typically evaluates supervised fine-tuning or continuous self-supervised pre-training in isolation, usually reporting final error rates without distinguishing the inductive effects introduced at each stage. Consequently, studies often treat transfer as a single-stage optimization problem. Furthermore, auxiliary language selection is frequently guided by intuition rather than principled criteria, and modern large-scale multilingual models like Whisper and Omnilingual offer limited insight into how specific languages interact during training.
related_work.id: Penelitian terdahulu mengenai *multilingual* ASR umumnya mengevaluasi *supervised fine-tuning* atau *continuous self-supervised pre-training* secara terpisah, biasanya melaporkan *error rate* akhir tanpa membedakan efek induktif yang diperkenalkan pada setiap tahap. Akibatnya, penelitian sering kali memperlakukan transfer sebagai masalah optimasi satu tahap saja. Selain itu, pemilihan bahasa bantu kerap kali dipandu oleh intuisi daripada kriteria yang sistematis, dan *multilingual model* berskala besar modern seperti Whisper serta Omnilingual memberikan wawasan yang terbatas tentang bagaimana bahasa tertentu berinteraksi selama pelatihan.

results.en: Results demonstrate that cross-lingual transfer is stage-dependent. Pipeline A effectively consolidates phonetic constraints and excels on clean in-domain speech, whereas Pipeline B substantially improves robustness to acoustic variability and yields lower error rates on parliamentary speech, achieving a Word Error Rate of 26.46 percent and Character Error Rate of 10.68 percent for the monolingual baseline and competitive scores across auxiliary configurations. Furthermore, the optimal auxiliary language depends heavily on the training strategy, with single-language variants like Icelandic, Danish, and Norwegian outperforming balanced mixtures in Pipeline B.
results.id: Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa transfer *cross-lingual* bersifat *stage-dependent*. *Pipeline* A secara efektif mengonsolidasikan batasan fonetik dan unggul pada *speech* dalam *domain* yang bersih, sedangkan *Pipeline* B secara substansial meningkatkan ketahanan terhadap variabilitas akustik serta menghasilkan *error rate* yang lebih rendah pada *speech* parlementer, mencapai *Word Error Rate* sebesar 26,46 persen dan *Character Error Rate* sebesar 10,68 persen untuk *baseline* monolingual serta skor kompetitif di berbagai konfigurasi bantu. Selain itu, bahasa bantu yang optimal sangat bergantung pada strategi pelatihan, di mana varian satu bahasa seperti Islandia, Denmark, dan Norwegia mengungguli campuran seimbang pada *Pipeline* B.

tldr.en: This paper investigates stage-aware cross-lingual transfer for Faroese automatic speech recognition using auxiliary Scandinavian languages. The findings demonstrate that transfer effectiveness fundamentally depends on whether cross-lingual information is introduced during pre-training or fine-tuning.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyelidiki transfer *cross-lingual* yang *stage-aware* untuk *automatic speech recognition* bahasa Faroese menggunakan bahasa bantu Skandinavia. Temuannya menunjukkan bahwa efektivitas transfer sangat bergantung pada apakah informasi *cross-lingual* dimasukkan saat *pre-training* atau *fine-tuning*.

acl:2026.speakable-1.17.title: Stage-Aware Cross-Lingual Transfer for Faroese ASR: When and Which Languages Matter
acl:2026.speakable-1.17.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.18.abstract: In recent years, there has been an upsurge in research on automatic speech recognition (ASR) for low-resource languages. Particularly, transfer learning using multi-lingual models has become a popular remedy for the lack of available datasets for target languages. However, given the complexities associated with each individual language, we argue it is unlikely that a single multi-lingual pre-training model will provide equal performance gains across all languages. We also recognise the important, and insufficiently studied influence that the specific pre-training dataset has on the performance of the model. In this paper, using the Irish language as a case study, we propose a more directed, incremental form of pre-training which we term multi-step fine-tuning. This method accounts for the complex relationships between the language and dataset features of the source pre-training and target datasets. We show multi-step fine-tuning improves performance over simple multi-lingual fine-tuning alone, and we investigate factors leading to certain pre-trained models achieving better results through linguistic and dataset similarity measures. This research also investigates the uniformity of the performance gains across different demographics. We show that the optimal pre-training strategy can differ between demographics suggesting that more careful pre-training dataset selection is necessary to ensure equitable outcomes in practice.
acl:2026.speakable-1.18.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.speakable-1.18.title: Doing More with Less: Determining Optimal Pre-training Model for Irish Automatic Speech Recognition through Multi-step Fine-tuning
acl:2026.speakable-1.18.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.19.abstract: We present a blank-aware decoding approach for transcript-free phoneme alignment with CTC-based speech foundation models, designed to improve annotation bootstrapping in low-resource languages. While CTC models provide frame-level phoneme posteriors without requiring transcripts, greedy decoding produces blank-dominated and temporally unstable segmentations that are difficult to correct manually. Our approach introduces two training-free blank-resolution strategies operating directly on CTC logits: (i) confidence-ratio substitution, which promotes competitive non-blank hypotheses relative to the blank symbol, and (ii) recursive context adjustment, which enforces local contextual consistency within blank spans. Experiments on English (TIMIT) and on Sardinian and Tyrolean dialect corpora show consistent improvements in boundary F1 prediction, phoneme duration regularity, and segmentation stability over greedy CTC decoding. Although absolute boundary deviations remain higher than transcript-conditioned aligners, the resulting alignments are structurally coherent and suitable for manual correction. A post-hoc phoneme-class analysis further reveals systematic asymmetries in blank resolution, highlighting complementary roles of local acoustic evidence and contextual cues, and outlining prominising venues for future improvements.
acl:2026.speakable-1.19.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

glossary.explanation_id: Sebuah fungsi *loss* dan kerangka kerja *decoding* dalam jaringan saraf tiruan yang memungkinkan pengenalan sekuens tanpa memerlukan *alignment* eksplisit tingkat *frame*.
Nilai mentah yang belum dinormalisasi yang dihasilkan oleh lapisan terakhir dari model sebelum fungsi aktivasi seperti *softmax* diterapkan.
Distribusi probabilitas dari label target yang dihitung oleh model setelah mempertimbangkan bukti akustik dari data input.
Proses pencocokan dan penentuan batas temporal dari fonem-fonem di dalam sinyal audio ucapan.
Strategi pencarian *decoding* yang selalu memilih token dengan probabilitas tertinggi pada setiap langkah waktu tanpa mempertimbangkan konteks global.
Proses menggunakan model otomatis untuk menghasilkan anotasi awal guna mempercepat pembuatan korpus data beranotasi.
Kelas fonem konsonan yang dihasilkan dengan obstruksi aliran udara di saluran vokal, seperti bunyi *stop* dan *fricative*.
Metrik yang dihitung sebagai rasio antara waktu koreksi manual manusia terhadap durasi audio yang diproses.

background.en: Developing speech corpora for low-resource and under-documented languages is difficult because manual phonetic annotation is labor-intensive, requires trained phoneticians, and many varieties lack standardized orthography. While Connectionist Temporal Classification speech foundation models provide frame-level phoneme posteriors without needing transcripts, greedy decoding yields unstable and fragmented boundaries due to the pervasive dominance of the blank symbol. Transcript-free alignment represents an appealing alternative for bootstrapping annotation when transcripts are unavailable, unreliable, or costly.
background.id: Pengembangan korpus ucapan untuk bahasa *low-resource* dan minim dokumentasi sulit dilakukan karena anotasi fonetik manual membutuhkan banyak tenaga, memerlukan ahli fonetik terlatih, dan banyak varietas bahasa yang tidak memiliki ortografi standar. Meskipun model dasar ucapan *Connectionist Temporal Classification* menyediakan *posterior* fonem tingkat *frame* tanpa memerlukan transkrip, *greedy decoding* menghasilkan batas yang tidak stabil dan terfragmentasi karena dominasi simbol kosong (*blank symbol*) yang merata. *Transcript-free alignment* merupakan alternatif menarik untuk melakukan *bootstrapping* anotasi ketika transkrip tidak tersedia, tidak dapat diandalkan, atau mahal.

contributions.en: The paper introduces two training-free blank-resolution strategies operating directly on Connectionist Temporal Classification logits: confidence-ratio substitution, which promotes competitive non-blank hypotheses relative to the blank symbol, and recursive context adjustment, which enforces local contextual consistency within blank spans. Furthermore, it evaluates these strategies across multiple datasets including English, Sardinian, and Tyrolean dialects, providing a comprehensive post-hoc analysis of phoneme-class asymmetries and human correction time.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan dua strategi resolusi kosong tanpa *training* yang beroperasi langsung pada *logit* *Connectionist Temporal Classification*: *confidence-ratio substitution*, yang mempromosikan hipotesis non-kosong yang kompetitif relatif terhadap simbol kosong, dan *recursive context adjustment*, yang menegakkan konsistensi kontekstual lokal dalam rentang kosong. Selain itu, penelitian ini mengevaluasi strategi-strategi tersebut di berbagai *dataset* termasuk dialek bahasa Inggris, Sardinia, dan Tirol, serta memberikan analisis *post-hoc* yang komprehensif mengenai asimetri kelas fonem dan waktu koreksi manusia.

future_work.en: The authors state that future work should assess generalization across different architectures, explore integrating adaptive blank resolution into semi-supervised or joint training pipelines for low-resource languages and dialects, and conduct larger-scale user studies to robustly quantify annotation time savings and inter-annotator variability.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyatakan bahwa penelitian mendatang harus menilai generalisasi di berbagai arsitektur, mengeksplorasi integrasi resolusi kosong adaptif ke dalam *pipeline* pelatihan *semi-supervised* atau *joint training* untuk bahasa dan dialek *low-resource*, serta melakukan studi pengguna skala besar secara lebih kuat untuk mengkuantifikasi penghematan waktu anotasi dan variabilitas antar-anotator.

method.en: The approach utilizes the wav2vec2-xlsr-53-espeak-cv-ft model to extract frame-level posterior distributions at twenty millisecond resolution from raw audio without supervision during feature extraction. Two main strategies are introduced without retraining: confidence-ratio substitution, using a ratio threshold to replace blanks when a candidate is sufficiently competitive, and recursive context adjustment, which builds proto-segments, defines neighborhood sets within a local window, and iteratively applies a blank resolution rule based on context consistency. Evaluation employs three datasets, namely TIMIT, Sardinian, and Tyrolean, using average boundary deviation, phoneme duration error, and boundary F1 score.
method.id: Pendekatan ini menggunakan model *wav2vec2-xlsr-53-espeak-cv-ft* untuk mengekstrak distribusi *posterior* tingkat *frame* pada resolusi 20 milidetik dari audio mentah tanpa pengawasan selama ekstraksi fitur. Dua strategi utama diperkenalkan tanpa *training* ulang: *confidence-ratio substitution*, yang menggunakan *ambang batas* rasio untuk mengganti simbol kosong ketika kandidat cukup kompetitif, dan *recursive context adjustment*, yang membangun *proto-segment*, mendefinisikan *neighborhood set* dalam *window* lokal, dan menerapkan aturan resolusi kosong secara iteratif berdasarkan konsistensi konteks. Evaluasi menggunakan tiga *dataset* yaitu TIMIT, Sardinia, dan Tirol, dengan menggunakan *average boundary deviation*, *phoneme duration error*, dan *boundary F1 score*.

related_work.en: Classical forced alignment relies on Hidden Markov Model pipelines such as HTK, MAUS, and the Montreal Forced Aligner, which achieve high accuracy with accurate transcripts but fail in low-resource settings. Neural approaches utilize Connectionist Temporal Classification models and Torchaudio alignments conditioned on transcripts, whereas zero-resource learning targets unsupervised phoneme segmentation through clustering, self-supervised representations, and predictive coding without offering phoneme-level temporal precision. Although ASR decoding heuristics such as confidence thresholding, top-k rescoring, and blank suppression exist for recognition, they have not been systematically studied for transcript-free alignment.
related_work.id: *Forced alignment* klasik mengandalkan *pipeline* *Hidden Markov Model* seperti HTK, MAUS, dan *Montreal Forced Aligner*, yang mencapai akurasi tinggi dengan transkrip akurat tetapi gagal pada pengaturan *low-resource*. Pendekatan neural menggunakan model *Connectionist Temporal Classification* dan *alignment* *Torchaudio* yang dikondisikan pada transkrip, sedangkan pembelajaran *zero-resource* menargetkan *phoneme segmentation* nirawas (*unsupervised*) melalui *clustering*, *self-supervised representations*, dan *predictive coding* tanpa menawarkan presisi temporal tingkat fonem. Meskipun heuristik *decoding* ASR seperti *confidence thresholding*, *top-k rescoring*, dan *blank suppression* ada untuk pengenalan, mereka belum dipelajari secara sistematis untuk *transcript-free alignment*.

results.en: Experiments on TIMIT, Sardinian, and Tyrolean corpora show consistent improvements in boundary F1 prediction, phoneme duration regularity, and segmentation stability over greedy Connectionist Temporal Classification decoding. Recursive context adjustment substantially improves duration regularity and boundary F1, reducing phoneme duration error on TIMIT from 63 to 55 milliseconds while increasing average boundary deviation. Post-hoc analysis reveals that vowels benefit strongly from context-driven blank resolution, whereas obstruents remain locally anchored, and human correction analysis indicates a real-time factor of approximately 40 for spontaneous Tyrolean monologues.
results.id: Percobaan pada korpus TIMIT, Sardinia, dan Tirol menunjukkan peningkatan yang konsisten dalam prediksi *boundary F1*, keteraturan durasi fonem, dan stabilitas *segmentation* dibandingkan *greedy* *Connectionist Temporal Classification* *decoding*. *Recursive context adjustment* secara substansial meningkatkan keteraturan durasi dan *boundary F1*, mengurangi *phoneme duration error* pada TIMIT dari 63 menjadi 55 milidetik sekaligus meningkatkan *average boundary deviation*. Analisis *post-hoc* mengungkapkan bahwa vokal sangat diuntungkan oleh resolusi kosong berbasis konteks, sedangkan *obstruent* tetap berakar secara lokal, dan analisis koreksi manusia menunjukkan *real-time factor* sekitar 40 untuk monolog spontan bahasa Tirol.

tldr.en: We present a blank-aware decoding approach for transcript-free phoneme alignment using Connectionist Temporal Classification models to improve annotation bootstrapping in low-resource languages. Experiments on English, Sardinian, and Tyrolean corpora show that our training-free strategies significantly improve segmentation stability and phoneme duration regularity over greedy decoding.
tldr.id: Kami menyajikan pendekatan *decoding* yang sadar-kosong untuk *phoneme alignment* tanpa transkrip menggunakan model *Connectionist Temporal Classification* guna meningkatkan *annotation bootstrapping* pada bahasa *low-resource*. Percobaan pada korpus bahasa Inggris, Sardinia, dan Tirol menunjukkan bahwa strategi tanpa *training* kami secara signifikan meningkatkan stabilitas *segmentation* dan keteraturan durasi fonem dibandingkan *greedy decoding*.

acl:2026.speakable-1.19.title: Blank-Aware Decoding for Transcript-Free Phoneme Alignment in Low-Resource Languages and Dialects
acl:2026.speakable-1.19.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.starsem-conference.16.abstract: Social biases based on regional identity (or regional bias) are often observed in Indian contexts on major online social networks and require critical attention. However, due to large linguistic and cultural diversity, high annotation costs, and inherent human biases, very little annotated data exists on regional biases in the Indian context. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have garnered attention for the automatic annotation of text. However, such annotation efforts are largely limited to English texts, and LLMs often perform poorly when applied to low-resource languages. Therefore, this paper focuses on understanding the capabilities and challenges of popular open-source LLMs in annotating Indian regional biases. We utilize the recently proposed IndRegBias dataset, which consists of Indian regionally biased social media comments in both English and code-mixed formats. First, we assess the annotation capabilities of LLMs in a zero-shot setting and critically analyze their performance across different writing styles, including code-mixing, transliteration, and English. We find that the majority of LLMs exhibit low agreement with human annotations (measured using Cohen’s kappa). Consequently, we extend our study by fine-tuning the models using 50% of the data and evaluating them on the remaining 50%. We observe a significant improvement in annotation agreement (kappa) for all the LLMs. To further assess the capabilities of the fine-tuned models, we evaluate them on 500 newly collected social media comments discussing regional issues in India. The results show that most fine-tuned LLMs outperform their zero-shot counterparts when annotating these new comments.
acl:2026.starsem-conference.16.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)
acl:2026.starsem-conference.16.title: Annotating Indian Regional Biases using Large Language Models: Evaluation and Analysis
acl:2026.starsem-conference.16.venue: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)

acl:2026.starsem-conference.17.abstract: Text detoxification, the automated detection and mitigation of abusive and harmful content, is essential for ensuring the safety of online communities and protecting users. However, low resource languages such as Tatar have received little research attention. In this paper we present Tatoxa, a novel state-of-the-art system for text detoxification in the Tatar language. Comparative experiments show that the proposed approach outperforms existing open source and proprietary commercial LLMs on key quality metrics. We also introduce a new dataset for text detoxification in Tatar, designed for fine tuning and evaluation in low resource settings. Finally, cross lingual transfer experiments indicate that transfer from other languages, including the culturally close Russian, performs significantly worse than training on native Tatar data even when a large Russian corpus is available.
acl:2026.starsem-conference.17.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)
acl:2026.starsem-conference.17.title: The Tatoxa System for Text Detoxification in Low-Resource Languages: The Case of Tatar
acl:2026.starsem-conference.17.venue: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)

acl:2026.starsem-conference.24.abstract: A large body of research has examined the linguistic abilities of language models (LMs) across various languages. However, conclusive evidence regarding their semantic competence and world knowledge remains limited, especially for low-resource languages. In this study, we explore the semantic competence of Italian BabyLMs, focusing on their sensitivity to semantic violations. To this end, we adapt a minimal pair benchmark targeting semantic violations to evaluate the semantic abilities of BAMBI, a family of small-scale models trained on progressively larger and more complex datasets. We further compare their performance, assessed through accuracy, mean log-likelihood offset, and expected calibration error, with that of three larger Italian LMs. Our findings shed light on this aspect of semantic competence in small-scale models and how this is affected by data scale and training strategies.
acl:2026.starsem-conference.24.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)
acl:2026.starsem-conference.24.title: Can a Remedy Find a Researcher? Exploring the Development of Semantic Knowledge in Italian BabyLMs
acl:2026.starsem-conference.24.venue: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)

acl:2026.stereacult-1.6.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perpetuate cultural stereotypes not only through biased associations but through systematic omission and orthographic erasure of underrepresented languages. We present empirical evidence of two compounding failure modes affecting Northeast Indian languages: (1) entity-level invisibility, where state-of-the-art NER systems score F1=0.000 on culturally critical named entities such as Khasi surnames, Garo festivals, and tribal names; and (2) orthographic corruption, where LLM tokenizers corrupt semantically meaningful diacritics (ï, ñ) and the Garo morpheme boundary marker (U+00B7) at rates of 18.8–50% across four of five evaluated models. Drawing on NortheastNER (F1=0.964, six entity categories, XLM-RoBERTa-base) and a systematic tokenization study across Khasi and Garo, we argue that stereotype-by-omission constitutes a distinct and measurable harm to indigenous language communities. We further show that a custom multilingual tokenizer achieves 26–50% token reduction over five baseline LLMs, demonstrating that culturally grounded infrastructure can partially remediate these failures. Our findings call for cultural representation audits as a standard component of multilingual NLP evaluation.
acl:2026.stereacult-1.6.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Stereotypes Across Cultures in Language Technologies (StereACuLT 2026)
acl:2026.stereacult-1.6.title: Stereotyped by Silence: How LLMs Erase Northeast Indian Languages Through Omission and Orthographic Corruption
acl:2026.stereacult-1.6.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Stereotypes Across Cultures in Language Technologies (StereACuLT 2026)

acl:2026.tacl-1.10.abstract: We introduce MultiBLiMP 1.0, a massively multilingual benchmark of linguistic minimal pairs, covering 101 languages and 2 types of subject-verb agreement, containing more than 128,000 minimal pairs. Our minimal pairs are created using a fully automated pipeline, leveraging the large-scale linguistic resources of Universal Dependencies and UniMorph. MultiBLiMP 1.0 evaluates abilities of LLMs at an unprecedented multilingual scale, and highlights the shortcomings of the current state-of-the-art in modelling low-resource languages.1
acl:2026.tacl-1.10.journal_ref: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 14

glossary.explanation_id: Pasangan kalimat yang hampir identik yang hanya berbeda dalam satu aspek spesifik untuk menguji pelanggaran gramatikal.
Sebuah koleksi *treebank* multibahasa yang menyediakan anotasi sintaksis dan morfologis yang seragam.
Koleksi multibahasa dari anotasi fitur morfologis yang mendefinisikan fitur tingkat kata untuk berbagai bahasa.
Sebuah ukuran seberapa baik model probabilitas memprediksi sampel data.
Analisis struktur gramatikal kalimat yang merepresentasikan hubungan antarkata dalam bentuk dependensi.
Tahap pelatihan lanjutan pada *large language model* setelah tahap *pre-training* dasar selesai.

background.en: Large language models are often trained on multilingual corpora and evaluated extensively on functional linguistic competence through tasks requiring world knowledge and understanding. However, little work has assessed their formal linguistic competence, which refers to the knowledge of rules and statistical regularities of a language. Existing targeted syntactic evaluation benchmarks structured as minimal pairs are largely limited to English and a few high-resource languages.
background.id: *Large language model* sering dilatih pada korpus multibahasa dan dievaluasi secara ekstensif pada kompetensi linguistik fungsional melalui tugas-tugas yang memerlukan pengetahuan dan pemahaman dunia. Namun, sedikit pekerjaan yang menilai kompetensi linguistik formal mereka, yang mengacu pada pengetahuan tentang aturan dan keteraturan statistik dari suatu bahasa. *Benchmark* evaluasi sintaksis terarah yang ada dan terstruktur sebagai *minimal pair* sebagian besar terbatas pada bahasa Inggris dan beberapa bahasa *high-resource*.

contributions.en: The paper introduces MultiBLiMP 1.0, a massively multilingual benchmark containing more than 128,000 minimal pairs across 101 languages. The authors propose a fully automated pipeline leveraging Universal Dependencies and UniMorph to extract candidates, validate agreement conditions using collocation statistics, and perform inflection and dataset balancing. Additionally, they provide a comprehensive evaluation of 42 large language models.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan MultiBLiMP 1.0, sebuah *benchmark* multibahasa massal yang berisi lebih dari 128.000 *minimal pair* di 101 bahasa. Para penulis mengusulkan *pipeline* otomatis yang memanfaatkan Universal Dependencies dan UniMorph untuk mengekstrak kandidat, memvalidasi kondisi persetujuan menggunakan statistik kolokasi, serta melakukan infleksi dan penyeimbangan data. Selain itu, mereka menyajikan evaluasi komprehensif terhadap 42 *large language model*.

future_work.en: The authors state limitations regarding the reliance on the size, diversity, and annotation quality of Universal Dependencies and UniMorph, as well as the challenge of extending the procedure to more complex phenomena. Future work includes expanding MultiBLiMP to more constructions beyond subject-verb agreement and enabling quantitative typological studies.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyatakan keterbatasan terkait ketergantungan pada ukuran, keragaman, dan kualitas anotasi dari Universal Dependencies dan UniMorph, serta tantangan dalam memperluas prosedur ke fenomena yang lebih kompleks. Pekerjaan masa depan mencakup memperluas MultiBLiMP ke lebih banyak konstruksi di luar persetujuan subjek-verba dan memungkinkan studi tipologis kuantitatif.
