results.en: The review provides an overview of the latest trends and challenges in authorship analysis, focusing on two key sub-tasks: authorship attribution and authorship verification. It identifies critical areas such as low-resource language processing and AI-generated text detection to support the development of more reliable and accurate systems.
results.id: Ulasan ini memberikan gambaran umum mengenai tren dan tantangan terkini dalam analisis kepengarangan, dengan fokus pada dua sub-tugas utama: *authorship attribution* dan *authorship verification*. Studi ini mengidentifikasi area kritis seperti pemrosesan bahasa *low-resource* dan deteksi teks buatan AI untuk mendukung pengembangan sistem yang lebih andal dan akurat.

tldr.en: This paper presents a systematic literature review on authorship attribution and verification from 2015 to 2024. The study highlights state-of-the-art methodologies, key research gaps, and emerging challenges across machine learning, deep learning, and large language models.

Studi ini menyoroti metodologi *state-of-the-art*, kesenjangan penelitian utama, dan tantangan yang muncul di berbagai *machine learning*, *deep learning*, dan *large language model*.

doi:10.1007/s40747-026-02498-8.abstract: Due to the scarcity of part-of-speech (POS) annotated data for low-resource languages, existing studies have predominantly relied on unsupervised methods. Among these methods, annotation projection transfers POS tags from a high-resource source language to a low-resource target language through word alignments derived from parallel corpora, making it particularly suitable for low-resource scenarios. However, its effectiveness depends heavily on the availability of parallel corpora, which remain scarce or entirely unavailable for many low-resource languages. To address this limitation, we propose a fully unsupervised cross-lingual POS tagging framework that relies solely on monolingual corpora and leverages an unsupervised neural machine translation (UNMT) system. Specifically, the UNMT system translates sentences from a high-resource language into a low-resource language to construct pseudo-parallel sentence pairs. A target language POS tagger is then trained based on the standard annotation projection procedure. Moreover, we introduce a multi-source projection technique to calibrate the POS tags projected on the target side, thereby improving the quality of the annotations used to train the target language POS tagger. We evaluate the proposed framework on 28 language pairs, covering four source languages (English, German, Spanish and French) and seven target languages (Afrikaans, Basque, Finnish, Indonesian, Lithuanian, Portuguese and Turkish). Experimental results show that our method achieves performance comparable to that of a baseline cross-lingual POS tagger trained on genuine parallel sentence pairs and even outperforms it for several target languages. Furthermore, the proposed multi-source projection technique further improves tagging performance, yielding an average gain of 1.3% over previous methods.

background.en: The scarcity of part-of-speech annotated data for low-resource languages has driven researchers to rely on unsupervised methods. While annotation projection effectively transfers part-of-speech tags using parallel corpora, these parallel corpora are often scarce or unavailable for many low-resource languages, creating a significant bottleneck.
background.id: Kelangkaan data beranotasi *part-of-speech* untuk bahasa *low-resource* telah mendorong para peneliti untuk mengandalkan metode tanpa supervisi. Meskipun *annotation projection* secara efektif mentransfer *tag* *part-of-speech* menggunakan korpus paralel, korpus paralel tersebut sering kali langka atau tidak tersedia untuk banyak bahasa *low-resource*, sehingga menciptakan hambatan yang signifikan.

contributions.en: The paper introduces a fully unsupervised cross-lingual part-of-speech tagging framework that relies solely on monolingual corpora and leverages an unsupervised neural machine translation system to construct pseudo-parallel sentence pairs. Additionally, it introduces a multi-source projection technique to calibrate projected tags and improve annotation quality.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan sebuah *framework* *part-of-speech* *tagging* lintas bahasa yang sepenuhnya tanpa supervisi dan hanya mengandalkan korpus monolingual serta memanfaatkan sistem *unsupervised* *neural* *machine* *translation* untuk membangun pasangan kalimat *pseudo-parallel*. Selain itu, makalah ini memperkenalkan teknik *multi-source projection* untuk mengkalibrasi *tag* yang diproyeksikan dan meningkatkan kualitas anotasi.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss limitations or future work in detail.

method.en: The method uses an unsupervised neural machine translation system to translate sentences from a high-resource language into a low-resource language, creating pseudo-parallel sentence pairs. A target language part-of-speech tagger is then trained using the standard annotation projection procedure, combined with a multi-source projection technique to calibrate the projected tags.
method.id: Metode ini menggunakan sistem *unsupervised* *neural* *machine* *translation* untuk menerjemahkan kalimat dari bahasa *high-resource* ke dalam bahasa *low-resource*, guna membuat pasangan kalimat *pseudo-parallel*. Sebuah *tagger* *part-of-speech* bahasa target kemudian dilatih menggunakan prosedur *annotation projection* standar, yang dikombinasikan dengan teknik *multi-source projection* untuk mengkalibrasi *tag* yang diproyeksikan.

related_work.en: Existing studies have predominantly relied on unsupervised methods such as annotation projection, which transfers tags from a high-resource source language to a low-resource target language through word alignments derived from parallel corpora. However, the limitation of this approach is that its effectiveness depends heavily on the availability of parallel corpora.
related_work.id: Studi-studi yang ada sebagian besar telah mengandalkan metode tanpa supervisi seperti *annotation projection*, yang mentransfer *tag* dari bahasa sumber *high-resource* ke bahasa target *low-resource* melalui *word alignment* yang diturunkan dari korpus paralel. Namun, keterbatasan dari pendekatan ini adalah efektivitasnya sangat bergantung pada ketersediaan korpus paralel.

results.en: Evaluated on 28 language pairs across four source languages and seven target languages, the method achieves performance comparable to a baseline trained on genuine parallel sentence pairs, and even outperforms it for several target languages. Furthermore, the multi-source projection technique yields an average gain of 1.3 percent over previous methods.
results.id: Dievaluasi pada 28 pasangan bahasa yang mencakup empat bahasa sumber dan tujuh bahasa target, metode ini mencapai performa yang sebanding dengan *baseline* yang dilatih pada pasangan kalimat paralel asli, bahkan mengunggulinya untuk beberapa bahasa target. Lebih lanjut, teknik *multi-source projection* menghasilkan peningkatan rata-rata sebesar 1,3 persen dibandingkan metode-metode sebelumnya.

tldr.en: This paper proposes a fully unsupervised cross-lingual part-of-speech tagging framework that relies solely on monolingual corpora and an unsupervised neural machine translation system. Results show that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to or better than a baseline trained on genuine parallel sentence pairs.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan sebuah *framework* *part-of-speech* *tagging* lintas bahasa yang sepenuhnya tanpa supervisi dan hanya mengandalkan korpus monolingual serta sistem *unsupervised* *neural* *machine* *translation*. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa metode yang diusulkan mencapai performa yang sebanding atau lebih baik daripada *baseline* yang dilatih menggunakan pasangan kalimat paralel asli.

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-01881-1.abstract: Abstract Emotion classification on social media provides valuable insights into public sentiment, but the performance of existing models is often limited by corpus size and linguistic variability. This research presents a transfer learning approach to analyze the benchmark EmoT corpus of 4401 emotion-labeled Indonesian Tweets, combined with a task-specific data augmentation strategy to enhance model generalization. Statistical analysis is performed using a linear mixed model of 10-fold cross validation folds, with folds modeled as a random intercept to control for within-fold variation. Results reveal that both Model and Augmentation Strategy have a significant effect on Accuracy, Macro F1, and Weighted F1 metrics. The top-performing model-strategy combination is IndoRoBERTa with augmentation via one-phase back translation, achieving a Weighted F1 score of approximately 0.859. These results highlight the effectiveness of integrating transfer learning with textual data augmentation for emotion classification in low-resource languages and suggest promising directions for future research in natural language processing.

glossary.explanation_id: Transfer learning adalah teknik di mana *model* yang telah dilatih pada suatu tugas digunakan kembali sebagai titik awal untuk tugas baru.
Back translation adalah teknik augmentasi data dengan menerjemahkan teks ke bahasa lain lalu menerjemahkannya kembali ke bahasa asli.
Cross-validation adalah teknik evaluasi untuk menguji seberapa baik *model* *machine learning* digeneralisasi ke *data* independen.

background.en: Emotion classification on social media offers valuable insights into public sentiment, yet the performance of existing models remains constrained by limited corpus size and high linguistic variability. Addressing this gap is crucial for improving natural language processing systems in low-resource settings.
background.id: Klasifikasi emosi pada media sosial menawarkan wawasan berharga mengenai sentimen publik, namun kinerja model yang ada masih terkendala oleh ukuran korpus yang terbatas dan variabilitas linguistik yang tinggi. Mengatasi kesenjangan ini sangat penting untuk meningkatkan sistem pemrosesan bahasa alami dalam pengaturan *low-resource*.

contributions.en: This research presents a transfer learning approach combined with a task-specific data augmentation strategy to enhance model generalization for emotion classification. It also provides a rigorous statistical analysis using a linear mixed model over cross-validation folds.

It integrates transfer learning with a task-specific data augmentation strategy, specifically one-phase back translation, and performs statistical analysis using a linear mixed model of 10-fold cross validation folds with random intercepts.

results.en: Statistical analysis reveals that both model choice and augmentation strategy have a significant effect on accuracy, macro F1, and weighted F1 metrics. The top-performing combination is IndoRoBERTa with one-phase back translation, achieving a weighted F1 score of approximately 0.859.
results.id: Analisis statistik menunjukkan bahwa pilihan model dan strategi augmentasi memiliki efek signifikan pada metrik *accuracy*, *macro F1*, dan *weighted F1*. Kombinasi dengan kinerja terbaik adalah IndoRoBERTa dengan *one-phase back translation*, yang mencapai skor *weighted F1* sekitar 0,859.

tldr.en: This paper proposes a transfer learning and data augmentation approach for emotion classification on Indonesian tweets. The results show that combining IndoRoBERTa with back translation achieves a high weighted F1 score.

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-01924-7.abstract: Text-to-Speech synthesis has evolved from rule-based and concatenative systems to highly natural neural architectures. This review surveys the historical development of TTS, core system components, representative model families, benchmark datasets, and evaluation protocols. We summarize major advances in end-to-end neural TTS, non-autoregressive generation, neural vocoders, multilingual and expressive synthesis, and zero-shot voice cloning. We additionally discuss persistent challenges related to prosody control, low-resource languages, real-time inference, and ethical risks. Finally, we outline promising research directions in diffusion-based generation and speech-language foundation models for controllable and robust TTS.

background.en: Text-to-speech synthesis has evolved from rule-based and concatenative systems to highly natural neural architectures. Understanding this evolution is crucial for identifying remaining challenges in prosody control, low-resource languages, real-time inference, and ethical risks.

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02243-7.abstract: Deploying trustworthy AI requires more than predictive accuracy; it demands population-representative data, transparent explainability, and user-centered design. Despite rapid mobile penetration across Southeast Asia, existing AI-based health tools remain predominantly trained on non-representative datasets and function as opaque black-box systems, limiting clinical trust. This study addresses these gaps through a deployable Explainable AI (XAI) framework for dysglycemia screening in Indonesia. Features were extracted from the Indonesia Family Life Survey 5 (IFLS5), a nationally representative longitudinal survey ( $$\sim $$ 83% of the Indonesian population), using its measured HbA1c-based labels for dysglycemia screening. Feature selection employed a four-stage XAI-in-the-loop pipeline combining literature review, statistical filtering, domain expert consultation, and SHAP-based evaluation. Among models trained, XGBoost achieved the highest performance (ROC-AUC = 0.72), with SHAP used both for post-hoc interpretation and feature selection. SHAP analysis indicated clinical alignment, with age, BMI, and hypertension as dominant risk factors, including a non-linear risk increase after age 45. The model was deployed as an Android application combining visual SHAP explanations with LLM-generated narratives. A pilot evaluation (n = 12) returned a mean comprehension score of 4.31/5. The framework illustrates an approach for developing transparent, population-representative mHealth AI that is meaningful and accessible to its intended users.

background.en:
Deploying trustworthy artificial intelligence in healthcare requires more than high predictive accuracy. It demands population-representative data, transparent explainability, and user-centered design to ensure clinical trust.

Despite rapid mobile penetration across Southeast Asia, existing AI-based health tools often rely on non-representative datasets and function as opaque black-box systems. This study addresses these critical gaps by developing a deployable Explainable AI framework for dysglycemia screening tailored to the Indonesian population.
background.id:
Penerapan kecerdasan buatan yang tepercaya dalam layanan kesehatan membutuhkan lebih dari sekadar akurasi prediktif yang tinggi. Hal ini menuntut data yang representatif bagi populasi, *explainability* yang transparan, dan desain yang berpusat pada pengguna untuk memastikan kepercayaan klinis.

Meskipun penetrasi seluler di Asia Tenggara berkembang pesat, perangkat kesehatan berbasis kecerdasan buatan saat ini sering kali mengandalkan *dataset* yang tidak representatif dan berfungsi sebagai sistem kotak hitam yang buram. Studi ini mengatasi kesenjangan krusial tersebut dengan mengembangkan *framework* *Explainable AI* yang dapat diterapkan untuk penapisan disglikemia yang disesuaikan dengan populasi Indonesia.

contributions.en:
The study introduces a deployable Explainable AI framework for dysglycemia screening that integrates population-representative data from a nationally representative longitudinal survey covering approximately 83 percent of the Indonesian population.

Furthermore, the work contributes a four-stage XAI-in-the-loop feature selection pipeline, clinical validation through SHAP analysis, and an end-user mobile application combining visual explanations with LLM-generated narratives, evaluated via a pilot study.
contributions.id:
Studi ini memperkenalkan *framework* *Explainable AI* yang dapat diterapkan untuk penapisan disglikemia dengan mengintegrasikan data yang representatif secara nasional dari survei longitudinal yang mencakup sekitar 83 persen populasi Indonesia.

Selain itu, penelitian ini berkontribusi melalui *pipeline* seleksi fitur *XAI*-in-the-loop empat tahap, validasi klinis melalui analisis *SHAP*, serta aplikasi seluler bagi pengguna akhir yang menggabungkan penjelasan visual dengan narasi buatan *LLM*, yang dievaluasi melalui studi percontohan.

future_work.en: The paper does not explicitly discuss future work or limitations.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas *future work* atau keterbatasan secara eksplisit.

method.en:
Features were extracted from the Indonesia Family Life Survey 5, a nationally representative longitudinal survey utilizing measured HbA1c-based labels for dysglycemia screening. Feature selection was conducted using a four-stage Explainable AI in-the-loop pipeline that combined literature review, statistical filtering, domain expert consultation, and SHAP-based evaluation.

Several models were trained, with XGBoost achieving the highest performance. The best model was subsequently deployed as an Android application combining visual SHAP explanations with language model-generated narratives, followed by a pilot evaluation involving 12 participants.
method.id:
Fitur diekstrak dari Indonesia Family Life Survey 5, sebuah survei longitudinal yang representatif secara nasional dengan menggunakan label berbasis HbA1c untuk penapisan disglikemia. Seleksi fitur dilakukan menggunakan *pipeline* *Explainable AI* *in-the-loop* empat tahap yang menggabungkan tinjauan pustaka, penyaringan statistik, konsultasi pakar domain, dan evaluasi berbasis *SHAP*.

Beberapa model dilatih, di mana *XGBoost* mencapai performa tertinggi. Model terbaik tersebut kemudian diterapkan sebagai aplikasi Android yang menggabungkan penjelasan visual *SHAP* dengan narasi buatan model bahasa, diikuti oleh evaluasi percontohan yang melibatkan 12 partisipan.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas *related work* secara mendetail.

results.en:
Among the evaluated models, XGBoost achieved the highest predictive performance with an ROC-AUC of 0.72. SHAP analysis demonstrated strong clinical alignment, identifying age, body mass index, and hypertension as dominant risk factors, including a non-linear risk increase observed after age 45.

Additionally, a pilot evaluation involving 12 participants yielded a mean comprehension score of 4.31 out of 5, indicating that the visual explanations and language model narratives were well understood by the intended users.
results.id:
Di antara model yang dievaluasi, *XGBoost* mencapai performa prediktif tertinggi dengan nilai ROC-AUC sebesar 0,72. Analisis *SHAP* menunjukkan keselarasan klinis yang kuat, dengan mengidentifikasi usia, indeks massa tubuh, dan hipertensi sebagai faktor risiko dominan, termasuk peningkatan risiko non-linear yang teramati setelah usia 45 tahun.

Selain itu, evaluasi percontohan yang melibatkan 12 partisipan menghasilkan skor pemahaman rata-rata 4,31 dari 5, yang mengindikasikan bahwa penjelasan visual dan narasi model bahasa dipahami dengan baik oleh pengguna yang dituju.

tldr.en: This study introduces a population-representative explainable AI framework for dysglycemia screening in Indonesia using data from the Indonesia Family Life Survey 5. The deployed mobile application combines XGBoost predictions with SHAP explanations and language model narratives, achieving high clinical alignment and user comprehension.
tldr.id: Studi ini memperkenalkan *framework* *explainable AI* yang representatif bagi populasi untuk penapisan disglikemia di Indonesia menggunakan data dari Indonesia Family Life Survey 5. Aplikasi seluler yang diterapkan menggabungkan prediksi *XGBoost* dengan penjelasan *SHAP* dan narasi *large language model*, serta mencapai keselarasan klinis dan pemahaman pengguna yang tinggi.

doi:10.1007/s44196-026-01586-4.abstract: Analysis of communication across cultures is essential in global digital interactions, requiring models that capture linguistic and paralinguistic features across diverse cultures. However, existing studies lack privacy-preserving frameworks that can effectively model both linguistic and paralinguistic features across distributed and culturally diverse datasets, highlighting a critical research gap. Existing centralized approaches pose privacy risks and often fail to preserve cultural nuances in distributed communication data. This research presents a CAFL to integrate linguistic and paralinguistic features across multiple cultural groups while maintaining data decentralization. A culture-specific gradient aggregation strategy is introduced to reduce representation bias and improve performance in low-resource languages. Evaluation across 27 cultural groups shows 93.7% accuracy in communication pattern recognition and an 87.4% reduction in privacy risk compared to centralized methods. The model captures prosodic variations, conversational timing, and non-verbal cues often overlooked by conventional NLP techniques. The findings reveal new cross-cultural communication patterns and provide a scalable, privacy-aware solution for intercultural collaboration, global communication systems, and culturally adaptive AI.

doi:10.1007/s44354-026-00047-w.abstract: In particular, the rapid dissemination of fake news using social media platforms has posed a severe threat to social stability and information reliability in language groups that lack sufficient resources. In addition, it has become difficult to automatically identify fake news in the case of Bengali digital media because fake news is mostly distributed using multimodal data like memes, screenshots, posters, photos with texts, etc. The effectiveness of the existing fake news detection methods is somewhat hindered by their inability to provide explainability and their focus mainly on either textual or visual data. This study proposes a context-aware multimodal reasoning approach for explainable Bengali fake news detection. The proposed model incorporates EasyOCR for Bengali textual information extraction, ResNet-50 and ViT for supplementing visual feature learning, and Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct for multimodal semantic inference. The proposed approach can detect semantic contradictions and associations between textual assertions and image information through matching textual and visual data based on a context-sensitive fusion technique. This methodology generates interpretable explanations beyond the fake/real binary categorization to enhance user trust in automated outcomes. According to an experiment conducted using a multimodal Bengali fake news dataset, the proposed approach surpasses conventional CNN, transformer, and unimodal baselines on several performance metrics. Results indicate how context-based multimodal reasoning can improve the efficiency and robustness of the model, along with making it more interpretable. The proposed method serves as an encouraging route towards the identification of fake news in multiple low resource languages, as well as in combating misinformation in the Bengali digital ecosystem.

doi:10.1007/s44443-026-01019-4.abstract: Low-resource languages remain challenging for cross-lingual semantic alignment because of limited parallel corpora. In addition, conventional symmetric alignment may distort the semantic space of a high-resource language through noisy low-resource updates. To address this issue, we propose Monolingual Anchoring for Cross-Lingual Semantic Alignment (MACA), focusing on Uyghur as a low-resource case study. MACA follows an asymmetric paradigm that treats the high-resource language as a fixed semantic anchor and transfers its semantic structure to the Uyghur side. The method consists of three components: (1) Anchored Embedding Initialization for newly introduced Uyghur subwords, (2) Cross-Lingual Neighborhood Anchoring for structural alignment between Uyghur and the anchor language, and (3) Monolingual Structure Anchoring for improving the internal semantic organization of Uyghur representations. Experiments centered on Uyghur-Chinese show that MACA outperforms LaBSE, the strongest off-the-shelf multilingual baseline in our comparison, by 7.67 points on cross-lingual STS. In an exploratory Uyghur-English zero-shot setting, MACA also surpasses LaBSE by 2.45 points without using Uyghur-English training data. These results provide evidence for the effectiveness of MACA in the evaluated Uyghur setting and suggest that monolingual anchoring may be further explored for related low-resource languages, such as Kazakh, Kyrgyz, and Uzbek.

doi:10.1016/j.array.2026.101157.abstract: Depression is a debilitating global health crisis; while digital social platforms offer an avenue for early detection through user-generated text, leveraging these digital traces is essential for timely clinical intervention. However, current computational linguistics for mental health are overwhelmingly English-centric. Standard natural language processing (NLP) methodologies may fail when applied to morphologically-rich low-resource languages like Hebrew, where non-concatenative structures and dense root-patterns obscure semantic markers of psychological distress. To bridge this gap, we propose a tailored machine learning framework explicitly designed for morphologically rich languages. We rigorously evaluated 16 classical and ensemble models across more than 130,000 configurations, isolating the optimal interactions between character-level n-grams and specialized Hebrew emotion lexicons to maximize feature extraction. This methodology is empirically tested on a curated dataset from "Camoni," Israel’s largest dedicated digital health community, which provides a high-value, clinically adjacent environment free from the noise of generalist social media platforms. Our optimized Stacking ensemble framework achieved an 84.1% accuracy rate, significantly outperforming standard baselines as well as fine-tuned, state-of-the-art Transformer models like AlephBERT. The integration of 3-to-5 character n-grams proved vital in navigating Hebrew’s morphological sparsity, proving that computationally efficient, expert-engineered features can surpass deep learning in low-resource clinical domains. This study provides a generalizable validated blueprint for deploying mental health screening tools. We urge the clinical and computational integration of these NLP frameworks into digital health ecosystems to facilitate early, life-saving interventions across diverse and underrepresented linguistic landscapes.

doi:10.1016/j.bspc.2026.111501.abstract: Background and objective Three-dimensional statistical shape modeling provides a computational method to quantify anatomical variation from medical imaging. This study aimed to construct statistical shape models of adult Asian craniofacial structures using computed tomography data, with the goal of identifying sex-, ethnicity-, and age-related morphological differences and establishing population-specific reference models. Methods A total of 300 high-resolution retrospective CT scans from healthy adults representing Chinese (n = 95), Indian (n = 100), and Malay (n = 105) groups were analyzed. Anatomical segmentation, landmark-guided rigid alignment, and Directed Distance Field-based Internal Structure Modeling (DDF-ISM) were used to generate dense-correspondence meshes for the head surface and craniofacial skeleton (skull and mandible). Principal component analysis was applied to quantify dominant modes of variation, and group differences were evaluated with ANOVA/MANOVA and localized difference mapping. Results Sex showed the largest overall effect size, with the greatest separation observed along PC1 for both the head surface and skeleton. Ethnic background most strongly influenced the nasal bridge, forehead, temporal bone, and alveolar region, while age-related changes were concentrated in vertex height, forehead curvature, nasal projection, and dentoalveolar remodeling. Difference mapping enabled high-resolution visualization of these localized variations across external soft tissue and the underlying bone framework. Conclusions The proposed CT-based computational pipeline demonstrates the feasibility of integrating statistical shape models and statistical analysis to generate population-specific craniofacial references. These models hold potential applications in clinical assessment, surgical planning and simulation, and forensic identification. Distinct from previous surface-only, bone-only, or prediction-oriented studies, the framework characterizes matched external and skeletal morphology across sex, three ethnic groups, and age within the same adult CT sample.

glossary.explanation_id: *Computed tomography* adalah teknik pencitraan medis yang menggunakan sinar-X untuk menghasilkan gambar penampang melintang dari tubuh.
*Statistical shape model* adalah representasi matematika dari bentuk anatomi yang menangkap variasi statistik di dalam suatu populasi.
*Dense-correspondence mesh* adalah representasi jaring tiga dimensi di mana setiap titik terhubung secara konsisten di seluruh sampel yang berbeda.
*Principal component analysis* adalah teknik reduksi dimensi statistik yang mengidentifikasi sumbu variasi utama dalam data.
*Landmark* adalah titik referensi anatomis yang digunakan untuk menyelaraskan dan mengukur struktur biologis.

background.en: Three-dimensional statistical shape modeling provides a computational method to quantify anatomical variation from medical imaging. Constructing statistical shape models of adult Asian craniofacial structures using computed tomography data aims to identify sex-, ethnicity-, and age-related morphological differences and establish population-specific reference models. This addresses the need for comprehensive reference models that capture morphological variations across diverse groups.
background.id: *Statistical shape model* tiga dimensi menyediakan metode komputasi untuk mengukur variasi anatomis dari pencitraan medis. Pembangunan *statistical shape model* dari struktur kraniofasial dewasa Asia menggunakan data *computed tomography* bertujuan untuk mengidentifikasi perbedaan morfologi yang terkait dengan jenis kelamin, etnis, dan usia serta menetapkan model referensi spesifik populasi. Hal ini mengatasi kebutuhan akan model referensi komprehensif yang menangkap variasi morfologi di berbagai kelompok.

contributions.en: The main contribution is a CT-based computational pipeline that integrates statistical shape models and statistical analysis to generate population-specific craniofacial references. The novelty lies in simultaneously characterizing matched external and skeletal morphology across sex, three ethnic groups, and age within the same adult CT sample, distinguishing it from previous surface-only, bone-only, or prediction-oriented studies.
contributions.id: Kontribusi utama adalah *pipeline* komputasi berbasis *CT* yang mengintegrasikan *statistical shape model* dan analisis statistik untuk menghasilkan referensi kraniofasial spesifik populasi. Kebaruannya terletak pada karakterisasi serentak morfologi eksternal dan kerangka yang cocok di antara jenis kelamin, tiga kelompok etnis, dan usia dalam sampel *CT* dewasa yang sama, yang membedakannya dari penelitian sebelumnya yang hanya berfokus pada permukaan, tulang, atau prediksi.

future_work.en: The authors state that the proposed models hold potential applications in clinical assessment, surgical planning and simulation, and forensic identification, but do not discuss specific future work or limitations in detail.
future_work.id: Penulis menyatakan bahwa model yang diusulkan memiliki potensi aplikasi dalam penilaian klinis, perencanaan dan simulasi bedah, serta identifikasi forensik, tetapi tidak membahas pekerjaan masa depan atau keterbatasan tertentu secara rinci.

method.en: The study analyzed a total of 300 high-resolution retrospective computed tomography scans from healthy adults representing Chinese, Indian, and Malay groups. Anatomical segmentation, landmark-guided rigid alignment, and Directed Distance Field-based Internal Structure Modeling were used to generate dense-correspondence meshes for the head surface and craniofacial skeleton. Principal component analysis was applied to quantify dominant modes of variation, and group differences were evaluated using ANOVA, MANOVA, and localized difference mapping.
method.id: Penelitian ini menganalisis total 300 *scan* *computed tomography* retrospektif beresolusi tinggi dari orang dewasa sehat yang mewakili kelompok Tionghoa, India, dan Melayu. Segmentasi anatomis, *rigid alignment* yang dipandu oleh *landmark*, dan *Directed Distance Field-based Internal Structure Modeling* digunakan untuk menghasilkan *mesh* *dense-correspondence* untuk permukaan kepala dan kerangka kraniofasial. *Principal component analysis* diterapkan untuk mengukur mode variasi yang dominan, dan perbedaan kelompok dievaluasi menggunakan *ANOVA*, *MANOVA*, dan pemetaan perbedaan terlokalisasi.

related_work.en: Previous studies have been limited to surface-only, bone-only, or prediction-oriented investigations. This paper builds upon prior research while addressing their limitations by characterizing matched external and skeletal morphology across sex, three ethnic groups, and age within the same adult CT sample.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya terbatas pada investigasi berbasis permukaan saja, tulang saja, atau berorientasi prediksi. Makalah ini dibangun di atas penelitian sebelumnya sekaligus mengatasi keterbatasan mereka dengan mengkarakterisasi morfologi eksternal dan kerangka yang cocok di antara jenis kelamin, tiga kelompok etnis, dan usia dalam sampel *CT* dewasa yang sama.

results.en: Sex showed the largest overall effect size, with the greatest separation observed along the first principal component for both the head surface and skeleton. Ethnic background most strongly influenced the nasal bridge, forehead, temporal bone, and alveolar region, whereas age-related changes were concentrated in vertex height, forehead curvature, nasal projection, and dentoalveolar remodeling. Difference mapping enabled high-resolution visualization of these localized variations across external soft tissue and the underlying bone framework.
results.id: Jenis kelamin menunjukkan ukuran efek keseluruhan terbesar, dengan pemisahan terbesar diamati di sepanjang *principal component* pertama untuk permukaan kepala maupun kerangka. Latar belakang etnis paling kuat memengaruhi pangkal hidung, dahi, tulang temporal, dan wilayah alveolar, sedangkan perubahan terkait usia terkonsentrasi pada tinggi verteks, kelengkungan dahi, proyeksi hidung, dan *remodeling* dentoalveolar. Pemetaan perbedaan memungkinkan visualisasi resolusi tinggi dari variasi terlokalisasi ini di seluruh jaringan lunak eksternal dan kerangka tulang di bawahnya.

tldr.en: This paper presents a computational framework using computed tomography scans to construct three-dimensional statistical shape models for adult Chinese, Indian, and Malay craniofacial structures. The results reveal that sex has the largest overall effect size, while ethnicity and age significantly influence specific morphological regions.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan *framework* komputasi menggunakan *scan* *computed tomography* untuk membangun *statistical shape model* tiga dimensi untuk struktur kraniofasial dewasa suku Tionghoa, India, dan Melayu. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa jenis kelamin memiliki ukuran efek keseluruhan terbesar, sementara etnis dan usia secara signifikan memengaruhi wilayah morfologi tertentu.

doi:10.1016/j.bspc.2026.111501.title: A computational framework for 3D statistical shape modeling of adult Chinese, Indian, and Malay craniofacial structures from CT imaging

doi:10.1016/j.datak.2026.102638.abstract: Many less-resourced languages struggle with a lack of large, task-specific datasets that are required for solving relevant tasks with modern transformer-based large language models (LLMs). On the other hand, many linguistic resources, such as dictionaries, are rarely used in this context despite their large information contents. We show how LLMs can be used to extend existing language resources in less-resourced languages for two important tasks: word-sense disambiguation (WSD) and threshold-based novelty detection (ND), a task similar to word-sense induction (WSI). We approach the two tasks through the related but much more accessible word-in-context (WiC) task where, given a pair of sentences and a target word, a classification model is tasked with predicting whether the sense of a given word differs between sentences. We demonstrate that a well-trained model for this task can distinguish between different word senses and can be adapted to solve the WSD and ND tasks. The advantage of using the WiC task, instead of directly predicting senses, is that the WiC task does not need pre-constructed sense inventories with a sufficient number of examples for each sense, which are rarely available in less-resourced languages. We show that sentence pairs for the WiC task can be successfully generated from dictionary examples using LLMs. The resulting prediction models outperform existing models on WiC, WSD, and ND tasks. We demonstrate our methodology on the Slovene language, where a monolingual dictionary is available, but word-sense resources are tiny.

Tugas mengidentifikasi data atau makna baru yang belum pernah terlihat sebelumnya dalam pelatihan model.
Tugas mengevaluasi apakah sebuah kata target memiliki makna yang sama dalam dua kalimat yang berbeda.
Bahasa-bahasa yang memiliki ketersediaan data digital, korpus, dan sumber daya komputasi yang terbatas.

background.en: Many less-resourced languages struggle with a lack of large, task-specific datasets required for solving relevant problems using modern transformer-based large language models. Although linguistic resources like dictionaries contain rich information, they are rarely utilized to address this data scarcity gap.
background.id: Banyak *less-resourced languages* mengalami kendala kekurangan *dataset* besar khusus tugas yang diperlukan untuk menyelesaikan masalah relevan menggunakan *large language models* berbasis *transformer* modern. Meskipun sumber daya linguistik seperti kamus memuat informasi yang kaya, sumber daya tersebut jarang dimanfaatkan untuk mengatasi kesenjangan kelangkaan data ini.

contributions.en: The paper demonstrates how large language models can be used to extend existing language resources in less-resourced languages for word-sense disambiguation and threshold-based novelty detection. It also shows that sentence pairs for the word-in-context task can be successfully generated from dictionary examples using large language models, yielding prediction models that outperform existing baselines.
contributions.id: Makalah ini mendemonstrasikan bagaimana *large language models* dapat digunakan untuk memperluas sumber daya bahasa yang ada pada *less-resourced languages* untuk *word-sense disambiguation* dan *threshold-based novelty detection*. Makalah ini juga menunjukkan bahwa pasangan kalimat untuk tugas *word-in-context* dapat berhasil dihasilkan dari contoh kamus menggunakan *large language models*, menghasilkan model prediksi yang mengungguli *baseline* yang ada.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss limitations or future work in detail.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas keterbatasan atau *future work* secara mendetail.

method.en: The authors approach word-sense disambiguation and novelty detection through the more accessible word-in-context task, where a classification model predicts whether a target word shares the same sense across a pair of sentences. This avoids the need for pre-constructed sense inventories with numerous examples. Furthermore, sentence pairs for the word-in-context task are generated from dictionary examples using large language models.
method.id: Para penulis mendekati *word-sense disambiguation* dan *novelty detection* melalui tugas *word-in-context* yang lebih mudah diakses, di mana model klasifikasi memprediksi apakah sebuah kata target memiliki makna yang sama di dalam sepasang kalimat. Pendekatan ini menghindari kebutuhan akan *sense inventories* prabangun dengan banyak contoh. Lebih lanjut, pasangan kalimat untuk tugas *word-in-context* dihasilkan dari contoh kamus menggunakan *large language models*.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas *related work* secara mendetail.

results.en: The resulting prediction models outperform existing models on the word-in-context, word-sense disambiguation, and novelty detection tasks. The methodology is successfully demonstrated on the Slovene language, which features an available monolingual dictionary but extremely small word-sense resources.
results.id: Model prediksi yang dihasilkan mengungguli model-model yang ada pada tugas *word-in-context*, *word-sense disambiguation*, dan *novelty detection*. Metodologi ini berhasil didemonstrasikan pada bahasa Slovene, yang memiliki kamus ekabahasa tetapi sumber daya *word-sense* yang sangat kecil.

tldr.en: This paper presents a method to extend language resources for less-resourced languages using dictionary examples and large language models for word-sense disambiguation and novelty detection. The results show that generating sentence pairs from dictionaries outperforms existing models on these tasks.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan metode untuk memperluas sumber daya bahasa untuk *less-resourced languages* menggunakan contoh kamus dan *large language models* untuk *word-sense disambiguation* dan *novelty detection*. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa pembuatan pasangan kalimat dari kamus mengungguli model-model yang ada pada tugas-tugas tersebut.

doi:10.1016/j.datak.2026.102638.title: Slovene word-sense disambiguation and novelty detection with dictionary examples

doi:10.1016/j.fraope.2026.100774.abstract: While emotion-based sentiment analysis is crucial for understanding user preferences and behavior, it poses a particular challenge for languages with limited resources, such as Hindi. Conventional feature engineering methods have dominated previous work on Hindi emotion identification; however, they struggle to capture the language's numerous semantic linkages and morphological variations. For detailed emotion recognition in Hindi text, we proposed a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) architecture. By modeling information from both previous and future word sequences, the proposed system effectively handles the contextual and syntactic complexities inherent in the Hindi language. The BHAAV dataset, comprising 20,304 textual utterances tagged with five distinct emotions—anger, suspense, joy, sadness, and neutrality—is utilized for various studies. We extensively compare our results to those of several baseline models, including mBERT and classical machine learning, as well as pre-trained transformer-based models. The proposed Bi-LSTM framework outperforms the gradient-boosting and transformer-based baselines experimentally, achieving a classification accuracy of 94%. These results demonstrate the efficacy of deep sequential models for low-resource language sentiment analysis, setting a high bar for Hindi emotion recognition.

Proses pemilihan dan transformasi variabel secara manual dari data mentah untuk meningkatkan kinerja *model bahasa*.

Model standar yang digunakan sebagai pembanding untuk mengukur peningkatan performa dari *model* baru yang diusulkan.

background.en: Emotion-based sentiment analysis is crucial for understanding user preferences and behavior, but it poses a particular challenge for low-resource languages such as Hindi. Conventional feature engineering methods struggle to capture the complex semantic linkages and morphological variations inherent in the Hindi language.
background.id: Analisis sentimen berbasis emosi sangat penting untuk memahami preferensi dan perilaku pengguna, namun menghadirkan tantangan tersendiri bagi bahasa dengan sumber daya rendah seperti bahasa Hindi. Metode rekayasa fitur konvensional kesulitan menangkap keterkaitan semantik dan variasi morfologi yang kompleks yang melekat pada bahasa Hindi.

contributions.en: The main contribution is an enhanced Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory architecture designed for detailed emotion recognition in Hindi text. The framework effectively handles contextual and syntactic complexities by modeling information from both previous and future word sequences.

Kerangka kerja ini secara efektif menangani kompleksitas kontekstual dan sintaksis dengan memodelkan informasi dari urutan kata sebelumnya dan masa depan.

method.en: The study utilizes the BHAAV dataset, which comprises 20,304 textual utterances tagged with five distinct emotions including anger, suspense, joy, sadness, and neutrality. The proposed Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory framework models information from past and future word sequences to tackle syntactic complexities, and is evaluated against multiple baselines.
method.id: Studi ini menggunakan *dataset* BHAAV, yang terdiri dari 20.304 ujaran tekstual yang diberi label dengan lima emosi berbeda termasuk kemarahan, ketegangan, kegembiraan, kesedihan, dan kenetralan. Kerangka kerja *Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory* yang diusulkan memodelkan informasi dari urutan kata masa lalu dan masa depan untuk mengatasi kompleksitas sintaksis, serta dievaluasi terhadap berbagai *baseline*.

related_work.en: Previous work on Hindi emotion identification has been dominated by conventional feature engineering methods. The authors compare their approach against several baseline models, including mBERT, classical machine learning, and pre-trained transformer-based models.
related_work.id: Pekerjaan sebelumnya mengenai identifikasi emosi bahasa Hindi didominasi oleh metode rekayasa fitur konvensional. Para penulis membandingkan pendekatan mereka dengan beberapa model *baseline*, termasuk mBERT, pembelajaran mesin klasik, dan model berbasis *transformer* prataret.

results.en: The proposed Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory framework experimentally outperforms gradient-boosting and transformer-based baselines, achieving a classification accuracy of 94 percent. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of deep sequential models for low-resource language sentiment analysis and set a high standard for Hindi emotion recognition.
results.id: Kerangka kerja *Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory* yang diusulkan secara eksperimental mengungguli *baseline* *gradient-boosting* dan berbasis *transformer*, serta mencapai tingkat akurasi klasifikasi sebesar 94 persen. Temuan ini menunjukkan keampuhan model sekuensial mendalam untuk analisis sentimen bahasa bersumber daya rendah dan menetapkan standar tinggi untuk pengenalan emosi bahasa Hindi.

tldr.en: This paper proposes an enhanced Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory architecture for emotion recognition in Hindi text using the BHAAV dataset. The proposed model outperforms classical machine learning and transformer-based baselines, achieving a classification accuracy of 94 percent.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan arsitektur *Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory* yang disempurnakan untuk pengenalan emosi pada teks bahasa Hindi menggunakan *dataset* BHAAV. Model yang diusulkan mengungguli *baseline* pembelajaran mesin klasik dan berbasis *transformer*, serta mencapai tingkat akurasi klasifikasi sebesar 94 persen.

doi:10.1016/j.fraope.2026.100774.title: Enhanced Bi-LSTM Model for Emotion Recognition in Hindi Text: A Deep Learning Approach Using the BHAAV Dataset

doi:10.1016/j.fsir.2026.100520.abstract: Developing Monolingual Setswana Datasets for Offensive Content Detection Reproducibility Package, Metadata, Tools, and Documentation Description This Zenodo release archives the full reproducibility package for the manuscript "Developing Monolingual Setswana Datasets for Offensive Content Detection." The package includes documentation, code, annotation schema, evaluation scripts, and dataset-format specifications supporting the construction, validation, and intended reuse of a manually curated Setswana offensive-language dataset. The work addresses the scarcity of publicly documented resources for low-resource African languages, focusing on the development of a structured Setswana corpus suitable for offensive-language detection research, digital forensic applications, and explainable AI investigations. This release is compliant with FAIR principles—ensuring all non-sensitive artefacts are reusable, accessible, and transparently documented. 📁 Contents of the Release Dataset Schema & Documentation (non-sensitive version) Dataset description following OLID Zampierietal.,2019 Zampierietal.,2019 and HateCheck Ro¨ttgeretal.,2021 Rottgeretal.,2021 formats. Column definitions (TEXT, TARGET, ID, SOURCE) Annotation guidelines and labelling protocol Ethical considerations and masking procedures Dataset card (HuggingFace style) ⚠️ Note: The raw offensive text dataset is not included in this Zenodo release to ensure ethical and legal compliance. Instead, we provide: metadata describing the dataset, annotation schema, sampling notes, cleaning pipeline, and usage guidelines. Annotation Framework & Instructions Includes: Complete annotation manual Examples of label categories (masked versions) Decision rubrics for offensive vs non-offensive distinctions Inter-annotator agreement (IAA) computation script (Cohen's kappa) Annotator training notes This allows reproducibility of annotation methodology without revealing harmful content. Preprocessing, Cleaning & Structuring Scripts Folder: scripts/preprocessing/ Includes: Text cleaning pipeline Normalisation for Setswana orthography Token masking functions Duplicate removal and source metadata stripping Tools for exporting to OLID/HateCheck CSV structure These scripts enable researchers to structure their own Setswana datasets using the same methodology. Evaluation Scripts Folder: scripts/evaluation/ Includes: Binary-class evaluation (Accuracy, F1, MCC, ROC-AUC) Stratified splitting tools Error analysis helper functions Label distribution checkers These enable reproducibility of experimental analysis described in the paper. Explainability & Counterfactuals (Sanitized) Folder: outputs/explainability/ Contains: LIME/S-LIME interpretation outputs (masked) Counterfactual examples (masked) explanation_notes.md describing methodology and sanitization policies No harmful text is included. Figures & Tables Used in the Manuscript Folder: outputs/figures/ and outputs/tables/ Includes: Dataset distribution plots Annotator agreement figures Offensive vs non-offensive category diagrams Tokenisation breakdowns Summary statistics Table files (CSV + LaTeX) These are all reproducible using provided scripts. Supporting Notebooks Folder: notebooks/ Provides: Dataset structuring and cleaning notebook (safe version) Annotation guidelines demonstration notebook Explainability notebook (masked text) Dataset export notebook All notebooks are sanitised and suitable for public release. 🔒 Ethical & Safety Considerations This release does not include: raw offensive text user-identifiable content social media data platform metadata detailed examples containing sensitive content All samples shown in figures or notebooks are masked using ***. The dataset described in the manuscript should be accessed only through controlled academic channels and under strict ethical governance. This Zenodo package is designed to enable reproducibility without distributing harmful language. 🎯 Intended Use This release supports: NLP research in low-resource languages Cyberbullying and hate speech detection studies Digital forensics investigations Linguistic analysis of Setswana online discourse Educational purposes Reproduction of the experimental methodology described in the manuscript It is not intended for: Real-time automated moderation Law-enforcement without expert oversight Deployment in production systems without additional safeguards 📖 Citation If using this release, please cite the manuscript: Kekgathetse, B. (2025). Developing Monolingual Setswana Datasets for Offensive Content Detection. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17824911 📝 Licensing Code: MIT / Apache-2.0 Documentation & annotation guidelines: CC-BY 4.0 Sanitized examples: CC-BY-SA 4.0 No raw data included 🌍 Audience NLP researchers Digital forensics experts Computer security practitioners Linguists working with Bantu languages

background.en: The paper addresses the severe scarcity of publicly documented resources for low-resource African languages in the context of offensive content detection. This lack of structured corpora hampers research in digital forensics, natural language processing, and explainable AI investigations.
background.id: Makalah ini mengatasi kelangkaan sumber daya yang terdokumentasi untuk *low-resource language* di Afrika dalam konteks deteksi konten ofensif. Kekurangan korpus terstruktur ini menghambat penelitian dalam bidang forensik digital, *natural language processing*, dan investigasi *explainable AI*.

contributions.en: The authors contribute a comprehensive reproducibility package for constructing, validating, and reusing a Setswana offensive-language dataset. The novel contributions include an annotation framework, preprocessing and cleaning scripts, evaluation tools, and sanitized explainability outputs aligned with FAIR principles.
contributions.id: Para penulis berkontribusi menyediakan paket *reproducibility* yang komprehensif untuk membangun, memvalidasi, dan menggunakan kembali *dataset* bahasa Setswana untuk teks ofensif. Kontribusi kebaruannya mencakup kerangka kerja anotasi, skrip prapemrosesan dan pembersihan, perangkat *evaluasi*, serta keluaran *explainability* yang disanitasi sesuai dengan prinsip FAIR.

method.en: The methodology involves manual curation and annotation protocols modeled after established formats such as OLID and HateCheck, supported by inter-annotator agreement computation using Cohen's kappa. The approach utilizes text normalization for Setswana orthography, token masking functions, and binary-class evaluation metrics including Accuracy, F1, MCC, and ROC-AUC.
method.id: Metodologinya melibatkan protokol kurasi manual dan anotasi yang dimodelkan setelah format mapan seperti OLID dan HateCheck, yang didukung oleh penghitungan *inter-annotator agreement* menggunakan *Cohen's kappa*. Pendekatan ini memanfaatkan normalisasi teks untuk ortografi bahasa Setswana, fungsi *token masking*, dan metrik *evaluasi* kelas biner termasuk *Accuracy*, *F1*, *MCC*, dan *ROC-AUC*.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas karya terkait secara mendetail.

results.en: The paper does not report experimental results from a trained model evaluation.
results.id: Makalah ini tidak melaporkan hasil eksperimen dari *evaluasi* *model* yang dilatih.

tldr.en: This paper presents a reproducibility package and methodology for developing a monolingual Setswana dataset for offensive content detection. The main takeaway is that structured resources, documentation, and evaluation tools can be shared for a low-resource language while maintaining ethical compliance and data privacy.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan paket *reproducibility* dan metodologi untuk mengembangkan *dataset* Setswana *monolingual* untuk deteksi konten ofensif. Kesimpulan utamanya adalah bahwa sumber daya terstruktur, dokumentasi, dan perangkat *evaluasi* dapat dibagikan untuk *low-resource language* dengan tetap menjaga kepatuhan etika dan privasi data.

doi:10.1016/j.geothermics.2026.103790.abstract: In 2013–2015, two deep wells, PTA-2 and KMA-1, were drilled in the Humu‘ula Saddle region of Hawai‘i for groundwater and geothermal exploration as part of a broader effort to understand the geological history and resource potential of subsurface environments on the island of Hawai‘i. This study focuses on the alteration mineralogy of the KMA-1 drill hole, complementing similar investigations conducted on PTA-2. Mineralogical analysis of KMA-1 involved a multi-scale characterization of aqueous alteration using bulk and high-resolution visible and short-wave infrared (VIS-SWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) spectral imaging, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and X-ray fluorescence (XRF). Several types of secondary phases, including alunite, jarosite, secondary hematite, and smectites, were identified. Spectroscopic data and the occurrence of alteration minerals suggest a correlation with confined groundwater units. Field surveys showed widespread alteration and abundant sulfates, while high-resolution techniques like XRD and XRF detected smaller quantities in bulk rock. This discrepancy suggests that spectroscopic methods are highly sensitive to strongly absorbing, albeit minor, mineral phases. Collectively, our analysis points to possible fumarole systems buried over time or acid-steam alteration during post-shield volcanic phases. This study contributes to ongoing efforts to characterize the mineralization associated with geothermal and groundwater systems in the Hawaiian subsurface, providing further insight into hydrothermal processes and alteration pathways.

doi:10.1016/j.ipm.2026.105162.abstract: Mobile application user reviews provide valuable insights into user-reported issues, including security concerns that are critical for software engineering activities such as requirements analysis and system design. However, existing research has largely focused on English reviews and lacks systematic approaches for identifying security-related feedback in Arabic, a low-resource language in this domain. In this paper, we address this gap by developing an integrated approach for automated binary classification of security-related versus non-security-related Arabic mobile app reviews, grounded in a structured set of security requirement categories derived from software engineering literature. We collected 14,667,283 reviews from 56 mobile applications across multiple domains, including government, finance, and social platforms. Using natural language processing techniques and sentiment-based filtering, positive reviews were removed as a dataset-reduction step, while neutral and negative reviews were retained for subsequent analysis. To construct a high-quality labeled dataset, we developed an annotation approach combining keyword-guided sample selection, expert annotation, and iterative dataset refinement using active learning. During the active learning phase, semantic feature representations were generated using Low-Rank Adaptation-enhanced sentence transformers and combined with machine learning classifiers within an agreement-based active learning strategy to identify candidate samples for expert validation. The process was conducted over ten iterations, starting with 300 expert-annotated reviews and terminating when classifier performance stabilized. Following the stopping criterion, the final classifier-agreement samples were expert-validated and used to construct a held-out test set rather than being added to the training data. The active learning process resulted in a final training dataset of 10,632 expert-validated reviews. In addition, 1000 expert-validated reviews were reserved as a held-out test set and excluded from model training. The training dataset was used to fine-tune three transformer models, namely CAMeLBERT, MARBERT, and Paraphrase, for binary classification of security-related and non-security-related reviews. CAMeLBERT achieved the highest performance among the fine-tuned models, with 95.76% accuracy and 95.77% F1-score under 10-fold cross-validation and 91.20% accuracy and 91.16% F1-score on the held-out test set. To support practical adoption, we developed a web-based interface integrated with a large language model to enable real-time classification and provide interpretable explanations. The resulting dataset and developed approach contribute to advancing security-aware analysis of Arabic user-generated content and support software engineers in identifying security-related concerns in mobile application reviews.

doi:10.1016/j.iswa.2026.200716.abstract: Accurate detection of periapical pathologies from dental radiographs remains a challenging task due to variations in image quality, anatomical complexity, and limited availability of labeled clinical datasets. This study proposes an intelligent deep learning framework, termed Triple Ensemble Artificial Intelligence for Teeth Disease Classification System (A-TDCS), designed to improve diagnostic accuracy and robustness in dental radiography analysis. The proposed framework integrates three complementary components: optimized image augmentation using a Non-Population-Based Artificial Multiple Intelligence System (np-AMIS), adaptive image segmentation guided by Population-Based AMIS (pop-AMIS), and a heterogeneous ensemble of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) combined through multiple decision-fusion strategies. A comprehensive factorial experimental design involving 450 configurations was conducted to identify optimal combinations of preprocessing, segmentation, network architecture, and fusion strategies. The resulting framework was evaluated on both benchmark datasets and real clinical datasets of periapical radiographs collected from the Postgraduate Endodontic Clinic, Faculty of Dentistry, Chiang Mai University. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed A-TDCS-AMIS model consistently outperforms single architectures and homogeneous ensembles. On the TD-XI clinical dataset, the model achieved 98.84% accuracy, while evaluation on the independent unseen TD-XIV dataset achieved 98.21% accuracy, confirming strong generalization capability under real-world conditions. The results demonstrate that combining heterogeneous CNN architectures with adaptive optimization-based fusion significantly improves diagnostic reliability for dental radiographic analysis. The proposed framework provides a scalable and robust solution for AI-assisted clinical decision support in dental diagnostics, demonstrating its practical applicability in real clinical environments and contributing to the advancement of intelligent medical imaging systems.
doi:10.1016/j.iswa.2026.200716.title: Intelligent diagnosis of periapical pathologies in dental radiographs using an optimized triple-ensemble deep learning framework with real-world clinical validation

doi:10.1016/j.nlp.2026.100233.abstract: Relation extraction for Assamese, a morphologically rich Indo-Aryan language spoken by roughly 15 million people, has been held back by the absence of an annotated corpus, a trained model, and any standardised evaluation protocol. We address all three gaps in this work. We first introduce AREX, the first manually annotated Assamese relation extraction dataset, comprising 1,927 triples across ten semantic relation categories drawn from biographical Wikipedia text, with inter-annotator agreement of κ = 0.84 . We benchmark four fine-tuned multilingual transformer encoders together with one instruction tuned large language model under a controlled five seed protocol, and we find that task specific fine tuning of the smaller multilingual encoders outperforms zero shot prompting of the substantially larger LLM, with mBERT reaching a macro F1 of 0.772 ± 0.012 against Llama-3.1-8B at 0.719 ± 0.016. To exploit the complementary strengths of the four fine tuned models, we then propose a Relation Guided Adaptive Ensemble that computes per relation weights from validation F1-scores and aggregates the corresponding probability distributions at inference. The ensemble achieves a macro F1 of 0.782 ± 0.007, significantly improving on mBERT under a paired t -test at p = 0.049 and reducing across seed variance by 40%. An ablation study confirms that both the F1-guided weighting and the per relation granularity are individually necessary, with uniform weight averaging performing worse than the strongest single model. The extracted triples are serialised into an RDF knowledge graph of 2,184 edges and 1,467 entities, queryable through SPARQL and enriched with temporal attributes for time anchored relations. A manually verified stratified sample of 50 triples yields a triple level precision of 84.0% with a 95% Wilson confidence interval from 71.7 to 91.2 percent and verification agreement κ = 0.86 . AREX, the trained models, and the constructed knowledge graph collectively provide the first end-to-end reproducible baseline for Assamese relation extraction and demonstrate a practical pipeline for extending information extraction to other morphologically rich low resource languages.

doi:10.1016/j.nlp.2026.100234.abstract: Recent advancements in Natural Language Processing and Deep Learning have enabled the development of Large Language Models (LLMs), which have significantly advanced the state-of-the-art across a wide range of tasks, including Question Answering (QA). Despite these advancements, research on LLMs has primarily targeted high-resourced languages (e.g., English), and only recently has attention shifted toward multilingual models. However, these models demonstrate a training data bias towards a small number of popular languages or rely on transfer learning from high- to under-resourced languages; this may lead to a misrepresentation of social, cultural, and historical aspects. To address this challenge, monolingual LLMs have been developed for under-resourced languages; however, their effectiveness remains less studied when compared to multilingual counterparts on language-specific tasks. In this study, we address this research gap in Greek QA by contributing: (i) DemosQA, a novel dataset, which is constructed using social media user questions and community-reviewed answers to better capture the Greek social and cultural zeitgeist; (ii) a memory-efficient LLM evaluation framework adaptable to diverse QA datasets and languages; and (iii) an extensive evaluation of 11 monolingual and multilingual LLMs on 6 human-curated Greek QA datasets using 3 different prompting strategies. We release our code and data to facilitate reproducibility.

doi:10.1016/j.ssaho.2026.103687.abstract: Textbook passages often claim alignment with proficiency benchmarks, yet such claims are rarely verified through empirical linguistic evidence, creating a risk of mismatch between curriculum targets and the reading input learners actually receive. This study examines whether Grade 8 reading passages in Indonesian EFL instructional materials align with CEFR-referenced proficiency expectations for Merdeka Curriculum Phase D (Grades 7–9), positioned around the A2 benchmark. Using descriptive document analysis, 28 comprehension-oriented reading passages were selected from a government-issued core textbook ( English for Nusantara ; n = 18) and a widely used commercial workbook ( LKS Bahasa Inggris Galileo ; n = 10) using explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (continuous paragraph-based texts used as main reading input; excluding dialogues, vocabulary lists, grammar notes, short instructions, and captions). Each passage was profiled with Text Inspector to estimate CEFR level, and complementary indicators (word count, average sentence length, average word length, and word complexity) were generated with Road to Grammar to contextualise the estimates. Results indicate that none of the analysed passages were classified at A2; the lowest level identified was B1 (21.4%), followed by B2 (35.7%) and C1–C2 (42.9%). The workbook contained a markedly higher concentration of C1–C2 passages than the core textbook, suggesting that supplementary materials can shift the overall difficulty environment well above the intended benchmark. These findings support treating CEFR alignment as an empirical claim and recommend routine screening plus targeted scaffolding or resequencing when supplementary resources raise text demands beyond curriculum expectations.
doi:10.1016/j.ssaho.2026.103687.title: Claimed vs. Measured CEFR Levels: Profiling Grade 8 EFL Reading Texts in Indonesia

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64104-8.abstract: The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) has transformed educational writing while introducing significant challenges for academic integrity and authorship verification. Existing AI-generated text detection systems predominantly rely on centralized cloud-based infrastructures, requiring student essays to be uploaded to external servers and raising concerns regarding privacy, data ownership, and regulatory compliance. To address these challenges, we propose RoBERTa-CNN+FL, a privacy-preserving framework that integrates a RoBERTa encoder for contextual semantic representation, a convolutional neural network (CNN) for local stylistic feature extraction, federated learning (FL) for decentralized collaborative model training, and differential privacy (DP) to protect sensitive educational data. The framework was evaluated on the LowResourceQAEssaysText dataset comprising human-written and AI-generated essays generated by multiple contemporary LLMs. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Matthews correlation coefficient, ROC-AUC, BLEU score, perplexity, and human evaluation conducted by independent academic reviewers to assess the consistency of model predictions with expert judgments. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework achieves robust and reliable detection performance while preserving data privacy and enabling on-device deployment. Comparative experiments further show competitive performance against widely used commercial and research AI-text detection systems, including Turnitin, Grammarly AI Detector, QuillBot, GPTZero, Copyleaks, Originality.ai, Sapling AI Detector, Writer.com Detector, DetectGPT, Fast-DetectGPT, Crossplag AI Detector, ZeroGPT, OpenAI AI Classifier, Hugging Face open-source detectors, and other academic detection frameworks. The proposed framework offers a scalable and privacy-preserving solution for AI-generated text detection in multilingual and low-resource educational environments, reducing dependence on centralized cloud-based services while supporting trustworthy academic integrity assessment.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-65518-0.abstract: Abstract Cross-lingual speech recognition for real-time applications is constrained by the joint requirements of low latency, high recognition accuracy, and strict privacy over conversational audio. This research work addresses these constraints by designing an adaptive dual-stream neural encoder that explicitly models acoustic and linguistic information in parallel while operating in a streaming regime. The proposed architecture was developed with two coordinated streams: an acoustic encoder that processed log-Mel features in fixed-size chunks and a linguistic encoder that consumed partial token embeddings, with an adaptive gating module that fused both representations to minimize re-computation and buffering delay. A privacy-preserving data augmentation pipeline was further introduced, in which non-identifying signal transforms, feature-space perturbations, and cross-lingual masking were applied without storing raw sensitive speech or speaker metadata. The framework was trained and evaluated on multilingual corpora including CoVoST 2, Common Voice, and MuST-C, achieving relative word error rate reductions of approximately 19% on average and up to 22% in low-resource languages compared with a strong streaming Transformer baseline. Under streaming conditions, the dual-stream encoder attained an operating Real-Time Factor of 0.60 with end-to-end latency below 320 ms for typical utterances, while maintaining character error rates below 7% across the majority of evaluated languages. Ablation studies indicated that the adaptive gating contributed a relative WER improvement of about 20% and that privacy-preserving augmentation yielded a further gain of about 14% in noisy and domain-shifted test scenarios. This research work therefore establishes a practical pathway toward low-latency, privacy-aware, cross-lingual speech-to-text systems suitable for deployment in real-time multilingual services

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-68159-5.abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of digital journalism has increased the need for automated systems that can organize large volumes of textual content. However, mature natural language processing resources remain concentrated in high-resource languages, while low-resource languages such as Somali continue to face limited availability of annotated datasets, language-specific preprocessing tools, and reproducible benchmarks. This study develops a lightweight supervised machine learning pipeline for Somali news topic classification using a manually curated corpus of 7240 articles collected from BBC Somali and VOA Somali. The articles were organized into eight mutually exclusive topic categories: Caafimaad, Ciyaaro, Dagaal, Diini, Ganacsi, Madadaalo, Siyaasad, and Tiknoolajiyad. The final model used word-level TF-IDF unigram features with a Linear Support Vector Machine classifier. In a stratified 80/20 holdout evaluation, the best Linear SVM configuration achieved 94.20% accuracy. Additional repeated stratified holdout testing and stratified five-fold cross-validation produced mean accuracies of 93.11% and 93.20%, respectively, indicating stable performance across data partitions. Supervised baseline comparisons showed that Linear SVM outperformed Multinomial Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and alternative SVM n-gram variants under the same preprocessing and evaluation conditions. Computational profiling further showed that the final pipeline trained in under two seconds, classified the test set in less than one quarter of a second, produced a serialized model below 1 MB, and required no GPU acceleration. The findings position TF-IDF + Linear SVM as a strong, transparent, and resource-efficient baseline for Somali news classification, while future work should compare this baseline with neural and transformer-based models under the same data, preprocessing, and evaluation protocol.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69201-2.abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) in low-resource languages remains challenging due to limited annotated data, speaker variability, and the multimodal nature of emotional expression. This paper repositions established components wav2vec 2.0, XLM-R, cross-modal attention, and multitask affective modeling into a framework jointly validated across speaker-independent, cross-lingual zero-shot, and attribution-faithfulness generalization for Urdu, a combination not jointly reported in prior Urdu SER work. The proposed multimodal multitask model achieves 91.3% emotion recognition accuracy on the Urdu Speech Emotion Corpus (UrSEC), outperforming strong audio-only and text-only baselines, with joint valence-arousal learning consistently improving over emotion-only training. Speaker-independent evaluation shows a performance drop relative to random-split testing but confirms substantial robustness to speaker-specific bias. Cross-lingual zero-shot evaluation on English datasets yields 80.2 ± 1.3% (IEMOCAP) to 86.3 ± 0.9% (CREMA-D) accuracy without fine-tuning, indicating substantial cross-lingual transfer, though this alone does not establish full language-neutrality. All performance gains are statistically validated across multiple runs, and attention/Integrated Gradients analyses, supported by quantitative faithfulness testing, show the model relies on emotionally salient acoustic regions and Urdu tokens rather than spurious correlations.

tldr.en: This paper introduces a cross-modal audio-text attention framework for speech emotion recognition in low-resource Urdu. The proposed model achieves 91.3 percent accuracy on the Urdu Speech Emotion Corpus and demonstrates strong cross-lingual zero-shot generalization.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69546-8.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) play a critical role in how humans access information. While their core functionality relies on the ability to comprehend written requests, our understanding of this ability is currently constrained, because most benchmarks evaluate LLMs in high-resource languages that are predominantly spoken by Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) communities. The default assumption is that English is the best-performing language for LLMs, while smaller, low-resource languages are linked to less natural or reliable outputs, even in multilingual, state-of-the-art models. To track fluctuations in the comprehension abilities of LLMs, we prompt 3 popular models across 12 languages, representing the Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Turkic, Sino-Tibetan, and Japonic language families. Our results suggest that the models exhibit remarkable accuracy across typologically diverse languages, yet they may fall behind human baselines, albeit to different degrees. Contrary to what was expected, English is not the best-performing language, as it was systematically outperformed by several Romance languages, even lower-resource ones. We frame the results by highlighting the role of factors that drive LLM performance, such as tokenization, language distance from Spanish and English, size of training data, and data origin in high- vs. low-resource languages and WEIRD vs. non-WEIRD communities.

background.en: Large language models play a critical role in how humans access information, relying fundamentally on their ability to comprehend written requests. However, current understanding of this comprehension ability is constrained because most evaluation benchmarks focus on high-resource languages spoken predominantly by Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic communities. The prevailing assumption is that English serves as the best-performing language for these models, while low-resource languages typically yield less natural or reliable outputs, even in state-of-the-art multilingual systems. This creates a significant gap in our knowledge regarding how models handle linguistic diversity beyond dominant Western languages.
background.id: *Large language model* memainkan peran krusial dalam cara manusia mengakses informasi, yang secara fundamental bergantung pada kemampuan mereka untuk memahami permintaan tertulis. Namun, pemahaman saat ini mengenai kemampuan pemahaman ini terbatas karena sebagian besar *benchmark* evaluasi berfokus pada bahasa *high-resource* yang dituturkan secara dominan oleh komunitas *Western*, *Educated*, *Industrialized*, *Rich*, and *Democratic*. Asumsi yang berlaku adalah bahwa bahasa Inggris berfungsi sebagai bahasa dengan kinerja terbaik untuk model-model ini, sementara bahasa *low-resource* biasanya menghasilkan keluaran yang kurang alami atau andal, bahkan dalam sistem multibahasa *state-of-the-art*. Hal ini menciptakan kesenjangan yang signifikan dalam pengetahuan kita mengenai bagaimana model menangani keragaman linguistik di luar bahasa barat yang dominan.

contributions.en: The paper investigates the comprehension abilities of three popular large language models across twelve languages representing diverse language families, including Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Turkic, Sino-Tibetan, and Japonic.
