doi:10.11594/ijmaber.07.08.13.abstract: The rapid spread of recommender algorithms has made the competencies that govern how young people interpret and act in digital spaces a pressing concern. This study examined levels of algorithmic and digital literacy, as well as perceived digital self-efficacy, among Filipino emerging adults and tested whether these competencies predicted their social media engagement. Using a descriptive-correlational and predictive design, a researcher-adapted survey was administered through non-probability sampling to 77 eligible emerging adults from the City of Manila. Given the non-probability sampling and ordinal data, levels were summarized using the median (Mdn) and interquartile range; associations were tested with Spearman’s rank-order correlation; and predictors were identified through median (quantile) regression. Respondents showed a very high level of algorithmic literacy (Mdn = 4.50) and high levels of digital literacy (Mdn = 4.11), perceived digital self-efficacy (Mdn = 4.20), and social media engagement (Mdn = 3.83). All three competencies were significantly and positively associated with engagement: algorithmic literacy (ρ = .30, p = .003), digital literacy (ρ = .39), and perceived digital self-efficacy (ρ = .41), the latter two at p < .001. In the median regression, however, digital literacy was the only significant unique predictor of engagement (b = 0.47, p = .003); perceived digital self-efficacy and algorithmic literacy did not contribute uniquely once digital literacy was accounted for. Practical digital competence, rather than algorithm awareness or digital confidence alone, appears to most directly account for how emerging adults engage online, underscoring the value of competency-based digital citizenship programs.
doi:10.11594/ijmaber.07.08.13.journal_ref: International Journal of Multidisciplinary Applied Business and Education Research
doi:10.11594/ijmaber.07.08.13.title: Algorithmic Literacy, Digital Literacy, and Perceived Digital Self-Efficacy as Predictors of Social Media Engagement Among Filipino Emerging Adults in the City of Manila
doi:10.11594/ijmaber.07.08.13.venue: International Journal of Multidisciplinary Applied Business and Education Research

doi:10.1177/10439862261485726.abstract: In November 2025, Karen National Liberation Army forces liberated more than 3,000 workers from 23 countries held inside the Shunda Park compound in Myanmar, exposing an industrial criminal model that confounds foundational criminological assumptions. Southeast Asian scam compounds, generating an estimated 64 billion dollars in annual global revenues, operate through a three-party economic structure in which trafficked laborers are coerced into perpetrating cryptocurrency investment fraud against a global victim pool. This article extends routine activity theory and rational choice theory to account for structurally coerced perpetrators, the labor-control and victim-extraction functions of cryptocurrency infrastructure, and the dual victimhood that defines these operations. Drawing on a mixed-methods analysis of federal indictments, sanctions designations, United Nations (UN) reports, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Internet Crime Complaint Center data, and blockchain analytics, three theoretical propositions are advanced with accompanying policy implications.
doi:10.1177/10439862261485726.title: Coerced Perpetrators and Cryptocurrency Control Infrastructure: Southeast Asian Scam Compounds and the Limits of Classical Criminal Opportunity Theory

doi:10.1177/10575677261485546.abstract: Cyber-slavery converges human trafficking and transnational cybercrime by coercing trafficked individuals into cyber-enabled fraud through confinement, violence, surveillance, and control. This study uses a hybrid qualitative and administrative data design. It combines a systematic narrative review with preanonymized law-enforcement metadata on 29,466 Indian nationals identified as probable cyber-slavery cases in Southeast Asia between 2022 and 2024. From these sources, we develop a five-tier victimization framework that conceptualizes cyber-slavery as a layered sociotechnical process with probabilistic transitions a exploitation and its aftermath. Tiers 1-3 capture recruitment, coercion, and sustained exploitation. Tiers 4-5 capture postexploitation harms, including reintegration barriers, criminalization, and persistent incriminating digital traces. Cases show substantial male predominance (21,182 males; 8,283 females) and concentration among those aged 20-39. The wider cybercrime ecosystem included 633,000 Indian SIM cards and 376,000 mule accounts. Thailand emerged as a major transit hub, accounting for 20,450 cases. Prolonged exposure to coercive cybercrime environments may also facilitate transitions from forced participation to voluntary criminal involvement, complicating victim-offender distinctions and legal accountability. The study calls for trafficking-aware cybercrime investigations and reforms that recognize forced criminality within digitally mediated transnational crime ecosystems.
doi:10.1177/10575677261485546.title: A Five-Tier Framework for Understanding Cyber-Slavery and Institutional Misclassification: Evidence from 29,466 Cases in Southeast Asia

doi:10.1177/18758967261476359.abstract: Abstract This study examines structural alignment between human and transformer-based multi-label emotion annotation in a low-resource language setting. A corpus of 408 Serbian narratives was manually annotated using soft-label scores mapped to the 28-category GoEmotions taxonomy. Inter-annotator agreement was moderate (micro F1 = 0.58), reflecting the inherent subjectivity of fine-grained emotion labeling. Four modeling paradigms were compared: a zero-shot English model applied to machine-translated texts, a domain-adapted fine-tuned model trained on the translated corpus, multilingual XLM-RoBERTa models trained under hard- and soft-label supervision, and regional South-Slavic models trained on original Serbian texts. The highest overall performance was achieved by the domain-adapted GoEmotions model fine-tuned on the translated corpus (micro F1 = 0.50), substantially outperforming zero-shot cross-lingual transfer. Among multilingual and regional models not originally trained on emotion-specific data, XLM-R-BERTić achieved the strongest micro-level performance (micro F1 = 0.36), indicating the contribution of regional language pre-training to human–machine alignment. Polarity analysis conducted on the pre-trained baseline model indicated low disagreement (≈6%), whereas divergences remained pronounced at the fine-grained category level. The intensity-weighted soft-label annotations reflect the fuzzy boundaries of affective categories, highlighting the importance of domain adaptation and emotion-specific training for improving human–machine alignment.

glossary.explanation_id: Skor probabilitas kontinu yang mewakili tingkat kepastian atau intensitas berbagai label kategori emosi.
Kemampuan *model* untuk melakukan tugas tanpa pelatihan sebelumnya pada *data* spesifik untuk tugas tersebut.
Proses pelatihan lanjutan pada *model* prarilis menggunakan *data* spesifik untuk meningkatkan performa pada tugas tertentu.
Metode penyesuaian *model* agar dapat bekerja dengan baik pada *domain* atau jenis *data* baru yang berbeda dari *data* latih awalnya.
Metrik *evaluasi* yang menghitung rata-rata harmonis antara presisi dan *recall* secara global di seluruh instansi *data*.

background.en: The paper investigates the structural alignment between human and transformer-based multi-label emotion annotation in a low-resource language setting using a corpus of 408 Serbian narratives. This is important because fine-grained emotion labeling suffers from inherent subjectivity and fuzzy boundaries among affective categories, creating a gap in understanding how well automated models match human emotional perception.
background.id: Makalah ini menyelidiki keselarasan struktural antara *anotasi* emosi *multi-label* oleh manusia dan *transformer* dalam pengaturan *low-resource language* menggunakan korpus 408 narasi bahasa Serbia. Hal ini penting karena *labeling* emosi tingkat halus memiliki subjektivitas bawaan dan batas-batas kategori afektif yang kabur, sehingga menciptakan celah dalam memahami seberapa baik *model* otomatis mencocokkan persepsi emosional manusia.

contributions.en: The study introduces a manually annotated corpus of 408 Serbian narratives using soft-label scores mapped to the 28-category GoEmotions taxonomy. It further contributes a comparative evaluation of four distinct modeling paradigms to assess human-machine alignment in emotion annotation.
contributions.id: Studi ini memperkenalkan korpus narasi bahasa Serbia sebanyak 408 data yang dianotasi secara manual menggunakan skor *soft-label* yang dipetakan ke taksonomi GoEmotions 28 kategori. Studi ini juga menyumbangkan *evaluasi* komparatif dari empat paradigma *model* yang berbeda untuk menilai keselarasan manusia dan mesin dalam *anotasi* emosi.

future_work.en: The paper does not state future work directions explicitly.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak menyatakan arah *future work* secara eksplisit.

method.en: The corpus of 408 Serbian narratives was manually annotated using soft-label scores mapped to the 28-category GoEmotions taxonomy. Four modeling paradigms were compared: a zero-shot English model applied to machine-translated texts, a domain-adapted fine-tuned model trained on the translated corpus, multilingual XLM-RoBERTa models trained under hard- and soft-label supervision, and regional South-Slavic models trained on original Serbian texts.
method.id: Korpus yang berisi 408 narasi bahasa Serbia dianotasi secara manual menggunakan skor *soft-label* yang dipetakan ke taksonomi GoEmotions 28 kategori. Empat paradigma *model* dibandingkan: *model* bahasa Inggris *zero-shot* yang diterapkan pada teks hasil *terjemahan mesin*, *model* *fine-tuning* yang beradaptasi dengan *domain* dan dilatih pada korpus terjemahan, *model* *multilingual* XLM-RoBERTa yang dilatih di bawah *supervision* *hard-label* dan *soft-label*, serta *model* regional Slavia Selatan yang dilatih pada teks asli bahasa Serbia.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas *related work* secara mendetail.

results.en: Inter-annotator agreement was moderate with a micro F1 score of 0.58. The highest overall performance was achieved by the domain-adapted GoEmotions model fine-tuned on the translated corpus with a micro F1 score of 0.50, outperforming zero-shot cross-lingual transfer. Among models not originally trained on emotion-specific data, XLM-R-Bertić achieved the strongest performance with a micro F1 score of 0.36. Polarity analysis showed low disagreement at approximately six percent, while divergences remained pronounced at the fine-grained category level.
results.id: Persetujuan antar-*annotator* berada pada tingkat sedang dengan skor *micro* F1 sebesar 0,58. Performa keseluruhan tertinggi dicapai oleh *model* GoEmotions yang diadaptasi ke *domain* dan melalui *fine-tuning* pada korpus terjemahan dengan skor *micro* F1 sebesar 0,50, mengungguli *zero-shot cross-lingual transfer*. Di antara *model* yang awalnya tidak dilatih pada *data* spesifik emosi, XLM-R-Bertić mencapai performa terkuat dengan skor *micro* F1 sebesar 0,36. *Analisis* polaritas menunjukkan ketidaksepakatan yang rendah sekitar enam persen, sementara perbedaan tetap tajam pada tingkat kategori halus.

tldr.en: This study examines structural alignment between human and transformer-based multi-label emotion annotation for Serbian narratives. The findings show that domain adaptation and emotion-specific training outperform zero-shot cross-lingual transfer.
tldr.id: Studi ini meneliti keselarasan struktural antara *anotasi* emosi *multi-label* oleh manusia dan *transformer* untuk narasi bahasa Serbia. Temuannya menunjukkan bahwa *domain adaptation* dan pelatihan spesifik emosi mengungguli *zero-shot cross-lingual transfer*.

doi:10.1177/18758967261476359.title: Between accuracy and empathy: A comparative study of human and transformer-based multi-label emotion annotation

doi:10.1344/dialectologia.37.8.abstract: In this paper I argue that textual data from WhatsApp Conversation among the Malaysian youths can be evidence of indexicality and enregisterment, in other words, expressions denoting various social meanings and recognised as a style of speech of the community. Using a corpus of WhatsApp conversations from 52 participants, I discuss a repertoire of features that was enregistered as “Manglish” to the youths. I do this by comparing data from a corpus of WhatsApp conversations from three major ethnic groups in Malaysia specifically Malay, Chinese and Indian and an online survey of the speakers’ perceptions of the Manglish dialect. I suggest that Manglish features are socially recognised and therefore enregistered forms of speech, indexical not only to place but also to ethnic groups.
doi:10.1344/dialectologia.37.8.title: ‘They Are Definitely Malaysian’

doi:10.1353/ol.2026.a1000271.abstract: Abstract: Indonesian reciprocals can be expressed through overt reciprocal markers or covertly, via constructions that are not explicitly reciprocal in form. This study focuses on covert reciprocals, adpoting an analysis grounded in a symmetric event approach, in which reciprocal meaning arises from two coordinated subevents involving the same participants in reversed agent-patient roles. These representations of these subevents are syntactically intransitive, but semantically structured as a single symmetric event, allowing for reciprocal interpretation even in the absence of dedicated reciprocal morphology. We examine three main types of covert reciprocals in Indonesian. The first involves seemingly reduplicated verbal forms, which we analyze as instances of asyndetic coordination, where active and passive predicates are combined, resulting in a plural subject that bears both agent and patient roles. The second involves verb roots with the circumfix ber- -an , denoting temporally extended eventualities that, in the presence of plural subjects, yield a reciprocal interpretation through sequential subevents. The third type involves verb roots prefixed with ber -, analyzed as an instance of ber - functioning as a middle voice. This prefix typically indicates a coreferential interpretation that, with specific nominal bases, can produce a reciprocal reading. In all cases, these constructions have more general, independently attested meanings that allow—but do not require—a reciprocal reading. The analysis highlights the heterogeneity of reciprocal formation in Indonesian and shows how covert reciprocals are licensed through event semantics and context, rather than dedicated reciprocal morphology.
doi:10.1353/ol.2026.a1000271.title: Covert Reciprocals in Indonesian

doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0353166.abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) is fundamental for automating administrative document processing in digital government systems. However, Vietnamese NLP research faces a critical infrastructure gap: existing datasets focus on generic information extraction (news, medical) rather than domain-specific administrative text. We present PAP_NER, the first large-scale, gold-standard Vietnamese administrative NER corpus comprising 162,801 sentences with 205,807 entity annotations across five entity types critical for e-Government workflows: Agency (CQ), Legal Document (VBPL), Object (ĐT), Datetime (NG), and Quantity (SL). The dataset was constructed through a rigorous human-in-the-loop annotation pipeline, achieving an inter-annotator agreement of κ = 0.85. We demonstrate PAP_NER's value through comprehensive benchmarking of an established hybrid deep learning architecture, PhoBERT-CRF, which couples monolingual Transformer embeddings (PhoBERT) with Conditional Random Fields for structured prediction. PhoBERT-CRF achieves 97.95% Micro F1-score on the PAP_NER test set, significantly outperforming established baselines: BiLSTM+CRF (+2.01%), multilingual XLM-RoBERTa (+2.52%), and pure Transformer approaches (+0.44%). Ablation analysis reveals that the CRF layer provides statistically significant improvements for structurally complex entities (VBPL: + 0.96%, p < 0.05, McNemar's test). We release PAP_NER publicly (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18044019) under Creative Commons BY 4.0 license to support reproducibility and enable further research in Vietnamese administrative NLP. This work establishes a foundational dataset and methodology for addressing the Vietnamese government NER gap, with implications for low-resource language NLP research.

glossary.explanation_id: Tugas *natural language processing* untuk mengekstrak dan mengklasifikasikan entitas bernama ke dalam kategori yang telah ditentukan dari teks tidak terstruktur.
Model diskriminatif probabilistik yang digunakan untuk pemodelan sekuens dengan memperhitungkan dependensi antarlabel.
Arsitektur jaringan saraf tiruan yang mengandalkan mekanisme *self-attention* untuk memproses data sekuensial secara paralel.
Metode evaluasi dalam eksperimen *machine learning* dengan menghapus komponen tertentu untuk mengukur kontribusi bagian tersebut terhadap performa model.
Metrik evaluasi yang menghitung rata-rata *F1-score* secara global dengan menggabungkan nilai *true positive*, *false positive*, dan *false negative* dari seluruh kelas.
Metrik evaluasi yang menghitung *F1-score* untuk setiap kelas secara terpisah dan mengambil rata-rata sederhananya tanpa memedulikan ukuran frekuensi kelas.
Proses memecah teks menjadi unit-unit kecil yang disebut *token*, seperti kata atau suku kata.
Teknik kompresi model di mana model kecil dilatih untuk meniru perilaku model besar yang lebih kompleks.

background.en:
Digital government transformation requires automated processing of administrative documents at scale, where named entity recognition serves as a foundational component. However, Vietnamese natural language processing research faces a critical infrastructure gap because existing datasets focus on generic news or medical information rather than domain-specific administrative text. These existing resources exhibit entity type mismatches, structural incompatibilities with lengthy legal citations, and linguistic domain gaps regarding formal legal terminology.

Vietnamese administrative procedures also exhibit a domain paradox combining high syntactic normativity with structurally complex, nested entities such as long legal citations, ambiguous government agency names, and context-dependent generic terms. Rule-based systems fail on nested structures, while pure deep learning models using token-level classification struggle to enforce structural constraints. This creates an urgent need for domain-specific training infrastructure and hybrid modeling approaches.
background.id:
Transformasi pemerintahan digital memerlukan pemrosesan dokumen administratif secara otomatis pada skala besar, di mana *named entity recognition* berfungsi sebagai komponen dasar. Namun, penelitian *natural language processing* bahasa Vietnam menghadapi kesenjangan infrastruktur yang krusial karena *dataset* yang ada berfokus pada ekstraksi informasi umum seperti berita atau medis, alih-alih teks administratif spesifik domain. Sumber daya yang ada ini menunjukkan ketidakcocokan tipe entitas, ketidakcocokan struktural dengan kutipan hukum yang panjang, serta kesenjangan domain linguistik terkait terminologi hukum formal.

Prosedur administratif Vietnam juga menunjukkan paradoks domain yang menggabungkan normativitas sintaksis tinggi dengan entitas bertingkat yang kompleks secara struktural, seperti kutipan hukum yang panjang, nama instansi pemerintah yang ambigu, dan istilah generik yang bergantung konteks. Sistem berbasis aturan gagal pada struktur bertingkat, sementara *deep learning* murni yang menggunakan *token-level classification* kesulitan menegakkan batasan struktural. Hal ini menciptakan kebutuhan mendesak akan infrastruktur pelatihan spesifik domain dan pendekatan pemodelan hibrida.

contributions.en: The authors make three primary contributions to address the Vietnamese administrative NLP gap. First, they construct and release PAP_NER, a gold-standard corpus of 162,801 sentences with 205,807 entity annotations derived from real-world administrative procedures across five fine-grained entity types engineered for e-Government workflows. Second, they provide a comprehensive deployment-aware benchmark evaluating five established architectures under realistic operational constraints including a memory budget, latency limits, and data sovereignty requirements, demonstrating that PhoBERT-CRF achieves the best accuracy-efficiency balance. Third, they provide complete experimental documentation and public dataset release to support reproducibility and community extension.
contributions.id: Para penulis memberikan tiga kontribusi utama untuk mengatasi kesenjangan NLP administratif di Vietnam. Pertama, mereka membangun dan merilis *PAP_NER*, sebuah korpus standar emas yang terdiri dari 162.801 kalimat dengan 205.807 anotasi entitas yang berasal dari prosedur administratif dunia nyata di dalam lima tipe entitas berbutir halus yang dirancang untuk alur kerja *e-Government*. Kedua, mereka menyediakan *benchmark* komprehensif yang sadar penerapan untuk mengevaluasi lima arsitektur mapan di bawah kendala operasional realistis, termasuk anggaran memori, batas latensi, dan persyaratan kedaulatan data, yang menunjukkan bahwa *PhoBERT-CRF* mencapai keseimbangan akurasi-efisiensi terbaik. Ketiga, mereka menyediakan dokumentasi eksperimental yang lengkap dan rilis *dataset* publik untuk mendukung reprodubilitas dan ekstensi komunitas.

future_work.en: The authors note several limitations, including that the model is optimized for formal administrative text and performance may degrade on informal language, that geographic coverage is limited to four provinces, that the quantity class suffers from class imbalance, and that the BIO tagging scheme does not natively support nested or discontinuous entities. Future research directions include applying knowledge distillation for model compression to enable edge computing on resource-constrained devices, exploring domain adaptation techniques to handle informal citizen queries in chatbots, and investigating span-based or nested NER architectures for extracting fine-grained legal sub-components.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat beberapa keterbatasan, termasuk bahwa model dioptimalkan untuk teks administratif formal dan performanya dapat menurun pada bahasa informal, cakupan geografis terbatas pada empat provinsi, kelas kuantitas mengalami ketidakseimbangan kelas, serta skema penandaan *BIO* tidak secara natif mendukung entitas bertingkat atau diskontinu. Arah penelitian masa depan meliputi penerapan *knowledge distillation* untuk kompresi model guna mengaktifkan *edge computing* pada perangkat dengan sumber daya terbatas, mengeksplorasi teknik *domain adaptation* untuk menangani kueri warga yang informal pada *chatbot*, serta menyelidiki arsitektur NER berbasis rentang atau bertingkat untuk mengekstrak sub-komponen hukum berbutir halus.

method.en:
The PAP_NER dataset was constructed through a rigorous human-in-the-loop pipeline combining rule-based pre-annotation, LLM-assisted annotation with local PII masking, and expert human validation achieving a strong inter-annotator agreement. The data engineering pipeline also incorporated MinHash deduplication to prevent template leakage and source-stratified splitting by procedure ID. For modeling, the authors employ a dual-engine architecture comprising a semantic engine using the monolingual Transformer PhoBERT for contextual embeddings and a structural engine using a Conditional Random Field layer for sequence-level constraints.

Training utilized the AdamW optimizer with a systematic hyperparameter search, mixed precision, and learning rate warmups. Evaluation followed the CoNLL-2003 protocol using strict matching for precision, recall, and F1-score across micro and macro averaging schemes, complemented by partial, entity type, and exact matching modes as well as McNemar's test for statistical significance.
method.id:
Dataset *PAP_NER* dibangun melalui *pipeline* *human-in-the-loop* yang ketat, menggabungkan pra-anotasi berbasis aturan, anotasi berbantuan LLM dengan *masking* PII lokal, serta validasi manusia ahli yang mencapai *inter-annotator agreement* yang kuat. *Pipeline* rekayasa data juga menggabungkan deduplikasi *MinHash* untuk mencegah kebocoran templat dan *splitting* terstratifikasi berdasarkan ID prosedur. Untuk pemodelan, para penulis menggunakan arsitektur mesin ganda yang terdiri dari mesin semantik menggunakan *Transformer* monolingual *PhoBERT* untuk *contextual embeddings* dan mesin struktural menggunakan *Conditional Random Field* untuk batasan tingkat sekuens.

Pelatihan menggunakan *optimizer* *AdamW* dengan pencarian *hyperparameter* yang sistematis, presisi campuran, dan *learning rate warmup*. Evaluasi mengikuti protokol *CoNLL-2003* menggunakan *strict matching* untuk metrik *precision*, *recall*, dan *F1-score* pada skema *micro* dan *macro averaging*, dilengkapi dengan mode *partial*, *entity type*, dan *exact matching*, serta uji *McNemar* untuk signifikansi statistik.

related_work.en:
The evolution of named entity recognition has transitioned from statistical approaches to deep neural architectures. Early neural models such as BiLSTM+CRF became the standard for administrative text processing due to their low computational footprint and ability to enforce global constraints via conditional random fields, though they struggle with sequential bottlenecks and long-range dependencies. The introduction of Transformer-based models like BERT and RoBERTa revolutionized the field through self-attention and deep contextual embeddings, but standard architectures typically utilize simple token-level classification heads that fail in normative domains requiring strict state-transition rules.

Recent research has explored hybrid architectures fusing pre-trained encoders with probabilistic decoding layers to balance semantic understanding with structural validity, alongside low-resource NER adaptations using multilingual models or large language models. In the Vietnamese context, existing resources like VLSP datasets and PhoNER_COVID19 address generic news and medical domains respectively, but lack the administrative specificity and scale required for e-Government applications.
related_work.id:
Evolusi *named entity recognition* telah bertransisi dari pendekatan statistik ke arsitektur *deep neural*. Model neural awal seperti *BiLSTM+CRF* menjadi standar untuk pemrosesan teks administratif karena jejak komputasi yang rendah dan kemampuan menegakkan batasan global melalui *conditional random fields*, meskipun model tersebut kesulitan dengan hambatan sekuensial dan dependensi jangka panjang. Pengenalan model berbasis *Transformer* seperti *BERT* dan *RoBERTa* merevolusi bidang ini melalui *self-attention* dan *deep contextual embeddings*, namun arsitektur standar umumnya menggunakan *token-level classification heads* sederhana yang gagal pada domain normatif yang memerlukan aturan transisi status yang ketat.

Penelitian terbaru telah mengeksplorasi arsitektur hibrida yang memadukan *encoder* pra-latih dengan *probabilistic decoding layers* untuk menyeimbangkan pemahaman semantik dengan validitas struktural, di samping adaptasi NER *low-resource* menggunakan model multilinguas atau *large language models*. Dalam konteks bahasa Vietnam, sumber daya yang ada seperti *dataset* *VLSP* dan *PhoNER_COVID19* masing-masing berfokus pada domain berita umum dan medis, namun kekurangan spesifisitas administratif dan skala yang diperlukan untuk aplikasi *e-Government*.

results.en:
The hybrid PhoBERT-CRF model achieved the highest performance with a Micro F1-score of 97.95 percent, significantly outperforming BiLSTM+CRF, XLM-RoBERTa, Electra, and the pure PhoBERT Softmax baseline. Ablation analysis revealed that adding the CRF layer provided statistically significant improvements for structurally complex entities such as legal documents, improving strict F1 by 0.96 percent by resolving nested citation boundary fragmentation and suppressing false positive noisy citations.

Per-entity analysis showed near-perfect recognition for datetimes while highlighting challenges in ambiguous objects and hierarchical agency names. Computational analysis confirmed that the CRF layer added only a negligible latency overhead of 1.6 milliseconds and 2 megabytes in model size, keeping the system well within real-time thresholds.
results.id:
Model hibrida *PhoBERT-CRF* mencapai performa tertinggi dengan *Micro F1-score* sebesar 97,95 persen, mengungguli *BiLSTM+CRF*, *XLM-RoBERTa*, *Electra*, dan *baseline* *PhoBERT* *Softmax* murni secara signifikan. Analisis ablasi mengungkapkan bahwa penambahan *layer* *CRF* memberikan peningkatan yang secara statistik signifikan untuk entitas yang kompleks secara struktural seperti dokumen hukum, meningkatkan *strict F1* sebesar 0,96 persen dengan menyelesaikan fragmentasi batas kutipan bersarang dan menekan kutipan bising positif palsu.

Analisis per entitas menunjukkan pengenalan yang nyaris sempurna untuk tanggal-waktu sekaligus menyoroti tantangan pada objek yang ambigu dan nama instansi hierarkis. Analisis komputasi mengonfirmasi bahwa *layer* *CRF* hanya menambahkan overhead latensi yang dapat diabaikan sebesar 1,6 milidetik dan ukuran model sebesar 2 megabita, menjaga sistem agar tetap berada di dalam ambang batas *real-time*.

tldr.en: This paper presents PAP_NER, a large-scale Vietnamese administrative named entity recognition corpus, and benchmarks a PhoBERT-CRF hybrid architecture. The proposed model achieves a 97.95 percent Micro F1-score, significantly outperforming established baselines on domain-specific administrative tasks.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan PAP_NER, yaitu korpus *named entity recognition* administratif bahasa Vietnam berskala besar, dan melakukan *benchmarking* pada arsitektur hibrida *PhoBERT-CRF*. Model yang diusulkan mencapai *Micro F1-score* sebesar 97,95 persen dan mengungguli *baseline* yang ada secara signifikan pada tugas administratif spesifik domain.

doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0353166.title: PAP_NER: A large-scale vietnamese administrative named entity recognition corpus and hybrid deep learning architecture

doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0354875.abstract: Hate speech detection in low-resource and informally written languages remains a significant challenge due to the lack of annotated corpora, orthographic variability, and complex code-mixing. Roman Urdu a non-standardized variant of Urdu written in the Latin script exemplifies these linguistic hurdles. In this paper, we propose LEXF-ATT-XLM, a novel hybrid deep learning architecture that synergizes contextual language modeling with explicit domain knowledge. Our model leverages XLM-RoBERTa for deep contextual embeddings, passed through a two-layer Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) and a multi-head attention mechanism to capture both sequential and salient linguistic patterns. Crucially, the pooled representations are fused via a learnable gating layer (Linear + tanh) before final classification. Furthermore, we integrate a domain specific Roman Urdu hate lexicon as an auxiliary regression supervision signal within a multi task learning framework to guide the model's focus. Evaluated on the RU-HSD-30K dataset using 3-fold stratified cross-validation, the proposed model achieves an average accuracy of 88.83% and a weighted F1 score of 88.83%, with fold wise weighted F1-scores of 88.58%, 89.19%, and 88.71%. Extensive ablation studies confirm that the lexicon-guided auxiliary supervision significantly enhances the model's ability to handle lexical variations, negations, and informal spelling. These findings demonstrate the robust effectiveness of our approach in addressing the unique linguistic challenges of Roman Urdu hate speech detection.

glossary.explanation_id: Sebuah *model* bahasa multibahasa berbasis *transformer* yang dilatih sebelumnya pada korpus besar dalam berbagai bahasa.
Arsitektur *recurrent neural network* yang memproses urutan teks secara dua arah, yaitu maju dan mundur.
Paradigma pembelajaran mesin di mana sebuah *model* dilatih untuk menyelesaikan beberapa tugas secara bersamaan guna meningkatkan generalisasi.
Eksperimen di mana bagian tertentu dari *model* dihapus secara sistematis untuk mengukur kontribusi komponen tersebut terhadap performa keseluruhan.
Fenomena di mana sinyal informasi penting yang berdensitas rendah dikaburkan oleh representasi fitur berdimensi tinggi.
Teknik *evaluasi* *model* di mana data dibagi menjadi beberapa bagian dengan proporsi kelas yang tetap sama di setiap bagiannya.
Tugas regresi tambahan yang ditambahkan ke *model* utama untuk memberikan sinyal supervisi sekunder selama pelatihan.

background.en:
Detecting hate speech in low-resource and informally written languages remains a significant challenge due to the lack of annotated corpora, orthographic variability, and complex code-mixing. Roman Urdu, a non-standardized variant of Urdu written in the Latin script, exemplifies these linguistic hurdles with high lexical variability and multiple spelling variants for a single concept. Most current models consider contextual and lexical signals as separate entities without considering sequence-level contingencies, and existing hybrid architectures often suffer from feature dilution when using basic feature concatenation.

To bridge these research gaps, the authors propose a structured and learnable form of interaction between deep contextual embeddings and explicit domain-specific lexical cues, specifically targeting the unique characteristics of Roman Urdu such as informal spellings, negations, and implicit slurs.
background.id:
Deteksi ujaran kebencian dalam bahasa yang minim sumber daya dan ditulis secara informal tetap menjadi tantangan besar karena kurangnya korpus beranotasi, variabilitas ortografis, dan percampuran kode yang kompleks. Bahasa Roman Urdu, sebagai varian Urdu yang tidak terstandarisasi dan ditulis dalam aksara Latin, menunjukkan hambatan linguistik ini dengan variabilitas leksikal yang tinggi dan berbagai varian ejaan untuk satu konsep tunggal. Sebagian besar *model* saat ini menganggap sinyal kontekstual dan leksikal sebagai entitas terpisah tanpa mempertimbangkan kontinjensi tingkat *sequence*, dan arsitektur hibrida yang ada sering kali mengalami *feature dilution* saat menggunakan penggabungan fitur dasar.

Untuk menjembatani kesenjangan penelitian ini, para penulis mengusulkan bentuk interaksi yang terstruktur dan dapat dipelajari antara *embeddings* kontekstual yang mendalam dan isyarat leksikal khusus domain yang eksplisit, dengan menargetkan karakteristik unik Roman Urdu seperti ejaan informal, negasi, dan *slurs* implisit.

contributions.en:
The paper introduces LEXF-ATT-XLM, a novel hybrid architecture that synergizes contextual language modeling with explicit domain knowledge. Its key contributions include a new hybrid model combining XLM-RoBERTa, BiGRU, and multi-head attention fused via a learnable gating layer (Linear + tanh) to capture semantic context and localized dependencies without feature dilution.

Additionally, the authors utilize a multi-task learning setup where domain-related hate lexicon scores act as an auxiliary regression signal to regularize the network. They also design a specialized preprocessing approach featuring negation-prefix transformations to preserve polarity and syntactic dependencies, ensuring robust handling of Roman Urdu text.
contributions.id:
Makalah ini memperkenalkan LEXF-ATT-XLM, sebuah arsitektur hibrida baru yang memadukan *pemodelan bahasa* kontekstual dengan pengetahuan domain yang eksplisit. Kontribusi utamanya mencakup *model* hibrida baru yang menggabungkan XLM-RoBERTa, BiGRU, dan *multi-head attention* yang digabungkan melalui *gating layer* yang dapat dipelajari (Linear + tanh) untuk menangkap konteks semantik dan dependensi lokal tanpa *feature dilution*.

Selain itu, para penulis menggunakan pengaturan *multi-task learning* di mana skor leksikon kebencian yang terkait dengan domain bertindak sebagai sinyal regresi sekunder untuk meregulasi jaringan. Mereka juga merancang pendekatan *preprocessing* khusus yang menampilkan transformasi awalan negasi untuk mempertahankan polaritas dan dependensi sintaksis, memastikan penanganan teks Roman Urdu yang tangguh.

future_work.en: The authors note that statistical testing such as paired t-tests over folds or confidence intervals using bootstrapping was not carried out and is left for subsequent work. Future efforts will also be directed towards extending the multi-task framework to multi-class conditions to detect fine-grained hate classes, incorporating multimodal data, integrating additional pragmatic features, sentiment cues, emoji or token context, conversation structure, and attention weight visualization.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa pengujian statistik seperti *paired t-tests* pada setiap *fold* atau *confidence intervals* menggunakan *bootstrapping* tidak dilakukan dan diserahkan untuk penelitian selanjutnya. Upaya di masa mendatang juga akan diarahkan untuk memperluas kerangka *multi-task* ke kondisi *multi-class* untuk mendeteksi kelas kebencian yang lebih terperinci, memasukkan data multimodal, mengintegrasikan fitur pragmatis tambahan, isyarat sentimen, konteks *emoji* atau *token*, struktur percakapan, dan visualisasi bobot *attention*.

method.en:
The study operates on the RU-HSD-30K dataset consisting of 30,000 Roman Urdu tweets annotated into Hate and Normal categories. The preprocessing pipeline includes character normalization, special character removal, lowercase conversion, and negation-prefix transformation (using a not_ marker) to preserve polarity semantics while keeping canonical forms for lexicon lookup.

The model architecture feeds preprocessed tokens into XLM-RoBERTa for contextual embeddings, passes them through a two-layer BiGRU and a multi-head attention mechanism, and fuses the representations via a learnable gating layer. A multi-task learning framework is employed, jointly optimizing a primary binary cross-entropy classification loss and an auxiliary mean squared error loss for predicting lexicon hate intensity scores, using a weight alpha of 0.1. Evaluation is conducted using 3-fold stratified cross-validation.
method.id:
Penelitian ini menggunakan *dataset* RU-HSD-30K yang terdiri dari 30.000 *tweet* Roman Urdu yang dianotasi ke dalam kategori *Hate* dan *Normal*. *Pipeline* *preprocessing* mencakup normalisasi karakter, penghilangan karakter khusus, konversi huruf kecil, dan transformasi awalan negasi (menggunakan penanda not_) untuk mempertahankan semantik polaritas sambil menjaga bentuk kanonis untuk pencarian leksikon.

Arsitektur *model* memasukkan *tokens* yang telah diproses ke dalam XLM-RoBERTa untuk *embeddings* kontekstual, melewatkannya melalui BiGRU dua lapisan dan mekanisme *multi-head attention*, serta menggabungkan representasi tersebut melalui *gating layer* yang dapat dipelajari. Kerangka *multi-task learning* digunakan, secara bersamaan mengoptimalkan fungsi kerugian klasifikasi *binary cross-entropy* utama dan kerugian *mean squared error* sekunder untuk memprediksi skor intensitas kebencian leksikon, menggunakan bobot alfa sebesar 0.1. Evaluasi dilakukan menggunakan *3-fold stratified cross-validation*.

related_work.en:
Prior studies on Roman Urdu hate speech detection explored various datasets and models, including augmented datasets like RUSOLD, RUT, and RU-HSD-30K using attention-based Bi-LSTM models. Other recent approaches investigated transformer architectures such as BERT-RU and Passion-Net, as well as multilingual versions and paradigms integrating mBERT with traditional classifiers like Support Vector Machines and Random Forests.

Despite these developments, the authors point out key limitations in prior work: most models treat contextual and lexical signals independently, lexicon-based cues are underutilized in transformer pipelines, negation handling and fine-grained intensity modeling are often absent, and few works incorporate auxiliary supervision or explicitly guide models using hate lexicon gradients.
related_work.id:
Studi sebelumnya mengenai deteksi ujaran kebencian dalam bahasa Roman Urdu mengeksplorasi berbagai *dataset* dan *model*, termasuk *dataset* teraugmentasi seperti RUSOLD, RUT, dan RU-HSD-30K menggunakan *model* Bi-LSTM berbasis *attention*. Pendekatan terbaru lainnya meneliti arsitektur *transformer* seperti BERT-RU dan Passion-Net, serta versi multibahasa dan paradigma yang mengintegrasikan mBERT dengan pengklasifikasi tradisional seperti *Support Vector Machines* dan *Random Forests*.

Meskipun ada perkembangan ini, para penulis menunjukkan keterbatasan utama dalam pekerjaan sebelumnya: sebagian besar *model* memperlakukan sinyal kontekstual dan leksikal secara independen, isyarat berbasis leksikon kurang dimanfaatkan dalam *pipeline* *transformer*, penanganan negasi dan pemodelan intensitas berbutir halus sering kali tidak ada, dan sedikit penelitian yang memasukkan supervisi sekunder atau secara eksplisit memandu *model* menggunakan gradien leksikon kebencian.

results.en:
Evaluated on the RU-HSD-30K dataset using 3-fold stratified cross-validation, the proposed LEXF-ATT-XLM model achieves an average accuracy of 88.83% and an average weighted F1-score of 88.83%, with fold-wise weighted F1-scores of 88.58%, 89.19%, and 88.71%. Class-wise F1-scores are balanced with 88.94% for the Hate class and 88.71% for the Non-Hate class.

Ablation studies confirm the cumulative efficacy of the components, showing that removing the lexicon supervision drops the weighted F1 to 0.8603 (-3.15%), while removing BiGRU or multi-head attention also results in performance drops. Qualitative analysis demonstrates that the model successfully identifies explicit hate speech and captures contextual hate without keyword matches, though subtle sarcasm and implicit hate remain challenging.
results.id:
Dievaluasi pada *dataset* RU-HSD-30K menggunakan *3-fold stratified cross-validation*, *model* LEXF-ATT-XLM yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi rata-rata sebesar 88.83% dan *weighted* F1-*score* rata-rata sebesar 88.83%, dengan *weighted* F1-*score* per *fold* masing-masing 88.58%, 89.19%, dan 88.71%. *F1-score* per kelas seimbang dengan 88.94% untuk kelas *Hate* dan 88.71% untuk kelas *Non-Hate*.

Studi ablasi mengonfirmasi efikasi kumulatif dari komponen-komponen tersebut, menunjukkan bahwa menghapus supervisi leksikon menurunkan *weighted* F1 menjadi 0.8603 (-3.15%), sementara menghapus BiGRU atau *multi-head attention* juga menghasilkan penurunan performa. Analisis kualitatif menunjukkan bahwa *model* berhasil mengidentifikasi ujaran kebencian eksplisit dan menangkap kebencian kontekstual tanpa kecocokan kata kunci, meskipun sarkasme halus dan kebencian implisit masih menjadi tantangan.

tldr.en: This paper proposes LEXF-ATT-XLM, a hybrid deep learning model for hate speech detection in Roman Urdu that combines contextual embeddings with a lexicon-guided auxiliary supervision. Evaluated on the RU-HSD-30K dataset, the model achieves an average weighted F1-score of 88.83% and demonstrates robust effectiveness against linguistic hurdles.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan LEXF-ATT-XLM, sebuah *model* *deep learning* hibrida untuk deteksi ujaran kebencian dalam bahasa Roman Urdu yang menggabungkan *embeddings* kontekstual dengan supervisi sekunder berbasis leksikon. Dievaluasi pada *dataset* RU-HSD-30K, *model* ini mencapai rata-rata *weighted* F1-*score* sebesar 88.83% dan menunjukkan efektivitas yang tangguh dalam menghadapi kendala linguistik.

doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0354875.title: LEXF-ATT-XLM: A hybrid lexicon-enhanced attention model for hate speech detection in low-resource language Roman Urdu

doi:10.14203/widyariset.12.3.2009.17-26.abstract: This research aims to investigate relationship between education indicator represented by literacy rate and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) real per capita as economic performance with annual data during period of 1980 until 2008 in Indonesia. The analysis method used in this research was Vector Auto Regression (VAR) with Granger Causality Test, Impulse Responses, and Variance Decomposition. In addition, Akaike and Schwarz Information Criterion determined optimum lag of 6 that could be estimated. Granger causality test showed literacy rate significantly Granger-caused GDP real per capita, but there was no significant Granger causality from GDP real per capita to literacy rate over research period. One of crucial implications of this research results is that we must and still need to make the highest priority of base education development especiallyliterate promotion so that high level of economic performance could be equally generated in improving the prosperity of Indonesian societies.

doi:10.14203/widyariset.12.3.2009.53-60.abstract: The objective of this research is to find out some idiomatic expressions in Minangkabau viewedf rom aspect form and meaning. The method used in this study is qualitative based on content analysis technique. Research findings are 27 idioms which consist of verbal idioms and nominal idioms. Verbal idioms may appear in (1) theconstruction VERB + NOUN as examplified by malapeh ao `to get no benefit' and (2) the contruction ADVERB + VERB as examplified by alah ilang 'to die'. Meanwhile, the construction of nominal idioms are three types: (1) NOUN + NOUN as examplified by kaeang miang fink, (2) NOUN + ADJECTIVE as exemplified kabau gadang'lazybones', and (3) ADJECTIVE + NOUN as examplified gadang kalang `coward'.
doi:10.14203/widyariset.12.3.2009.53-60.title: UNGKAPAN IDIOMATIS DALAM BUDAYA MASYARAKAT MINANGKABAU

doi:10.14203/widyariset.13.1.2010.173-18.abstract: The study of Morphophonemic on Javanese of Banyumas Dialect is part of phonology and morphology. Morphophonemic process is the change processes of morphemic form in the process of morphologic, either affixation, clitich, composition, reduplication or internal modification. To answer the problems in this study, the writer uses the structural theory and qualitative descriptive approach. The result of the study shows that morphophonemic process in Javanese of Banyumas Dialect occurred on affixation and internal modification cause the process of phonemic as the change of phoneme, phoneme appearance, phoneme omission, and phoneme perpetuation. One of four kinds of phonemic processes that mostly occured in morphophonemic process is affixation and internal modification process seldom occured.

doi:10.14445/22312803/ijctt-v74i7p105.abstract: One of the basic Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks is Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging, which helps in various applications like sentiment analysis and information retrieval. However, creating accurate POS taggers for low-resource African languages continues to be difficult due to the scarcity of linguistic resources that are annotated. Its contribution is a deep learning method for POS tagging of Dholuo, a less-resourced Western Nilotic language, spoken by about four million people in Kenya and Tanzania. The suggested system uses DistilBERT, a small transformer model, in addition to FastText and Word2Vec vector representations of words that are used to capture the context and meaning of a word. The KenCorpus Dholuo POS dataset was carefully preprocessed, normalized, and standardized with the Universal POS tags and balanced using a hybrid resampling strategy to bring about class representation. The proposed method combines contextual transformer representations with complementary word representations and a training strategy that is optimized for the linguistic features of Dholuo, while previous studies primarily used multilingual transformer models or traditional sequence-labeling methods. The framework developed is a computationally efficient one that is well-suited for low-resource language processing. The results of the experiments reveal that the proposed DistilBERT-based model outperforms the baseline Conditional Random Field (CRF) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) models with an accuracy 79.05%, precision 80.63%, recall 79.05% and F1-score 79.24%. To our best knowledge, these results are the best reported for Dholuo POS tagging, and for under-resourced languages in Africa in general, highlighting the suitability of lightweight transformer architectures.
doi:10.14445/22312803/ijctt-v74i7p105.journal_ref: International Journal of Computer Trends and Technology

glossary.explanation_id: Proses pemberian label kategori gramatikal pada setiap kata dalam sebuah kalimat.
Sifat morfologis bahasa di mana kata dibentuk dengan menggabungkan beberapa morfem imbuhan tanpa mengubah bentuk dasarnya.
Representasi vektor numerik dari kata atau token yang menangkap makna semantik dan kontekstualnya.
Teknik penyesuaian distribusi data dengan menambah atau mengurangi sampel untuk mengatasi masalah *class imbalance*.
Arsitektur *deep learning* yang mengandalkan mekanisme *self-attention* untuk memproses data sekuensial secara paralel.
Parameter eksternal yang nilainya diset sebelum proses pelatihan model dimulai untuk mengontrol jalannya pembelajaran.
Kondisi di mana model *machine learning* mempelajari data latih terlalu baik sehingga gagal melakukan generalisasi pada data baru.
Model standar atau metode pembanding yang digunakan sebagai tolok ukur kinerja untuk model baru yang diusulkan.

background.en: Part-of-Speech tagging is a fundamental preprocessing task in natural language processing that assigns grammatical categories to tokens in a sentence. However, creating accurate POS taggers for low-resource African languages remains challenging due to the scarcity of annotated linguistic resources. This challenge is especially severe for Dholuo, a Western Nilotic language spoken by about four million people, because of its agglutinative structure, tones, and lexical ambiguity.
background.id: *Part-of-Speech tagging* adalah tugas *preprocessing* fundamental dalam *natural language processing* yang menetapkan kategori gramatikal pada *token* dalam sebuah kalimat. Namun, membuat *POS tagger* yang akurat untuk bahasa-bahasa di Afrika yang ber-*status low-resource* tetap menjadi tantangan karena kelangkaan sumber daya linguistik beranotasi. Tantangan ini sangat parah bagi bahasa Dholuo, sebuah bahasa Nilotic barat yang dituturkan oleh sekitar empat juta orang, karena struktur aglutinatif, nada, dan ambiguitas leksikalnya.

contributions.en: This study introduces a novel deep learning framework for Dholuo POS tagging that integrates DistilBERT with FastText subword embeddings and Word2Vec distributional semantics. It explicitly addresses agglutination by breaking words into subwords and implements a two-stage tag standardization and mixed resampling pipeline to transform 70 fine-grained tags into 12 balanced classes.
contributions.id: Studi ini memperkenalkan kerangka *deep learning* baru untuk *POS tagging* bahasa Dholuo yang mengintegrasikan DistilBERT dengan *subword embedding* FastText dan *semantik distribusional* Word2Vec. Pendekatan ini secara eksplisit mengatasi aglutinasi dengan memecah kata menjadi *subword* dan mengimplementasikan *pipeline* standardisasi tag dua tahap serta *mixed resampling* untuk mengubah 70 tag berbutir halus menjadi 12 kelas seimbang.

future_work.en: The authors suggest expanding the corpus with more varied text sources, testing advanced data augmentation and cross-lingual transfer learning methods, developing large-scale pre-trained language models tailored for Dholuo or Africa, and integrating a rule-based or statistical morphological analyzer built with linguists to explicitly segment agglutinated forms.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyarankan untuk memperluas korpus dengan sumber teks yang lebih bervariasi, menguji metode *data augmentation* tingkat lanjut dan *cross-lingual transfer learning*, mengembangkan *pre-trained language model* skala besar yang disesuaikan untuk Dholuo atau Afrika, serta mengintegrasikan *morphological analyzer* berbasis aturan atau statistik yang dibangun bersama para linguis untuk melakukan segmentasi bentuk aglutinasi secara eksplisit.

method.en: The study utilized the KenCorpus Dholuo POS dataset containing 4,794 sentences and 53,357 tokens, preprocessing them through whitespace normalization and mapping fine-grained tags to 12 universal POS categories. A hybrid resampling strategy balanced the dataset to 3,808 instances per class, resulting in 45,696 tokens total. The architecture modifies a 6-layer DistilBERT-base-cased model by concatenating FastText and Word2Vec token vectors at the embedding layer, optimized end-to-end using the AdamW optimizer and cross-entropy loss.
method.id: Studi ini menggunakan *dataset* KenCorpus Dholuo POS yang berisi 4.794 kalimat dan 53.357 *token*, melakukan *preprocessing* melalui *whitespace normalization* dan pemetaan tag berbutir halus ke 12 kategori POS universal. Strategi *hybrid resampling* menyeimbangkan *dataset* menjadi 3.808 *instance* per kelas, menghasilkan total 45.696 *token*. Arsitektur ini memodifikasi model DistilBERT-base-cased 6 lapis dengan menggabungkan *token vector* FastText dan Word2Vec pada *embedding layer*, serta dioptimalkan secara *end-to-end* menggunakan *optimizer* AdamW dan *cross-entropy loss*.

related_work.en: Prior approaches to POS tagging relied on traditional machine learning and statistical methods such as Hidden Markov Models, Conditional Random Fields, Support Vector Machines, and memory-based learning, which depend on hand-crafted features and struggle with unseen words and complex morphology. Recent deep learning methods include BiLSTM and CNN models, alongside large multilingual transformer models like BERT and AfroXLMR. However, these prior models often face limitations with class imbalance, high computational demands, or insufficient tailoring to specific low-resource morphologies.
related_work.id: Pendekatan terdahulu untuk *POS tagging* mengandalkan *machine learning* tradisional dan metode statistik seperti *Hidden Markov Model*, *Conditional Random Field*, *Support Vector Machine*, dan *memory-based learning*, yang bergantung pada *hand-crafted features* serta kesulitan menangani *unseen words* dan morfologi kompleks. Metode *deep learning* baru-baru ini mencakup model BiLSTM dan CNN, beserta *multilingual transformer model* besar seperti BERT dan AfroXLMR. Namun, model-model terdahulu ini sering kali menghadapi keterbatasan dengan *class imbalance*, kebutuhan komputasi yang tinggi, atau penyesuaian yang kurang terhadap morfologi *low-resource* tertentu.

results.en: The proposed DistilBERT-based model achieved an accuracy of 79.05%, precision of 80.63%, recall of 79.05%, and an F1-score of 79.24%, significantly outperforming the CRF and BiLSTM baselines. Two-proportion significance tests confirmed that these performance gains were statistically significant with p-values less than 0.001. Qualitative error analysis identified issues related to agglutination misclassification of pronouns, context-dependent homograph errors, and minority class under-detection.
results.id: Model berbasis DistilBERT yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi 79,05%, *precision* 80,63%, *recall* 79,05%, dan *F1-score* 79,24%, yang secara signifikan mengungguli *baseline* CRF dan BiLSTM. Uji signifikansi dua proporsi mengonfirmasi bahwa peningkatan performa ini signifikan secara statistik dengan *p-value* kurang dari 0,001. Analisis kesalahan kualitatif mengidentifikasi masalah yang berkaitan dengan salah klasifikasi aglutinasi pada pronomina, kesalahan *homograph* yang bergantung konteks, dan deteksi kurang pada *minority class*.

tldr.en: This paper proposes a DistilBERT-based deep learning model combined with FastText and Word2Vec embeddings for Part-of-Speech tagging in the low-resource Dholuo language. The proposed approach achieves superior accuracy and F1-score compared to traditional baseline models like CRF and BiLSTM.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan *deep learning model* berbasis DistilBERT yang dikombinasikan dengan *embedding* FastText dan Word2Vec untuk *Part-of-Speech tagging* pada bahasa Dholuo yang ber-*status low-resource*. Pendekatan yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi dan *F1-score* yang lebih unggul dibandingkan *baseline model* tradisional seperti CRF dan BiLSTM.

doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i7p110.abstract: Reading proficiency is considered a critical educational challenge in a highly multilingual nation such as the Philippines. Digital literacy tools available on the market and those that are found in the literature are mostly English-centric and often lack interactive mechanisms. This study shows the design, technical validation, and implementation of the iRead mobile application software. It is a multilingual mobile reading platform with offline speech recognition function available for three languages, specifically English, Filipino, and Hiligaynon. The mobile application was developed specifically for the Android Operating System using the Flutter framework, while the Vosk API was used for the speech recognition engine. Publicly available pretrained speech recognition models were utilized for English and Filipino languages, while a novel baseline small-vocabulary speech recognition model for Hiligaynon was developed and trained from scratch. A Gaussian Mixture Model-Hidden Markov Model (GMM-HMM) pipeline within the Kaldi framework was then used to form the Hiligaynon speech recognition model. Recognition vocabulary was limited to a 380-word phonics-based lexicon that is aligned with early literacy instruction. Cross-speaker generalization for Hiligaynon was evaluated using a leave-one-speaker-out cross-validation technique across four speakers. Recognition stability was further assessed using standard deviation and confidence interval analysis. The overall system evaluation was conducted using 540 utterances across the three languages under controlled conditions. Recognition performance achieved average accuracies of 92.8% for English, 88.3% for Filipino, and 85.6% for Hiligaynon. Category-level analysis demonstrated the highest performance for vowels, followed by consonants, then consonant–vowel blends. Results suggest that a classical small-vocabulary acoustic model combined with grammar-constrained decoding is technically viable and deployment-ready in a multilingual offline speech-supported literacy app for low-resource educational settings.

Proses penerjemahan suara ke teks yang dibatasi oleh aturan tata bahasa atau kosa kata tertentu untuk mengurangi kesalahan.
Metode validasi silang di mana data dari satu penutur digunakan sebagai pengujian sementara sisanya digunakan untuk pelatihan.
Komponen dalam sistem pengenalan suara yang merepresentasikan hubungan antara sinyal audio dan unit fonetik.

background.en: Reading proficiency in early education is a critical challenge in multilingual nations like the Philippines, where students often struggle with comprehension and decoding. Existing digital literacy tools are predominantly English-centric, lack interactive features, and frequently require internet connectivity, making them impractical for remote or underserved schools.
background.id: Kemampuan membaca pada pendidikan anak usia dini merupakan tantangan kritis di negara-negara multilinguistik seperti Filipina, di mana siswa sering kali mengalami kesulitan dalam pemahaman dan *decoding*. Alat literasi digital yang ada sebagian besar berpusat pada bahasa Inggris, kurang memiliki fitur interaktif, dan sering kali memerlukan koneksi internet, sehingga tidak praktis untuk sekolah di daerah terpencil atau kurang terlayani.

contributions.en: The study introduces iRead, a mobile application designed to support early literacy in three languages with full offline functionality. Its primary novelty lies in developing a novel small-vocabulary acoustic model for Hiligaynon trained from scratch using child speech data, integrated alongside pretrained models for English and Filipino within a grammar-constrained decoding framework.
contributions.id: Studi ini memperkenalkan iRead, sebuah aplikasi seluler yang dirancang untuk mendukung literasi dini dalam tiga bahasa dengan fungsionalitas *offline* penuh. Kebaruan utamanya terletak pada pengembangan *acoustic model* *small-vocabulary* yang baru untuk bahasa Hiligaynon yang dilatih dari awal menggunakan data ucapan anak, yang diintegrasikan bersama *pretrained model* untuk bahasa Inggris dan Filipina dalam kerangka kerja *grammar-constrained* *decoding*.

future_work.en: The authors note limitations including a small training dataset for Hiligaynon from only four speakers, a focus on isolated single-word phonics tasks rather than continuous speech, and a lack of longitudinal educational outcome assessments. Future work includes expanding training data for better accent and age-group generalization, supporting longer speech inputs such as sentences and paragraphs, and conducting real-world classroom evaluations.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat keterbatasan termasuk *dataset* pelatihan yang kecil untuk bahasa Hiligaynon dari hanya empat penutur, fokus pada tugas fonik kata tunggal terisolasi daripada ucapan kontinu, dan kurangnya penilaian hasil pendidikan longitudinal. Pekerjaan di masa mendatang mencakup memperluas data pelatihan untuk generalisasi aksen dan kelompok usia yang lebih baik, mendukung masukan ucapan yang lebih panjang seperti kalimat dan paragraf, serta melakukan evaluasi kelas di dunia nyata.

method.en: The iRead application was developed for Android using the Flutter framework, utilizing the Vosk API with Kaldi-based acoustic models for offline speech recognition. For Hiligaynon, a small-vocabulary dataset of 380 phonics-based words was collected from four child speakers, and a GMM-HMM pipeline was employed for training using Leave-One-Speaker-Out cross-validation. The system evaluation utilized 540 total utterances across English, Filipino, and Hiligaynon under controlled conditions.
method.id: Aplikasi iRead dikembangkan untuk Android menggunakan *framework* Flutter, dengan memanfaatkan API Vosk dan *acoustic model* berbasis Kaldi untuk *offline speech recognition*. Untuk bahasa Hiligaynon, *dataset* *small-vocabulary* yang terdiri dari 380 kata berbasis fonik dikumpulkan dari empat penutur anak, dan *pipeline* *GMM-HMM* digunakan untuk pelatihan dengan validasi silang *Leave-One-Speaker-Out*. Evaluasi sistem menggunakan total 540 ujaran di bahasa Inggris, Filipina, dan Hiligaynon di bawah kondisi terkontrol.

related_work.en: Prior mobile reading applications developed in the Philippines mostly focused on English or limited combinations of English and Filipino, with minimal support for regional languages such as Hiligaynon and Bisaya. Furthermore, these existing tools generally lacked offline capabilities, culturally relevant content, and integrated speech recognition for local languages.
related_work.id: Aplikasi membaca seluler sebelumnya yang dikembangkan di Filipina sebagian besar berfokus pada bahasa Inggris atau kombinasi terbatas antara bahasa Inggris dan Filipina, dengan dukungan minimal untuk bahasa regional seperti Hiligaynon dan Bisaya. Selain itu, alat-alat yang ada ini umumnya tidak memiliki kemampuan *offline*, konten yang relevan secara budaya, dan pengenalan suara terintegrasi untuk bahasa lokal.

results.en: Evaluation results showed average recognition accuracies of 92.8 percent for English, 88.3 percent for Filipino, and 85.6 percent for Hiligaynon, with Leave-One-Speaker-Out validation showing high consistency for Hiligaynon. Category-level analysis revealed that vowels achieved the highest accuracy, followed by consonants and consonant-vowel blends, demonstrating that a classical GMM-HMM approach combined with grammar-constrained decoding is viable for low-resource mobile literacy applications.
results.id: Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan akurasi pengenalan rata-rata sebesar 92,8 persen untuk bahasa Inggris, 88.3 persen untuk bahasa Filipina, dan 85.6 persen untuk bahasa Hiligaynon, dengan validasi *Leave-One-Speaker-Out* yang menunjukkan konsistensi tinggi untuk Hiligaynon. Analisis tingkat kategori mengungkapkan bahwa vokal mencapai akurasi tertinggi, diikuti oleh konsonan dan *consonant-vowel blends*, yang menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan *GMM-HMM* klasik yang dikombinasikan dengan *grammar-constrained* *decoding* layak untuk aplikasi literasi seluler *low-resource*.

tldr.en: This paper presents iRead, a multilingual mobile reading application featuring integrated offline speech recognition for English, Filipino, and Hiligaynon. Evaluations demonstrate that the small-vocabulary system achieves high recognition accuracies across all three languages.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan iRead, sebuah aplikasi membaca seluler multilinguistik yang dilengkapi *offline speech recognition* terintegrasi untuk bahasa Inggris, Filipina, dan Hiligaynon. Evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa sistem *small-vocabulary* ini mencapai akurasi pengenalan yang tinggi di ketiga bahasa.

doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p116.abstract: Evaluating linguistically diverse descriptive answers in a consistent and accurate manner in modern digital education systems is a growing challenge, especially in low-resource languages like Hindi. Traditional lexical and rule-based grading systems cannot adequately reflect the meaning behind the words, negation, paraphrasing, and so on, which leads to low grading reliability. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an automated evaluation framework with intelligent rule-based linguistic preprocessing and transformer-based deep learning. The framework uses a fine-tuned multilingual BERT (mBERT) model bhavikardeshna/multilingual-bert-base-cased-hindi to provide contextual embeddings, and cosine similarity-based semantic alignment with the model l3cube-pune/hindi-sentence-similarity-sbert is used to provide automated scores. With optimal setting of learning rate = 5×10⁻⁴, batch size = 24 and epochs = 40, accuracy, precision, recall and F1 score of 78.9%, 80.6%, 77.4% and 79.0% respectively is achieved on HindiRC-Data-master dataset (24 passages, 127 question-answer pairs, grades 2-5) which is more than 14% higher than lexical similarity baselines and is better than previous Hindi QA architectures without domain-specific preprocessing pipelines. The suggested system will save about 40% manual grading, and will enable scalable, consistent and repeatable assessment.

glossary.explanation_id: Arsitektur *deep learning* yang sepenuhnya mengandalkan mekanisme *attention* untuk memproses data sekuensial secara paralel.
Model bahasa BERT multibahasa yang dilatih pada korpus dari banyak bahasa termasuk bahasa Indonesia dan Hindi.
Modifikasi dari arsitektur BERT yang menggunakan *siamese network* untuk menghasilkan *embedding* kalimat yang efisien untuk tugas penghitungan kemiripan.
Proses memecah teks masukan menjadi unit-unit kecil yang disebut *token* seperti kata atau subkata sebelum diproses oleh model.
Proses pengubahan bentuk infleksi suatu kata kembali ke bentuk dasar atau kamusnya yang disebut *lemma*.

Proses pencarian pengaturan parameter pelatihan terbaik seperti *learning rate* dan *batch size* untuk mengoptimalkan performa model.
Proses melatih ulang model bahasa yang sudah dilatih sebelumnya pada *dataset* spesifik domain tertentu.

background.en:
Evaluating linguistically diverse descriptive answers consistently and accurately in modern digital education systems is a growing challenge, especially in low-resource languages like Hindi. Traditional lexical and rule-based grading systems fail to capture underlying meanings, negations, and paraphrasing, resulting in low grading reliability. Furthermore, manual grading is time-consuming, highly subjective, and prone to significant inter-rater variability across large volumes of student assessments.

This paper addresses the gap by providing a fully automated evaluation pipeline tailored for Hindi descriptive answers in primary education. Hindi poses specific difficulties due to its rich morphology, complex negation patterns, and limited NLP tooling compared to well-resourced languages. The proposed system aims to replace subjective human grading with scalable, consistent, and repeatable automated assessments.
background.id:
Evaluasi jawaban deskriptif yang beragam secara linguistik secara konsisten dan akurat dalam sistem pendidikan digital modern menjadi tantangan yang semakin besar, terutama pada bahasa *low-resource* seperti Hindi. Sistem penilain leksikal dan berbasis aturan tradisional gagal menangkap makna mendalam, negasi, dan parafrase, yang berakibat pada rendahnya keandalan penilaian. Selain itu, penilaian manual memerlukan waktu yang lama, sangat subjektif, dan rentan terhadap variabilitas antarpenilai yang signifikan pada volume penilaian siswa yang besar.

Makalah ini mengatasi kesenjangan tersebut dengan menyediakan *pipeline* evaluasi yang sepenuhnya otomatis yang disesuaikan untuk jawaban deskriptif bahasa Hindi pada pendidikan dasar. Bahasa Hindi menghadirkan kesulitan khusus karena morfologinya yang kaya, pola negasi yang kompleks, dan perangkat NLP yang terbatas dibandingkan dengan bahasa yang memiliki sumber daya melimpah. Sistem yang diusulkan bertujuan untuk menggantikan penilaian manusia yang subjektif dengan asesmen otomatis yang dapat *skalabel*, konsisten, dan dapat diulang.

contributions.en:
The primary contributions of this paper include a complete and reproducible Hindi evaluation pipeline designed specifically for primary school reading comprehension tasks. The authors perform systematic hyperparameter optimization via grid search over learning rates and batch sizes to identify optimal training configurations.

Furthermore, the study provides empirical benchmarking that achieves an accuracy of 78.9% on the HindiRC-Data-master dataset, outperforming baseline models significantly. Finally, the paper offers a transparent analysis of system limitations along with a clear roadmap for future improvements.
contributions.id:
Kontribusi utama dari makalah ini meliputi *pipeline* evaluasi bahasa Hindi yang lengkap dan dapat direproduksi yang dirancang khusus untuk tugas pemahaman bacaan sekolah dasar. Para penulis melakukan optimasi *hiperparameter* secara sistematis melalui *grid search* pada *learning rate* dan *batch size* untuk mengidentifikasi konfigurasi pelatihan yang optimal.

Selain itu, studi ini memberikan *benchmarking* empiris yang mencapai akurasi 78.9% pada *dataset* HindiRC-Data-master, mengungguli model *baseline* secara signifikan. Terakhir, makalah ini menawarkan analisis transparan tentang keterbatasan sistem beserta peta jalan yang jelas untuk perbaikan di masa depan.

future_work.en: Future work should focus on five key directions to address current limitations. First, expanding the training corpus to include passages from grades 6 to 10 and STEM subjects, targeting at least 1,000 QA pairs. Second, incorporating explicit negation handling through a dedicated preprocessing step. Third, exploring alternative pretrained models such as MuRIL or L3Cube-HindBERT for potential accuracy gains. Fourth, investigating generative sequence-to-sequence models to overcome single-word output constraints. Finally, benchmarking open-source Hindi-capable large language models against the proposed pipeline.
future_work.id: Pekerjaan di masa depan harus fokus pada lima arah utama untuk mengatasi keterbatasan saat ini. Pertama, memperluas korpus pelatihan untuk menyertakan bacaan dari kelas 6 hingga 10 dan subjek STEM, menargetkan setidaknya 1.000 pasang QA. Kedua, menggabungkan penanganan negasi eksplisit melalui langkah pra-pemrosesan khusus. Ketiga, mengeksplorasi model *pre-trained* alternatif seperti MuRIL atau L3Cube-HindBERT untuk potensi peningkatan akurasi. Keempat, menyelidiki model *generative sequence-to-sequence* untuk mengatasi batasan keluaran satu kata. Terakhir, melakukan *benchmarking* pada *large language model* sumber terbuka yang mampu berbahasa Hindi terhadap *pipeline* yang diusulkan.

method.en:
The proposed framework operates in two main phases: a fine-tuning phase for answer span extraction and an evaluation phase for semantic similarity scoring. The dataset consists of 127 question-answer pairs extracted from 24 reading comprehension passages across grades 2 to 5, split into 101 training pairs and 26 evaluation pairs. Data preprocessing involves stripping extraneous characters, removing Hindi stop words, and applying stemming and lemmatization to collapse morphological variants, reducing the vocabulary size by 62 percent.

The fine-tuning phase uses the bhavikardeshna/multilingual-bert-base-cased-hindi model, trained with the AdamW optimizer, gradient clipping, and a linear warm-up scheduler. For the scoring phase, the l3cube-pune/hindi-sentence-similarity-sbert model produces 768-dimensional dense sentence embeddings via mean pooling. Cosine similarity is computed between predicted and reference answers, using an empirical classification threshold of tau equals 0.2 to categorize predictions as correct or incorrect.
method.id:
Kerangka kerja yang diusulkan beroperasi dalam dua fase utama: fase *fine-tuning* untuk ekstraksi rentang jawaban dan fase evaluasi untuk penilaian kemiripan semantik. *Dataset* ini terdiri dari 127 pasang pertanyaan-jawaban yang diekstrak dari 24 bacaan pemahaman dari kelas 2 hingga 5, yang dibagi menjadi 101 pasang pelatihan dan 26 pasang evaluasi. Pra-pemrosesan data melibatkan penghilangan karakter asing, penghapusan *stop word* bahasa Hindi, serta penerapan *stemming* dan *lemmatization* untuk menyatukan varian morfologi, yang mengurangi ukuran kosa kata sebesar 62 persen.

Fase *fine-tuning* menggunakan model bhavikardeshna/multilingual-bert-base-cased-hindi, yang dilatih dengan *optimizer* AdamW, *gradient clipping*, dan penjadwal *linear warm-up*. Untuk fase penilaian, model l3cube-pune/hindi-sentence-similarity-sbert menghasilkan *dense sentence embedding* berdimensi 768 melalui *mean pooling*. Kemiripan kosinus dihitung antara jawaban prediksi dan referensi, menggunakan ambang batas klasifikasi empiris sebesar tau sama dengan 0.2 untuk mengkategorikan prediksi benar atau salah.

related_work.en:
The automated scoring of descriptive responses has evolved from early Latent Semantic Analysis-based systems like Intelligent Essay Assessor and GradeAid, which fail to capture word order and negation. Subsequent research explored machine learning approaches, ensemble methods, and deep learning architectures such as CNN-LSTM models for short answer grading in various languages including Arabic and Hindi. In multilingual scenarios, prior works utilized multilingual BERT ensembles for comprehension tasks, while models like Sentence-BERT introduced efficient dense sentence embeddings using cosine similarity to reduce computational overhead.

Other notable studies investigated transformer-based automated short answer grading and domain-specific pre-training to overcome limited training data. While recent works have explored Large Language Models such as GPT-4 for grading, they face significant challenges regarding explainability, inference costs, and availability in low-resource languages. The present study builds upon these foundations by utilizing domain-adapted multilingual BERT variants and specialized sentence similarity models.
related_work.id:
Skor otomatis untuk respons deskriptif telah berkembang dari sistem awal berbasis *Latent Semantic Analysis* seperti Intelligent Essay Assessor dan GradeAid, yang gagal menangkap urutan kata dan negasi. Penelitian selanjutnya mengeksplorasi pendekatan *machine learning*, metode *ensemble*, dan arsitektur *deep learning* seperti model CNN-LSTM untuk penilaian jawaban singkat dalam berbagai bahasa termasuk bahasa Arab dan Hindi. Dalam skenario *multilingual*, karya-karya sebelumnya memanfaatkan *ensemble* BERT *multilingual* untuk tugas pemahaman, sementara model seperti Sentence-BERT memperkenalkan *dense sentence embedding* yang efisien menggunakan kesamaan kosinus untuk mengurangi beban komputasi.

Studi penting lainnya menyelidiki penilaian jawaban singkat otomatis berbasis *transformer* dan *pre-training* spesifik domain untuk mengatasi keterbatasan data pelatihan. Meskipun karya-karya terbaru telah mengeksplorasi *large language model* seperti GPT-4 untuk penilaian, mereka menghadapi tantangan signifikan terkait keterjelasan (*explainability*), biaya inferensi, dan ketersediaan dalam bahasa *low-resource*. Studi saat ini dibangun di atas fondasi ini dengan memanfaatkan varian mBERT *multilingual* yang diadaptasi domain dan model kemiripan kalimat khusus.

results.en:
The proposed mBERT system achieved an accuracy of 78.9%, precision of 80.6%, recall of 77.4%, and an F1-score of 79.0% on the test set. This represents a 14.2 percentage point improvement over the BM25 lexical baseline, which scored 64.7% in accuracy. To validate these findings, the authors computed Cohen's Kappa coefficient, obtaining kappa equals 0.71, which indicates substantial inter-rater agreement with a human expert.

Hyperparameter analysis revealed that a learning rate of 5 multiplied by 10 to the power of -4 combined with a batch size of 24 achieved the best performance. Embedding space visualizations through 2D PCA demonstrated substantial overlap between actual and predicted answer clusters, confirming the effectiveness of the semantic space alignment. Error analysis identified single-word answer span inaccuracies, implicit negation questions, and long passages exceeding 120 tokens as the primary failure modes.
results.id:
Sistem mBERT yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi 78.9%, presisi 80.6%, *recall* 77.4%, dan *F1-score* 79.0% pada *set* pengujian. Ini merupakan peningkatan sebesar 14.2 persentase poin dari *baseline* leksikal BM25, yang memperoleh akurasi 64.7%. Untuk memvalidasi temuan ini, para penulis menghitung koefisien Cohen's Kappa, memperoleh *kappa* sama dengan 0.71, yang menunjukkan kesepakatan antarpenilai yang substansial dengan ahli manusia.

Analisis *hiperparameter* mengungkapkan bahwa *learning rate* sebesar 5 dikalikan 10 pangkat -4 yang dikombinasikan dengan *batch size* 24 mencapai performa terbaik. Visualisasi ruang *embedding* melalui PCA 2D menunjukkan tumpang tindih yang substansial antara klaster jawaban aktual dan prediksi, yang mengkonfirmasi efektivitas penyelarasan ruang semantik. Analisis kesalahan mengidentifikasi ketidakakuratan rentang jawaban satu kata, pertanyaan negasi implisit, dan bacaan panjang yang melebihi 120 token sebagai mode kegagalan utama.

tldr.en: This study proposes an automated evaluation framework for Hindi descriptive answers using a fine-tuned mBERT model and SBERT-based semantic alignment. The system achieves 78.9% accuracy on the HindiRC-Data-master dataset, outperforming lexical baselines by over 14%.
tldr.id: Studi ini mengusulkan kerangka evaluasi otomatis untuk jawaban deskriptif bahasa Hindi menggunakan model *fine-tuning* mBERT dan penyelarasan semantik berbasis SBERT. Sistem ini mencapai akurasi 78.9% pada *dataset* HindiRC-Data-master, mengungguli *baseline* leksikal lebih dari 14%.
