doi:10.3390/data11080196.abstract: Automatic extraction of genealogical information from historical archival-genealogical documents in Uzbek is an understudied problem for low-resource languages. Multi-layer NLP benchmarks are not sufficient to automatically identify individuals, family relationships, dates, place names, and archival identifiers in such texts. Also, the same people are mentioned in various forms: full name, pronoun (18.8%), initial, surname-name order, indirect expression (9.4%), and title. Existing NER and relation extraction corpora are mainly focused on high-resource languages or general domain texts and do not sufficiently cover the FAMILY_ROLE signals, historical spelling variants, and fond–opis–delos identifiers specific to Uzbek archival-genealogical texts. Proposed resource: We present the ArchiveGene Corpus, a controlled, fully synthetic, and reproducible five-layer resource consisting of 1000 Uzbek archival-genealogical-style documents, divided into 700 training, 150 validation, and 150 test documents. The corpus contains 8366 named entities, 10,625 person mentions, 2000 coreference chains, and 1000 genealogical relation triples. The dataset was generated using a deterministic template-based pipeline and a lexicon of Uzbek names, and is fully reproducible. Inter-annotator agreement values were 0.847 for NER, 0.793 for coreference, and 0.821 for RE, according to Cohen’s κ. Comparative results are presented with four baseline models (rule-based, BiLSTM-CRF, mBERT, and XLM-RoBERTa). The dataset is openly hosted on the Zenodo platform under the CC BY 4.0 license; concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20670360, v1.1.1 version DOI: 10.5281/zenodo. 21429998. Scientific significance: To the best of our knowledge, ArchiveGene is among the first openly released, controlled synthetic resources for Uzbek that integrates named-entity recognition, person-mention detection, coreference resolution, genealogical relation extraction, and final tuple generation within a single annotation framework. The baseline analysis provides three main conclusions: (1) on the clean synthetic test set, the transformer models already reach 100.00 Micro-F1 for NER and 100.00 Macro-F1 for coreference-aware relation extraction, so coreference aggregation adds little on synthetic data (+2.25 for mBERT and +0.04 for XLM-RoBERTa) but its contribution is expected to grow on real archival text; (2) the rule-based and heuristic baselines lag far behind (Macro-F1 50.28 and 70.73) and fail entirely on spouse_of, showing the limits of lexical rules; and (3) a zero-shot evaluation on a real-document pilot reduces NER Micro-F1 from 100.00 to 22.17, indicating that the synthetic corpus is trivially learnable and that real-archival validation is essential.

glossary.explanation_id: Bahasa *low-resource* adalah bahasa yang memiliki ketersediaan data digital dan sumber daya komputasi yang sangat terbatas.
*Named entity recognition* adalah tugas mendeteksi dan mengklasifikasikan entitas bernama seperti nama orang, lokasi, atau organisasi di dalam teks.
*Coreference resolution* adalah proses mengidentifikasi semua ekspresi dalam teks yang merujuk pada entitas dunia nyata yang sama.
Evaluasi *zero-shot* adalah pengujian model pada domain atau tugas baru tanpa melakukan pelatihan ulang atau *fine-tuning* pada data target.
Model *transformer* adalah arsitektur jaringan saraf tiruan yang mengandalkan mekanisme *attention* untuk memproses data sekuensial.

background.en: Automatic extraction of genealogical information from historical archival documents in Uzbek is an understudied problem for low-resource languages. Existing named entity recognition and relation extraction corpora primarily focus on high-resource languages or general domain texts, failing to cover specialized challenges such as family role signals, historical spelling variants, and specific archival identifiers.
background.id: Ekstraksi otomatis informasi silsilah dari dokumen arsip historis dalam bahasa Uzbek merupakan masalah yang kurang diteliti untuk bahasa *low-resource*. Korpus *named entity recognition* dan ekstraksi relasi yang ada terutama berfokus pada bahasa *high-resource* atau teks domain umum, sehingga gagal mencakup tantangan khusus seperti sinyal peran keluarga, varian ejaan historis, dan pengidentifikasi arsip tertentu.

contributions.en: The paper presents the ArchiveGene Corpus, a controlled, fully synthetic, and reproducible five-layer resource consisting of one thousand Uzbek archival-genealogical-style documents. To the best of the authors knowledge, ArchiveGene is among the first openly released, controlled synthetic resources for Uzbek that integrates named-entity recognition, person-mention detection, coreference resolution, genealogical relation extraction, and final tuple generation within a single annotation framework.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyajikan Korpus *ArchiveGene*, sebuah sumber daya lima lapis yang terkontrol, sepenuhnya sintetis, dan dapat direproduksi yang terdiri dari seribu dokumen bergaya arsip-silsilah bahasa Uzbek. Sepengetahuan penulis, *ArchiveGene* adalah salah satu sumber daya sintetis terkontrol yang dirilis secara terbuka untuk bahasa Uzbek yang mengintegrasikan *named-entity recognition*, deteksi *person-mention*, resolusi *coreference*, ekstraksi relasi silsilah, dan pembuatan *tuple* akhir dalam satu kerangka kerja *anotasi* tunggal.

future_work.en: The authors note that while coreference aggregation adds little on synthetic data, its contribution is expected to grow on real archival text, and they emphasize that real-archival validation is essential due to the drop in performance during zero-shot evaluation.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa meskipun agregasi *coreference* memberikan sedikit tambahan pada data sintetis, kontribusinya diharapkan meningkat pada teks arsip nyata, dan mereka menekankan bahwa validasi arsip nyata sangat penting karena penurunan performa selama evaluasi *zero-shot*.

method.en: The dataset was generated using a deterministic template-based pipeline and a lexicon of Uzbek names, comprising 700 training, 150 validation, and 150 test documents containing thousands of named entities, person mentions, coreference chains, and genealogical relation triples. Inter-annotator agreement was measured using Cohens kappa, and comparative results were presented with four baseline models including rule-based approaches, BiLSTM-CRF, mBERT, and XLM-RoBERTa.
method.id: Dataset dihasilkan menggunakan *pipeline* berbasis templat deterministik dan leksikon nama-nama bahasa Uzbek, yang terdiri dari 700 dokumen pelatihan, 150 validasi, dan 150 pengujian yang mencakup ribuan entitas bernama, penyebutan orang, rantai *coreference*, dan tripel relasi silsilah. Persetujuan antar-*anotator* diukur menggunakan kappa Cohen, dan hasil komparatif disajikan dengan empat model *baseline* termasuk pendekatan berbasis aturan, *BiLSTM-CRF*, *mBERT*, dan *XLM-RoBERTa*.

related_work.en: Existing corpora for named entity recognition and relation extraction are mainly focused on high-resource languages or general domain texts, and they do not sufficiently cover the family role signals, historical spelling variants, and specific archival identifiers found in Uzbek archival-genealogical texts.
related_work.id: Korpus yang ada untuk *named entity recognition* dan ekstraksi relasi terutama berfokus pada bahasa *high-resource* atau teks domain umum, serta tidak cukup mencakup sinyal peran keluarga, varian ejaan historis, dan pengidentifikasi arsip spesifik yang ditemukan dalam teks arsip silsilah bahasa Uzbek.

results.en: On the clean synthetic test set, transformer models reach 100.00 Micro-F1 for NER and 100.00 Macro-F1 for coreference-aware relation extraction, whereas rule-based and heuristic baselines lag far behind with Macro-F1 scores of 50.28 and 70.73 while failing entirely on spouse relationships. However, a zero-shot evaluation on a real-document pilot reduces NER Micro-F1 from 100.00 to 22.17, indicating that the synthetic corpus is trivially learnable and that real-archival validation is essential.
results.id: Pada *test set* sintetis yang bersih, model *transformer* mencapai 100.00 *Micro-F1* untuk *NER* dan 100.00 *Macro-F1* untuk ekstraksi relasi yang sadar-*coreference*, sedangkan *baseline* berbasis aturan dan heuristik tertinggal jauh dengan skor *Macro-F1* sebesar 50.28 dan 70.73 serta gagal total pada relasi pasangan suami istri. Namun, evaluasi *zero-shot* pada uji coba dokumen nyata menurunkan *NER Micro-F1* dari 100.00 menjadi 22.17, yang mengindikasikan bahwa korpus sintetis tersebut mudah dipelajari dan validasi arsip nyata sangat penting.

tldr.en: This paper introduces ArchiveGene, a synthetic multi-layer benchmark for genealogical information extraction from Uzbek historical archival documents. The authors present a controlled dataset and baseline evaluations demonstrating that transformer models achieve high performance on synthetic data while highlighting challenges in transferring to real archival texts.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan *ArchiveGene*, sebuah *benchmark* multi-lapis sintetis untuk ekstraksi informasi silsilah dari dokumen arsip sejarah bahasa Uzbek. Para penulis menyajikan *dataset* terkontrol dan evaluasi *baseline* yang menunjukkan bahwa model *transformer* mencapai performa tinggi pada data sintetis sekaligus menyoroti tantangan dalam transfer ke teks arsip asli.

doi:10.3390/data11080196.title: The ArchiveGene Corpus: A Synthetic Multi-Layer Benchmark for Genealogical Information Extraction from Uzbek Historical Archival Texts

doi:10.3390/data11090217.abstract: The availability of large, structured legal datasets is essential for advancing legal natural language processing, information retrieval, and the development of reliable language technologies. However, such resources remain scarce for Kazakh, a morphologically rich and comparatively low-resource language, limiting the development and evaluation of domain-specific NLP methods. This data descriptor presents KazakhLawCorpus, a curated corpus of 215,889 document-level legislative metadata records from the Republic of Kazakhstan. The dataset was derived from a PostgreSQL export containing 223,245 source records and constructed through Kazakh-language field selection, essential-field filtering, source-preserving normalization, schema reconstruction, and systematic quality validation, resulting in a retention rate of 96.705%. The final release comprises 25 fields covering document identifiers, temporal attributes, legal status, registry information, Kazakh-language titles and descriptions, legal and institutional categories, geographical information, and source URLs. The records cover legislative acts adopted between 30 October 1947 and 20 July 2026. Quality-control procedures confirmed unique law_id values, complete title and description fields, and parseable adoption dates, while 4635 records with potential source-level or historical anomalies were retained and transparently documented through diagnostic flags. KazakhLawCorpus provides a large-scale, traceable resource for metadata-based legal information retrieval, document classification, temporal and institutional analysis, provenance tracking, and the development of downstream Kazakh legal NLP resources.

glossary.explanation_id: *Metadata* adalah informasi terstruktur yang mendeskripsikan, menjelaskan, atau mempermudah penemuan dan pengelolaan suatu *dataset* atau dokumen.
*Information retrieval* adalah proses menemukan dokumen atau informasi relevan dari suatu koleksi data berskala besar.
*Low-resource* merujuk pada kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain memiliki ketersediaan *data* dan sumber daya komputasi yang sangat terbatas.
*Normalization* adalah proses penyesuaian format *data* agar seragam dan konsisten tanpa merusak informasi aslinya.
*Schema* adalah kerangka kerja atau struktur logis yang mendefinisikan bagaimana basis *data* atau catatan diorganisasikan.
*Provenance* adalah catatan historis mengenai asal-usul, kepemilikan, dan perjalanan suatu *data* atau dokumen.

background.en: The availability of large, structured legal datasets is essential for advancing legal natural language processing, information retrieval, and reliable language technologies. However, such resources remain scarce for Kazakh, a morphologically rich and comparatively low-resource language. This scarcity limits the development and evaluation of domain-specific methods.
background.id: Ketersediaan *dataset* hukum yang besar dan terstruktur sangat penting untuk memajukan *natural language processing* hukum, *information retrieval*, dan teknologi bahasa yang andal. Namun, sumber daya tersebut masih langka untuk bahasa Kazakh, bahasa yang kaya secara morfologis dan relatif *low-resource*. Kelangkaan ini membatasi pengembangan dan evaluasi metode yang spesifik domain.

contributions.en: This data descriptor presents KazakhLawCorpus, a curated corpus of 215,889 document-level legislative metadata records from the Republic of Kazakhstan. The resource offers 25 fields covering identifiers, temporal attributes, legal status, registry information, titles and descriptions, categories, geographical information, and source URLs, spanning from October 1947 to July 2026.
contributions.id: Deskripsi data ini mempresentasikan *KazakhLawCorpus*, sebuah korpus terkurasi yang terdiri dari 215.889 catatan metadata legislatif tingkat dokumen dari Republik Kazakhstan. Sumber daya ini menawarkan 25 bidang yang mencakup pengenal, atribut temporal, status hukum, informasi registri, judul dan deskripsi, kategori, informasi geografis, dan *URL* sumber, yang mencakup rentang waktu dari Oktober 1947 hingga Juli 2026.

future_work.en: The authors state that KazakhLawCorpus provides a traceable resource for metadata-based legal information retrieval, document classification, temporal and institutional analysis, provenance tracking, and the development of downstream Kazakh legal NLP resources.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyatakan bahwa *KazakhLawCorpus* menyediakan sumber daya yang dapat ditelusuri untuk *information retrieval* hukum berbasis metadata, klasifikasi dokumen, analisis temporal dan institusional, pelacakan *provenance*, dan pengembangan sumber daya *NLP* hukum Kazakh hilir.

method.en: The dataset was derived from a PostgreSQL export containing 223,245 source records. It was constructed through Kazakh-language field selection, essential-field filtering, source-preserving normalization, schema reconstruction, and systematic quality validation. Quality control procedures confirmed unique law_id values, complete title and description fields, and parseable adoption dates, while 4635 records with anomalies were retained and documented through diagnostic flags.
method.id: Kumpulan data ini berasal dari ekspor *PostgreSQL* yang berisi 223.245 catatan sumber. Korpus ini dibangun melalui pemilihan bidang bahasa Kazakh, pemfilteran bidang esensial, normalisasi yang mempertahankan sumber, rekonstruksi skema, dan validasi kualitas sistematis. Prosedur kontrol kualitas mengonfirmasi nilai *law_id* yang unik, bidang judul dan deskripsi yang lengkap, serta tanggal adopsi yang dapat diurai, sementara 4.635 catatan dengan anomali tetap dipertahankan dan didokumentasikan melalui *diagnostic flag*.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.

results.en: The construction process achieved a retention rate of 96.705 percent, resulting in 215,889 valid document-level records. The final release successfully covers legislative acts adopted between 30 October 1947 and 20 July 2026 with verified unique identifiers and complete textual fields.
results.id: Proses konstruksi mencapai tingkat retensi sebesar 96,705 persen, menghasilkan 215.889 catatan tingkat dokumen yang valid. Rilis akhir berhasil mencakup undang-undang yang diadopsi antara 30 Oktober 1947 dan 20 Juli 2026 dengan pengenal unik yang diverifikasi dan bidang tekstual yang lengkap.

tldr.en: This paper presents KazakhLawCorpus, a large-scale curated corpus of legislative metadata records from the Republic of Kazakhstan. The dataset provides a traceable resource for legal information retrieval and downstream legal natural language processing tasks in a low-resource setting.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mempresentasikan *KazakhLawCorpus*, sebuah korpus terkurasi berskala besar yang berisi catatan metadata legislatif dari Republik Kazakhstan. Kumpulan data ini menyediakan sumber daya yang dapat ditelusuri untuk *information retrieval* hukum dan tugas *natural language processing* hukum hilir dalam pengaturan *low-resource*.

doi:10.3390/economies14090419.abstract: This study explores the drivers of income inequality using crude oil prices, consumer prices, economic development, trade openness, unemployment, and human capital as predictors. Despite a lot of research conducted on income inequality, there have been very few studies capable of simultaneously analysing the influence of energy prices, macroeconomic conditions, trade openness, conditions in the labour market, and human capital, as well as accounting for the dynamic persistence and potential endogeneity of inequality across countries. To fill this research gap, based on a panel of 230 observations, analyses are run using pooled ordinary least squares, as well as fixed and random effects derived from model-selection tests that favour the random effects specification. An analysis using a dynamic panel data model was also carried out in this study. The empirical results show that crude oil prices, trade openness, and unemployment are all positively correlated with income inequality and that GDP per capita and human capital have a significant deterrent effect on the expansion of income inequality. With the random effects model, a US$1 increase in crude oil prices increases the Gini index by 0.0186 points; meanwhile, one-percentage-point increases in trade openness and unemployment contribute to increases in inequality of 0.0142 points and 0.722 points, respectively. On the other hand, a US$1000 increase in GDP per capita lowers the Gini index by about 0.0699 points, and an improvement of 0.1 point in human capital decreases inequality by approximately 1.497 points. Controlling for country-specific effects does little to show an association with consumer prices. The model accounts for 43.11 per cent of the variation in income inequality. The findings show that inclusive growth strategies, investment in human capital and labour-market policies are evidently pivotal to addressing inequality fostered by economic transformation and energy-price volatility.

doi:10.3390/electronics15173856.abstract: Real-time event detection from social media has become increasingly important for emergency response, public safety, and situational awareness. However, accurately identifying emerging events from Thai social media remains challenging because Thai is a low-resource language without explicit word boundaries, while social media text is often characterized by informal writing, spelling variations, and noisy user-generated content. This paper proposes an entity-centric real-time event detection framework for Thai social media that employs a Multi-Granularity Thai Character Cluster (TCC)-Aware Named Entity Recognition (NER) model as its core information extraction component. The proposed NER architecture integrates contextual word embeddings, character-level representations, Thai Character Cluster features, and Part-of-Speech embeddings through an attention-based feature fusion mechanism to improve entity recognition under noisy conditions. Recognized entities are subsequently used as semantic anchors for event construction, clustering, temporal trend analysis, event ranking, and alert generation within a unified streaming framework. Event discovery combines Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) and Exponential Moving Average (EMA)-based temporal analysis to identify emerging events in real time. Experiments conducted on a large-scale Thai social media corpus demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an F1-score of 94.14% for named entity recognition and 92.2% for downstream event detection, outperforming representative baseline methods. Additional ablation studies, qualitative error analysis, and statistical significance tests confirm the effectiveness of the proposed multi-granularity representation. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective solution for real-time event monitoring in low-resource language environments.

glossary.explanation_id: Named Entity Recognition adalah tugas *information extraction* untuk mengidentifikasi dan mengklasifikasikan entitas bernama di dalam teks ke dalam kategori yang telah ditentukan.
Thai Character Cluster adalah gugus karakter dalam bahasa Thai yang sering kali dibaca atau ditulis bersama sebagai unit sub-kata karena tidak adanya spasi antar kata.
Streaming framework adalah arsitektur sistem yang memproses aliran data secara berkelanjutan dan *real-time*.

Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise adalah algoritma *clustering* berbasis kepadatan yang dapat mengelompokkan data dengan bentuk sewenang-wenang dan mendeteksi pencilan sebagai *noise*.
glossary.term: Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise

glossary.explanation_id: Exponential Moving Average adalah jenis rata-rata bergerak yang memberikan bobot dan signifikansi lebih besar pada titik data terbaru.
Ablation study adalah metode evaluasi model dengan menghapus bagian tertentu untuk mengukur kontribusi komponen tersebut terhadap performa keseluruhan.

background.en: Real-time event detection from social media is increasingly crucial for emergency response, public safety, and situational awareness. However, performing this task on Thai social media is challenging because Thai is a low-resource language lacking explicit word boundaries, and social media text typically contains informal writing, spelling variations, and noisy user-generated content. This creates a clear gap in building robust information extraction systems capable of handling noisy, unsegmented text for real-time monitoring.
background.id: Deteksi peristiwa *real-time* dari media sosial semakin krusial untuk tanggap darurat, keselamatan publik, dan kesadaran situasional. Namun, melakukan tugas ini pada media sosial bahasa Thai sangat menantang karena bahasa Thai adalah bahasa *low-resource* yang tidak memiliki batasan kata eksplisit, serta teks media sosial umumnya berisi tulisan informal, variasi ejaan, dan konten buatan pengguna yang bising. Hal ini menciptakan kesenjangan nyata dalam membangun sistem *information extraction* yang tangguh untuk menangani teks bising dan tidak bersegmen demi pemantauan *real-time*.

contributions.en: The main contribution is an entity-centric real-time event detection framework designed specifically for Thai social media. The core novelty lies in a Multi-Granularity Thai Character Cluster-Aware Named Entity Recognition model that integrates contextual word embeddings, character-level representations, Thai Character Cluster features, and Part-of-Speech embeddings via an attention-based feature fusion mechanism.
contributions.id: Kontribusi utama adalah kerangka kerja deteksi peristiwa *real-time* berbasis entitas yang dirancang khusus untuk media sosial bahasa Thai. Kebaruan inti terletak pada model *named entity recognition* sadar *Thai Character Cluster* multi-granular yang mengintegrasikan *contextual word embeddings*, representasi tingkat karakter, fitur *Thai Character Cluster*, dan *Part-of-Speech embeddings* melalui mekanisme *attention-based feature fusion*.

future_work.en: The paper does not explicitly discuss specific future work directions in the abstract.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas arah pekerjaan masa depan secara spesifik di dalam abstrak.

method.en: The framework uses a multi-granularity named entity recognition model as its core information extraction component to handle noisy conditions in Thai text. Recognized entities serve as semantic anchors for event construction, clustering, temporal trend analysis, event ranking, and alert generation within a unified streaming framework. Event discovery combines Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise and Exponential Moving Average-based temporal analysis to identify emerging events in real time.
method.id: Kerangka kerja ini menggunakan model *named entity recognition* multi-granular sebagai komponen *information extraction* inti untuk menangani kondisi bising pada teks bahasa Thai. Entitas yang dikenali berfungsi sebagai jangkar semantik untuk konstruksi peristiwa, *clustering*, analisis tren temporal, *event ranking*, dan pembuatan *alert* dalam kerangka kerja *streaming* terpadu. Penemuan peristiwa menggabungkan *Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise* dan analisis temporal berbasis *Exponential Moving Average* untuk mengidentifikasi peristiwa yang muncul secara *real-time*.

related_work.en: The paper compares the proposed approach against representative baseline methods to validate its effectiveness. Further detailed discussions of prior related works are not explicitly elaborated in the abstract.
related_work.id: Makalah ini membandingkan pendekatan yang diusulkan terhadap metode *baseline* representatif untuk memvalidasi efektivitasnya. Pembahasan mendetail lebih lanjut mengenai karya terkait sebelumnya tidak diuraikan secara eksplisit di dalam abstrak.

results.en: Evaluated on a large-scale Thai social media corpus, the proposed model achieves an F1-score of 94.14 percent for named entity recognition and 92.2 percent for downstream event detection, outperforming representative baseline methods. Additional ablation studies, qualitative error analysis, and statistical significance tests confirm the effectiveness of the multi-granularity representation.
results.id: Dievaluasi pada korpus media sosial bahasa Thai berskala besar, model yang diusulkan mencapai *F1-score* sebesar 94,14 persen untuk *named entity recognition* dan 92,2 persen untuk deteksi peristiwa hilir, mengungguli metode *baseline* representatif. Studi ablasi tambahan, analisis *error* kualitatif, dan uji signifikansi statistik mengonfirmasi efektivitas dari representasi multi-granular tersebut.

tldr.en: This paper proposes an entity-centric real-time event detection framework for Thai social media using a multi-granularity Thai Character Cluster-aware named entity recognition model. Experiments on a large-scale corpus show that the framework achieves high performance and outperforms representative baselines in both named entity recognition and event detection.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan kerangka kerja deteksi peristiwa *real-time* berbasis entitas untuk media sosial bahasa Thai menggunakan model *named entity recognition* yang sadar *Thai Character Cluster* multi-granular. Eksperimen pada korpus skala besar menunjukkan bahwa kerangka kerja ini mencapai performa tinggi dan mengungguli metode *baseline* representatif dalam pengenalan entitas bernama maupun deteksi peristiwa.

doi:10.3390/electronics15173856.title: An Entity-Centric Real-Time Event Detection Framework for Thai Social Media Using Multi-Granularity TCC-Aware Named Entity Recognition

doi:10.3390/electronics15194398.abstract: Text-to-SQL research has concentrated on English, while prior work on Arabic, Japanese, and Vietnamese has largely relied on grammar-constrained parsers or zero-shot prompting, with recent work beginning to explore trained LLM-based alternatives. We investigate whether a unified fine-tuned open-source pipeline can serve typologically distant low-resource languages and quantify the same-pipeline English-to-target gap on parallel Spider instances. We fine-tune Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with QLoRA using shared schema grounding, value grounding, an English translation hint, and execution-based self-consistency voting over eight candidates. Architecture, constants, and inference are fixed across languages, while each language uses its own training data and adapter. On Ar-Spider, MultiSpider-JA, and MultiSpider-VI, the pipeline reaches 75–80% execution accuracy (EX), with raw exact set match (ESM) within 0.7 points of the strongest prior Arabic parser and above the strongest multilingual MultiSpider baseline for Japanese (+2.5) and Vietnamese (+3.5). An English same-pipeline run (85.3% EX) yields gaps of −10.1, −10.5, and −5.4 percentage points for Arabic, Japanese, and Vietnamese, respectively. Removing the complete value-grounding group causes the largest degradation. The EX–ESM gap persists without voting and repair, indicating differences in generated SQL rather than decoder effects; we therefore recommend reporting both metrics.

glossary.explanation_id: Tugas mengubah teks bahasa alami menjadi kueri basis data SQL secara otomatis.
Metode *parameter-efficient fine-tuning* yang menggunakan kuantisasi untuk mengurangi penggunaan memori.
Proses menghubungkan istilah dalam teks dengan kolom atau tabel yang sesuai dalam *schema* basis data.
Proses mengidentifikasi dan mencocokkan nilai data spesifik yang disebutkan dalam teks dengan isi basis data.
Strategi *decoding* yang memilih keluaran konsisten terbanyak dari beberapa kandidat hasil *generation*.
Metrik evaluasi yang mengukur kecocokan persis antara struktur SQL buatan dan SQL referensi.
Analisis dengan menghapus bagian tertentu dari model untuk mengukur dampak kontribusinya.

background.en: Text-to-SQL research has historically concentrated heavily on English, leaving typologically distant low-resource languages underexplored. Prior work on Arabic, Japanese, and Vietnamese has largely relied on grammar-constrained parsers or zero-shot prompting, with only recent studies beginning to explore trained large language model alternatives. The primary gap addressed by this research is determining whether a single unified pipeline can effectively serve these diverse low-resource languages while quantifying the performance gap relative to English.
background.id: Penelitian *text-to-sql* secara historis sangat terpusat pada bahasa Inggris, sehingga bahasa *low-resource* yang secara tipologis jauh menjadi kurang terjelajahi. Penelitian sebelumnya pada bahasa Arab, Jepang, dan Vietnam sebagian besar mengandalkan *parser* berbasis batasan tata bahasa atau *zero-shot* *prompting*, dengan hanya studi terbaru yang mulai mengeksplorasi alternatif *large language model* terlatih. Kesenjangan utama yang diatasi oleh penelitian ini adalah menentukan apakah satu *pipeline* yang disatukan dapat melayani bahasa-bahasa *low-resource* yang beragam ini secara efektif sekaligus mengukur kesenjangan performa relatif terhadap bahasa Inggris.

contributions.en: The main contribution of this work is a unified fine-tuned open-source pipeline designed for typologically distant low-resource languages using Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with QLoRA. The framework incorporates shared schema grounding, value grounding, an English translation hint, and execution-based self-consistency voting over eight candidates. Furthermore, the paper provides a quantitative analysis of the same-pipeline English-to-target gap and ablation insights regarding specific components like value grounding.
contributions.id: Kontribusi utama dari pekerjaan ini adalah sebuah *pipeline* sumber terbuka yang disempurnakan dan disatukan yang dirancang untuk bahasa *low-resource* yang berbeda secara tipologis menggunakan Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct dengan QLoRA. *Framework* ini menggabungkan *schema* *grounding* bersama, *value* *grounding*, petunjuk terjemahan bahasa Inggris, serta *voting* *self-consistency* berbasis eksekusi atas delapan kandidat. Selain itu, makalah ini memberikan analisis kuantitatif mengenai kesenjangan dari bahasa Inggris ke target pada *pipeline* yang sama serta wawasan ablasi mengenai komponen tertentu seperti *value* *grounding*.

future_work.en: The authors note that the execution accuracy and exact set match gap persists even without voting and repair, pointing to underlying differences in generated SQL rather than decoder effects. Consequently, they recommend reporting both metrics in future evaluations.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa kesenjangan antara akurasi eksekusi dan *exact* *set* *match* tetap bertahan meskipun tanpa *voting* dan *repair*, yang mengindikasikan adanya perbedaan mendasar pada SQL yang dihasilkan alih-alih efek *decoder*. Oleh karena itu, mereka merekomendasikan untuk melaporkan kedua metrik tersebut dalam evaluasi mendatang.

method.en: The authors fine-tune Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct utilizing QLoRA, incorporating shared schema grounding, value grounding, an English translation hint, and execution-based self-consistency voting over eight candidates. Architecture, constants, and inference settings remain fixed across all evaluated languages, whereas each language utilizes its own specific training data and adapter. Evaluation is conducted on Ar-Spider, MultiSpider-JA, and MultiSpider-VI, alongside an English baseline run for comparison.
method.id: Para penulis menyempurnakan Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct menggunakan QLoRA, dengan memasukkan *schema* *grounding* bersama, *value* *grounding*, petunjuk terjemahan bahasa Inggris, serta *voting* *self-consistency* berbasis eksekusi atas delapan kandidat. Arsitektur, konstanta, dan pengaturan *inference* dibuat tetap di semua bahasa yang dievaluasi, sementara setiap bahasa menggunakan data latih dan *adapter* khususnya sendiri. Evaluasi dilakukan pada Ar-Spider, MultiSpider-JA, dan MultiSpider-VI, berdampingan dengan *baseline* bahasa Inggris untuk perbandingan.

related_work.en: Prior approaches for non-English languages have heavily depended on grammar-constrained parsers or zero-shot prompting strategies. While some recent studies have begun exploring trained alternatives using large language models, they typically lack a unified evaluation framework across typologically distinct languages. This paper builds upon existing multilingual benchmarks like MultiSpider and instances from Spider to compare its proposed unified pipeline against these prior methods.
related_work.id: Pendekatan sebelumnya untuk bahasa non-Inggris sangat bergantung pada *parser* berbasis batasan tata bahasa atau strategi *zero-shot* *prompting*. Meskipun beberapa studi terbaru mulai mengeksplorasi alternatif terlatih menggunakan *large language model*, studi tersebut umumnya kekurangan *framework* evaluasi yang disatukan di berbagai bahasa yang berbeda secara tipologis. Makalah ini dibangun di atas *benchmark* multilingual yang sudah ada seperti MultiSpider dan instans dari Spider untuk membandingkan *pipeline* terpadu yang diusulkan terhadap metode-metode terdahulu ini.

results.en: On Ar-Spider, MultiSpider-JA, and MultiSpider-VI, the proposed pipeline achieves 75 to 80 percent execution accuracy. Raw exact set match scores come within 0.7 points of the strongest prior Arabic parser and exceed the strongest multilingual MultiSpider baseline by 2.5 points for Japanese and 3.5 points for Vietnamese. An English run on the same pipeline achieves 85.3 percent execution accuracy, resulting in performance gaps of negative 10.1, negative 10.5, and negative 5.4 percentage points for Arabic, Japanese, and Vietnamese respectively. Ablation shows that removing the complete value-grounding group causes the most severe degradation.
results.id: Pada Ar-Spider, MultiSpider-JA, dan MultiSpider-VI, *pipeline* yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi eksekusi 75 hingga 80 persen. Skor *exact* *set* *match* mentah berada dalam jarak 0,7 poin dari *parser* bahasa Arab terdahulu yang terkuat dan melampaui *baseline* MultiSpider multilingual terkuat sebesar 2,5 poin untuk bahasa Jepang serta 3,5 poin untuk bahasa Vietnam. Uji coba bahasa Inggris pada *pipeline* yang sama mencapai akurasi eksekusi 85,3 persen, menghasilkan kesenjangan performa berturut-turut sebesar minus 10,1, minus 10,5, dan minus 5,4 persentase poin untuk bahasa Arab, Jepang, dan Vietnam. Ablasi menunjukkan bahwa penghilangan kelompok *value* *grounding* secara utuh menyebabkan penurunan performa yang paling parah.

tldr.en: This paper investigates a unified fine-tuned large language model framework for text-to-sql translation across Arabic, Japanese, and Vietnamese. The results show that the proposed pipeline achieves strong performance while quantifying the execution accuracy gap compared to English.
tldr.id: Makalah ini meneliti *framework* *large language model* yang disempurnakan dan disatukan untuk penerjemahan *text-to-sql* pada bahasa Arab, Jepang, dan Vietnam. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa *pipeline* yang diusulkan mencapai performa yang kuat sekaligus mengukur kesenjangan akurasi eksekusi dibandingkan dengan bahasa Inggris.

doi:10.3390/electronics15194398.title: Text-to-SQL for Low-Resource Languages: A Unified Large Language Model Framework Evaluated on Arabic, Japanese, and Vietnamese

doi:10.3390/info17080753.abstract: Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging is a foundational task in Natural Language Processing (NLP), yet it remains challenging for low-resource and morphologically rich languages such as Amazigh. This paper proposes a hybrid ensemble framework for Amazigh POS tagging that integrates three complementary models: a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network (BiLSTM), a Conditional Random Field model (CRF), and a rule-based morphological analyzer (RBMA). Rather than treating prior results obtained on different corpora and tag inventories as directly comparable, the study evaluates all proposed components under a common 54-tag experimental setting based on the publicly available Amazigh Linguistic Dataset. Three ensemble strategies are examined: majority voting, validation-weighted voting, and logistic-regression stacking. An additional late-fusion ablation applies hard and soft RBMA constraints to CRF and Stacking outputs; hard masking degrades performance substantially, whereas soft masking is more robust but remains below unconstrained decoding. The best micro-level performance is obtained by the stacking ensemble, which reaches 98.51% Micro-F1/accuracy, whereas the boosting-like weighted ensemble obtains the strongest Macro-F1 among the ensemble variants, reaching 74.24%. These results show that hybrid ensemble methods can improve token-level accuracy in low-resource POS tagging, while also revealing a trade-off between frequent-tag accuracy and rare-tag robustness. The findings highlight the usefulness of combining neural, probabilistic, and rule-based information for Amazigh POS tagging, and point to class-balanced meta-learning and character/subword representations as important directions for improving rare and out-of-vocabulary categories.

Teknik *ensemble* di mana *meta-model* dilatih untuk menggabungkan prediksi dari beberapa model dasar.
Metode evaluasi dengan menghapus atau mengubah komponen tertentu dari sebuah *model* untuk mengukur dampaknya.

*Metrik* evaluasi yang menghitung rata-rata *F1-score* untuk setiap kelas secara terpisah tanpa memandang frekuensinya.

background.en: Part-of-speech tagging is a foundational task in natural language processing, but it remains difficult for languages that are low-resource and morphologically rich like Amazigh. The study notes that prior results from different corpora and tag inventories are not directly comparable, establishing a common 54-tag experimental setting based on the publicly available Amazigh Linguistic Dataset.
background.id: *Part-of-speech* *tagging* adalah tugas fundamental dalam *natural* *language* *processing*, tetapi tetap sulit untuk bahasa yang *low-resource* dan kaya secara morfologis seperti Amazigh. Studi ini mencatat bahwa hasil sebelumnya dari berbagai *korpus* dan inventaris *tag* tidak dapat langsung dibandingkan, sehingga menetapkan pengaturan eksperimental 54 *tag* yang umum berdasarkan Amazigh Linguistic Dataset yang tersedia untuk umum.

contributions.en: The paper introduces a hybrid ensemble framework for Amazigh part-of-speech tagging that integrates three complementary models: a bidirectional long short-term memory network, a conditional random field model, and a rule-based morphological analyzer. It also examines three ensemble strategies and evaluates late-fusion ablation using hard and soft rule-based constraints.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan *framework* *ensemble* hibrida untuk *part-of-speech* *tagging* bahasa Amazigh yang mengintegrasikan tiga model komplementer: *bidirectional* *long* *short-term* *memory* *network*, model *conditional* *random* *field*, dan *rule-based* *morphological* *analyzer*. Studi ini juga menguji tiga strategi *ensemble* dan mengevaluasi *ablation* *late-fusion* menggunakan *constraint* berbasis aturan keras dan lunak.

future_work.en: The authors point to class-balanced meta-learning and character or subword representations as important directions for improving rare and out-of-vocabulary categories.
future_work.id: Para penulis menunjuk *class-balanced* *meta-learning* serta representasi karakter atau *subword* sebagai arah penting untuk meningkatkan kategori yang langka dan di luar kosakata.

method.en: The study evaluates a bidirectional long short-term memory network, a conditional random field model, and a rule-based morphological analyzer under a common 54-tag experimental setting using the Amazigh Linguistic Dataset. Three ensemble strategies are tested: majority voting, validation-weighted voting, and logistic-regression stacking, alongside an ablation applying hard and soft rule-based constraints.
method.id: Studi ini mengevaluasi *bidirectional* *long* *short-term* *memory* *network*, model *conditional* *random* *field*, dan *rule-based* *morphological* *analyzer* di bawah pengaturan eksperimental 54 *tag* yang sama menggunakan Amazigh Linguistic Dataset. Tiga strategi *ensemble* diuji: *majority* *voting*, *validation-weighted* *voting*, dan *logistic-regression* *stacking*, beserta *ablation* yang menerapkan *constraint* berbasis aturan keras dan lunak.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan terkait secara mendetail.

results.en: The stacking ensemble achieves the best micro-level performance at 98.51 percent micro-F1 and accuracy, while the weighted ensemble obtains the strongest macro-F1 among ensemble variants at 74.24 percent. Hard masking substantially degrades performance, whereas soft masking is more robust but remains below unconstrained decoding, revealing a trade-off between frequent-tag accuracy and rare-tag robustness.
results.id: *Ensemble* *stacking* mencapai performa tingkat mikro terbaik pada 98,51 persen *micro-F1* dan akurasi, sedangkan *ensemble* terbobot memperoleh *macro-F1* terkuat di antara varian *ensemble* pada 74,24 persen. *Masking* keras menurunkan performa secara substansial, sedangkan *masking* lunak lebih *robust* tetapi tetap berada di bawah *decoding* tanpa *constraint*, yang mengungkap adanya *trade-off* antara akurasi *tag* yang sering muncul dan *robustness* *tag* yang langka.

tldr.en: This paper proposes a hybrid ensemble framework for Amazigh part-of-speech tagging that integrates bidirectional long short-term memory networks, conditional random fields, and a rule-based morphological analyzer. The stacking ensemble achieves the best micro-level performance with 98.51 percent micro-F1 and accuracy.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan *framework* *ensemble* hibrida untuk *part-of-speech* *tagging* bahasa Amazigh yang mengintegrasikan *bidirectional* *long* *short-term* *memory* *networks*, *conditional* *random* *fields*, dan *rule-based* *morphological* *analyzer*. *Ensemble* *stacking* mencapai performa tingkat mikro terbaik dengan *micro-F1* dan akurasi sebesar 98,51 persen.

doi:10.3390/info17080753.title: Ensemble-Based Approach for Amazigh POS Tagging: Leveraging Multiple Models for Enhanced Performance in Low-Resource Language Processing

doi:10.3390/info17090921.abstract: Fine-tuning is often treated as a prerequisite for deploying large language models in low-resource languages, yet its value for recent open-weight models is unclear. We evaluate eleven checkpoints of 7–14 billion parameters before and after Low-Rank Adaptation on 5000 human-curated Kazakh instruction–response pairs. Evaluation is performed on the Kazakh splits of KazMMLU, ARC, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and GSM8K, with Russian GSM8K as a higher-resource comparison. Our central finding is a language asymmetry: the same Kazakh-trained adapters improved Russian GSM8K more than the Kazakh GSM8K they targeted. Excluding one checkpoint that collapsed after fine-tuning by up to 58 percentage points, the remaining ten gained +2.6 percentage points on average on Kazakh (range −6.1 to +13.6) against +6.9 on Russian, significant under a paired signed-rank test. A manual audit of 400 responses identifies a contributing mechanism: Kazakh outputs were more often truncated before a final answer, and correct Kazakh reasoning more often scored wrong by answer extraction, so part of the gap reflects response form, not reasoning. Adaptation produced no meaningful average change on the four multiple-choice benchmarks. GSM8K is the suite’s only free-form task, so generality is untested. These results suggest that low-resource fine-tuning should be evaluated per checkpoint, benchmark, and language rather than being adopted by default.

glossary.explanation_id: Sebuah metode *parameter-efficient fine-tuning* yang melatih matriks rank rendah untuk memperbarui bobot model dengan efisien.
Model bahasa besar yang bobot parameternya dibagikan secara publik untuk penggunaan dan penelitian lebih lanjut.
Keadaan tersimpan dari parameter model pada tahap tertentu selama proses pelatihan atau penyesuaian.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain memiliki ketersediaan data dan sumber daya komputasi yang sangat terbatas.
Kemampuan model untuk melakukan tugas baru tanpa memerlukan contoh pelatihan atau penyesuaian sebelumnya.

background.en: Fine-tuning is commonly regarded as a necessary prerequisite for deploying large language models in low-resource languages. However, the actual value and impact of fine-tuning for recent open-weight models remain unclear, particularly given the potential risks of model degradation and language asymmetry during adaptation.
background.id: Fine-tuning umumnya dianggap sebagai prasyarat yang diperlukan untuk menerapkan large language model pada bahasa low-resource. Namun, nilai aktual dan dampak dari fine-tuning untuk model open-weight terbaru masih belum jelas, terutama mengingat potensi risiko penurunan degradasi model dan asimetri bahasa selama adaptasi.

contributions.en: The paper contributes an evaluation of eleven open-weight models ranging from 7 to 14 billion parameters before and after Low-Rank Adaptation using five thousand human-curated Kazakh instruction-response pairs. It provides empirical insights into the language asymmetry observed between Kazakh and Russian benchmarks.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memberikan kontribusi evaluasi terhadap sebelas model open-weight dengan rentang 7 hingga 14 miliar parameter sebelum dan sesudah Low-Rank Adaptation menggunakan lima ribu pasang instruksi dan respons bahasa Kazakh yang dikurasi oleh manusia. Penelitian ini memberikan wawasan empiris mengenai asimetri bahasa yang diamati antara benchmark bahasa Kazakh dan bahasa Rusia.

future_work.en: The authors note that since GSM8K is the only free-form task in the evaluation suite, the broader generality of these findings remains untested. They suggest that low-resource fine-tuning should be evaluated per checkpoint, benchmark, and language rather than adopted by default.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa karena GSM8K adalah satu-satunya tugas bentuk bebas dalam rangkaian evaluasi, generalisasi yang lebih luas dari temuan ini masih belum diuji. Mereka menyarankan agar fine-tuning bahasa low-resource dievaluasi per checkpoint, benchmark, dan bahasa, alih-alih diadopsi secara bawaan.

method.en: The evaluation uses eleven checkpoints of models with 7 to 14 billion parameters before and after applying Low-Rank Adaptation. The training dataset consists of 5,000 human-curated Kazakh instruction-response pairs. Evaluation is conducted on Kazakh splits of KazMMLU, ARC, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and GSM8K, with Russian GSM8K included as a higher-resource comparison. Additionally, a manual audit of 400 responses is performed to investigate error mechanisms such as output truncation and answer extraction failures.
method.id: Evaluasi ini menggunakan sebelas checkpoint dari model dengan parameter 7 hingga 14 miliar sebelum dan sesudah menerapkan Low-Rank Adaptation. Kumpulan data pelatihan terdiri dari 5.000 pasang instruksi dan respons bahasa Kazakh yang dikurasi oleh manusia. Evaluasi dilakukan pada pembagian bahasa Kazakh dari KazMMLU, ARC, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, dan GSM8K, dengan GSM8K bahasa Rusia yang disertakan sebagai perbandingan sumber daya yang lebih tinggi. Selain itu, audit manual terhadap 400 respons dilakukan untuk menyelidiki mekanisme kesalahan seperti pemotongan keluaran dan kegagalan ekstraksi jawaban.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan terkait secara mendetail.

results.en: The central finding is a language asymmetry: Kazakh-trained adapters improved Russian GSM8K performance more than the target Kazakh GSM8K. Excluding one collapsed checkpoint, ten models gained an average of 2.6 percentage points on Kazakh compared to 6.9 on Russian, which is statistically significant under a paired signed-rank test. A manual audit revealed that Kazakh outputs were frequently truncated before a final answer and correct reasoning was often penalized by answer extraction issues. Meanwhile, adaptation produced no meaningful average change on the four multiple-choice benchmarks.
results.id: Temuan utamanya adalah asimetri bahasa: adapter yang dilatih pada bahasa Kazakh meningkatkan performa GSM8K bahasa Rusia lebih besar daripada GSM8K bahasa Kazakh target. Tidak termasuk satu checkpoint yang mengalami keruntuhan, sepuluh model memperoleh rata-rata 2,6 persentase poin pada bahasa Kazakh dibandingkan dengan 6,9 pada bahasa Rusia, yang signifikan secara statistik di bawah uji peringkat bertanda berpasangan. Audit manual mengungkapkan bahwa keluaran bahasa Kazakh sering kali terpotong sebelum jawaban akhir dan penalaran yang benar sering kali disalahkan oleh masalah ekstraksi jawaban. Sementara itu, adaptasi tidak menghasilkan perubahan rata-rata yang berarti pada keempat benchmark pilihan ganda.

tldr.en: This paper evaluates eleven open-weight large language models before and after fine-tuning on Kazakh instruction data across multiple benchmarks. The findings reveal a language asymmetry where adapters improved Russian performance more than Kazakh, and show that low-resource fine-tuning should be evaluated per checkpoint and benchmark rather than adopted by default.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengevaluasi sebelas *large language model* *open-weight* sebelum dan sesudah *fine-tuning* pada data instruksi bahasa Kazakh di berbagai *benchmark*. Temuan utama mengungkapkan adanya asimetri bahasa di mana *adapter* meningkatkan performa bahasa Rusia lebih besar daripada bahasa Kazakh, serta menunjukkan bahwa *fine-tuning* bahasa *low-resource* harus dievaluasi per *checkpoint* dan *benchmark* dan bukan diadopsi secara bawaan.

doi:10.3390/info17090921.title: When Does Fine-Tuning Matter for a Low-Resource Language? Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs on Kazakh Benchmarks

doi:10.3390/jmse14171658.abstract: A collision avoidance decision-making method that integrates intention recognition with predictive risk perception is proposed to address the uncertainty and dynamic complexity of multi-ship encounters. First, the probabilities of avoidance maneuvers are derived from COLREGs and maritime practice to establish predictive distributions of course alterations. Second, an avoidance-maneuver intention (AMI) confidence coefficient is formulated from evidence fused using Dempster–Shafer (DS) evidence theory to quantify the reliability of the target ship’s maneuver behavior. Third, a predictive risk-perception-based line-of-sight (PRP-LOS) method is developed by introducing a predicted-equivalent virtual ship position into a navigation risk field. Simulation results show that the proposed method accurately infers target-ship AMIs and effectively reduces collision risk while balancing safety and smoothness. These research results provide effective methodological support for improving autonomous decision-making capabilities.

doi:10.3390/languages11080170.abstract: This paper focuses on historical and new linguistic minorities in educational contexts in Italy. It argues that, despite increasing multilingualism, the Italian educational system remains shaped by a persistent monolingual ideology. Drawing on data from two research projects, La classe plurilingue (2018–2020) and MinEdu—Supporting Minority Languages in Educational Contexts (2023–2026), it examines how different forms of multilingualism, both of which can be framed within a heritage language profile, are managed across educational settings. The analysis highlights a fundamental asymmetry: while historical minority languages are institutionally recognized but internally contested (particularly with respect to standardization), languages associated with migration are largely marginalized. The paper argues that both phenomena can be understood within a broader ideological framework described as “monolingualism within multilingualism”, and calls for a rethinking of language education policies in Italy.
doi:10.3390/languages11080170.title: Historical and New Minority Languages in Italian Educational Contexts: Practices, Challenges, and Ideologies

doi:10.3390/make8080246.abstract: Target-speaker automatic speech recognition (TS-ASR) enables transcription of a specific speaker in multi-talker environments, yet remains largely unexplored for multilingual, low-resource languages. Existing TS-ASR systems predominantly target monolingual English using diarization-based or speaker-embedding approaches, leaving a critical gap for languages such as Kazakh, where code-switching with Russian and English is commonplace. We propose Persona-ASR, a modular two-stage architecture. The first stage is an explicit target-presence gate that verifies whether the enrolled speaker appears in the mixture and emits a token to suppress transcription when the speaker is absent, directly addressing the acoustic-hallucination failure mode of prior systems. The second stage performs enrollment-conditioned recognition: a 192-dimensional ECAPA-TDNN speaker embedding modulates a WavLM-Base-Plus encoder through feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), while language-specific CTC heads enable joint Kazakh and English decoding without forcing Latin and Cyrillic symbols to compete in a single output space. To evaluate the system, we introduce KazMix3, a Kazakh overlap dataset for TS-ASR training, and PersonaMix, a controlled bilingual benchmark spanning same- and cross-language enrollment across varying interferer counts (1–3) and signal-to-noise ratios (−3 to +3 dB). Persona-ASR outperforms a strong off-the-shelf cascade baseline by 13.3 WER points on English and 24.6 on Kazakh, and matches a published monolingual English baseline. On PersonaMix, speaker conditioning reduces relative word error rate by 40.7% on English and 59.3% on Kazakh mixtures over an unconditioned variant of the same model, and cross-language enrollment (unseen during training) remains effective, increasing average raw WER by only 4.1 points (English) and 2.2 points (Kazakh) relative to same-language enrollment. To our knowledge, Persona-ASR is the first TS-ASR system for the Kazakh language, establishing a foundation for multilingual personalized ASR in low-resource settings.

background.en: Target-speaker automatic speech recognition enables the transcription of a specific speaker in multi-talker environments. However, this technology remains largely unexplored for multilingual and low-resource languages, leaving a critical gap for languages such as Kazakh where code-switching is common.

Namun, teknologi ini sebagian besar masih belum dieksplorasi untuk bahasa multinasional dan *low-resource*, menygalkan celah kritis untuk bahasa seperti Kazakh di mana *code-switching* sering terjadi.

contributions.en: The authors propose Persona-ASR, a modular two-stage architecture designed for bilingual target-speaker speech recognition. Additional contributions include the introduction of KazMix3, a Kazakh overlap dataset, and PersonaMix, a controlled bilingual benchmark.

Kontribusi tambahan mencakup pengenalan KazMix3, sebuah *dataset* tumpang tindih bahasa Kazakh, dan PersonaMix, sebuah *benchmark* dwibahasa yang terkontrol.

method.en: The first stage of Persona-ASR uses an explicit target-presence gate to verify whether the enrolled speaker appears in the mixture and suppresses transcription when absent. The second stage performs enrollment-conditioned recognition where a 192-dimensional ECAPA-TDNN speaker embedding modulates a WavLM-Base-Plus encoder through feature-wise linear modulation, while language-specific Connectionist Temporal Classification heads enable joint Kazakh and English decoding.

Tahap kedua melakukan *enrollment-conditioned recognition* di mana *speaker embedding* ECAPA-TDNN 192-dimensi memodulasi *encoder* WavLM-Base-Plus melalui *feature-wise linear modulation*, sementara kepala *Connectionist Temporal Classification* yang spesifik bahasa memungkinkan dekode gabungan bahasa Kazakh dan Inggris.

related_work.en: Existing target-speaker speech recognition systems predominantly target monolingual English using diarization-based or speaker-embedding approaches. These prior systems suffer from acoustic-hallucination failure modes when the target speaker is absent.

Sistem pendahulu ini menderita mode kegagalan berupa *acoustic-hallucination* ketika pembicara target tidak hadir.

results.en: Persona-ASR outperforms a strong off-the-shelf cascade baseline by 13.3 WER points on English and 24.6 on Kazakh, while matching a published monolingual English baseline. On PersonaMix, speaker conditioning reduces relative word error rate by 40.7 percent on English and 59.3 percent on Kazakh mixtures compared to an unconditioned variant.
results.id: Persona-ASR mengungguli *baseline* *cascade* bawaan yang kuat sebesar 13.3 poin *WER* pada bahasa Inggris dan 24.6 pada bahasa Kazakh, serta menyamai *baseline* bahasa Inggris *monolingual* yang telah dipublikasikan. Pada PersonaMix, *speaker conditioning* mengurangi tingkat kesalahan kata relatif sebesar 40.7 persen pada campuran bahasa Inggris dan 59.3 persen pada bahasa Kazakh dibandingkan dengan varian tanpa kondisi.

tldr.en: This paper introduces Persona-ASR, a bilingual target-speaker speech recognition system for Kazakh and English overlapping speech. It achieves significant performance improvements over baselines by combining a target-presence gate with enrollment-conditioned recognition.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan Persona-ASR, sebuah sistem *target-speaker speech recognition* dwibahasa untuk ucapan tumpang tindih dalam bahasa Kazakh dan Inggris. Sistem ini mencapai peningkatan performa yang signifikan dibandingkan *baseline* dengan menggabungkan *target-presence gate* dan *enrollment-conditioned recognition*.

doi:10.34044/j.kjss.2026.47.3.18.abstract: Students in Indonesia must complete the study of regional languages as their mother tongue learning. Regional languages for students are considered difficult because of inadequate teaching materials, especially Using (Osing) language teaching materials for elementary school students. This study is an analysis of the need to determine the foundation to be used in the development of teaching material products in elementary school in Banyuwangi, East Java, Indonesia. This study used convergent parallel mixed method and qualitative approach to conduct surveys and interviews for data analysis. The results showed that students need teaching materials Using (Osing) regional languages for mother tongue learning. Analyze student needs by pointing out eight things: who the language learner is, proficiency level, intercultural competence, learning preferences, attitudes, goals and expectations, target context, and student interests. Meanwhile, four things for teachers ‘ needs are related to problems and identifying priorities facing teachers, identifying abilities, identifying attitudes, and solutions. These results will be the basis for the development of Using (Osing) language teaching materials for elementary school students in Indonesia.
doi:10.34044/j.kjss.2026.47.3.18.title: Need analysis on developing Using (Osing) teaching material as a mother tongue learning in Indonesia

doi:10.34778/a48xn206.abstract: Brief Description This variable proposes LLM-Assisted Dialect Gloss Detection (see also Bommarito & Michael, 2025; Liang et al., 2026) and refers to the automated identification, contextual interpretation, and measurement of dialectal, vernacular, or otherwise non-standard linguistic forms in digital texts (Joshi et al., 2025). The procedure combines dictionary-based detection with large language model (LLM)-assisted contextual glossing. A gloss is understood here as a standardized explanation or rendering of a dialectal expression that supports computational analysis while preserving the original linguistic form (Bommarito & Michael, 2025). The variable operationalizes dialect use by identifying vernacular tokens, phrases, or grammatical forms and converting these observations into measurable outputs. One output is dialect intensity, calculated either as a continuous measure, such as the number or proportion of dialect markers per comment, post, or document, or as an ordinal measure, such as low, medium, or high dialect presence. Additional outputs may include glossed text, lists of detected dialect terms, uncertainty scores (provided by the model), and dialect dictionaries developed from corpus-level aggregation. For instance, the comment “cah even scratch my bamcee in peace inno” contains three detected dialect forms: cah, bamcee, and inno. These are contextually glossed as “I can't even scratch my behind in peace, you know,” while the original wording is retained for analysis. Based on the proportion and distribution of detected dialect forms, the comment receives a dialect intensity score of 0.38. LLM-Assisted Dialect Gloss Detection is particularly relevant for automated content analysis in dialect-rich environments where standard preprocessing pipelines may normalize, misclassify, or erase vernacular forms. In such contexts, spelling variation, code-switching, phonetic writing, regional grammar, and culturally specific vocabulary can reduce the validity of downstream analyses such as sentiment analysis, topic modeling, stance detection, or frame analysis. The original text remains unchanged, while the gloss layer provides a machine-readable representation for subsequent automated analysis. While low-resource language glossing is fairly successful if the model is provided with sufficient context, the approach should be combined with a human/machine-in-the-loop approach to avoid reintroducing the language-flattening aspects of automated translation that this approach aims to avoid (Alqazlan et al., 2025; Hong et al., 2022). Field of Application/Theoretical Foundation The theoretical foundation of the variable lies in sociolinguistic work on language variation, indexicality, and the social meaning of dialect (Eckert, 2008; Labov, 1972). Vernacular forms can signal locality, group membership, stance, affect, humor, intimacy, resistance, or cultural belonging (Ming, 2020). At the same time, the variable is grounded in computational communication research and automated content analysis. Dictionary-based procedures are widely used but depend on the quality and coverage of the underlying dictionary. This is problematic in dialect-rich contexts, where relevant terms may be absent from standard dictionaries, may appear in multiple spellings, or may only be interpretable within local context. LLM-assisted glossing can help address these limitations by identifying additional candidate forms and producing contextual metadata. References/Combination with other Methods of Data Collection LLM-Assisted Dialect Gloss Detection can be combined with manual content analysis or serve as a preprocessing step for other automated content analysis variables. For example, sentiment analysis may be conducted on both the original text and the glossed text to examine whether dialect-aware preprocessing changes sentiment scores. Topic modeling or frame analysis may be applied after glossing to reduce the exclusion of dialect-rich comments from interpretable topic clusters. A typical automated procedure consists of the following steps: Corpus preparation: Collect digital texts and retain the original text without normalization or spelling correction. Seed dictionary construction: Develop an initial vernacular dictionary from existing linguistic resources, prior research, expert knowledge, or manually reviewed corpus samples. Dictionary-based detection: Identify known dialect tokens or phrases through rule-based or dictionary-based matching. LLM-assisted glossing: Use constrained prompts to identify additional dialect forms, propose contextual glosses, and generate structured metadata. Human validation: Review a benchmark sample of extracted terms and glosses, ideally with coders or validators familiar with the relevant language variety. Validators assess whether the extracted forms are contextually valid, whether the glosses accurately represent their meaning, and whether cultural meaning, pragmatic force, and the voice of the original comment have been preserved. Disagreements or inaccurate outputs are used to revise the dictionary, glosses, and prompting procedure. External sources, including published online and offline dictionaries are used as external validators. Dictionary refinement: Terms are shown to validators in batches of 25 to confirm Add validated forms to the dictionary and remove false positives. Scoring: Calculate dialect intensity as a raw count, normalized rate, binary indicator, or ordinal category, e.g. Downstream analysis: Use the original and glossed text for further automated or qualitative analysis. Example Studies for Automated Content Analysis Table 1 provides examples of work on dialect detection in low resource languages. Robinson et al. (2024) introduce Kreyòl-MT, a large-scale machine-translation dataset and model infrastructure for Creole languages across Latin America, the Caribbean, and Africa. Smith et al. (2026) develop CariBOT, a Trinidadian English Creole to Standard English architecture for improving chatbot responses. Their Caribe library preprocesses Creole input before it reaches a standard English chatbot. Jackson et al. (2025) assess GPT-4’s communicative competence with Trinidadian English Creole and show the struggle with vocabulary, authenticity, and correct identification. glossary.explanation_id: Proses memberikan penjelasan atau terjemahan standar pada ekspresi dialek untuk mempermudah analisis komputasi.
Bahasa atau bentuk linguistik sehari-hari yang digunakan oleh kelompok atau komunitas tertentu.
Penggunaan dua bahasa atau lebih secara bergantian dalam satu percakapan atau konteks.
Kumpulan teks terstruktur yang digunakan sebagai dasar penelitian linguistik atau pelatihan *model bahasa*.

background.en: Automated content analysis in dialect-rich environments often suffers because standard preprocessing pipelines normalize, misclassify, or erase vernacular forms. Spelling variations, code-switching, and regional grammar can severely reduce the validity of downstream tasks such as sentiment analysis or topic modeling.
background.id: Analisis konten otomatis di lingkungan yang kaya dialek sering kali terkendala karena pipa pemrosesan awal standar menormalisasi, salah mengklasifikasikan, atau menghapus bentuk-bentuk vernakular. Variasi ejaan, alih kode, dan tata bahasa regional dapat secara drastis mengurangi validitas tugas hilir seperti analisis sentimen atau pemodelan topik.

contributions.en: The paper introduces a hybrid workflow combining dictionary-based detection with large language model-assisted contextual glossing, generating machine-readable gloss layers alongside quantitative dialect intensity scores without altering the original text.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan alur kerja hibrida yang menggabungkan deteksi berbasis kamus dengan *pengharkatan kontekstual* berbantuan *large language model*, menghasilkan lapisan glos yang dapat dibaca mesin beserta skor intensitas dialek kuantitatif tanpa mengubah teks asli.

future_work.en: The authors emphasize the necessity of combining automated approaches with a human-in-the-loop methodology to avoid language flattening and ensure the preservation of original voice and cultural meaning.
future_work.id: Para penulis menekankan perlunya menggabungkan pendekatan otomatis dengan metodologi *human-in-the-loop* untuk menghindari perataan bahasa dan memastikan pelestarian suara asli serta makna budaya.

method.en: The procedure consists of corpus preparation, seed dictionary construction, dictionary-based matching, large language model-assisted glossing using constrained prompts, human validation with domain experts, dictionary refinement in batches, and computation of dialect intensity.
method.id: Prosedur ini terdiri dari penyiapan korpus, pembangunan kamus awal, pencocokan berbasis kamus, *pengharkatan* berbantuan *large language model* menggunakan *prompt* terbatas, validasi manusia dengan pakar domain, penyempurnaan kamus secara bertahap, serta penghitungan intensitas dialek.

related_work.en: Prior approaches rely heavily on static dictionaries or direct machine translation, which often fail due to limited vocabulary coverage, spelling variations, and the loss of local pragmatic force and cultural nuance.
related_work.id: Pendekatan sebelumnya sangat mengandalkan kamus statis atau terjemahan mesin langsung, yang sering kali gagal akibat cakupan kosakata yang terbatas, variasi ejaan, serta hilangnya kekuatan pragmatis lokal dan nuansa budaya.

results.en: The framework successfully processes large corpora, such as 30,000 TikTok comments, by pairing automated dictionary lookups and zero-shot large language model prompting with rigorous human validation to assess detection and glossing performance separately.
results.id: Kerangka kerja ini berhasil memproses korpus besar, seperti 30.000 komentar TikTok, dengan memasangkan pencarian kamus otomatis dan *prompt* *zero-shot* *large language model* dengan validasi manusia yang ketat untuk menilai kinerja deteksi dan pengharkatan secara terpisah.

tldr.en: This paper proposes LLM-Assisted Dialect Gloss Detection to identify, interpret, and measure non-standard linguistic forms in digital texts. The method combines dictionary lookup with large language model-assisted contextual glossing to preserve original wording while supporting downstream computational analysis.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan *LLM-Assisted Dialect Gloss Detection* untuk mengidentifikasi, menginterpretasi, dan mengukur bentuk-bentuk linguistik non-standar dalam teks digital. Metode ini menggabungkan pencarian kamus dengan *pengharkatan kontekstual* berbasis *large language model* untuk mempertahankan kata-kata asli sembari mendukung analisis komputasi hilir.

doi:10.35307/saltel.v9i2.183.abstract: The characteristics of social media influencers (charismatic personas, storytelling, humour and the use of layman’s terms) have increasingly permeated into higher education, but there has been little empirical research on how the delivery of social media influencers influences the attitudes of students in formal university setting, especially in Southeast Asian settings. The study investigates the attitudes of university students towards the use of influencer’s pedagogical style, based on Petty and Cacioppo’s (1986) Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM), which distinguishes between the academic content quality (central route) and the stylistic/persona cues (peripheral route). A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was conducted on a convenience sample of 120 students (70 from Brunei Darussalam and 50 from Bandung, Indonesia) with five-point Likert scales and analysed with SPSS with Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression and independent samples t-text. The reliability of all constructs was very high (α = .908 – .951) The results showed that there was a strong and positive correlation between content quality and attitudes (r = .860) and also between stylistic/persona cues and attitudes (r = .796). The overall model accounted 80.2% of the variance in attitude, with content quality being the more powerful predictor (β = .597) and stylistic/persona cues being a significant independent predictor (β = .363). A significant difference in positive attitudes was found between the Indonesian (M – 3.83) and Bruneian (M = 3.51) respondents. Lastly, the study suggests that the influence-pedagogy approach combine intellectual rigour with entertaining presentations and be applied culturally appropriate to each country’s higher education system.

doi:10.35307/saltel.v9i2.183.title: University Students’ Attitudes Toward Influencer-Style Pedagogical Delivery: A Cross-National Study of Brunei Darussalam and Indonesia
